engines.name: WebGLRenderer
engines.does: WebGL 2 renderer that draws scenes into a canvas or render target, with tone mapping, shadow maps, clipping, sorting and state control.

engines.name: PMREMGenerator
engines.does: Turns equirectangular maps, cube maps or captured scenes into roughness-prefiltered cube maps for image-based lighting.

engines.name: Animation system
engines.does: Clips of keyframe tracks played by a mixer with per-action weight, speed, looping and cross-fades.

engines.name: Loaders and exporters
engines.does: Addon loaders and exporters for glTF, FBX, OBJ, USD, Draco, KTX2 and HDR image formats.

engines.name: EffectComposer
engines.does: Post-processing chain for WebGLRenderer built from addon passes such as bloom, AO, outline, depth of field and anti-aliasing.

engines.name: WebXRManager
engines.does: Wraps the WebXR Device API behind renderer.xr, with sessions, controllers, hands, foveation and depth sensing.

engines.name: Raycaster
engines.does: Casts rays for picking against meshes, lines, points, sprites, instances and batches.

engines.name: ShaderChunk and ShaderLib
engines.does: Source-level library of GLSL snippets and full built-in material programs used to assemble every built-in material.

engines.name: Colour management
engines.does: Working colour space, space definitions and conversions between linear and sRGB.

scripting: custom GLSL via ShaderMaterial and onBeforeCompile
outcomes: interactive 3D scenes in a browser canvas

entries.verified: 2026-11-02, how: docs class pages and repository source files read through WebFetch; entry url not opened in this sweep (official domain, unchecked)

capabilities.does: Draws a scene seen by a camera into a canvas or OffscreenCanvas using WebGL 2. WebGL 1 support ended at release r163.
capabilities.inputs: scene, camera; options canvas (or OffscreenCanvas), context
capabilities.outputs: frame on the canvas or in a render target

capabilities.does: Constructor flags choose what the drawing buffer holds: alpha, premultipliedAlpha, stencil, depth, preserveDrawingBuffer, default shader precision, and failIfMajorPerformanceCaveat.
capabilities.inputs: parameters object: alpha, premultipliedAlpha, stencil, depth, preserveDrawingBuffer, precision (highp/mediump/lowp), failIfMajorPerformanceCaveat

capabilities.does: The antialias constructor flag turns on multisample anti-aliasing for the default framebuffer. It is off by default.
capabilities.outputs: smoothed polygon edges on the canvas

capabilities.does: powerPreference asks the browser for the low-power or high-performance GPU on machines with two GPUs.
logarithmicDepthBuffer spreads depth precision over very large near-to-far ranges by writing gl_FragDepth. It can cost speed and is ignored with a reversed depth buffer.
capabilities.outputs: stable depth over huge scale ranges

capabilities.does: reversedDepthBuffer stores depth in reverse order, needs the EXT_clip_control extension, and is described as faster and more accurate than the logarithmic buffer.
capabilities.outputs: higher depth precision at long range

capabilities.does: outputBufferType sets the pixel type of the output buffer. HalfFloatType is advised for high dynamic range rendering with tone mapping and post-processing.
The renderer maps linear HDR colour to display range with a chosen operator and an exposure multiplier.

Operator constants: NoToneMapping, LinearToneMapping, ReinhardToneMapping, CineonToneMapping, ACESFilmicToneMapping, AgXToneMapping, NeutralToneMapping (Khronos PBR Neutral), and CustomToneMapping supplied through shader code.
Each material has a toneMapped flag that excludes it from the renderer tone mapping.
The renderer converts to an output colour space at the end of the pipeline. Default is sRGB; linear sRGB can be chosen instead.
Global constants name colour spaces and transfer functions: NoColorSpace, SRGBColorSpace, LinearSRGBColorSpace, LinearTransfer, SRGBTransfer.

Colour textures such as map and emissiveMap use SRGBColorSpace. Data textures such as roughness, metalness, normal, AO and bump stay at NoColorSpace. Lighting textures such as envMap and lightMap are normally linear.
Shadow rendering is switched on at the renderer and chosen per light. The shadowMap object holds enabled, autoUpdate, needsUpdate and type.
capabilities.outputs: shadows from lights that set castShadow

capabilities.does: Shadow filter types: BasicShadowMap (unfiltered, fastest), PCFShadowMap (default), VSMShadowMap (variance maps). PCFSoftShadowMap is deprecated since r186.
Shadow radius above 1 blurs the edges of the shadow map, except with BasicShadowMap. A VSM map has its own blurSamples count (default 8).
bias shifts the depth compared in the shadow test, with small values around 0.0001 cutting acne. normalBias shifts the lookup along the surface normal, which can distort shadows.
mapSize sets the shadow texture resolution, ideally powers of two. Larger gives sharper shadows and costs more.
Every light shadow owns a camera that views the scene from the light. Its frustum is also used to cull casters.
A shadow can be frozen for static lighting with autoUpdate false, then refreshed once by setting needsUpdate true. Shadow strength has an intensity from 0 to 1.
shadowSide on a material says which faces cast shadows. When null it is derived from the render side.
The renderer separates logical size from the drawing buffer. setPixelRatio, setSize and setDrawingBufferSize set them, and getters return both.
Global clipping planes in world space cut away points with a negative distance. Setting localClippingEnabled makes per-material planes work too.
A material takes its own world-space Plane list. clipIntersection clips only where all planes overlap, and clipShadows applies the planes to shadows.
The info object reports memory use (geometries, textures) and per-frame counts of calls, triangles, points, lines and compiled programs. autoReset and reset() control the counters.
capabilities exposes read-only context limits, for example maxTextureSize, maxSamples, shader precision and getMaxAnisotropy().
setRenderTarget directs drawing into a render target, optionally one cube face and mip level. Passing null returns to the canvas.
Viewport and scissor rectangles restrict drawing to part of the target, which allows split screens and picture-in-picture views.
Pixels of a render target can be read into a typed array, either blocking or through a Promise. The async form is the one advised.
Copy calls move data from the framebuffer into a FramebufferTexture or between two textures, with source region, destination position and mip levels.
capabilities.inputs: copyFramebufferToTexture(texture, position, level), copyTextureToTexture(src, dst, srcRegion, dstPosition, srcLevel, dstLevel)

capabilities.does: compile builds all material programs for a scene up front to avoid a first-frame stall. compileAsync does it with KHR_parallel_shader_compile and returns a Promise.
initTexture uploads a texture before first use. initRenderTarget allocates a target before anything is copied into it.
Opaque and transparent draw lists are sorted by default and sortObjects toggles this. Custom sort functions replace the defaults, and null restores them.
Automatic clearing is split by buffer (colour, depth, stencil), and the clear colour and alpha can be set and read.
capabilities.inputs: autoClear, autoClearColor, autoClearDepth, autoClearStencil, setClearColor(color, alpha), clear(color, depth, stencil)

capabilities.does: setAnimationLoop runs a frame callback and is preferred over a hand-written requestAnimationFrame loop.
Debug options toggle shader compile and link checks and allow a custom handler that receives the context, program and both shader sources.
resetState clears the renderer idea of GL state so the context can be shared with other libraries. forceContextLoss and forceContextRestore simulate loss.
A scale factor on the transmission backdrop target lowers its resolution to speed up glass materials.
setEffects registers effects that run after the scene render, as a post-processing hook on the renderer.
setNodesHandler lets the WebGL renderer run TSL node materials through a handler object.
MeshStandardMaterial shades with a metalness and roughness model. Scalars multiply texture values, and roughness defaults to 1, metalness to 0.
capabilities.inputs: color, map, roughness, roughnessMap, metalness, metalnessMap

capabilities.does: Roughness is read from the green channel, metalness from blue, ambient occlusion from red, and alpha from green, so one packed texture can serve several maps.
A normal map perturbs lighting per pixel without moving geometry. It can be tangent-space or object-space, has a Vector2 strength, and left-handed maps need the y scale negated.
A grey-scale bump map fakes surface depth in the lighting only. It is ignored when a normal map is present.
A displacement map moves vertices, so displaced geometry casts shadows and hides objects. Scale and bias set the range.
A baked occlusion texture darkens crevices. It reads the red channel, needs a second UV set, and has an intensity from 0 to 1.
A light map carries pre-baked lighting, needs a second UV set, and is usually linear data such as EXR or HDR.
Emissive colour adds self-lit output not changed by other lights. A map and an intensity multiplier modulate it.
A material can carry its own environment map with intensity and rotation. It is prefiltered internally with PMREMGenerator.
flatShading renders per-face normals instead of smoothed vertex normals.
A second glossy layer sits over the base, with its own intensity, roughness and optional normal map.
capabilities.inputs: clearcoat, clearcoatRoughness, clearcoatMap (R), clearcoatRoughnessMap (G), clearcoatNormalMap, clearcoatNormalScale

capabilities.does: Sheen adds a soft rim layer for cloth, with colour, roughness and map channels.
capabilities.inputs: sheen (0 to 1), sheenColor, sheenRoughness (default 1), sheenColorMap, sheenRoughnessMap

capabilities.does: Transmission makes a surface optically transparent with a screen-space backdrop, tied to thickness and ior. Opacity should be 1 when it is used.
capabilities.inputs: transmission (0 to 1), transmissionMap (R), thickness, thicknessMap (G), ior

capabilities.does: Light travelling through a thick transmissive object is tinted: attenuationColor is what white becomes at attenuationDistance. Thickness 0 means thin-walled.
ior sets refraction for non-metals, from 1.0 to 2.333, default 1.5.

Thin-film colour shift varying with view angle, with a film IOR and a thickness range in nanometres (100 to 400 by default), optionally from a map. The older iridescenceThicknessRange array is deprecated since r187.
capabilities.inputs: iridescence, iridescenceIOR (1.3), iridescenceThicknessMinimum, iridescenceThicknessMaximum, iridescenceMap, iridescenceThicknessMap

capabilities.does: Anisotropic highlights for brushed metal. A map gives direction in red and green and strength in blue, and a rotation turns the direction.
Dispersion adds colour splitting to transmissive objects. It has no effect on opaque ones.
specularIntensity scales non-metal specular, with 0 giving a near-Lambertian look. specularColor tints reflection at normal incidence, and reflectivity sets non-metal reflectance.
Above zero, diffuse roughness replaces Lambertian shading with the EON energy-preserving model.
Retroreflectivity sends specular light back toward its source.
MeshToonMaterial bands the lighting with a lookup gradientMap. Nearest filtering is needed so the steps stay hard.
MeshMatcapMaterial takes shading and colour from a lit-sphere image. Scene lights do nothing; it casts shadows onto others but does not self-shadow or receive them.
capabilities.inputs: matcap (SRGB for LDR, linear for EXR), color, map, normalMap, bumpMap

capabilities.does: ShaderMaterial runs your GLSL with uniforms and defines, and the engine adds its built-in uniforms and attributes. glslVersion picks GLSL1 or GLSL3, and uniformsGroups binds uniform buffers.
capabilities.inputs: uniforms, defines, vertexShader, fragmentShader, uniformsGroups, glslVersion

capabilities.does: Flags pass engine data to a custom shader: lights supplies light uniforms, fog supplies fog uniforms (merged from UniformsLib), clipping supplies clip planes.
RawShaderMaterial adds no built-in uniform or attribute declarations, so the source declares everything. It works only with WebGLRenderer.
onBeforeCompile hands over the program source and uniforms of a built-in material so it can be patched. customProgramCacheKey names the variant for caching. WebGLRenderer only.
Transparent materials draw after opaque ones, with opacity from 0 to 1. Blending modes: None, Normal, Additive, Subtractive, Multiply, Custom.
alphaTest discards pixels whose alpha is below a threshold.
alphaHash uses a random threshold per pixel to get transparency without sorting; noise can be reduced with temporal anti-aliasing.
alphaToCoverage smooths alpha-tested or clipped edges and needs an MSAA context.
With CustomBlending the equation and source and destination factors, plus separate alpha-channel versions and constant blend colour, are set by hand.
capabilities.inputs: blendEquation, blendSrc, blendDst, blendEquationAlpha, blendSrcAlpha, blendDstAlpha, blendColor, blendAlpha

capabilities.does: Material depth state: test on or off, write on or off, and comparison function.
Stencil use is enabled per material, with function, reference, masks and the three pass/fail operations.
capabilities.inputs: stencilWrite, stencilFunc, stencilRef, stencilFuncMask, stencilWriteMask, stencilFail, stencilZFail, stencilZPass

capabilities.does: Polygon offset shifts depth by a slope factor and a constant, which helps with decals and hidden-line rendering.
Which faces draw: front, back or double. Double-sided transparent objects are normally drawn in two passes; forceSinglePass disables that.
Turning colorWrite off while still writing depth lets a mesh hide what is behind it without showing itself, combined with renderOrder.
Per-vertex RGB or RGBA colours can be used, and dithering reduces banding in gradients.
A material may force its own shader precision instead of the renderer default.
setValues assigns many properties at once; needsUpdate forces a program rebuild and bumps the version counter.
Lights everything equally from no direction, so it adds no highlights and casts no shadows.
Colour fades from a sky colour above to a ground colour below. It cannot cast shadows.
Parallel rays from an infinitely distant source, aimed at a target object rather than by rotation. Targets must be in the scene when moved.
PointLight radiates from a point in all directions. Intensity is in candela, power in lumens, distance 0 means unlimited range, decay 2 is physically correct.
capabilities.inputs: color, intensity, distance (0), decay (2), power, shadow

capabilities.does: SpotLight is a cone from a point: angle (max pi/2), penumbra 0 to 1, decay, distance, a projected texture map, a target and a shadow.
capabilities.inputs: color, intensity (cd), distance, angle (pi/3), penumbra, decay (2), power, map, target

capabilities.does: RectAreaLight is a rectangle emitter for windows and strips. No shadows, PBR materials only, and RectAreaLightUniformsLib must be initialised for WebGLRenderer.
LightProbe stores diffuse lighting as spherical harmonics and emits nothing. LightProbeGenerator builds one from a cube texture or render target.
Point and spot lights take intensity in candela. Setting power in lumens rewrites intensity accordingly.
Scene.environment gives an environment map to all physical materials without overriding their own envMap. It has an intensity and an Euler rotation.
PMREMGenerator turns an equirectangular map, a cubemap or a captured scene into a roughness-prefiltered cube target. fromScene takes a blur sigma, near, far, size and position.
capabilities.inputs: fromEquirectangular(tex, target), fromCubemap(cube, target), fromScene(scene, sigma, near, far, {size, position})

capabilities.does: compileEquirectangularShader and compileCubemapShader compile the conversion shaders early, overlapping with texture download. dispose frees the generator but not its outputs.
A static helper maps a mip level to the roughness it was filtered for.
scene.background can be a colour, a flat texture or a cube or equirectangular environment, with blurriness 0 to 1, intensity and rotation.
overrideMaterial draws every object with one material, except materials that opt out with allowOverride false.
Fog blends to a colour between near (1) and far (1000) distances.
FogExp2 thickens with distance by a density factor, default 0.00025.
Materials opt in or out of scene fog with a boolean (default true for standard and toon materials).
Texture min and mag filters (Nearest, Linear, mipmap variants) and wrap modes (clamp, repeat, mirrored repeat) are set per texture.
Mipmaps are generated automatically by default and can be user-supplied. Anisotropy raises sharpness at grazing angles; the cap comes from renderer.capabilities.getMaxAnisotropy().
Offset, repeat, rotation about a centre and a matrix build the UV transform. A texture can pick UV set 0 to 3 with channel.
capabilities.inputs: offset, repeat, rotation, center, matrix, matrixAutoUpdate, channel

capabilities.does: Format, type and internalFormat choose pixel layout, bit depth and GPU storage. Size cannot change after first use; dispose and recreate.
capabilities.inputs: format, type, internalFormat, normalized, premultiplyAlpha, flipY, unpackAlignment

capabilities.does: Only subranges of texture data can be re-uploaded with update ranges; needsUpdate re-uploads the whole texture.
CompressedTexture wraps pre-compressed mip chains, since a GPU cannot build mipmaps from block-compressed data. Flip and mip generation are forced off.
Format constants cover S3TC/DXT, PVRTC, ETC1/ETC2, EAC, RGTC, BPTC and ASTC from 4x4 to 12x12 blocks.
KTX2Loader reads KTX 2.0 files holding Basis Universal data and transcodes them into a format the device supports, using workers and a transcoder path.
capabilities.inputs: setTranscoderPath(path), setWorkerLimit(n), detectSupport(renderer), load(url,...), parse(buffer,...), dispose()

capabilities.does: DataTexture builds a texture from a typed array, with nearest filtering and no mipmaps by default. Useful for lookup tables and simulation buffers.
CubeTexture holds six face images for reflections and skyboxes; the loader example passes them in the order px, nx, py, ny, pz, nz.
Mapping constants: UVMapping, cube reflection and refraction, equirectangular reflection and refraction.
BufferGeometry stores named vertex attributes and an optional index. Groups split it into draw ranges per material, and a draw range limits what renders.
Normals are computed by averaging face normals on indexed geometry. Tangents need an indexed mesh with position, normal and uv.
Transforms can be baked into the vertex data: matrix, quaternion, axis rotations, translate, scale, center to origin, lookAt.
capabilities.inputs: applyMatrix4, applyQuaternion, rotateX/Y/Z, translate, scale, center, lookAt

capabilities.does: Bounding box and sphere are computed on demand and used for culling. They must be recomputed after vertices change.
setFromPoints fills positions from Vector2 or Vector3 lists; toNonIndexed returns an unshared-vertex copy.
Morph targets live in morphAttributes and can be absolute positions or offsets via morphTargetsRelative.
BufferGeometry can hold an indirect draw buffer with byte offsets. WebGPU only.
InstancedMesh draws many copies of one geometry and material with a per-instance matrix, which cuts draw calls. After editing matrices the attribute needs needsUpdate set.
capabilities.inputs: geometry, material, count; setMatrixAt(i, Matrix4), instanceMatrix.needsUpdate
capabilities.outputs: many copies in one draw call

capabilities.does: Each instance can have its own colour through the instanceColor attribute, which is null until colours are set and needs needsUpdate after edits.
Morph target weights can differ per instance. They are stored in a DataTexture named morphTexture.
InstancedMesh bounds do not follow moving instances. computeBoundingBox and computeBoundingSphere must be called again so frustum culling and raycasting stay right.
BatchedMesh holds many different geometries that share one material, each instance with its own transform. Capacity limits are fixed at construction for instances, vertices and indices.
Geometries are added, replaced, resized and removed at run time. Reserved counts allow a later larger replacement, and optimize repacks freed space.
capabilities.inputs: addGeometry(geo, reservedVertex, reservedIndex), setGeometryAt, deleteGeometry, optimize(), setGeometrySize, setInstanceCount

capabilities.does: Each batched instance has its own matrix, colour (Vector4 gives alpha), visibility flag and geometry id.
capabilities.inputs: addInstance(geometryId), setMatrixAt, setColorAt, setVisibleAt, setGeometryIdAt, deleteInstance

capabilities.does: Batched objects are frustum culled one by one and sorted to reduce overdraw: transparent back to front, others front to back. A custom sort function can replace this.
LOD switches between objects by camera distance. Each level has a distance threshold and a hysteresis fraction that stops flicker at the border.
capabilities.inputs: addLevel(object, distance, hysteresis), removeLevel(distance), getCurrentLevel(), getObjectForDistance(d), autoUpdate, update(camera)

capabilities.does: SkinnedMesh deforms geometry through a Skeleton using skin index and weight attributes. Attached bind mode shares world space with the skeleton, detached mode lets one skeleton drive several meshes.
capabilities.inputs: bind(skeleton, bindMatrix), bindMode, bindMatrix, normalizeSkinWeights(), pose()

capabilities.does: applyBoneTransform gives a vertex position or direction after skinning, and a bounding box can be computed from the deformed mesh.
An AnimationMixer plays clips on one root object. Time advances with update(delta), a timeScale scales or pauses everything, and actions are cached per clip.
capabilities.inputs: new AnimationMixer(root); clipAction(clip), existingAction, update(dt), setTime, timeScale, stopAllAction()

capabilities.does: Mixers can free cached clips, roots and actions once they are stopped, to release memory.
An action has loop mode (once, repeat, ping-pong), repetitions, time, timeScale (negative plays backward), pause, and clampWhenFinished to hold the last frame.
capabilities.inputs: play(), stop(), reset(), setLoop(mode, reps), setDuration, startAt, clampWhenFinished, paused

capabilities.does: Several actions can mix by weight. fadeIn, fadeOut and crossFade ramp weights over a duration, with optional time warping between differing speeds.
capabilities.inputs: weight, fadeIn(d), fadeOut(d), crossFadeFrom(action, d, warp), crossFadeTo, warp(start, end, d), halt(d), syncWith(action)

capabilities.does: A clip or action can blend normally or additively over other animations.
An AnimationClip bundles KeyframeTracks with a name and a duration (computed from the keys when negative). It can be cloned, trimmed, optimised, validated and serialised.
capabilities.inputs: new AnimationClip(name, duration, tracks, blendMode); optimize(), trim(), resetDuration(), validate(), clone()

capabilities.does: Static helpers build clips from morph target sequences, grouping names like Walk_001 and Walk_002 into separate clips by frame rate.
capabilities.inputs: CreateFromMorphTargetSequence(name, targets, fps, noLoop), CreateClipsFromMorphTargetSequences(targets, fps, noLoop), findByName

capabilities.does: A KeyframeTrack maps times to values for a named property of a bone, morph target or object. Methods can scale, shift, trim, optimise and validate the keys.
capabilities.inputs: new KeyframeTrack(name, times, values, interpolation); scale(), shift(), trim(), optimize(), validate()

capabilities.does: Interpolation constants: InterpolateLinear (default), InterpolateDiscrete, InterpolateSmooth, InterpolateBezier. Bezier needs inTangents and outTangents in track settings.
Zero-slope start and end smooth the interpolation at the clip boundaries so separate start or end clips are not needed.
PerspectiveCamera takes vertical field of view in degrees, aspect, near and far. Zoom scales the view; projection must be rebuilt after changes.
capabilities.inputs: fov (50), aspect (1), near (0.1), far (2000), zoom, updateProjectionMatrix()

capabilities.does: Field of view can be set from a focal length against a film gauge (default 35 mm), with a film offset for off-centre projection.
capabilities.inputs: setFocalLength(mm), getFocalLength(), filmGauge (35), filmOffset (0), getFilmWidth(), getFilmHeight()

capabilities.does: A sub-window of a larger virtual frustum can be rendered, for multi-monitor or multi-machine setups.
capabilities.inputs: setViewOffset(fullW, fullH, x, y, w, h), clearViewOffset()

capabilities.does: The view rectangle at a given distance can be queried for fitting content to the screen.
capabilities.inputs: getViewSize(distance, target), getViewBounds(distance, minTarget, maxTarget), getEffectiveFOV()

capabilities.does: OrthographicCamera has parallel projection with left, right, top, bottom, near and far planes, a zoom and a view offset. Near may be 0.
capabilities.inputs: new OrthographicCamera(left, right, top, bottom, near, far), zoom, setViewOffset

capabilities.does: ArrayCamera renders several perspective sub-cameras, each into its own viewport rectangle, as a split-screen or VR layout. Per-camera culling is optional.
capabilities.inputs: cameras[] each with a viewport, perCameraFrustumCulled (false)

capabilities.does: StereoCamera makes left and right eye cameras from one camera with an eye separation of 0.064 by default. The eyes sit on layers 1 and 2.
Raycaster casts a ray and returns sorted hits on objects. The ray can come from normalised device coordinates and a camera, from a WebXR controller, or from an origin and direction.
capabilities.inputs: set(origin, direction), setFromCamera(ndc, camera), setFromXRController(c), intersectObject(s)(obj, recursive)

capabilities.does: A hit carries distance, world point, face, face index, object, uv, uv1, interpolated normal, plus instanceId for InstancedMesh and batchId for BatchedMesh.
Layers limit what is tested. Params set line and point thresholds in world units, and only front faces hit unless the material is double sided.
A RenderTarget has format, type, filtering, wrap, anisotropy, colour space, optional depth and stencil buffers, mipmap flags, and a depth texture. Width and height are constructor arguments.
capabilities.inputs: new RenderTarget(w, h, {format, type, minFilter, magFilter, colorSpace, depthBuffer, stencilBuffer, depthTexture, generateMipmaps, ...})

capabilities.does: The samples option turns on multisampling for a target. Resolve flags choose whether colour, depth and stencil are resolved, and store flags can drop multisampled data to save bandwidth.
capabilities.inputs: samples (0), resolveColorBuffer, resolveDepthBuffer, resolveStencilBuffer, storeMultisampled* flags

capabilities.does: The count option gives a target several colour attachments, held in the textures array, so one pass can write several outputs.
A target keeps its own viewport and scissor rectangles, with a scissor test flag.
Options for array depth and multiview rendering (OVR_multiview2) exist on render targets.
DepthTexture stores scene depth in a texture bound to a render target, for later sampling in post-processing. A compare function enables comparison sampling.
WebGLCubeRenderTarget is a cube target that can convert an equirectangular texture to a cube map and clear itself.
capabilities.inputs: new WebGLCubeRenderTarget(size, options), fromEquirectangularTexture(renderer, tex), clear(renderer, c, d, s)

capabilities.does: Clock reports delta seconds and total elapsed seconds. Its constructor is marked deprecated since r183 in the docs.
GLTFLoader reads glTF 2.0 .gltf and .glb into a result with scene, scenes, animations, cameras and asset data. Async loading and parsing are provided, and an extension plugin hook can be registered.
capabilities.inputs: load(url), loadAsync(url), parse(data, path), parseAsync, register(plugin)

capabilities.does: Compressed glTF needs helper objects: a Draco loader, a KTX2 loader and a Meshopt decoder are attached to the glTF loader.

Built-in handling covers the glTF material extensions for anisotropy, clearcoat, diffuse roughness, dispersion, emissive strength, IOR, specular, transmission, iridescence, unlit, volume and bump, plus texture transform.
Supported geometry extensions: Draco, Meshopt (KHR and EXT), mesh quantization and GPU instancing. Lights come from KHR_lights_punctual and textures from basisu, AVIF and WebP.
capabilities.inputs: KHR_draco_mesh_compression, EXT_meshopt_compression, KHR_mesh_quantization, EXT_mesh_gpu_instancing, KHR_lights_punctual, KHR_texture_basisu, EXT_texture_avif, EXT_texture_webp

capabilities.does: Some extensions come from outside packages and are registered as plugins, for example KHR_materials_variants, MSFT_texture_dds, KHR_animation_pointer and NEEDLE_progressive. KHR_gaussian_splatting is also listed.

GLTFExporter writes scenes to glTF 2.0 as JSON text or, with binary set, a GLB ArrayBuffer. Options cover node transform form, visibility filter, texture size cap, animations, copyright and custom extensions.
capabilities.inputs: parseAsync(scene, {binary, trs, onlyVisible, maxTextureSize, animations, includeCustomExtensions, copyright})

capabilities.does: Supported export extensions include lights, clearcoat, dispersion, emissive strength, IOR, iridescence, specular, sheen, transmission, unlit, volume, bump, mesh quantization, texture transform, GPU instancing and WebP.
The exporter has a plugin hook and a texture utils setter for compressed textures (WebGLTextureUtils or WebGPUTextureUtils).
DRACOLoader decodes .drc Draco geometry into a BufferGeometry using workers and a decoder path. It chooses JS or WASM decoding by itself.
A Meshopt decoder module passed to GLTFLoader decodes EXT_meshopt_compression and KHR_meshopt_compression content.
FBXLoader reads ASCII FBX 7.0 and later and binary FBX 6400 and later, and returns a Group. Morph normals are not supported, and clips can be trimmed to their stack range.
OBJLoader parses Wavefront OBJ text into a Group. MTL material files are loaded by MTLLoader and attached with setMaterials.

EffectComposer chains post-processing passes for WebGLRenderer, with read and write buffers. Passes can be added, inserted and removed, and render(deltaTime) replaces renderer.render. It is WebGL only.
capabilities.inputs: new EffectComposer(renderer, renderTarget); addPass, insertPass, removePass, render(dt), setSize, setPixelRatio, swapBuffers, reset, dispose

capabilities.does: RenderPass draws the scene into the composer as the first pass. An optional override material, clear colour and alpha apply, and clearDepth can clear only depth.
capabilities.inputs: new RenderPass(scene, camera, overrideMaterial, clearColor, clearAlpha)

capabilities.does: OutputPass applies the renderer tone mapping and colour space conversion at the end of a composer chain. A pass that needs sRGB input, such as FXAA, goes after it.
ShaderPass runs a GLSL shader (or a ShaderMaterial) on the previous result, reading it through a texture uniform named tDiffuse unless changed. It is how FXAAShader is used.
UnrealBloomPass builds a mip chain of bloom textures, each blurred with a different radius. It needs renderer tone mapping on. Strength defaults to 1, radius is 0 to 1.
SSAOPass is a basic screen-space occlusion pass: kernelSize 32, kernelRadius 8, minDistance 0.005, maxDistance 0.1, and an output selector. The docs say SAO and GTAO give better but costlier results.
capabilities.inputs: new SSAOPass(scene, camera, width, height, kernelSize); kernelRadius, minDistance, maxDistance, output

capabilities.does: GTAOPass uses ground-truth AO with a Poisson denoise stage, blend intensity, an optional external depth and normal G-buffer, and a clip box limiting where AO applies.
capabilities.inputs: new GTAOPass(scene, camera, w, h, params, aoParams, pdParams); blendIntensity, setGBuffer(depth, normal), setSceneClipBox(box), updateGtaoMaterial(), updatePdMaterial()

capabilities.does: SAOPass is a further screen-space ambient occlusion pass built from a scene, a camera and a resolution, with its settings held in a params object.
OutlinePass draws outlines on selected objects with edge strength, glow, thickness, pulse period, optional pattern texture, visible and hidden edge colours and a downsample ratio.
capabilities.inputs: new OutlinePass(resolution, scene, camera, selectedObjects); edgeStrength (3), edgeGlow (0), edgeThickness (1), pulsePeriod, visibleEdgeColor, hiddenEdgeColor, downSampleRatio (2)

capabilities.does: BokehPass blurs out-of-focus areas from scene depth. Options: focus distance (default 1), aperture (0.025) and maxblur (1), also reachable as shader uniforms at run time.
SMAAPass applies subpixel morphological anti-aliasing in linear space, so it runs before OutputPass. It has no constructor parameters.
FXAA is used by passing FXAAShader to a ShaderPass. It needs sRGB input, so it runs after OutputPass.
TAARenderPass accumulates jittered camera samples over frames when the scene is still. It uses no reprojection. Properties: accumulate, accumulateIndex, sampleLevel, unbiased.

The CSM addon splits the view frustum into cascades, each with its own directional light and shadow map. Split modes are uniform, logarithmic, practical and custom, with optional fade between cascades. WebGLRenderer only; CSMShadowNode is named for WebGPURenderer.
capabilities.inputs: new CSM({camera, parent, cascades (3), mode, maxFar, shadowMapSize (2048), shadowBias, lightDirection, lightIntensity, lightNear, lightFar, lightMargin}); setupMaterial(m), update(), updateFrustums()
capabilities.outputs: sharp near and far sun shadows

capabilities.does: CubeCamera renders the scene into a cube render target each time update is called, giving live reflections when the target texture is used as envMap. Hide the reflector first.
capabilities.inputs: new CubeCamera(near, far, renderTarget); update(renderer, scene)

capabilities.does: The Sky addon is a dome mesh using the Preetham daylight model. Its uniforms are set on the material, and showSunDisc should be off when rendering an environment map. WebGLRenderer only; SkyMesh is named for WebGPU.
HDRLoader reads Radiance RGBE .hdr files into a half or full float texture, to be used as an equirectangular environment.
EXRLoader reads OpenEXR files with ZIP, ZIPS, RLE, PIZ, B44, DWA compression. Output format (RGBA, RG, Red), data type (half or float) and part index of multi-part files are settable.
capabilities.inputs: new EXRLoader(); setDataType, setOutputFormat, setPart, loadAsync(url)

capabilities.does: UltraHDRLoader reads JPEG with a gain map (XMP and ISO 21496-1 metadata) and rebuilds an HDR texture. EXIF, ICC and non-JPEG are not implemented.

USDZExporter writes a scene as USDZ in an ArrayBuffer. Options: texture size cap (default 1024), AR anchoring properties, a Quick Look workaround, visible-only, and animation baking of position, quaternion and scale tracks at a chosen frame rate.
capabilities.inputs: parseAsync(scene, {maxTextureSize, includeAnchoringProperties, ar, quickLookCompatible, onlyVisible, animations, animationFrameRate})

capabilities.does: OrbitControls moves a camera around a target: rotate, dolly, pan, with damping, auto-rotate, zoom to cursor, polar and azimuth limits, distance and zoom limits, and keyboard, mouse and touch maps.
capabilities.inputs: new OrbitControls(camera, domElement); enableDamping, dampingFactor (0.05), autoRotate, zoomToCursor, minDistance, maxPolarAngle, target, update()

capabilities.does: Controls expose state saving, reset, angle and distance getters, and programmatic dolly, pan and rotate calls. Events: start, change, end.
capabilities.inputs: saveState(), reset(), getPolarAngle(), getDistance(), dollyIn/Out, pan, rotateLeft/Up, listenToKeyEvents()

capabilities.does: renderer.xr is a WebXRManager. Enable it, request a session, and the manager builds an ArrayCamera with one sub-camera per view. Reference space type, framebuffer scale and foveation (0 to 1) are settable.
capabilities.inputs: xr.enabled, setSession(session), getSession(), setReferenceSpaceType(type), setFramebufferScaleFactor(v), setFoveation(v), getCamera()

capabilities.does: Controllers are groups in target-ray or grip space, and hands have their own group for tracking.
The manager reports environment blend mode, depth sensing support, the depth texture and mesh, and a raw camera frame texture.
InstancedBufferGeometry draws one base shape many times with custom per-instance attributes read by a custom shader. instanceCount defaults to Infinity so it must be set.

Timer is the Clock alternative: update(timestamp) advances state, getDelta and getElapsed read it, setTimescale scales delta, and connect(document) uses the Page Visibility API to avoid huge deltas after a hidden tab.
capabilities.inputs: update(ts), getDelta(), getElapsed(), reset(), setTimescale(), connect(document), dispose()

capabilities.does: WebGLRenderer accepts an OffscreenCanvas as its canvas option, in place of a canvas element.

The ColorManagement object holds an enabled flag (true) and a working colour space (linear sRGB). convert moves a colour between spaces through XYZ when primaries differ, with sRGB decode and encode steps.
capabilities.inputs: ColorManagement.enabled, workingColorSpace, convert(color, src, dst), workingToColorSpace, colorSpaceToWorking

capabilities.does: Helpers return the primaries, the transfer function and the luminance coefficients (0.2126, 0.7152, 0.0722 for sRGB and linear sRGB) of a colour space. define adds new space definitions.

An addon math file defines extra spaces as implementation objects with primaries, white point, transfer and matrices: Display P3, linear Display P3, linear Rec. 2020 and extended sRGB. Display P3 variants set display-p3 as drawing buffer space.
The core ColorManagement object defines only sRGB and linear sRGB, and its define() call merges more space definitions, which the addon file supplies for Display P3 and Rec. 2020.

ShaderChunk is a JavaScript object mapping names to GLSL snippets, one per file in a ShaderChunk folder (about 100 pieces such as begin_vertex, lights_physical_fragment, fog_pars_fragment, shadowmap_vertex). Names ending _pars hold declarations.

The folder listing (partly read) shows chunks for alpha test, AO, batching, bump, clearcoat, clipping, colour space, dithering, emissive, environment map, fog, iridescence, lights (Lambert, Phong, physical, toon), log depth, morph targets, normals, roughness, shadow maps and skinning.
capabilities.outputs: map of what each material stage is made of

capabilities.does: ShaderLib holds the full vertex and fragment programs of built-in materials: background, backgroundCube, cube, depth, distance, equirect, linedashed, meshbasic, meshlambert, meshmatcap, meshnormal, meshphong, meshphysical, meshtoon, points, shadow, sprite, vsm. Each is also exposed in ShaderChunk with _vert and _frag keys.
capabilities.outputs: base programs to copy or patch

capabilities.does: MapControls shares OrbitControls code but pans with the left button, rotates with the right, and pans orthogonal to camera.up (screenSpacePanning false) for bird-eye map views.
capabilities.inputs: new MapControls(camera, domElement); mouseButtons, touches, screenSpacePanning

capabilities.does: TrackballControls does not keep a constant up vector, so orbiting over the poles does not flip. Speeds for rotate (1), zoom (1.2), pan (0.3), static or damped motion, and per-action disable flags are set by properties.
capabilities.inputs: rotateSpeed, zoomSpeed, panSpeed, staticMoving, dynamicDampingFactor (0.2), noRotate, noZoom, noPan, handleResize()

capabilities.does: PointerLockControls captures the mouse for first-person looking, with pitch limits, a pointer speed, lock and unlock calls (optionally raw input), and forward and sideways moves in the xz plane.
capabilities.inputs: lock(unadjustedMovement), unlock(), moveForward(d), moveRight(d), getDirection(v), minPolarAngle, maxPolarAngle, pointerSpeed

capabilities.does: TransformControls shows on-screen handles to translate, rotate or scale an attached object, in world or local space, with axis and plane visibility flags, snapping steps, position limits, colours and change events.
capabilities.inputs: attach(obj), detach(), setMode(translate|rotate|scale), setSpace(world|local), translationSnap, rotationSnap, scaleSnap, minX..maxZ, setColors()

capabilities.does: The controls folder also holds ArcballControls, DragControls, FirstPersonControls and FlyControls modules.

The Lensflare addon is attached to a light and draws flare sprites along the line through screen centre. Each element has a texture, size in pixels and distance. It is never frustum culled and renders last. WebGLRenderer only.
capabilities.inputs: new Lensflare(); addElement(new LensflareElement(texture, size, distance))

capabilities.does: Reflector is a flat mirror mesh that renders the scene from a mirrored camera into a target (default 512 x 512, multisample 4). Options: tint colour, clip bias, custom shader, forceUpdate. WebGLRenderer only.
capabilities.inputs: new Reflector(geometry, {color, textureWidth, textureHeight, clipBias, shader, multisample})

capabilities.does: LightProbeGenerator builds a LightProbe from a cube texture (synchronous) or from an RGBA cube render target (asynchronous, with a renderer).
USDLoader reads USDA (text), USDC (binary) and USDZ archives into a Group. Textures load after the group is created, so onLoad signals completion.
capabilities.inputs: new USDLoader(); load(url), loadAsync(url), parse(buffer, path, onLoad, onError)

capabilities.does: Float environment formats covered by addon loaders: Radiance .hdr (HDRLoader), OpenEXR (EXRLoader) and Ultra HDR JPEG (UltraHDRLoader), all defaulting to half-float output.
Each Object3D has castShadow and receiveShadow flags, both false by default, that decide whether it is drawn into shadow maps and whether shadows fall on it.
Objects are skipped when off screen unless frustumCulled is turned off. renderOrder overrides draw order within the opaque and transparent groups.
Objects belong to up to 32 layers. An object is drawn only when it shares a layer with the rendering camera. Layers are set, enabled, disabled, toggled and tested by bit mask, and filter raycasts.
Object3D builds a parent-child scene graph with add, remove, attach (keeps world transform), traverse, traverseVisible, name lookup, world position queries, clone and JSON serialisation.
capabilities.inputs: add(o), remove(o), attach(o), traverse(cb), getObjectByName(n), getWorldPosition(t), clone(), toJSON()

capabilities.does: Matrices update automatically each frame; matrixAutoUpdate and matrixWorldAutoUpdate can be turned off for static objects so matrices are managed by hand.
A static flag tells WebGPURenderer an object will not change after its first render so it can be handled faster.
onBeforeRender and onAfterRender callbacks run around the draw of one object.

Mesh pairs a geometry with one material or an array of materials. A morph target weight list and a name dictionary exist when the geometry has morph targets. getVertexPosition returns the local position after morphing and skinning.
capabilities.inputs: new Mesh(geometry, material | material[]); morphTargetInfluences, morphTargetDictionary, updateMorphTargets(), getVertexPosition(i, target)

capabilities.does: Morph target influences weight each target, usually 0 to 1, and can be driven by animation tracks or set directly.
Mesh and Sprite carry a count property for several instances, which works only with WebGPURenderer.
Points draws each vertex of a geometry as a point with a PointsMaterial by default. It supports morph targets, ray intersection and frustum tests.
Sprite is a plane that always faces the camera, with an anchor and pivot called center (default 0.5, 0.5). It casts no shadows and can be ray-picked.

LoadingManager counts pending assets across loaders and reports start, progress, completion and errors. A URL modifier rewrites requests, for example to blobs, and handlers route file patterns to specific loaders.
capabilities.inputs: new LoadingManager(onLoad, onProgress, onError); setURLModifier(fn), addHandler(regex, loader), removeHandler, resolveURL, abort()

capabilities.does: The library is used from JavaScript modules: core classes come from the main package and addons (loaders, exporters, controls, passes) are imported from an addons path, for example three/addons/loaders/GLTFLoader.js.

entries.name: three.js WebGPURenderer and TSL

licence.name: MIT

engines.name: WebGPURenderer
engines.does: Renderer on the WebGPU API with a WebGL 2 backend selectable by forceWebGL; runs node materials, compute and render pipelines.

engines.name: TSL (Three.js Shading Language)
engines.does: JavaScript node-graph language that compiles to WGSL or GLSL, with functions, uniforms, textures, control flow and compute built-ins.

engines.name: NodeMaterial
engines.does: Material base class whose shader stages and slots can be replaced or edited by nodes.

engines.name: RenderPipeline
engines.does: Post-processing chain for WebGPURenderer defined by an output node, fed by scene passes and effect nodes.

engines.name: Compute
engines.does: ComputeNode and storage buffer nodes for GPU compute dispatched with renderer.compute.

scripting: TSL (JavaScript node graph that compiles to WGSL or GLSL)

rea.notes: Same MIT repository as three-js. Only what the opened pages show is listed; the PostProcessing class is a deprecated name for RenderPipeline (since r183).

entries.verified: 2026-11-02, how: docs class pages and the TSL wiki page read through WebFetch; entry url not opened in this sweep (official domain, unchecked)

capabilities.does: WebGPURenderer draws with the WebGPU API and offers a forceWebGL switch that uses the WebGL 2 backend even where WebGPU is available. Its library property is a StandardNodeLibrary used for type mapping.
A WebGL 2 backend sits behind the same renderer class. The base Renderer takes a backend plus a getFallback option, and forceWebGL picks the fallback by hand.

Constructor options: antialias (4 samples when true), samples, alpha (true by default), depth, stencil, logarithmicDepthBuffer, reversedDepthBuffer, multiview for WebXR, outputType, and outputBufferType (HalfFloatType by default).
capabilities.inputs: antialias, samples, alpha, depth, stencil, logarithmicDepthBuffer, reversedDepthBuffer, multiview, outputType, outputBufferType

capabilities.does: init() returns a Promise and must finish before compute runs. hasFeature(name) answers false before initialisation. compileAsync precompiles materials and pipelines to avoid stutter.
capabilities.inputs: init(), hasFeature(name), compileAsync(scene, camera, targetScene, onProgress)

capabilities.does: Compute nodes are dispatched with compute or computeAsync, which take one or more nodes and an optional dispatch size. Compute only works after init.

ComputeNode wraps shader logic with a thread count or dispatch size and a workgroup size (default [64]). The count creates a bounds check against instanceIndex. As a node it has a per-frame update type.
capabilities.inputs: new ComputeNode(node, workgroupSize); count, dispatchSize, workgroupSize, onInit(cb), setName(name)

capabilities.does: A storage buffer attribute can be copied from GPU to CPU with a Promise, with optional target, offset and count.
The renderer holds an MRT configuration that routes several named outputs to separate attachments.
Renderer carries toneMapping (NoToneMapping default) and toneMappingExposure (1), a contextNode for override nodes, an info object and an inspector slot.
highPrecision uses CPU-side 64-bit model-view and normal-view matrices, which helps at large coordinates. It does not work with InstancedMesh or SkinnedMesh.

TSL is a JavaScript node-graph language that compiles to WGSL for WebGPU or GLSL for WebGL 2. Fn wraps logic in a builder scope that allows assign and conditionals; parameters can be positional or an object with defaults.
TSL has constructors for float, int, uint, bool, color, vec2 to vec4, mat2 to mat4 and the ivec, uvec, bvec families, plus conversion methods such as toFloat, toVec3, toColor.
uniform and uniformArray create shader uniforms, with hooks that update them per object, per render or per frame.
vertexStage computes a value in the vertex stage, varying passes a value to the fragment stage, and varyingProperty declares one without initial value.
Vertex data nodes: attribute, uv, vertexColor, instanceIndex, vertexIndex, drawIndex, and the batch and instance helpers for batched and instanced meshes.
capabilities.inputs: attribute(), uv(), vertexColor(), instanceIndex, vertexIndex, drawIndex, batch(), instance()

capabilities.does: Texture nodes cover filtered sampling, direct load, store, size, bicubic sampling, cube, 3D and triplanar sampling.
capabilities.inputs: texture(), textureLoad(), textureStore(), textureSize(), textureBicubic(), cubeTexture(), texture3D(), triplanarTexture()

capabilities.does: Conditionals If/ElseIf/Else and Switch/Case/Default, the ternary select, and Loop with counts, ranges, nesting, reverse order and conditions. Break, Continue, Discard and Return control flow.
capabilities.inputs: If(), Switch(), select(), Loop(), Break(), Continue(), Discard(), Return()

capabilities.does: Operator and math nodes: add, sub, mul, div, mod, comparisons, logic, bitwise ops, assignment ops, abs, sin, cos, pow, mix, smoothstep, clamp, normalize, dot, cross, reflect, refract and others. Most can be chained as methods.
capabilities.inputs: add, mul, mix, smoothstep, dot, cross, assign, addAssign, PI

capabilities.does: toVar and toConst make variables, property declares one, array and uniformArray hold lists, and struct defines custom types. outputStruct returns several values.
capabilities.inputs: toVar(), toConst(), property(), array(), struct(), outputStruct()

capabilities.does: Ready-made nodes expose position, normal, tangent and bitangent in geometry, local, world and view space, plus camera and model matrices.
capabilities.inputs: positionLocal, positionWorld, normalView, tangentWorld, cameraProjectionMatrix, modelWorldMatrix, ...

capabilities.does: Screen and viewport nodes give screen UV and coordinate, size, shared viewport texture, depth texture, linear depth and a mip texture of the viewport.
capabilities.inputs: screenUV, screenCoordinate, screenSize, viewportSharedTexture(), viewportDepthTexture(), viewportLinearDepth, viewportMipTexture()

capabilities.does: Helpers include blend modes (burn, dodge, overlay, screen), UV tools (matcap, rotate, spherize, spritesheet, equirect), remap, hash, range, oscillators, time and deltaTime, normal packing, colour adjustments (luminance, saturation, vibrance, hue, posterize), checker and billboarding.
capabilities.inputs: blendOverlay, rotateUV, remap, hash, oscSine, time, saturation, checker, billboarding

capabilities.does: Fog is available as nodes: a fog function and range and density factor nodes.

NodeMaterial replaces parts of the built-in shader with nodes: colorNode, opacityNode, normalNode, positionNode, depthNode, alphaTestNode, aoNode, envNode, vertexNode, fragmentNode, outputNode and more. Each defaults to null.
A slot replaces the default value, while a material helper node (materialColor, materialNormal, materialOpacity, materialAO, materialAlphaTest) lets you modify the existing one.

vertexNode and fragmentNode replace the whole built-in stage. outputNode replaces only the final colour so built-in lighting still runs. geometryNode is a function for geometry edits such as GPU particles.
lightsNode restricts which lights affect one material, using a lights list node.
backdropNode filters whatever is behind an object, for glass-like or filter effects on lit materials. backdropAlphaNode scales its effect.
Shadow behaviour is customisable: castShadowNode (coloured shadows, per-fragment discard), maskShadowNode, receivedShadowNode, and the position nodes used for shadow projection.
mrtNode at material level overrides what is written into multiple render targets. maskNode discards fragments when false.
A node material subclass can override setup steps for position, diffuse colour, normal, depth, AO, environment, lighting model, output, fog and premultiplied alpha.
capabilities.inputs: setupDiffuseColor, setupNormal, setupLightingModel, setupOutput(builder, outputNode), setupFog, ...

capabilities.does: MeshStandardNodeMaterial adds emissiveNode, metalnessNode and roughnessNode on top of the base slots. Helpers materialEmissive, materialMetalness and materialRoughness edit the existing values.

Other node materials: MeshPhysicalNodeMaterial (clearcoat, sheen, iridescence, specular, IOR, transmission, thickness, attenuation, dispersion, anisotropy nodes), MeshPhongNodeMaterial, LineDashedNodeMaterial and SpriteNodeMaterial.

instancedArray and attributeArray create GPU storage buffers (a StorageBufferNode). element(index) reads or writes one entry, toAttribute feeds a material, and access modes include read-only and atomic.
StorageInstancedBufferAttribute is a typed attribute whose data is produced by compute shaders on the GPU. WebGPURenderer only.

IndirectStorageBufferAttribute is a storage buffer for compute shaders that holds indirect draw parameters, so a GPU pass can decide what is drawn without CPU readback. It needs WebGPURenderer with a WebGPU backend.
Compute built-ins: workgroupId, localId, globalId, numWorkgroups, subgroupSize; atomic add, sub, min, max, and, or, xor, store and load; workgroup, storage and texture barriers.
storage and storageTexture nodes give compute shaders read/write access to buffers and textures.

RenderPipeline manages the post-processing chain for WebGPURenderer. An outputNode defines the final image, and render() replaces renderer.render in the loop. A default output transform (tone mapping and colour conversion) is on and can be disabled.
capabilities.inputs: new RenderPipeline(renderer, outputNode); outputNode, outputColorTransform, needsUpdate, render()

capabilities.does: pass(scene, camera) renders a scene once per frame and exposes named output textures, linear depth, view Z and previous-frame textures. It has resolution scale, layers, an override material and clear flags.
capabilities.inputs: pass(scene, camera); getTextureNode(name), getLinearDepthNode(), getViewZNode(), getPreviousTextureNode(), setResolutionScale(), setLayers(), overrideMaterial

capabilities.does: mrt() sets several named outputs for a pass, each with its own blend mode and clear colour, so later effects can read normals, emissive or other buffers.
capabilities.inputs: mrt({output, normal}), setMRT(), getBlendMode/setBlendMode, getClearColor/setClearColor, merge()

capabilities.does: BloomNode extracts bright areas by luminance, blurs them over mip levels and adds them back. Strength 1, radius 0 and threshold 0 are the defaults, with smoothWidth, per-mip tints and a custom high-pass function.
capabilities.inputs: bloom(input, strength, radius, threshold), smoothWidth, bloomTintColors, highPassFn

capabilities.does: Bloom limited to chosen objects by writing the emissive value to an MRT output and bloom-filtering that texture.
DepthOfFieldNode blurs by distance from a focal plane using view-space depth, a focus distance, a focal length and a bokeh scale, each a float node.

SSRNode ray-marches colour, depth and normal buffers. Controls: maxDistance, thickness, quality, resolutionScale, intensity, screenEdgeFade, stochastic GGX mode, an optional HDR environment for misses and history for multi-bounce.
capabilities.inputs: ssr(color, depth, normal, options); maxDistance, thickness, quality, stochastic, setEnvMap(), setHistory()

capabilities.does: GTAONode computes ground-truth ambient occlusion from depth and normals, with radius, thickness, scale, sample count, resolution scale and optional temporal filtering. It can be applied through a built-in AO context on the scene pass.
capabilities.inputs: ao(depth, normal, camera); radius, thickness, scale, samples, resolutionScale, useTemporalFiltering

capabilities.does: SSGINode estimates indirect diffuse light and AO from depth and normals. Controls: sliceCount, stepCount, radius, expFactor, thickness, giIntensity, aoIntensity, backfaceLighting, temporal filtering. Outputs separate GI and AO textures.
capabilities.inputs: ssgi(beauty, depth, normal, camera); getGINode(), getAONode()

capabilities.does: DenoiseNode filters noisy screen data such as raw AO, guided by depth and normals, with luma, depth and normal weighting uniforms.
capabilities.inputs: denoise(texture, depth, normal, camera); radius, lumaPhi, depthPhi, normalPhi

capabilities.does: TRAANode blends the current frame with reprojected history, using depth and velocity and a jittered camera. MSAA must be off. Tunable depth threshold, edge depth difference, subpixel correction and velocity limit.
capabilities.inputs: traa(beauty, depth, velocity, camera); depthThreshold (0.0005), edgeDepthDiff (0.001), maxVelocityLength (128), useSubpixelCorrection

capabilities.does: The TSL notes list node effects: afterImage, anamorphic, bloom, boxBlur, chromaticAberration, denoise, dof, dotScreen, film, fxaa, gaussianBlur, grayscale, hashBlur, lut3D, motionBlur, outline, rgbShift, sepia, smaa, sobel, ssr, ssgi, ao, transition, traa, renderOutput.
renderOutput applies tone mapping and colour conversion explicitly when the default output transform is disabled, for effects that need sRGB input such as FXAA.
overrideNode and overrideNodes swap target nodes during compilation, reached through a material context node.
RectAreaLight on WebGPURenderer needs RectAreaLightTexturesLib initialised and its LTC textures registered, unlike the WebGL path.
LightShadow has biasNode, a node version of bias that overrides it, for WebGPURenderer only.
CSMShadowNode is the cascaded shadow map implementation for WebGPURenderer, counterpart of the CSM class. It wraps a directional light with cascades (3), maxFar, split mode, lightMargin and fade.
capabilities.inputs: new CSMShadowNode(light, {cascades, maxFar, mode, lightMargin}); fade; updateFrustums()

capabilities.does: FXAANode applies FXAA to a texture node. It needs sRGB input, so tone mapping and colour conversion must be done before it.

OutlineNode renders masks of the visible and hidden edges of selected objects, so the final look can be composed with chosen colours. Params: selectedObjects, edgeThickness (1), edgeGlow (0), downSampleRatio (2).
The PostProcessing class was renamed RenderPipeline and is deprecated since r183, kept as a compatibility wrapper that will be removed.
A pass can return the previous frame texture and swap current and previous buffers, which temporal effects such as TRAA and SSGI use.
A pass can render only chosen layers, apply an override material to all objects, and use its own context node, with per-pass viewport and scissor and clear flags.
capabilities.inputs: setLayers(layers), overrideMaterial, contextNode, setViewport(), setScissor(), autoClear*

capabilities.does: DepthOfFieldNode takes the image, view-space depth, focus distance, focal length and bokeh scale as nodes, so each can be a constant or animated value.

BloomNode exposes strength, radius, threshold and smoothWidth as uniform nodes plus per-mip tint vectors and a replaceable high-pass function, for warm or anamorphic looks. Resolution scale is settable.
capabilities.inputs: strength, radius, threshold, smoothWidth, bloomTintColors[], highPassFn, setResolutionScale()

capabilities.does: The SSGI page recommends slice and step counts per quality: low 1x12, medium 2x8, high 3x16 with temporal filtering; without it 2x6, 3x8, 4x12. Total samples per pixel are slices x steps x 2.
SSRNode can trace one mirror ray and blur by roughness, or trace stochastic GGX rays per pixel. Material inputs: roughness, metalness, diffuse, specular nodes.
TRAANode jitters the camera view offset every frame and exposes calls to set and clear that offset.
LightProbeGenerator can build a probe from a cube render target using either a WebGPURenderer or a WebGLRenderer, with an async call that needs an RGBA target.
On WebGPURenderer the planar mirror is ReflectorNode, named on the Reflector addon page as the replacement for the WebGL-only Reflector mesh.
On WebGPURenderer the physical sky is SkyMesh, named on the Sky addon page as the replacement for the WebGL-only Sky.
On WebGPURenderer lens flares use LensflareMesh, named on the Lensflare addon page as the replacement for the WebGL-only Lensflare.
GLTFExporter and USDZExporter take a texture utils module (WebGPUTextureUtils for WebGPURenderer, WebGLTextureUtils for WebGLRenderer) when compressed textures must be exported.
Node materials and TSL are used from JavaScript through dedicated import paths, for example MeshStandardNodeMaterial from three/webgpu and texture, uv, float, sin, time from three/tsl.
capabilities.inputs: import { MeshStandardNodeMaterial } from "three/webgpu"; import { float, sin, time } from "three/tsl"

entries.name: Babylon.js

licence.name: Apache-2.0 (stated in the GitHub README)

engines.name: Engine (WebGL 2) and WebGPUEngine
engines.does: Two renderer back ends. WebGPUEngine needs an awaited initAsync call and is chosen before the scene exists.

engines.name: PBRMaterial and NodeMaterial
engines.does: Physically based material with layered extras, and a graph-built material that compiles to GLSL or WGSL.

engines.name: Rendering pipelines
engines.does: Ready-made post-process chains: DefaultRenderingPipeline, SSR, SSAO, TAA, IBL shadows, lens effects, FSR 1.

engines.name: Frame Graph
engines.does: A task-based description of the frame that reuses textures and is edited in the Node Render Graph Editor.

engines.name: Physics V2 with Havok
engines.does: Rigid bodies, shapes, constraints, ragdolls and a character controller through the Havok plugin.

engines.name: Particle systems and fluid renderer
engines.does: CPU and GPU particle systems, solid particles, point clouds, and a renderer that draws particles as liquid.

engines.name: Babylon Viewer
engines.does: A packaged model viewer as a custom element, with a core Viewer class usable outside the browser.

capabilities.does: PBRMaterial exposes albedoColor, albedoTexture, metallic, roughness, metallicTexture channel switches (green roughness, blue metalness), microSurface, reflectivityColor, ambient occlusion with ambientTextureStrength, bumpTexture and reflectionTexture.
capabilities.inputs: albedoColor, metallic, roughness, microSurface, ambientTexture, bumpTexture, reflectionTexture

capabilities.does: PBRSpecularGlossinessMaterial takes diffuseColor, specularColor and glossiness, with a specularGlossinessTexture that stores specular in RGB and glossiness in alpha. PBRMetallicRoughnessMaterial is the simpler variant with baseColor, metallic, roughness and metallicRoughnessTexture.

The clearCoat group adds a lacquer layer: isEnabled, intensity, roughness, indexOfRefraction, an optional tint (isTintEnabled, tintColor, tintColorAtDistance, tintThickness) and textures for amount, bump and tint.
capabilities.inputs: clearCoat.isEnabled, intensity, roughness, indexOfRefraction, tintColor, texture, bumpTexture

capabilities.does: The sheen group adds fabric-like edge light: isEnabled, intensity, color and texture.
The anisotropy group stretches highlights along a direction: isEnabled, intensity, direction and texture.
The iridescence group simulates a thin film: isEnabled, intensity, indexOfRefraction, minimumThickness, maximumThickness, texture and thicknessTexture.
The subSurface group drives refraction: isRefractionEnabled, refractionIntensity, indexOfRefraction, tintColor and tintColorAtDistance, with a thicknessTexture and minimumThickness/maximumThickness.
subSurface also covers translucency (isTranslucencyEnabled, translucencyIntensity) and scattering (isScatteringEnabled with a scatteringDiffusionProfile).

A baked lightmap is applied with lightmapTexture; useLightmapAsShadowmap treats it as shadow data only. Other flags: useRadianceOverAlpha and useSpecularOverAlpha keep reflections on transparent surfaces.
capabilities.outputs: baked lighting on a PBR surface

capabilities.does: NodeMaterial builds a material from connected blocks (InputBlock, TransformBlock, Lerp, Discard, Loop with StorageRead and StorageWrite). It generates GLSL by default or WGSL, loads from files or snippet ids, and is edited in the Node Material Editor.

NodeGeometry builds meshes from a block graph inspired by Blender geometry nodes: primitive sources, set-position/normal/colour/UV blocks, InstantiateOnVertices and OnFaces, Noise, Random, Merge. build then createMesh produces the mesh; an editor exists.

ShadowGenerator renders a shadow map for one light (size, light). Casters sit in renderList; receiveShadows is a mesh flag. Options: bias (0.00005), forceBackFacesOnly, frustumEdgeFalloff, transparencyShadow, enableSoftTransparentShadow, refreshRate to freeze static shadows.

Filtering modes: usePoissonSampling, useExponentialShadowMap (default), useBlurExponentialShadowMap (blurScale, blurBoxOffset, useKernelBlur, blurKernel), close-exponential variants, usePercentageCloserFiltering (WebGL 2) and useContactHardeningShadow with contactHardeningLightSizeUVRatio; filteringQuality trades speed for quality.

CascadedShadowGenerator for directional lights: numCascades (2 to 4, default 4), lambda (0.5 linear-to-log mix), cascadeBlendPercentage (0.1), stabilizeCascades, shadowMaxZ, depthClamp, autoCalcDepthBounds, penumbraDarkness, debug colouring, freezeShadowCastersBoundingInfo.

IblShadowsRenderPipeline casts shadows from an HDR environment using a voxel grid of registered casters, importance-sampled directions and screen-space detail. Properties: shadowOpacity, sampleDirections, shadowRemanence, resolutionExp, ssShadowsEnabled and more. Suited to static casters.

Global illumination from reflective shadow maps (directional and spot lights only): classes ReflectiveShadowMap, GIRSM and GIRSMManager; tuning through radius, intensity, numSamples, noiseFactor, blur thresholds. No occlusion, so light can leak; suited to small scenes.

ClusteredLightContainer groups many point and spot lights into a screen grid (horizontalTiles, verticalTiles 64 each; depthSlices 16; maxRange). It needs WebGPU or WebGL 2 float targets and does not support shadow-casting lights.
capabilities.inputs: lights array, horizontalTiles, verticalTiles, depthSlices, maxRange
capabilities.outputs: cheap shading with hundreds of lights

capabilities.does: DefaultRenderingPipeline(name, hdr, scene, cameras) bundles MSAA (samples), FXAA, sharpen, bloom, depth of field, chromatic aberration, grain, glow layer and image processing, each behind an Enabled flag.
In the default pipeline: bloomEnabled, bloomThreshold (0.9), bloomWeight (0.15), bloomKernel (64), bloomScale (0.5).
In the default pipeline: depthOfFieldEnabled, depthOfFieldBlurLevel, and depthOfField.focusDistance (mm, default 2000), focalLength (50), fStop (1.4), lensSize (50).

LensRenderingPipeline: chromatic_aberration, edge_blur, distortion, grain_amount, grain_texture, and depth of field through dof_focus_distance, dof_aperture (1), dof_darken, dof_pentagon (true, pentagon bokeh), dof_gain, dof_threshold and blur_noise. Zero disables most effects; 1 is the realistic setting.

imageProcessing offers exposure, contrast, a colour grading LUT (.3dl or .png via colorGradingTexture), and ColorCurves with global, highlights, midtones and shadows density/exposure/hue/saturation. The page also lists tone mapping and vignette.
grainEnabled with grain.intensity (30) and grain.animated (false) animating the grain every frame.

chromaticAberrationEnabled with aberrationAmount (30, channel separation), radialIntensity, direction.x and direction.y (both 0 points toward screen centre), alphaMode, enablePixelPerfectMode and forceFullscreenViewport (true).
sharpenEnabled with sharpen.edgeAmount (0.3) and sharpen.colorAmount (1; 0 gives edge detection output).
In the default pipeline, samples sets hardware MSAA (1 means off, WebGL 2 only) and fxaaEnabled adds FXAA, with fxaa.samples and fxaa.adaptScaleToCurrentViewport.

TAARenderingPipeline accumulates samples over frames. Properties: samples, factor (history blend), disableOnCameraMove (default true), reprojectHistory (needs a velocity buffer and MRT), clampHistory (keeps colour in the 3x3 neighbourhood range).

SSRRenderingPipeline: strength (1), reflectivityThreshold (0.04), thickness (0.5), maxDistance and maxSteps (1000), step, roughnessFactor (0.2), blurDispersionStrength (0.03), attenuation switches, environmentTexture fallback, enableAutomaticThicknessComputation, useFresnel.
capabilities.inputs: strength, thickness, maxSteps, roughnessFactor, blurDispersionStrength, environmentTexture

capabilities.does: SSAORenderingPipeline takes a name, scene and ratios (ssaoRatio, combineRatio) and uses the depth map renderer. The page advises ratios below 1 for speed and notes the SSAOCombineRenderEffect can be disabled to inspect raw output.
MotionBlurPostProcess: motionStrength (1), motionBlurSamples (32), isObjectBased (true uses per-object velocity; false uses camera movement only).

VolumetricLightScatteringPostProcess(name, ratio, camera, lightSourceMesh, samplesNum 100, samplingMode, engine, reusable, scene). Properties: invert, useCustomMeshPosition with setCustomMeshPosition, mesh, useDiffuseColor.

GlowLayer renders emissive meshes into a blurred buffer. Options: mainTextureRatio, mainTextureFixedSize, blurKernelSize (32), mainTextureSamples; intensity; customEmissiveColorSelector and customEmissiveTextureSelector; addIncludedOnlyMesh and addExcludedMesh.

WebGPUEngine from the core package, started with await initAsync. Options: swapChainFormat (rgba16float), canvasToneMapping standard or extended, canvasColorSpace srgb or display-p3, xrCompatible. Core shaders are native WGSL; the engine is picked before scene creation.
capabilities.outputs: WebGPU rendering with HDR output options

capabilities.does: Frame Graph describes the frame as composable rendering tasks and reuses textures to save memory. The Node Render Graph Editor builds a frame layout visually; Node Render Graph Blocks are documented on a separate page.
capabilities.inputs: task graph; Node Render Graph Editor

capabilities.does: Flow Graph connects event and action blocks to script scene behaviour without code. glTF files with the KHR_interactivity extension load into Flow Graphs. A Flow Graph Editor exists for creating, testing and debugging.

GaussianSplattingMesh loads .ply (including compressed), .splat, .spz (SH up to order 4), .SOG, glTF with KHR_gaussian_splatting, and streamed SOG bundles. Splats sort in a worker (optional GPU sort on WebGPU); compound meshes hold parts; splat data is editable via updateData.

Physics V2 with the Havok plugin: scene.enablePhysics(gravity, plugin) makes the engine; PhysicsAggregate(mesh, PhysicsShapeType, {mass, restitution}) creates a body quickly; PhysicsBody sits on mesh.physicsBody; PhysicsViewer.showBody() draws it for debugging.
Physics V2 pages cover aggregates, rigid-body core concepts, shapes, forces, compounds, collision events, raycast, shape cast, prestep and performance tips, plus migration from Physics V1.
The physics section has pages for constraints, ragdolls built with the V2 API, collision events, a physics character controller, prestep hooks and Physics V1 migration.

ParticleSystem (CPU) and GPUParticleSystem (WebGL 2, falls back to CPU) with subtopics: shape emitters, property changes over time, animating particles, color ramps and billboard mode, attractors, flow maps, sub emitters, particle helper, snippet server, JSON loading and a Node Particle Editor.
Beyond ParticleSystem the particles section covers a Solid Particle System, a Point Cloud System and a Fluid Renderer.
The scene fluid renderer (since 5.36.0) draws particles from ParticleSystem, GPUParticleSystem or custom vertex buffers as a liquid surface.

mesh.simplify(settings, parallelProcessing, type, callback) builds LOD levels asynchronously with quadric error decimation. Each setting has quality (0 to 1), distance and optimizeMesh. QuadraticErrorSimplification exposes decimationIterations (100) and aggressiveness (7).

Loader plugins: .babylon built in; glTF, OpenUSD (.usd, .usda, .usdc, .usdz), STL, OBJ, splat via plugins. Also an asset manager, asset containers, incremental loading, loading from memory and a loader-writing guide.
capabilities.outputs: meshes, materials and animations in a scene

capabilities.does: A glTF 2.0 exporter plus 3ds Max, Maya and Blender exporter plugins, a scene serializer for .babylon, and a 3MF exporter page.

Babylon GUI draws 2D controls onto a texture layer or onto meshes, with 3D GUI for VR, scroll viewer, XML loader, nine-patch stretching, sprite sheets and a GUI Editor. Rendered by the 3D engine, not the DOM.

Cameras named: Universal, Arc Rotate, Follow (free and arc), Anaglyph, Device Orientation, Virtual Joysticks, Geospatial and VR cameras. Pages cover collisions, custom inputs, multi-view and layer masks.
Animation pages: designing, sequencing, grouping and combining animations, character animation, render-loop animation, baked texture animation, retargeting and root motion.

The Viewer package gives an HTML3DElement (babylon-viewer), CreateViewerForCanvas for frameworks and a core Viewer class. It picks WebGL or WebGPU, suspends rendering when idle, and lowers resolution to hold frame rate.
The README lists a Playground for trying the API, a Sandbox for dropping in .babylon and glTF files, and a shader creation tool (CYOS) for GLSL.

scripting: Node Material, Node Geometry, Node Particle and Flow Graph editors

rea.notes: Apache-2.0 per README. SSAO2 and SSR post-process pages were not found at the guessed URLs; SSAORenderingPipeline and SSRRenderingPipeline pages were read instead.
