entries.name: PlayCanvas (engine and Editor)

licence.name: Engine: MIT (GitHub README). Editor: hosted browser service (plans and terms not read).

engines.name: PlayCanvas Engine
engines.does: Open-source runtime for 2D and 3D on WebGL 2 and WebGPU, installed as the playcanvas npm package.

engines.name: PlayCanvas Editor
engines.does: Browser editor with scene hierarchy, inspector, asset pipeline, real-time collaboration, version control and publishing.

engines.name: Graphics back ends
engines.does: WebGPU (listed as Beta), WebGL 2.0, and a Null back end for headless use such as Node.

engines.name: Ammo.js physics
engines.does: A WebAssembly build of the Bullet engine used through rigid-body and collision components.

engines.name: SuperSplat and SplatTransform
engines.does: Companion tools for editing and converting Gaussian splat files.

capabilities.does: Three back ends: WebGPU (Beta), WebGL 2.0 and Null for headless runs. The engine falls back from WebGPU to WebGL by browser support. Rendering features include render passes, multiple render targets, depth pre-pass, TAA, instancing and batching.
capabilities.outputs: same scene on WebGPU or WebGL

capabilities.does: The physical material uses diffuse, metalness (0 to 1) and gloss (0 to 100, the inverse of roughness), each with a map slot. A specular workflow is the alternative. Additional slots named: AO, emissive, opacity, normal map, height map.
The graphics overview lists metallic/roughness and specular/glossiness workflows plus clearcoat, anisotropy, sheen and transmission materials.
Directional, point and spot lights with shadows and cookies, area lights and image-based lighting, as listed in the graphics overview.

light.shadowType chooses PCF 1x1, 3x3 (default) or 5x5, VSM (vsmBlurSize, vsmBlurMode, vsmBias) or PCSS (penumbraSize, penumbraFalloff, shadowSamples, shadowBlockerSamples). Also shadowResolution (16 to 4096), shadowDistance, shadowBias, normalOffsetBias, shadowIntensity.

Directional lights split the camera frustum with numCascades (1 to 4, default 1) and cascadeDistribution (0 linear to 1 logarithmic). Each added cascade can raise the cost because casters may draw into several maps.

Clustered lighting settings: Cells, Max Lights Per Cell, atlas resolutions for shadows and cookies, Shadows Type (PCF1/3/5), Area Lights Enabled, Cookies Enabled. Default cap is 255 visible lights; maxLights in LightingParams raises it. Directional lights stay outside the clusters.
capabilities.outputs: many lights with shadows and cookies

capabilities.does: Runtime lightmap baking: mark lights with Bake Lightmap (optionally Bake Direction), mark models Lightmapped, then set Size Multiplier, Max Resolution, Mode, Ambient Bake with samples, and bilateral Filtering. Needs a UV1 set; global illumination is not supported.
capabilities.inputs: Bake Lightmap, Size Multiplier, Max Resolution, Mode, Ambient Bake, Filtering

capabilities.does: CameraFrame is the modern chain: HDR bloom, SSAO, depth of field, TAA, colour grading with LUT, vignette, fringing, tone mapping and sharpness. Legacy script effects include Bloom, Brightness-Contrast, Hue-Saturation, FXAA, Sepia and Vignette.

cameraFrame.colorEnhance has enabled, shadows and highlights (-3 to 3), midtones, vibrance and dehaze (-1 to 1). cameraFrame.vignette has intensity, color, inner, outer and curvature. cameraFrame.debug shows scene, ssao, bloom, vignette, dofcoc, dofblur or depth.

ShaderMaterial takes vertexGLSL/fragmentGLSL or vertexWGSL/fragmentWGSL plus attributes. The preprocessor supports #define, #if, #include. Chunks such as transformCoreVS, gammaPS, tonemappingPS, fogPS, shadowCasterPS and pickPS give skinning, tone mapping and shadow output. Pass defines include FORWARD_PASS and SHADOW_PASS.
WebGPU compute shaders are listed among the custom shader features in the graphics overview.

Pages exist for rendering without entities, batching, hardware instancing, multi-draw, render targets, multiple render targets, dual-source blending, indirect drawing, transform feedback, HTML-in-canvas and device loss recovery.

The particle system component supports depthSoftening (soft particles, needs a depth map on the camera), autoplay, and reset() and play() calls from script. Further settings are in the Editor component reference.

Splats load from .ply or .sog files or stream as Streamed SOG. All splats across components share one global depth sort, using one work buffer per camera and layer. GSplatContainer builds splats in code.
capabilities.outputs: splat scene in a PlayCanvas app

capabilities.does: Formats compared: PLY (lossless, large, slow), SOG (about 15 to 20 times smaller, lossy), Streamed SOG (on-demand chunks for very large scenes), GLB (lossless, interoperable), SPZ (about 10 times smaller, parser script shipped).
Ammo.js (Bullet) physics: static, dynamic and kinematic rigid bodies with sleeping, primitive, mesh and compound collision shapes, forces, impulses, torque and velocity control.

Joints cover hinges, sliders, ball joints, springs and breakable welds. Trigger volumes detect entry and exit; ray casting queries the scene; collision events respond to contacts; ammo.js can be called directly for unexposed Bullet features.

State graphs hold states, transitions and parameters, built in the Editor or code. Blend trees mix clips by one or two parameters. Layers play several graphs at once, masks limit a layer to chosen nodes, and events fire at clip times.

Scripts are ESM .mjs classes extending Script (recommended for new projects) or classic .js using pc.createScript; both can coexist. A static scriptName names the script, an attribute annotation exposes a field, and update(dt) runs per frame.
The Editor includes a code editor with syntax highlighting, autocomplete and error checking, a VS Code extension and hot reloading of scripts.

Several users edit the same scene at once, see each other’s selection and viewport focus, and chat. Version control gives checkpoints, branches, visual merging and change history for assets and entities.
Publishing targets: web (PlayCanvas hosting or self-hosting), mobile, desktop and playable ads. An Editor API supports custom tools and automation, and an MCP server page exists.
Assets stream asynchronously. The engine README lists glTF 2.0, Draco and Basis compression as supported.

MiniStats shows frame time, CPU and GPU cost and GPU memory; AppStats exposes counters for dashboards; a profiler inspects Editor launch; GPU Profiling uses native capture tools; the Inspector shows video memory, frame passes and per-mesh usage.

The engine README lists WebXR for AR and VR, mouse, keyboard, touch and gamepad input, and 3D positional sound through the Web Audio API. Related packages: @playcanvas/react and @playcanvas/web-components.

rea.notes: Engine source is public under MIT (README). Editor is a hosted service; its terms and pricing were not read.

entries.name: react-three-fiber (@react-three/fiber)

licence.name: MIT (listed on the GitHub page)

engines.name: React reconciler for three.js
engines.does: Turns JSX elements into three.js objects and keeps the scene graph in step with React state.

engines.name: Canvas and render loop
engines.does: Canvas creates renderer, camera, scene and raycaster; useFrame subscribes to the loop.

engines.name: Event system
engines.does: Raycasts pointer events against the scene and delivers them to objects through React props.

engines.name: Native entry
engines.does: The package has a React Native entry, @react-three/fiber/native.

capabilities.does: Lowercase JSX tags become three.js classes, so mesh becomes THREE.Mesh. Props set object fields; setter-style props accept arrays (position={[1,2,3]}), scale={1} calls setScalar, and dashes reach nested fields (rotation-x, shadow-camera-far).

args passes constructor arguments as an array and rebuilds the object when they change. attach binds a child to a parent property (geometry, material by default, nested paths with dashes, indexed paths like material-0 for multi-materials, or a function).

primitive inserts an existing object (not disposed on unmount). extend registers third-party classes such as OrbitControls as JSX tags. On unmount R3F calls dispose when present; dispose={null} opts out.

Canvas props: gl, camera (default fov 75, near 0.1, far 1000, position [0,0,5]), scene, raycaster, frameloop (always, demand or never), orthographic, dpr (default [1,2]), resize, fallback, onCreated, onPointerMissed. shadows true selects PCFsoft; other values basic, percentage, soft, variance.
capabilities.inputs: gl, camera, shadows, frameloop, dpr, orthographic, resize

capabilities.does: Canvas legacy turns on THREE.ColorManagement; linear disables automatic sRGB and gamma; flat swaps the default ACES filmic tone mapping for no tone mapping.
With frameloop="demand" a frame renders when props change. Calling invalidate() requests a frame, for example after camera controls move objects outside React.

useFrame(callback(state, delta, xrFrame), renderPriority) runs every frame. A positive renderPriority takes over rendering, so the callback must render. Negative values only order callbacks, lowest first. The page warns against setState in the callback.

useThree(selector?) returns state: gl, scene, camera, raycaster, pointer, clock, xr, size, viewport, performance, frameloop, plus setters and methods set, get, invalidate, advance, setSize, setDpr, setFrameloop, setEvents.

useLoader(loader, url|urls, extensions, onProgress) suspends the component, caches by URL and loads arrays in parallel; useLoader.preload loads ahead. Results with a scene also give nodes and materials; useGraph(object3D) builds that name-keyed map from any object.

Handlers: onClick, onContextMenu, onDoubleClick, onWheel, onPointerDown/Up/Move/Over/Out/Enter/Leave, and onPointerMissed on Canvas. The event carries point, distance, object, eventObject, intersections, ray, camera, delta and stopPropagation().

e.target.setPointerCapture(e.pointerId) and releasePointerCapture route events to one object during a drag. Capture adds the object to the hit test rather than replacing it, and only one pointer is supported.

Canvas events prop customises the manager (enabled, priority, filter, compute). eventSource picks the DOM element that receives events; eventPrefix switches the pointer coordinate prefix from offset to another such as client. state.events.update() forces a raycast.

The docs list sharing geometries and materials, instancedMesh, Detailed LOD and PerformanceMonitor from drei, performance.regress() to lower quality while moving, nested Suspense for progressive loading, and React transitions to defer work.
The introduction states that v10 is in alpha and adds WebGPU support and a new frame-loop scheduler. Versions 8 and 9 pair with React 18 and 19.
Importing from @react-three/fiber/native runs the same components in React Native. The README notes Metro may need asset extensions (glb, png, jpg) configured for loaders.

Listed companions: drei, gltfjsx, postprocessing, uikit, test-renderer, offscreen, flex, xr, csg, rapier, cannon, p2, a11y, gpu-pathtracer, plus leva, zustand, jotai, valtio, react-spring and use-gesture.
capabilities.outputs: physics, XR, UI and effects add-ons

outcomes: interactive product viewers and web experiences

rea.notes: MIT per GitHub page. No WebGPU mention in the README; the docs introduction mentions it for v10 alpha.

entries.verified: 2026-11-02, how: docs pages and README read

entries.name: @react-three/drei

licence.name: MIT (LICENSE file read)

engines.name: Staging helpers
engines.does: Environment, Stage, shadows, sky, clouds, camera shake and float for setting up a scene quickly.

engines.name: Shader materials
engines.does: Transmission, reflector, refraction, wobble, distort and portal materials built on three.js.

engines.name: Performance helpers
engines.does: Instances, Merged, Points, Segments, Detailed (LOD), Bvh, adaptive DPR and a performance monitor.

engines.name: Controls, gizmos and loaders
engines.does: Camera and pointer controls, transform gizmos, and hooks that load glTF, FBX, KTX2 and textures.

capabilities.does: Environment sets scene.environment and optionally the background. Props: files (one file or six), path, preset, map, scene, background (true, false, "only"), backgroundBlurriness, backgroundIntensity, backgroundRotation, environmentIntensity, environmentRotation, plus near, far, resolution and frames when children render the environment.

The loader depends on file type: .hdr RGBELoader, .exr EXRLoader, gain-map .jpg and .webp loaders, or CubeTextureLoader for an array. Ten presets map to HDRI files: apartment, city, dawn, forest, lobby, night, park, studio, sunset, warehouse. The page says presets are not for production.
Environment ground option (true or an object) projects the map onto a floor: height 15, radius 60, scale 1000 are the documented values.

Stage wraps a model with lights, shadow and camera fit. preset: rembrandt (default), portrait, upfront, soft, or custom main/fill positions. shadows (default contact) accepts contact or accumulative with offset, bias, normalBias, size. Also adjustCamera, environment (default city), intensity (0.5), center.

ContactShadows draws a fake soft shadow on a ground plane. Props seen: scale (number or [x,y]), opacity, blur, far, resolution, color, frames. frames={1} renders once for static objects. The shadow faces up by default.
capabilities.inputs: scale, opacity, blur, far, resolution, color, frames

capabilities.does: AccumulativeShadows builds soft shadows over frames from RandomizedLight children. temporal (false), frames (40), limit (Infinity), blend (100), opacity (1), alphaTest (0.65), color, colorBlend (2), resolution (1024). RandomizedLight takes amount and position.
capabilities.inputs: temporal, frames, blend, alphaTest, colorBlend, resolution

capabilities.does: MeshTransmissionMaterial props: transmission (1), thickness (0), roughness (0), chromaticAberration (0.03), anisotropicBlur (0.1), distortion (0), distortionScale (0.5), temporalDistortion (0), samples (6), resolution, backside, backsideThickness, backsideResolution, transmissionSampler, buffer, background.
capabilities.inputs: transmission, thickness, roughness, chromaticAberration, samples, backside

capabilities.does: MeshReflectorMaterial extends MeshStandardMaterial with ground reflections. Props: blur [w,h], mixBlur (1), mixStrength, mixContrast, resolution, mirror, depthScale, minDepthThreshold, maxDepthThreshold, depthToBlurRatioBias (0.25), distortion with distortionMap, reflectorOffset.
capabilities.inputs: blur, mixBlur, mixStrength, resolution, mirror, depthScale, distortionMap

capabilities.does: MeshRefractionMaterial traces refraction through a gem-like shape: envMap, bounces (2), ior (2.4), fresnel (0), aberrationStrength (0), color, fastChroma (true, fewer ray casts for the RGB shift).
capabilities.inputs: envMap, bounces, ior, fresnel, aberrationStrength, fastChroma

capabilities.does: Caustics projects light patterns from contents. Props: frames (1), debug, causticsOnly, backside, ior (1.1), backsideIOR, worldRadius (0.3125), intensity (0.05), color, resolution (2048), lightSource ([5,5,5] or an object ref).

Instances wraps THREE.InstancedMesh declaratively, with limit and range; each Instance takes position, rotation, scale, color and pointer handlers. createInstances supports several sets; InstancedAttribute adds a per-instance shader attribute (name, defaultValue).
capabilities.outputs: many objects in one draw call

capabilities.does: Bvh wraps a subtree with three-mesh-bvh raycasting and restores the normal raycast when disabled. Props: enabled (true), firstHitOnly (false), splitStrategy (SAH, CENTER or AVERAGE), verbose, setBoundingBox (true), maxDepth (40), maxLeafTris (10).

README lists Merged, Points, Segments, Detailed (level of detail), Preload, BakeShadows, meshBounds, AdaptiveDpr, AdaptiveEvents and PerformanceMonitor for lowering cost while moving or when frame rate drops.
CameraShake props shown: maxYaw, maxPitch, maxRoll, yawFrequency, pitchFrequency, rollFrequency, intensity, decay, decayRate, controls. A ref gives getIntensity and setIntensity.
capabilities.inputs: maxYaw, maxPitch, maxRoll, frequencies, intensity, decayRate

capabilities.does: Float bobs and tilts its children: speed (1), rotationIntensity (1), floatIntensity (1), floatingRange ([-0.1, 0.1]), autoInvalidate for demand frameloops.
Sparkles scatters drifting points: count (100), speed (1), opacity (1), size (random 0 to 1), scale (1), noise (1) and color. Several accept per-particle Float32Array values.
capabilities.inputs: count, speed, opacity, color, size, scale, noise

capabilities.does: Html places DOM content at a 3D position. Props: as, center, fullscreen, distanceFactor, transform (matrix3d), sprite, occlude (true, refs, or "blending"), onOcclude, zIndexRange, prepend, portal, calculatePosition, and custom material, geometry, castShadow, receiveShadow for blending occlusion.
capabilities.outputs: labels and UI tied to 3D points

capabilities.does: Text renders high-quality antialiased signed-distance-field text with troika; all troika props are accepted. It suspends while font data loads. characters pre-builds glyphs to avoid a flash of unstyled text.
Bounds frames its content. Props: fit, clip, observe, margin, maxDuration, interpolateFunc. useBounds gives refresh, clip, fit, reset, moveTo and lookAt({target, up}).

View draws several scenes in one canvas into scissor regions tied to DOM elements. Props: as, visible, index (1), frames, track (deprecated). View.Port inside Canvas renders them; the Canvas eventSource must be a parent of both.
Control components in the README: CameraControls, ScrollControls, PresentationControls, KeyboardControls, FaceControls, MotionPathControls. Cameras: PerspectiveCamera, OrthographicCamera, CubeCamera.
Gizmos: GizmoHelper, PivotControls, DragControls, TransformControls, Grid, and a Helper / useHelper wrapper for three.js helpers.

Shape components include Plane, Box, Sphere, Circle, Cone, Cylinder, Tube, Torus, TorusKnot, Ring, the Platonic solids, Extrude, Lathe, Shape, RoundedBox, ScreenQuad, Line, QuadraticBezierLine, CubicBezierLine, CatmullRomLine and Facemesh.
Shader components: MeshWobbleMaterial, MeshDistortMaterial, MeshDiscardMaterial, PointMaterial, MeshPortalMaterial, SoftShadows and a shaderMaterial helper for authoring custom materials.
Abstractions: Image, Text, Text3D, Billboard, ScreenSpace, GradientTexture, Edges, Outlines, Trail, Sampler, Clone, useAnimations, MarchingCubes, Decal, Svg, AsciiRenderer, Splat, PositionalAudio.
More staging parts: Center, Resize, BBAnchor, Backdrop, Shadow, Sky, Stars, Cloud, Lightformer, SpotLight, SpotLightShadow, ShadowAlpha, useEnvironment, MatcapTexture and NormalTexture helpers.

Loading helpers: Gltf / useGLTF, Fbx / useFBX, Texture / useTexture, Ktx2 / useKTX2, CubeTexture, VideoTexture, TrailTexture, useFont, useSpriteLoader, plus Loader and useProgress for a loading indicator.
Portals: Hud, View, RenderTexture, RenderCubeTexture, Fisheye, Mask and MeshPortalMaterial for drawing one scene inside another, as an overlay or into a texture.
Hooks: useFBO, useCubeCamera, useDepthBuffer, useBoxProjectedEnv, useSurfaceSampler, useIntersect, useAspect, useCursor, useDetectGPU and the FaceLandmarker helper.

outcomes: product viewers and staged 3D scenes in React

rea.notes: MIT LICENSE file read; the docs folder is public on GitHub. Docs site (drei.docs.pmnd.rs) rendered no text for the fetcher, so raw .mdx files were read.

entries.name: postprocessing (pmndrs)

licence.name: Zlib (README states Zlib; original code from three.js examples is MIT)

engines.name: EffectComposer
engines.does: Stands in for the plain WebGLRenderer, owns the frame buffers and runs the list of passes in order.

engines.name: EffectPass
engines.does: Takes a list of effects and merges them into as few fullscreen shader passes as it can.

engines.name: Effect and Pass classes
engines.does: Base classes for writing new effects and passes; about 34 ready-made effects and 21 passes ship in the package.

capabilities.does: EffectComposer replaces the renderer for the final image. Passes are added with addPass and removed with removePass; render runs enabled passes in the order added. Options: depthBuffer, stencilBuffer, multisampling, frameBufferType. reset drops all passes and buffers.
capabilities.inputs: renderer, options {depthBuffer, stencilBuffer, multisampling, frameBufferType}; passes
capabilities.outputs: final frame drawn to screen or target

capabilities.does: EffectPass accepts any combination of effects and organises them so the shader work is merged into fewer render operations. Each effect keeps its own BlendFunction.

RenderPass draws the scene with a camera as the first step of the chain. The composer buffer can use HalfFloatType or UnsignedByteType; the renderer tone mapping is left off and ToneMappingEffect is added at the end.
capabilities.outputs: scene colour in the composer buffer

capabilities.does: BloomEffect blurs bright areas and adds them back. Options: luminanceThreshold (1.0), luminanceSmoothing (0.03), intensity (1.0), mipmapBlur (true), radius (0.85), levels (8), blendFunction (SCREEN).
capabilities.inputs: luminanceThreshold, luminanceSmoothing, intensity, mipmapBlur, radius, levels

capabilities.does: SelectiveBloomEffect limits bloom to objects held in a Selection set. Flags: ignoreBackground and inverted (use the selection as an exclusion list). Needs the main scene and camera.

DepthOfFieldEffect blurs by circle of confusion. Options: focusDistance (3.0), focusRange (2.0), bokehScale (1.0), resolutionScale (0.5). A target Vector3 gives auto focus; calculateFocusDistance returns the distance to a point.

SSAOEffect darkens creases using depth and normals. Options: samples (9), rings (7), radius (0.1825), intensity (1.0), bias (0.025), fade (0.01), luminanceInfluence (0.7), color, minRadiusScale, world distance and proximity thresholds with falloff, depthAwareUpsampling.
capabilities.outputs: screen-space occlusion term, multiplied into the image

capabilities.does: SMAAEffect applies morphological anti-aliasing. Options: preset (SMAAPreset, default MEDIUM), edgeDetectionMode (default COLOR), predicationMode (default DISABLED). Internals exposed: edgeDetectionMaterial, edgesTexture, weightsMaterial, weightsTexture.
The class index also lists FXAAEffect as a cheaper screen-space anti-aliasing option. The README names Antialiasing as an included effect.

ToneMappingEffect maps HDR to display range. The mode option defaults to AGX; ToneMappingMode also has an adaptive Reinhard variant. Other options: resolution (256, power of two), middleGrey (0.6), whitePoint (4.0), averageLuminance (1.0), minLuminance (0.01), adaptationRate (1.0).
capabilities.inputs: mode, resolution, middleGrey, whitePoint, averageLuminance, minLuminance, adaptationRate

capabilities.does: OutlineEffect draws edges around a Selection of objects. Options: edgeStrength (1.0), pulseSpeed (0 off), visibleEdgeColor, hiddenEdgeColor, xRay (true), blur, patternTexture, patternScale, multisampling, resolutionScale (0.5).

The effect set includes ColorAverage, Sepia, BrightnessContrast, HueSaturation and LUT effects (LUT1DEffect and LUT3DEffect). Loaders read LUT files (LUT3dlLoader, LUTCubeLoader); LookupTexture and TetrahedralUpscaler are listed as LUT texture classes.
capabilities.inputs: LUT file or texture; per-effect parameters

capabilities.does: GodRaysEffect is the light-shaft effect of the package. The README lists it among the included effects.
ChromaticAberrationEffect is the colour-fringing effect; the README groups it with Glitch and Noise.
VignetteEffect darkens the frame edges; the VignetteTechnique enum selects the falloff style.
LensDistortionEffect warps the image optically. TiltShiftEffect with TiltShiftBlurPass blurs outside a focus band.
Stylising effects in the class index: DotScreen, Grid, Scanline, Pixelation, ASCII (with ASCIITexture), Glitch (GlitchMode enum) and Noise.
ShockWaveEffect is a ripple distortion effect. The README lists Depth Picking under it, and DepthPickingPass is the pass that reads depth at a point.
Each effect has its own BlendFunction, an enum of blend modes, so effects can be combined in different ways when merged into one pass.
Blur utilities as passes: GaussianBlurPass, KawaseBlurPass, BoxBlurPass and MipmapBlurPass, with KernelSize presets and matching blur materials.
Utility passes write scene buffers for other effects: DepthPass, NormalPass, DepthDownsamplingPass and DepthCopyPass. MaskPass and ClearMaskPass are listed alongside.
Custom work goes through the Effect base class (EffectAttribute and EffectShaderSection enums exist), ShaderPass and LambdaPass.
LuminancePass and AdaptiveLuminancePass measure scene brightness, with LuminanceMaterial and AdaptiveLuminanceMaterial as the matching materials.

The separate @react-three/postprocessing package wraps the library for react-three-fiber: an EffectComposer component containing effects as JSX (the README example uses DepthOfField, Bloom, Noise and Vignette). WebGL 2 MSAA is its default; MIT licence listed.

outcomes: bloom, depth of field, SSAO, outlines, grading and anti-aliasing on three.js frames

rea.notes: Zlib licence per README; class docs list deprecated members next to current ones. React wrapper @react-three/postprocessing is a separate package.

entries.name: three-gpu-pathtracer

licence.name: MIT (LICENSE file read)

engines.name: WebGPUPathTracer
engines.does: Accumulates path-traced samples of a three.js scene on a WebGPURenderer, one batch per renderSample call.

engines.name: OIDNDenoiser
engines.does: Optional neural denoiser (oidn-webgpu weights) that can use albedo and normal buffers as guides.

engines.name: FSRUpscaler
engines.does: Optional upscaler (from @pmndrs/upscaler) that lets the tracer run at a lower render scale.

engines.name: BVH build (three-mesh-bvh)
engines.does: Mesh BVHs are built for the scene, in workers when setSceneAsync is used.

capabilities.does: WebGPUPathTracer renders a three.js scene by progressive path tracing on the GPU. setScene captures the scene and builds acceleration structures; renderSample accumulates one batch of samples per frame and presents it.

Bounce limits are separate counters: maxBounces (15) for scatters, maxTransparentBounces (15) for alpha-tested surfaces passed through, maxSubsurfaceBounces (256) for scatter events inside subsurface volumes.

Sample count per pixel is capped by maxSamples (0 means no end) and gated by minSamples. pause freezes accumulation, reset restarts it, and a complete event fires when all pixels are done and any denoiser has finished.

Three random-number generators are offered: RANDOM_PCG (plain random), RANDOM_SOBOL (scrambled per-pixel Sobol, the default) and RANDOM_BLUE_DITHER (shared Sobol with blue-noise offset). setRandom swaps the generator and recompiles. stableNoise (true) restarts the sequence on reset.
multipleImportanceSampling (default true) combines light sampling and BSDF sampling. Switching it off makes lights noisier. setMultipleImportanceSampling sets the flag.
The README gotchas say point, spot and directional lights work only with MIS, and emissive materials are supported but do not use MIS.

Noise controls: clampDirect (0, off) and clampIndirect (10) cap the light a path segment adds, and filterGlossyFactor (1) blurs sharp reflections seen through rough surfaces. A value of 0 turns each one off.

transmissiveBackground sets how the backdrop looks through glass: TRANSMISSIVE_BACKGROUND_ENVIRONMENT samples the environment, _OVERLAY (default) derives opacity from transmitted light tinted by the environment, _TRANSPARENT attenuates the background so glass renders over transparency.
capabilities.outputs: glass over environment, overlay or alpha

capabilities.does: Scatter inside subsurface volumes is traced as real paths, bounded by maxSubsurfaceBounces (256), counted separately from maxBounces.
Only MeshStandardMaterial and MeshPhysicalMaterial are supported; other three.js material types are not. The README does not list their individual properties.
All scene textures are packed into one atlas read by the tracer (textureAtlas, readonly); renderTextureAtlas(layer) draws one atlas layer for debugging.
Area lights and spot lights are shown as supported by the areaLight and spotLights demos in the README.
capabilities.outputs: soft and cone lighting in the trace

capabilities.does: scene.environment and scene.background feed the trace, including intensity, rotation and blur; updateEnvironment re-reads them. BlurredEnvMapGenerator.generate(texture, blur, width, height) returns a blurred, downsampled copy of an environment map (the source stays untouched).

OIDNDenoiser attaches through setDenoiser. Options: initUNetFromURL, auxWeightsUrl, colorWeightsUrl, useAuxiliaryBuffers (albedo and normal guides), maxTileSize, dynamicTile. update runs a pass each frame; denoise, reset and an error event are also exposed.
FSRUpscaler (needs the Upscaler class from @pmndrs/upscaler, optional sharpness) is attached with setUpscaler. renderScale sets the trace resolution as a fraction of the canvas.

While the camera moves, a low-resolution preview is shown: dynamicLowRes (true), lowResScale (0.1), renderDelay (500 ms), fadeDuration (500 ms), adaptiveDynamicRes (true, needs trackTimestamp). The full render fades in after the delay.

frameBudget (250000 path slots per call) sets work per frame regardless of resolution. adaptiveFrameBudget (true) tunes it toward targetFrameTime (16 ms GPU) and needs timestamp tracking. frameTime reports a recent call.

After a change call updateMaterials, updateTransforms, updateCamera, updateEnvironment or updateLights; each resets accumulation. Geometry changes need setScene. setSceneAsync builds BVHs in workers (setBVHWorker); skinned meshes still build on the main thread.

renderAuxBuffer shows the albedo or normal auxiliary buffer. renderDebugBounds draws a BVH-box heatmap (displayTLAS, displayBLAS, stopAtSurface, saturationCount). renderSampleDensity shows per-pixel sample counts. getSampleCountsAsync returns min, max, avg and samplesPerSecond.
renderToCanvas (true) can be set false so samples only accumulate; target is the accumulation render target. synchronizeRenderSize (true) follows the canvas, or setSize sets a fixed resolution.
A depth-of-field demo ships with the repository; the README gives no option names for it.
A demo renders an animation frame by frame (renderVideo). The README also lists a Model Viewer fidelity comparison scene.
asyncCompile (false) compiles kernels without stalling the page; compiling reports state. generateMissingAttributes (true) adds the commonAttributes normal and tangent to geometry that lacks them.

outcomes: browser path-traced stills and frame sequences

rea.notes: README on main now documents a WebGPU-only tracer; older WebGL-era API names were not found on the pages read.

entries.name: three-mesh-bvh

licence.name: MIT (LICENSE file read)

engines.name: MeshBVH and BVH variants
engines.does: Builds a bounding volume hierarchy on a geometry and answers ray, shape and distance queries against it.

engines.name: GPU shader support (WebGL)
engines.does: Packs a BVH into textures and ships GLSL structs and functions so shaders can traverse it.

engines.name: BVHComputeData (WebGPU)
engines.does: Packs scene objects into top-level and bottom-level BVH storage buffers for WGSL and TSL queries.

capabilities.does: computeBoundsTree builds a BVH on a BufferGeometry and disposeBoundsTree removes it. Assigning acceleratedRaycast to Mesh.prototype.raycast makes the standard three.js Raycaster use the tree. computeBatchedBoundsTree and disposeBatchedBoundsTree do the same per geometry of a BatchedMesh.

Build options: strategy (CENTER default, AVERAGE, SAH), maxDepth (40), targetLeafSize (10), setBoundingBox (true), useSharedArrayBuffer (false), indirect (false, leaves the index untouched), verbose (true), onProgress, range (limit to a geometry group).
capabilities.inputs: strategy, maxDepth, targetLeafSize, indirect, range, onProgress
capabilities.outputs: tree tuned for build time or query speed

capabilities.does: raycast returns all hits unsorted and raycastFirst returns the nearest or null; raycastObject3D takes a mesh and returns world-frame results. intersectsGeometry, intersectsBox and intersectsSphere answer yes or no for local-space shapes.
capabilities.inputs: ray, near, far, materialOrSide; shape and transform

capabilities.does: shapecast walks the tree with user callbacks: intersectsBounds, intersectsTriangle, intersectsRange and boundsTraverseOrder. It is the general query form; selection and sculpt are among the demos.
closestPointToPoint(point, target, minThreshold, maxThreshold) finds the nearest surface point. closestPointToGeometry finds the closest pair of points between the mesh and another geometry.
capabilities.inputs: point or geometry, thresholds, target vectors

capabilities.does: bvhcast tests two BVHs against each other with a matrix between them, reporting intersecting ranges or triangles through callbacks.
refit updates bounds after vertex positions change, so deforming or animated meshes avoid a full rebuild. Optional node indices limit the update.
MeshBVH.serialize(bvh, {cloneBuffers}) turns a tree into plain buffers and MeshBVH.deserialize(data, geometry, {setIndex}) restores it, which allows caching or transfer from a worker.

GenerateMeshBVHWorker builds trees in a web worker; ParallelMeshBVHWorker splits the work across workers when SharedArrayBuffer is available and falls back otherwise (import from three-mesh-bvh/worker).
capabilities.outputs: tree built off the main thread

capabilities.does: Besides MeshBVH there are PointsBVH, LineBVH, LineLoopBVH, LineSegmentsBVH, SkinnedMeshBVH and ObjectBVH (a scene-level tree). The README warns the last two may change.
capabilities.outputs: trees for points, lines, skinned meshes and objects

capabilities.does: MeshBVHUniformStruct (updateFrom, dispose) uploads a BVH to a shader. Shader strings bvh_struct_definitions, bvh_ray_functions, bvh_distance_functions and common_functions provide traversal. VertexAttributeTexture and its Float, UInt and Int variants store attributes.

BVHComputeData packs objects into TLAS plus BLAS buffers (attributes default to position as vec4f). getShapecastFn generates a WGSL shapecast from your shape and result structs. TSL helpers: intersectRayTriangle, closestPointToTriangle, ndcToCameraRay; structs rayStruct and result structs.
BVHComputeData.update rebuilds buffers on topology change, updateAsync waits for BVH generation first, and updateTransforms refits and rewrites transforms when only matrices or visibility change.
BVHHelper(mesh, bvh, depth=10) draws the tree as boxes. Properties: color, opacity, depth, displayParents, displayEdges, instanceId, edgeMaterial, meshMaterial; update rebuilds the display.
StaticGeometryGenerator takes meshes and bakes them into one static geometry; options useGroups, applyWorldTransforms and attributes; generate fills a target geometry.

ExtendedTriangle adds sphere, triangle and segment tests plus distanceToPoint and distanceToTriangle. OrientedBox gives box tests with a matrix: intersectsBox, intersectsTriangle, closestPointToPoint, distanceToBox.
Demos named in the README include raycast, shapecast, SDF generation, voxelize, clipped edges, sculpt, selection, physics, character movement, GPU path tracing and diamond rendering.

outcomes: fast raycasts and spatial queries on large meshes
GPU BVH traversal for path tracers and SDF generation

entries.name: A-Frame

licence.name: MIT (stated on the introduction page)

engines.name: Entity-component system on three.js
engines.does: HTML elements (a-scene, a-entity and primitives) carry components that hold behaviour and appearance, built on three.js.

engines.name: Visual inspector
engines.does: Built-in 3D inspector opened with Ctrl+Alt+I (Ctrl+Option+I on Mac).

engines.name: Renderer system
engines.does: Scene-level settings for the WebGL renderer: antialias, colour management, tone mapping, exposure, foveation.

capabilities.does: Scenes are written as HTML: a-scene plus entities and 28 primitives (a-box, a-sphere, a-gltf-model, a-sky, a-text, a-videosphere and others) with attributes for position, rotation and appearance. Components are the unit of behaviour.
capabilities.outputs: a three.js scene built from markup

capabilities.does: The documentation lists 52 built-in components, including animation, geometry, material, light, shadow, raycaster, cursor, look-controls, wasd-controls, gltf-model, obj-model, sound, text, fog, camera, renderer and webxr.

The material component default shader is standard (MeshStandardMaterial): color, emissive, emissiveIntensity, metalness (0), roughness (0.5), maps for src, normal, displacement and ambient occlusion, each with scale, repeat and offset where listed.
capabilities.inputs: color, metalness, roughness, normalMap, displacementMap, ambientOcclusionMap

capabilities.does: Other shaders: phong (specular, shininess 30, combine, reflectivity 0.9, refract, refractionRatio 0.98) and flat (unlit, toneMapped). Base properties: opacity, transparent, alphaTest, side, blending (none, normal, additive, subtractive, multiply), depthTest, dithering, flatShading, vertexColorsEnabled.

AFRAME.registerShader takes a schema (properties marked is: uniform become uniforms), optional vertexShader and fragmentShader strings, raw (RawShaderMaterial), init and update handlers. Uniform types: array, color, int, number, map, time, vec2, vec3, vec4.

The light component type: ambient, directional (default), hemisphere (groundColor), point (decay, distance), spot (angle 60, penumbra, target, decay, distance) and probe (envMap). Common: color, intensity.
capabilities.inputs: type, color, intensity, decay, distance, angle, penumbra

capabilities.does: Lights set castShadow (false by default) with shadowBias and shadowCamera settings (near, far, left, right, top, bottom, fov, automatic, visible) and shadowMapWidth/Height (512). Entities use the shadow component with cast and receive (both true). Scene shadow type: basic, pcf (default) or pcfsoft.

Renderer system keys with defaults: antialias auto, colorManagement true, foveationLevel 1, highRefreshRate false, logarithmicDepthBuffer auto, maxCanvasWidth/Height -1, multiviewStereo false, sortTransparentObjects false, precision high, alpha true, stencil false, toneMapping no, exposure 1, anisotropy 1.

The animation component tweens any property with anime.js: property, from, to, dur (1000), easing (easeInQuad), loop, dir, delay, elasticity, round, startEvents, pauseEvents, resumeEvents, autoplay, enabled. Events animationbegin and animationcomplete.
capabilities.inputs: property, from, to, dur, easing, loop

capabilities.does: gltf-model loads glTF 2.0 from an asset item, url() or data URL. Decoder paths on a-scene: dracoDecoderPath, basisTranscoderPath (KTX2) and meshoptDecoderPath. Events model-loaded and model-error. Animations need animation-mixer from aframe-extras.

The raycaster component: objects, origin, direction, near, far, interval, useWorldCoordinates, showLine, lineColor, lineOpacity, autoRefresh, enabled. Events raycaster-intersected(-cleared), raycaster-intersection(-cleared), raycaster-closest-entity-changed; methods getIntersection and refreshObjects.

hand-tracking-controls shows a tracked hand (hand left or right, modelColor, modelOpacity, modelStyle mesh or dots) and emits pinchstarted, pinchended and pinchmoved with world coordinates. It can run beside controller components such as meta-touch-controls.

Targets VR and AR headsets and phones: Meta Quest, Apple Vision Pro, PICO, Lynx-R1, Valve Index and desktop browsers. Components include webxr, ar-hit-test, anchored, real-world-meshing, hide-on-enter-ar/vr, laser-controls, hand-controls and several controller models.

rea.notes: MIT stated on the introduction page. Version 1.7.0 docs read; 1.8.0 docs exist.

entries.name: regl

licence.name: MIT (README); example assets carry other licences

engines.name: Commands
engines.does: A command is a full description of GPU state for one draw (shaders, uniforms, attributes, depth, blend) that is called with props.

engines.name: Resources
engines.does: Buffers, elements, textures, cube maps, renderbuffers and framebuffers created through the regl object.

capabilities.does: regl({...}) returns a draw command from vert and frag source strings, attributes, uniforms and count. Calling the command (optionally with props) draws. regl.prop makes a value dynamic, regl.buffer makes an array buffer, regl.clear clears and regl.frame wraps the animation loop.
capabilities.inputs: vert, frag, attributes, uniforms, count, regl.prop

capabilities.does: Startup options: gl, canvas, container, attributes (context settings), pixelRatio, extensions (required), optionalExtensions, profile, onDone callback.
capabilities.inputs: gl, canvas, container, extensions, optionalExtensions, pixelRatio, profile

capabilities.does: Command state blocks: depth (enable, mask, range, func), blend, stencil, cull, polygonOffset, frontFace, dither, lineWidth, colorMask, sample coverage, scissor and viewport.
Context values available inside a command: tick, time, viewportWidth/Height, framebufferWidth/Height, drawingBufferWidth/Height and pixelRatio.
capabilities.outputs: frame and size data for uniforms

capabilities.does: Resource kinds with create, update, resize, subimage or subdata, properties and destroy: buffers, elements (index buffers), textures, cube maps, renderbuffers, framebuffers and cube framebuffers.
A command-level framebuffer property sets the render target; null targets the drawing buffer. Framebuffers have create, update, bind, resize and destroy operations.
The instances command property sets how many instances a draw call renders, next to count and offset.
Setting profile gives each command count, cpuTime and gpuTime stats. Pages also cover stats, timers, limits (device capabilities), extension queries, reading pixels, context loss and cleanup.
Stated values: simplicity, correctness, performance, minimalism and stability; no dependencies; over 30,000 unit tests and above 95 percent code coverage; continuous benchmarking with npm run bench.

entries.name: CesiumJS

licence.name: Apache-2.0 (README); Cesium ion is a separate commercial platform

engines.name: @cesium/engine
engines.does: Core rendering and data APIs: Scene, Globe, Camera, 3D Tiles, terrain, imagery, Entity and data sources.

engines.name: @cesium/widgets
engines.does: UI widgets such as Viewer, Animation, Timeline, InfoBox, Geocoder and HomeButton.

engines.name: Cesium ion
engines.does: Commercial hosting platform from which terrain, imagery and 3D Tiles can be streamed; other sources also work.

capabilities.does: Globe properties: enableLighting, dynamicAtmosphereLighting, atmosphereLightIntensity (10), showWaterEffect, depthTestAgainstTerrain, baseColor, translucency, undergroundColor, showGroundAtmosphere, material, clippingPlanes, cartographicLimitRectangle, maximumScreenSpaceError (2), tileCacheSize (100).
Scene mode defaults to SCENE3D; Columbus View and 2D are the other modes, and morphTime (1.0 means 3D, 0.0 means flat) sets the transition between them.

Viewer builds the whole app: options for terrain, baseLayer, sceneMode, shadows, shouldAnimate, requestRenderMode, msaaSamples (4), targetFrameRate, scene3DOnly, orderIndependentTranslucency, and toggles for timeline, animation, geocoder, homeButton, sceneModePicker, baseLayerPicker, infoBox, vrButton.

Cesium3DTileset streams 3D Tiles with screen-space-error refinement: maximumScreenSpaceError (16), dynamicScreenSpaceError, foveatedScreenSpaceError, progressiveResolutionHeightFraction, preferLeaves, cullRequestsWhileMoving, preloadFlightDestinations, skipLevelOfDetail with skipLevels and baseScreenSpaceError.
capabilities.outputs: streamed city, photogrammetry or point cloud

capabilities.does: cacheBytes (512 MiB default) is the GPU cache target and maximumCacheOverflowBytes (also 512 MiB) allows temporary overflow when required tiles do not fit.

Tilesets take a style, clippingPlanes and clippingPolygons, classificationType for draping on terrain or tiles, colorBlendMode (HIGHLIGHT) with colorBlendAmount, splitDirection for split-screen compare, customShader (experimental), pointCloudShading, imageBasedLighting and outline options (showOutline, outlineColor).

Debug flags: debugFreezeFrame, debugColorizeTiles, debugWireframe, debugShowBoundingVolume, debugShowContentBoundingVolume, debugShowViewerRequestVolume, debugShowGeometricError, debugShowRenderingStatistics, debugShowMemoryUsage, debugShowUrl, debugHeatmapTilePropertyName.

Scene settings: skyBox (stars), skyAtmosphere, sun with sunBloom, moon, fog, atmosphere for tiles and models, highDynamicRange, light (Sun directional by default), backgroundColor, msaaSamples, logarithmicDepthBuffer, verticalExaggeration with a relative height.
requestRenderMode renders only when the scene changes or requestRender() is called; maximumRenderTimeChange sets the simulation-time change that triggers a frame.

Scene methods: pickPosition (world position from depth), sampleHeight(position, objectsToExclude, width), clampToHeight, drillPick(windowPosition, limit, width, height). Globe adds getHeight and pick(ray). invertClassification tints unclassified tile geometry.

ImageryLayer options: rectangle, alpha, nightAlpha, dayAlpha, brightness, contrast, hue, saturation, gamma, splitDirection, minification and magnification filters, colorToAlpha with colorToAlphaThreshold, cutoutRectangle, minimumTerrainLevel, maximumTerrainLevel, maximumAnisotropy. Several can be per-tile functions.

Imagery providers named on the layer page: OpenStreetMapImageryProvider, IonImageryProvider (fromAssetId) and createWorldImageryAsync with IonWorldImageryStyle.AERIAL; BingMapsImageryProvider and MapboxImageryProvider are listed in the sidebar.
The reference index lists a Terrain class, TerrainProvider, TerrainData and CesiumTerrainProvider with related providers; Viewer accepts a terrain object that supplies terrain asynchronously.

Model.fromGltfAsync loads .gltf or .glb with options such as asynchronous, incrementallyLoadTextures, upAxis, forwardAxis, heightReference and projectTo2D. Properties: silhouetteColor and silhouetteSize, color with colorBlendMode, clippingPlanes, shadows, minimumPixelSize, maximumScale, customShader (experimental).
capabilities.outputs: glTF model placed on the globe

capabilities.does: Supported glTF extensions include KHR draco_mesh_compression, meshopt_compression, texture_basisu, texture_transform, mesh_quantization, materials_unlit; EXT mesh_gpu_instancing, mesh_features, structural_metadata, texture_webp, mesh_primitive_edge_visibility; and CESIUM_RTC, CESIUM_primitive_outline, AGI_articulations.

activeAnimations is a ModelAnimationCollection of playing glTF animations; clampAnimations holds a pose between keyframes. setArticulationStage(key, value) plus applyArticulations drives articulated parts; getNode(name) lets a script set a node transform.

CzmlDataSource.load(czml, options) reads CZML, a JSON format for time-dynamic scenes, from a URL or object. process adds to existing data; options sourceUri and credit; a clock is taken from the document or from combined availability. Events changedEvent, errorEvent, loadingEvent.

The reference lists Entity, EntityCollection, EntityCluster and graphics classes, and data sources CzmlDataSource, GeoJsonDataSource and KmlDataSource, with DataSourceDisplay. Animation and Timeline widgets are listed under widgets.
capabilities.outputs: vector and time-based data on the globe

capabilities.does: PostProcessStageLibrary creators and their uniforms: createBlackAndWhiteStage (gradations), createBlurStage (delta, sigma, stepSize), createBrightnessStage, createDepthOfFieldStage (focalDistance, delta, sigma, stepSize), createEdgeDetectionStage (color, length), createLensFlareStage (intensity, distortion, ghostDispersal, haloWidth, dirtAmount), createNightVisionStage, createSilhouetteStage.

CesiumJS can stream terrain, imagery and 3D Tiles from the Cesium ion platform or from other online or offline sources. Packages: cesium, @cesium/engine, @cesium/widgets; modules can be imported separately for tree shaking.

entries.name: <model-viewer>

licence.name: Apache-2.0 (docs footer and GitHub link)

engines.name: model-viewer web component
engines.does: A custom element that loads a glTF/GLB and draws it with three.js, with camera, lighting, AR and animation attributes.

engines.name: model-viewer-effects
engines.does: A post-processing plugin package listed in the repository.

engines.name: Editor (space-opera) and render-fidelity-tools
engines.does: A hosted editor project and a package for testing render quality.

capabilities.does: Loads glTF/GLB from src with alt text, a poster image, loading (auto, lazy, eager), reveal (auto or manual dismissPoster) and with-credentials. Static properties set decoder URLs for DRACO, KTX2 and Meshopt; modelCacheSize defaults to 5.
capabilities.inputs: src, alt, poster, loading, reveal, dracoDecoderLocation, ktx2TranscoderLocation

capabilities.does: camera-controls enables orbit, zoom and pan. camera-orbit (default 0deg 75deg 105%), camera-target, field-of-view, min/max-camera-orbit, min/max-field-of-view, orbit-sensitivity, zoom-sensitivity, pan-sensitivity, disable-pan, disable-zoom, disable-tap, interpolation-decay (50 ms), touch-action.
auto-rotate with auto-rotate-delay (3000 ms) and rotation-per-second (pi/32). interaction-prompt (auto) with style wiggle or basic and a threshold (3000 ms) shows a hint; slots replace the hand icon.

environment-image takes neutral, legacy or a URL; skybox-image gives an equirectangular background that also lights the model; skybox-height projects it onto the ground. An environment-change event fires on updates.
tone-mapping selects the HDR-to-SDR function (default neutral); exposure (1) scales model and skybox.
shadow-intensity (0 disables) sets shadow opacity and shadow-softness (1) the blur. hasBakedShadow() reports a baked shadow plane in the model.

ar enables AR; ar-modes is a prioritised list (default webxr scene-viewer quick-look); ar-scale auto or fixed; ar-placement floor or wall; ios-src for a USDZ; ar-usdz-max-texture-size; xr-environment for WebXR lighting estimation. canActivateAR and activateAR() plus ar-status and ar-tracking events.

animation-name picks a clip, autoplay starts it, animation-crossfade-duration (300 ms) blends changes. Properties availableAnimations, currentTime, timeScale, duration, paused; methods play, pause, appendAnimation and detachAnimation blend clips together.
variant-name selects a model variant by name; availableVariants lists them. orientation (roll, pitch, yaw) and scale transform the model.
The model property exposes materials. materialFromPoint returns the material under a point. createTexture, createVideoTexture, createCanvasTexture and createLottieTexture make textures to assign.

Children with slot hotspot-* are pinned to the model. Methods: updateHotspot({name, position, normal, surface}), queryHotspot, positionAndNormalFromPoint, surfaceFromPoint. CSS variables --min-hotspot-opacity (0.25) and --max-hotspot-opacity (1).
exportScene(options) exports the model as glTF or GLB.
toBlob(options) returns a Promise of an image Blob and toDataURL(type, encoderOptions) returns a data URL; both default to image/png.

registerEffectComposer swaps in an EffectComposer and registerRenderer replaces the render stack. Static minimumRenderScale (0.5) sets the lowest dynamic render scale; powerPreference defaults to high-performance; a render-scale event reports DPR changes.

Events: load, progress, error, before-render, poster-dismissed, model-visibility, camera-change, play, pause, loop, finished. getDimensions and getBoundingBoxCenter return metres; mapURLs rewrites request URLs.
alt gives a screen-reader description; the a11y attribute takes JSON of orientation names for WCAG; the default poster and progress bar have slots and CSS parts.
The repository holds the component, a model-viewer-effects post-processing plugin, the documentation site, render-fidelity-tools, shared assets and the space-opera editor source.
