engines.name: Render pipeline
engines.does: Lua-scripted draw pipeline with predicates and render targets

engines.name: Physics
engines.does: Box2D for 2D and Bullet for 3D

engines.name: ParticleFX
engines.does: Emitter-based particle effects with modifiers

engines.name: GUI
engines.does: Node-based user interface scenes

engines.name: Bob builder
engines.does: Command line bundler used by the editor

capabilities.does: The render pipeline is a Lua render script with init, update and on_message. It uses render.predicate (material tags) and render.draw (frustum culling, sort order back-to-front, front-to-back or none), render.set_view, set_projection, set_viewport, clear, and enable_state for depth, stencil, blend and cull face.

Render targets are made in script with render.render_target: per-buffer attachments with format, width, height, filters and wrap; sample_count of 1, 2, 4, 8 or 16 (default 1). set_render_target switches target; resource.get_render_target_info returns the effective sample_count.

Camera component: Aspect Ratio, Fov (vertical, radians), Near Z, Far Z, Auto Aspect Ratio, Orthographic Projection, Orthographic Zoom and Orthographic Mode Fixed, Auto Fit or Auto Cover. camera.* functions convert between screen and world.
capabilities.inputs: Fov, Near Z, Far Z, Orthographic Mode, Orthographic Zoom

capabilities.does: Materials pair a vertex program (.vp) and fragment program (.fp). Constants include engine matrices (world, view, projection and combinations) and time; user constants change at runtime with go.set and go.animate. Samplers set wrap and filter modes and max anisotropy.

Material attributes are per-vertex streams with a semantic type (position, texcoord, colour, normal, tangent, world matrix and others), data type, normalize flag, coordinate space, vector type and step function (per vertex or per instance).
capabilities.inputs: Attribute name, semantic type, data type, step function

capabilities.does: Many copies of a model draw in fewer calls when they share a material with local vertex space, at least one per-instance attribute and matching constants. Only Model components support it for now.

glTF 2.0 material data reaches shaders in a PbrMaterial uniform block. Metallic roughness is the default: baseColorFactor, metallicAndRoughnessFactor (both default 1.0), colour and metallic-roughness textures, plus normal, occlusion and emissive maps. No built-in PBR lighting exists; the shader supplies the BRDF.
capabilities.outputs: PBR parameters for custom lighting shaders

capabilities.does: Extension data passed the same way: specular-glossiness, clearcoat, ior, specular, iridescence, sheen, transmission, volume and emissive strength, each as a struct such as PbrClearCoat or PbrSheen. A #define flag per feature lets you drop unused structs from the shader.
capabilities.outputs: Extra PBR layers as shader data only

capabilities.does: Light components: ambient, directional, point and spot, each with color and intensity; point and spot lights add range; spot lights add inner_cone_angle and outer_cone_angle. A LightBuffer uniform block feeds shaders; light.max_count defaults to 64.

ParticleFX emitters: Play Mode (Once, Loop), Emission Space (World, Emitter), Blend Mode (Alpha, Add, Multiply, Screen), Emitter Type (Circle, 2D Cone, Box, Sphere, Cone), Particle Orientation, Inherit Velocity, Stretch With Velocity. Keyable properties include Spawn Rate, Particle Life Time and Initial Speed with spread.
capabilities.inputs: Spawn Rate, Particle Life Time, Initial Speed, Emitter Type, Blend Mode

capabilities.does: Particle modifiers change velocity: Acceleration, Drag, Radial (attract or repel) and Vortex (swirl), with Magnitude and Max Distance for the last two. A modifier on the effect root affects all emitters; under an emitter, only that one. Curve editor shapes keyed properties.

Physics uses Box2D for 2D (App Manifest options: Box2D Version 3, Box2D legacy, None) and Bullet for 3D. Collision objects, shapes, groups, messages, joints and ray casts are supported; Physics scale maps pixels to metres; Use Fixed Timestep sets a stable step.
capabilities.inputs: Physics 2D setting, Physics scale, Use Fixed Timestep, Fixed Update Frequency

capabilities.does: go.animate tweens numbers, vectors and quaternions, with playback modes, easing (linear, back, bounce, elastic, sine, expo, circ, quad, cubic, quart, quint with IN, OUT, INOUT, OUTIN), custom easing vectors and completion callbacks. gui.animate does the same for GUI nodes.
capabilities.inputs: go.animate url, property, playback, target, easing, duration

capabilities.does: Models play baked skeletal animations only. model.play_anim takes playback modes (once, loop, pingpong, forward or backward). Bones are game objects (model.get_go); a cursor property scrubs an animation.
Morph targets with weights from 0 to 1 are imported from glTF with initial weights and weight animations; model.get_blend_weights and set_blend_weights read or override them.

GUI scenes have Box, Text, Pie, Template and ParticleFX nodes with Size Mode, Adjust Mode (Fit, Zoom, Stretch), Pivot, Blend Mode, Layer, X/Y Anchor, 9-slice, text Leading and Tracking, stencil clipping and a GUI script.
The Tile Map component paints tiles from a Tile Source onto layers using a brush with rotate and flip; Blend Mode Alpha, Add, Multiply, Screen; runtime tilemap.get_tile and set_tile.

Bundle targets: Android (.apk), iOS (.ipa), macOS (.app), Linux, Windows (.exe), HTML5 and Facebook Instant Games, via the editor or the Bob command line. Options: build report, release or debug, bundle_resources, custom_resources.
Game logic is written in Lua scripts. The manual index also lists editor scripts, an editor HTTP API, automated testing, hot reloading and live update topics.
Native extensions are written in C/C++ with the Defold SDK, with extension manifests, Gradle and CocoaPods dependencies, and a build server (Extender) that can be set up locally.

entries.name: Unity (Unity 6 line)

licence.name: Unity Personal is free (games and entertainment only); Pro lists 210 USD per month on the products page and is required above 200K USD revenue or funding; Enterprise and Industry have custom pricing. Enterprise adds read-only source access.

engines.name: HDRP
engines.does: High Definition Render Pipeline for high-end real-time rendering: ray tracing, path tracing, physical sky, volumetrics, SSS and decals.

engines.name: URP
engines.does: Universal Render Pipeline, a prebuilt scriptable pipeline for platforms from mobile to high-end; Forward+, renderer features, 2D renderer.

engines.name: Visual Effect Graph
engines.does: Node-based GPU particle and mesh effect authoring on compute shaders.

engines.name: Shader Graph
engines.does: Node-based shader authoring for URP and HDRP.

engines.name: Timeline
engines.does: Sequencing tool for cutscenes, gameplay sequences and audio.

engines.name: Cinemachine
engines.does: Procedural camera modules for the Unity camera.

engines.name: Animation (Mecanim)
engines.does: Animator, Animator Controller, clips and blend trees.

engines.name: Physics
engines.does: PhysX integration for 3D, Box2D for 2D, Unity Physics with optional Havok for DOTS.

engines.name: Progressive Light Baker
engines.does: Baked lightmaps and light probes with GPU, CPU and compute backends.

engines.name: Adaptive Probe Volumes
engines.does: Automatically placed probe lighting with baking sets and streaming.

engines.name: Post-processing Volumes
engines.does: Global and local volumes holding overrides that blend by contribution.

engines.name: Rendering Layers
engines.does: Layer masks that limit which renderers a light or effect affects.

engines.name: LOD Group
engines.does: Component that swaps renderer sets by screen size with optional cross-fade.

engines.name: GPU Resident Drawer and GPU occlusion culling
engines.does: BatchRendererGroup-based instanced drawing with GPU-side occlusion culling.

engines.name: Occlusion culling window
engines.does: Baked visibility data with bake parameters and view volumes.

engines.name: Havok Physics for Unity
engines.does: Binary Havok backend for the Unity Physics DOTS package.

engines.name: Entities (DOTS)
engines.does: Data-oriented ECS package.

engines.name: Burst
engines.does: LLVM-based compiler for a C# subset.

engines.name: Recorder
engines.does: Play-mode capture to video, images, AOV EXR, animation and audio.

capabilities.does: HDRP path tracer accumulates frames into a reference image. Controls how many frames build up, how many bounces each path takes, a clamp on bright samples, a layer filter, sky importance sampling and the random seed pattern.
capabilities.inputs: State, LayerMask, Maximum Samples, Minimum Depth, Maximum Depth, Maximum Intensity, Sky Importance Sampling, Seed Mode (Non Repeating, Repeating, Custom)

capabilities.does: Cleans the path-traced image with an external denoiser chosen in the override. Options can keep AOV detail, use neighbouring frames for stability, and denoise volumetric scattering as a separate layer.
capabilities.inputs: Denoising (None, Intel Open Image Denoise, NVIDIA OptiX), Use AOVs, Temporal, Separate Volumetrics

capabilities.does: Replaces shadow maps with traced rays for directional, point, spot and rectangle lights. Gives soft penumbra from light size, colored shadows through transmissive objects, and an optional spatio-temporal denoiser.
capabilities.inputs: Sun Angle, Sample Count, Color Shadow, Semi-Transparent Shadow, Radius, Denoise, Denoiser Radius, Distance Based Denoising

capabilities.does: Traces reflection rays in the screen-space reflection override, in a performance or a quality mode. Sets what lights a ray that misses, how many bounces, how many rays per pixel and how strongly the denoiser filters.
capabilities.inputs: Tracing (Ray Marching, Ray Tracing, Mixed), Ray Miss, Last Bounce, Mode, Max Ray Length, Full Resolution, Sample Count, Bounce Count, Denoise, Denoiser Radius, Anti-flickering Strength

capabilities.does: Screen-space reflection override with a fast approximation or a multi-frame PBR accumulation. Fades by smoothness and screen edge, can reflect sky, and rejects history by speed.
capabilities.inputs: Algorithm (Approximation, PBR Accumulation), Minimum Smoothness, Smoothness Fade Start, Reflect Sky, Screen Edge Fade Distance, Object Thickness, Max Ray Steps, Accumulation Factor, Speed Rejection

capabilities.does: Ray-traced indirect lighting is switched on with the Ray Tracing option of the Screen Space Global Illumination override. Needs a project and camera set up for ray tracing.
capabilities.inputs: Ray Tracing option on the SSGI override; Ray Tracing frame setting

capabilities.does: Adaptive Probe Volumes place light probes automatically with density control, bake several scenes in one Baking Set, switch Lighting Scenarios at runtime, stream probe data, and fix light leaks with adjustment volumes.
capabilities.inputs: volume size, probe density, Baking Sets, Lighting Scenarios, sky occlusion, Probe Adjustment Volume

capabilities.does: Progressive Light Baker makes lightmaps and light probes. Backends are the Progressive GPU Lightmapper (OpenCL), a deprecated CPU one, and the Compute Light Baker for URP and HDRP. Scripts reach the settings through the Lightmapping and LightmapEditorSettings classes.
capabilities.inputs: Default Light Baker, Lightmapper (Progressive CPU or GPU); GPU needs OpenCL 1.2 and 2 GB VRAM (Unity current manual)

capabilities.does: Rendering Layers are a 32-bit mask on renderers and lights. A light affects only renderers sharing a layer; shadow layers can be set apart. Effects that use the mask see the first 16 layers.
capabilities.inputs: Rendering Layer Mask on light and renderer, Custom Shadow Layers, Rendering Layer Names

capabilities.does: Physically based sky simulates planet atmosphere: air, aerosol and ozone layers with density, altitude and tint, plus ground and space emission textures. The sky also feeds environment light with an update mode.
capabilities.inputs: Air Density R/G/B, Aerosol Density, Aerosol Anisotropy, Ozone Density Dimmer, Ground Color Texture, Space Emission Texture, Horizon Tint, Zenith Tint, Intensity Mode, Update Mode

capabilities.does: Fog override with height-based and distance fog, a volumetric buffer with budget or manual slice controls, denoising and directional-only mode. Local fog volumes and a fog shader graph are also listed.
capabilities.inputs: Fog Attenuation Distance, Base Height, Maximum Height, Volumetric Fog Distance, Slice Distribution Uniformity, Denoising Mode, Anisotropy (-1 to 1), Volumetric Fog Budget, Directional Lights Only

capabilities.does: Raymarched clouds with Simple, Advanced and Manual shape control. Sets density curves, cloud types, erosion, wind, temporal accumulation, light scattering and cloud shadows.
capabilities.inputs: Cloud Preset, Density Curve, Erosion Factor, Bottom Altitude, Altitude Range, Global Horizontal Wind Speed, Num Primary Steps, Num Light Steps, Multi Scattering, Shadow Resolution

capabilities.does: Water system with pool, river and ocean/sea/lake surfaces. Wind, swell, ripples and current drive waves, with multi-band simulation, foam, caustics, refraction, underwater view and masks. Scripts can read the surface for buoyancy.
capabilities.inputs: surface type, Current, Simulation Band, foam amount and smoothness, caustic resolution, Refraction, Scattering

capabilities.does: HDRP Lit material uses a base color map, metallic and smoothness values or a packed mask map, and min-max remapping of mask channels. UV mapping can be UV0 to UV3, planar or triplanar.
capabilities.inputs: Base Map, Metallic, Smoothness, Mask Map, Metallic Remapping, Smoothness Remapping, Ambient Occlusion Remapping, Base UV Mapping, Tiling, Offset

capabilities.does: Lit material accepts tangent-space or object-space normal maps with an intensity from 0 to 8, and bent normal maps that improve ambient occlusion on diffuse light.
capabilities.inputs: Normal Map Space, Normal Map, Normal Map OS, Bent Normal Map, Bent Normal Map OS

capabilities.does: Vertex displacement or pixel displacement from a height map. Pixel displacement takes min and max sample steps, a mip fade start and a depth offset so depth effects see the shifted surface.
capabilities.inputs: Displacement Mode, Lock With Object Scale, Minimum Steps, Maximum Steps, Fading Mip Level Start, Primitive Length, Primitive Width, Depth Offset

capabilities.does: Alpha Clipping discards pixels below a threshold, with separate thresholds for shadows, the transparent depth prepass and postpass, and an alpha-to-mask option for MSAA.
capabilities.inputs: Alpha Clipping, Threshold (default 0.5), Use Shadow Threshold, Shadow Threshold, Alpha to Mask, Prepass Threshold, Postpass Threshold

capabilities.does: Transparent surface type with alpha, additive or premultiply blending, rendering pass choice, sorting priority, back-then-front rendering, depth pre and post passes and motion vectors for transparents.
capabilities.inputs: Surface Type, Rendering Pass, Blending Mode, Preserve Specular Lighting, Sorting Priority, Back Then Front Rendering, Transparent Writes Motion Vectors

capabilities.does: Emission map with color, intensity in nits or EV100, exposure weight and a toggle for how emission feeds global illumination (realtime, baked, none).
capabilities.inputs: Emission Map, Emission Intensity, Exposure Weight, Emission Multiply with Base, Global Illumination

capabilities.does: Lit material has a Coat Mask from 0 to 1 that adds a clear coat layer on the base. Ray-traced reflections then apply to the coat when the mask is above zero.
Material Type switch to Anisotropy gives stretched highlights on brushed or fibrous surfaces. Other types are Standard, Iridescence, Specular Color, Translucent and Subsurface Scattering.
Material Type switch to Iridescence gives thin-film color shifts on the Lit material.

Diffusion profiles drive screen-space subsurface scattering and transmission. They set scattering color, multiplier, maximum radius, refraction index, world scale, dual specular lobes, and thick or thin object transmission with a thickness remap in millimeters.
capabilities.inputs: Scattering Color, Multiplier, Max Radius, Index of Refraction, World Scale, Texturing Mode, Dual Lobe Multipliers, Lobe Mix, Transmission Mode, Transmission Tint, Thickness Remap

capabilities.does: A detail map adds micro albedo, normal and smoothness variation with its own UV mapping, tiling and scales, optionally locked to the base tiling.
capabilities.inputs: Detail Map, Detail UV Mapping, Detail Albedo Scale, Detail Normal Scale, Detail Smoothness Scale (0 to 2)

capabilities.does: Geometric specular anti-aliasing reduces shimmering highlights on curved or bumpy geometry by raising roughness with a variance strength and a maximum offset.
capabilities.inputs: Geometric Specular AA, Screen Space Variance (0 to 1), Threshold

capabilities.does: Decal projector box projects a decal material onto meshes and terrain that share a Decal Layer. Has draw distance, fade, angle fade, tiling, fade factor and an option to draw on transparent surfaces through an atlas.
capabilities.inputs: Scale Mode, Size, Projection Depth, Pivot, Material, Decal Layer, Draw Distance, Start Fade, Angle Fade, Fade Factor, Affects Transparent

capabilities.does: Shader Graph builds shaders from connected nodes. A graph ends in one Master Stack with a Vertex and a Fragment context holding blocks; the stack contents depend on the Graph Settings.
capabilities.inputs: nodes, Master Stack blocks, Graph Settings

capabilities.does: Depth of field override with off, physical camera and manual range modes. Manual mode sets near and far blur start and end plus sample counts and maximum radius; the physical camera supplies aperture, blades and curvature. Path tracing computes it at full resolution.
capabilities.inputs: Focus Mode, Focus Distance Mode, Near Blur Start/End, Far Blur Start/End, Near/Far Blur Sample Count, Near/Far Blur Max Radius

capabilities.does: Motion blur override from motion vectors with an intensity, sample count, velocity limits in pixels and separate clamping of camera rotation and translation.
capabilities.inputs: Intensity, Quality, Sample Count, Maximum Velocity, Minimum Velocity, Camera Motion Blur, Camera Clamp Mode, Rotation Clamp, Translation Clamp

capabilities.does: Bloom override with threshold, intensity, scatter, tint, a lens dirt texture, bicubic filtering and quarter or half resolution. An anamorphic option follows the camera.
capabilities.inputs: Threshold, Intensity, Scatter, Tint, Dirt Texture, Dirt Intensity, High Quality Filtering, Resolution, Anamorphic

capabilities.does: Tonemapping override with None, Neutral, ACES, Custom curve (toe, shoulder, gamma) and External lookup texture modes.
capabilities.inputs: Mode, Toe Strength, Toe Length, Shoulder Strength, Shoulder Length, Shoulder Angle, Gamma, Lookup Texture, Contribution

capabilities.does: Temporal anti-aliasing uses a history buffer and motion vectors; it also stabilises ambient occlusion and volumetrics. It cannot combine with MSAA or dynamic resolution. FXAA and SMAA are cheaper post-process alternatives.
capabilities.inputs: Antialiasing drop-down on the camera: FXAA, TAA, SMAA

capabilities.does: MSAA works in forward rendering with 2x, 4x or 8x samples. It disables screen-space reflections, screen-space shadows and TAA, and does not work with ray tracing or water.
capabilities.inputs: Lit Shader Mode (Both or Forward Only), Multisample Antialiasing Quality

capabilities.does: Volumes hold overrides in Volume Profiles. Global volumes act everywhere, local volumes act near their collider, and HDRP blends all volumes with non-zero contribution. Two default volumes have lowest priority.
capabilities.inputs: Volume, Volume Profile, Volume Override, global or local mode

capabilities.does: Custom Passes inject extra rendering at chosen points of the HDRP frame. They can use depth and color buffers, camera AOVs and a material, and can run from a volume or from the global custom pass API.
capabilities.inputs: injection points, Custom Pass Volume, buffers and pyramids, AOVs

capabilities.does: GPU Resident Drawer draws GameObjects with GPU instancing through BatchRendererGroup. Needs compute shader support; enabled in the HDRP or URP asset as Instanced Drawing, with BatchRendererGroup Variants set to Keep All.
capabilities.inputs: GPU Resident Drawer = Instanced Drawing, BatchRendererGroup Variants = Keep All

capabilities.does: GPU occlusion culling removes hidden objects on the GPU. Requires the GPU Resident Drawer and the GPU Occlusion setting in the asset.

Baked occlusion culling in the Occlusion Culling window with Bake parameters and view volumes. Smallest Occluder, Smallest Hole and Backface Threshold trade data size against precision. No culling happens outside the baked camera volumes.
capabilities.inputs: Smallest Occluder, Smallest Hole, Backface Threshold, Occlusion Area, Is View Volume (Unity 6.6 manual)

capabilities.does: LOD Group switches renderer sets by screen-height percentage. Fade Mode is None, Cross Fade or Speed Tree; cross-fade can run on a timer or over a transition width. Bounds and lightmap scale can be recalculated (Unity 6.4 manual).
capabilities.inputs: Transition (% Screen Size), Fade Mode, Animate Cross-fading, Fade Transition Width, Recalculate Bounds, Object Size

capabilities.does: Visual Effect Graph builds particle and mesh-output effects as node graphs. A particle system chains Initialize, Update and Output contexts; a Spawn context sets how many particles are born. Simulation runs on compute shaders.
capabilities.inputs: Spawn, Initialize, Update, Output contexts, Blocks, Operators, exposed properties, events

capabilities.does: Timeline asset plus instance for cutscenes and sequences. Tracks hold clips with ease, blend, split, trim, speed and gap extrapolation; Activation, Animation and Audio tracks, Control clips, markers and signals, sub-timelines and a Playable Director.
capabilities.inputs: tracks, clips, markers, signals, Playable Director

capabilities.does: Cinemachine drives the Unity camera from procedural behaviours: Cinemachine Camera, Brain, position and rotation composers, spline dolly, target group, confiners and a deoccluder that avoids obstacles.
capabilities.inputs: CinemachineCamera, CinemachineBrain, Position Composer, Rotation Composer, Spline Dolly, Target Group, Confiner 2D/3D, Deoccluder

capabilities.does: Cinemachine adds Perlin noise profiles and an impulse system with sources, listeners, filtering and collision-triggered sources for camera shake.
capabilities.inputs: Noise Settings, Basic Multi Channel Perlin, Impulse Source, Impulse Listener, Collision Impulse Source

capabilities.does: Unity Recorder captures Play mode to video or animated GIF, image sequences, animation clips and WAV audio. It runs from the Editor, Timeline or command line, but not in standalone players.
capabilities.inputs: recorder type, Timeline track, command line
capabilities.outputs: video, image sequence, audio, animation clip

capabilities.does: Recorder saves Arbitrary Output Variable passes as multi-part EXR files for compositing.
Recorder accumulation mode captures sub-frames for motion blur or path-tracing convergence.
Mecanim animation system uses an Animator component with an Animator Controller, the Animation window for clips, curves on imported clips, and a Legacy system kept for compatibility.
capabilities.inputs: Animator, Animator Controller, animation clips, curves

capabilities.does: Animator Controller holds animation states and transitions, edited in the Animator window.
Blend trees mix similar motions by animation parameters. Blend types are 1D, 2D and Direct; created from the Animator Controller as a new state.
A humanoid definition lets animation move between models that share it.
Built-in 3D physics is an NVIDIA PhysX integration with Rigidbody components for physics-driven GameObjects. A 2D system integrates Box2D.
Colliders define collision between GameObjects.
Joints connect GameObjects and simulate pivoting, movement and restriction. Articulations configure complex systems of rigid bodies and joints.
Physics-based character control for first-person and third-person characters.
Cloth component simulates fabric movement for character clothing and other textiles.
Ragdoll physics setup for characters.

Havok Physics for Unity is a binary-only backend for the Unity Physics (DOTS) package using the same data formats. The package page says scenes with many rigid bodies can run more than twice as fast, with stable stacking by default.
capabilities.inputs: Unity Physics data, Havok Visual Debugger (Windows)

capabilities.does: Entities package is a data-oriented implementation of the Entity Component System, part of the DOTS stack.

Burst compiles a C# subset (High-Performance C#) from IL to native CPU code with LLVM. Applied with the BurstCompile attribute to jobs and static methods, with SIMD intrinsics and an Inspector window.
URP SSAO is a Renderer Feature, not a Volume effect. Options are noise method, radius, intensity, falloff, normal source, downsample, after-opaque and blur quality.
capabilities.inputs: Method, Intensity, Radius, Falloff Distance, Direct Lighting Strength, Source, Normal Quality, Downsample, After Opaque, Blur Quality, Samples

capabilities.does: URP Forward+ path has no per-object light limit; a per-camera limit remains. Adds blending of more than two reflection probes. Selected as the Rendering Path of the Universal Renderer (URP 16 package docs).
URP Decal Renderer Feature with Automatic, DBuffer and Screen Space techniques. DBuffer surface data is Albedo, Albedo Normal or Albedo Normal MAOS; Screen Space has normal reconstruction quality.
capabilities.inputs: Technique, Surface Data, Normal Blend, Max Draw Distance, Use Rendering Layers

capabilities.does: URP 2D lighting uses Light 2D components affecting sprites by Target Sorting Layers, with optional volumetric light and falloff. Unity 6.5 manual.
capabilities.inputs: Target Sorting Layers, Volumetric, Volume Intensity, Falloff

capabilities.does: URP 17 Render Graph allocates only resources used per frame and sets sync points between compute and graphics queues. Scriptable Render Passes and Renderer Features add custom passes.
capabilities.inputs: Scriptable Render Pass, Scriptable Renderer Feature, RenderGraph API

capabilities.does: Spatial-Temporal Post-processing upscales frames rendered at lower resolution; enabled under Quality, Upscaling Filter in the URP asset.

outcomes: captured video, image sequences and EXR passes through Recorder

rea.restrictions: The UnityCsReference README says the C# part of the engine and editor source may be used for reference purposes only. The linked reference-only licence page allows reproducing the software for reference and says no other distribution or modification is permitted. Modifying C# or C++ source needs a commercial licence from Unity sales. The products page lists read-only source access under Enterprise.
rea.notes: Manual pages moved from docs.unity3d.com to docs.unity.com in 2025/2026; HDRP and package pages were read at version 17.0 (Unity 6.0). Some pages are from newer manual versions as noted in does. Clean-room work should treat the C# reference source as off limits. Not read (404 or redirect only): docs.unity.com class-LODGroup, occlusion-culling and progressive-lightmapper at 6000.0, the URP table of contents, the VFX Graph requirements page, and the raw UnityCsReference LICENSE.md. HDRP Ray-Traced-Reflections and Ray-Traced-Global-Illumination pages were thin; their properties come from the screen-space reflection reference page. Timeline and Cinemachine entries rest on table-of-contents pages.

entries.name: Godot Engine 4.x

licence.name: MIT (as stated in the Godot README and introduction page)

engines.name: Forward+ renderer
engines.does: Clustered forward renderer on Vulkan, Direct3D 12 or Metal with all features.

engines.name: Mobile renderer
engines.does: Single-pass forward renderer for mobile and XR on RenderingDevice.

engines.name: Compatibility renderer
engines.does: OpenGL renderer for low-end hardware and the web.

engines.name: SDFGI, VoxelGI, LightmapGI
engines.does: Three global illumination systems: real-time cascades, baked voxel grid, baked lightmaps.

engines.name: Environment and Camera Attributes
engines.does: Sky, ambient light, tonemap, SSR, SSAO, SSIL, glow, fog, adjustments, DOF and exposure.

engines.name: Shading language and VisualShader
engines.does: GLSL-like text shaders and a node graph editor.

engines.name: AnimationPlayer and AnimationTree
engines.does: Clip playback plus state machines, blend spaces and blend trees.

engines.name: Jolt Physics
engines.does: Built-in alternative 3D physics engine since 4.4.

engines.name: GPUParticles3D
engines.does: GPU-processed particles with attractors and collision.

engines.name: Compositor
engines.does: Custom compute-based passes in the 3D pipeline.

engines.name: Movie Maker mode
engines.does: Offline recording of video and audio.

capabilities.does: Forward+ renderer runs on Vulkan, Direct3D 12 or Metal through RenderingDevice and uses clustered lighting with up to 512 elements per cluster. It supports all rendering features and is the default on desktop.
capabilities.inputs: renderer choice in editor or Project Settings

capabilities.does: Mobile renderer uses single-pass forward lighting on RenderingDevice (8 omni/spot lights per mesh, 256 per view). It lacks VoxelGI, SDFGI, SSR, volumetric fog and SSAO but supports PCSS, light projectors and CompositorEffects.
capabilities.outputs: lighter 3D rendering for mobile and XR

capabilities.does: Compatibility renderer uses OpenGL, covers low-end hardware and the web, supports 2D, core 3D and SSAO, but no compute shaders or advanced lighting and GI.

SDFGI is real-time bounced light from cascaded signed distance fields that follow the camera, including off-screen geometry. Forward+ only. Needs no baking but has no dynamic occluders or dynamic emissive surfaces.
capabilities.inputs: Use Occlusion, Read Sky Light, Bounce Feedback, Cascades, Min Cell Size, Cascade 0 Distance, Max Distance, Y Scale, Energy, Normal Bias, Probe Bias; SDFGI Probe Ray Count project setting

capabilities.does: VoxelGI bakes a voxel grid of direct and indirect light inside a box node. Static meshes feed the bake; dynamic objects receive light. Forward+ only; up to 8 nodes render at once and 2 blend per pixel.
capabilities.inputs: Subdiv, Extents, VoxelGIData: Energy, Bias, Normal Bias, Propagation, Use Two Bounces, Interior, Dynamic Range

capabilities.does: LightmapGI bakes static lightmaps on the GPU from a UV2 layer. Settings cover quality level, bounces, supersampling, directional data, shadowmask, interior mode, denoiser (JNLM or OIDN) and automatic light probes for dynamic objects.
capabilities.inputs: Quality, Bounces (default 3), Directional, Shadowmask Mode, Interior, Use Denoiser, Denoiser Strength, Max Texture Size, Gen Probes Subdiv

capabilities.does: Screen-space indirect lighting (SSIL) adds bounce light from visible pixels. It complements VoxelGI, SDFGI or LightmapGI and is not a full GI solution. Forward+ only.
capabilities.inputs: Radius, Intensity, Sharpness, Normal Rejection; project settings Quality, Half Size, Adaptive Target, Blur Passes

capabilities.does: SSR reflects opaque geometry visible on screen. Forward+ only; renders at half size by default.
capabilities.inputs: Max Steps, Fade In, Fade Out, Depth Tolerance

capabilities.does: SSAO darkens creases from depth and normals with a horizon threshold, a sharpness and a light-affect control. Compatibility renderer keeps only radius and intensity (since 4.6).
capabilities.inputs: Radius, Intensity, Power, Detail, Horizon, Sharpness, Light Affect, AO Channel Affect; Quality, Half Size, Adaptive Target

capabilities.does: Environment background can be a sky resource: PanoramaSkyMaterial (HDR panorama), ProceduralSkyMaterial (colors, up to 4 suns) or PhysicalSkyMaterial (scattering parameters, 1 sun). Ambient and reflected light can be taken from the sky.
capabilities.inputs: Background mode Sky, Ambient Light mode, Sky Contribution, Reflected Light mode

capabilities.does: Tonemap modes are Linear, Reinhard, Filmic, ACES and AgX, with exposure, white point and AgX contrast. AgX keeps hue best at high brightness but is the slowest.
capabilities.inputs: Tonemap Mode, Exposure, White, AGX Contrast

capabilities.does: Adjustments after tonemapping set brightness, contrast and saturation and accept a gradient texture or a 3D LUT for color correction.
capabilities.inputs: Brightness, Contrast, Saturation, Color Correction (GradientTexture1D or Texture3D LUT)

capabilities.does: Glow adds bloom around bright pixels with intensity, strength, HDR threshold and scale, level weights, an optional glow map and blend modes Additive, Screen, Softlight, Replace and Mix.
capabilities.inputs: Intensity, Strength, Bloom, HDR Threshold, HDR Scale, Levels, Normalized, Map, Blend Mode

capabilities.does: Non-volumetric fog by camera depth or by height with adjustable curves, sun scatter toward the directional light and aerial perspective blended with the sky color.
capabilities.inputs: Depth Fog, Height Fog, Sun Scatter, Aerial Perspective

capabilities.does: Volumetric fog in a froxel buffer reacts to lights. Controls cover density, albedo, emission, GI and ambient injection, anisotropy, length, detail spread, sky effect and temporal reprojection. Forward+ only.
capabilities.inputs: Density, Albedo, Emission, Emission Energy, GI Inject, Anisotropy (-1 to 1), Length, Detail Spread, Ambient Inject, Sky Affect, Temporal Reprojection

capabilities.does: FogVolume nodes add local fog in ellipsoid, cone, cylinder, box or world shapes. A FogMaterial sets density, albedo, emission, height falloff, edge fade and a density texture; a fog shader allows animated fog.
capabilities.inputs: shape, Extents, FogMaterial: Density, Albedo, Emission, Height Falloff, Edge Fade, Density Texture

capabilities.does: Camera attributes provide far and near blur with distance, transition and amount.
capabilities.inputs: Far Blur, Near Blur: Distance, Transition, Amount

capabilities.does: CameraAttributesPhysical uses real-world units (focal length in mm, EV100) and locks the field of view; CameraAttributesPractical uses ISO-style exposure. Auto exposure has scale, sensitivity or EV limits and speed (Forward+ only).
capabilities.inputs: Exposure, Auto Exposure Scale, Min/Max Sensitivity, Min/Max Exposure Value, Speed

capabilities.does: StandardMaterial3D and ORMMaterial3D give a metallic-roughness model with albedo, metallic, specular (default 0.5) and roughness. The ORM variant reads occlusion, roughness and metallic from one packed texture.
capabilities.inputs: Albedo color and texture, Metallic, Specular, Roughness

capabilities.does: Shading can be per-pixel, per-vertex or unshaded. Diffuse mode is Burley, Lambert, Lambert Wrap or Toon; specular mode is SchlickGGX, Toon or off.
capabilities.inputs: Shading Mode, Diffuse Mode, Specular Mode, Disable Ambient Light, Disable Fog

capabilities.does: Transparency mode Alpha blends with no shadows; blend modes are Mix, Add, Subtract, Multiply and Premultiplied Alpha. Depth pre-pass and depth draw mode help sorting.
capabilities.inputs: Transparency, Blend Mode, Cull Mode, Depth Draw Mode, No Depth Test

capabilities.does: Alpha Scissor discards pixels under a threshold and casts shadows; Alpha Hash dithers the cutoff for hair; alpha antialiasing options smooth edges with MSAA.
capabilities.inputs: Alpha Scissor Threshold, Alpha Antialiasing (Alpha Edge Blend, Alpha Edge Clip), Alpha Antialiasing Edge

capabilities.does: Emission adds light to the material image; it lights nearby geometry only through VoxelGI or SDFGI.
Normal map (OpenGL red-green convention) and bent normal map for better indirect lighting and specular occlusion; an AO map reduces ambient light in crevices.
capabilities.inputs: Normal Map, Bent Normal Map, AO Map

capabilities.does: Clearcoat adds a second transparent specular layer such as car paint.
Anisotropy stretches the highlight along tangent space for hair or brushed metal.
Rim lighting approximates fabric micro-fur scattering; rim tint blends between light color and albedo.
Subsurface scattering for thin or translucent surfaces; a back-lighting option passes light to the shadowed side for leaves and ears. Forward+ only for scattering.
Refraction distorts the screen behind an object, optionally with a refraction normal texture; it forces transparency.
A height map fakes cavity depth by ray marching in the shader; no real geometry is added.
Detail mask with secondary albedo and normal textures and blend mode Mix, Add, Sub or Mul.
capabilities.inputs: Detail Mask, Detail Blend Mode, Detail Albedo, Detail Normal

capabilities.does: Triplanar mapping projects textures along X, Y and Z blended by normal, in object or world space, with UV1 and UV2 channels offset and scale.
capabilities.inputs: UV1 and UV2 Offset, Scale, Triplanar, World Triplanar

capabilities.does: Proximity fade softens where a surface meets other geometry; distance fade fades by viewer distance using pixel alpha, pixel dither or object dither.
capabilities.inputs: Proximity Fade, Distance Fade, Fade Mode

capabilities.does: Stencil modes Outline, X-Ray and Custom run through the Next Pass material (Godot 4.5 or later). A Grow option pushes vertices along normals for outlines.
Billboard modes Enabled, Y-Billboard and Particle Billboard (flipbook) with fixed on-screen size, point size and Z clip scale options.
capabilities.inputs: Billboard Mode, Billboard Keep Scale, Fixed Size, Use Point Size

capabilities.does: Decal node projects albedo, normal, ORM and emission textures onto surfaces with fades by angle and distance and a cull mask. Forward+ and Mobile only; Mobile limits 8 decals per mesh.
capabilities.inputs: Extents, Emission Energy, Modulate, Albedo Mix, Normal Fade, Upper Fade, Lower Fade, Distance Fade, Cull Mask

capabilities.does: Godot shading language resembles GLSL ES 3.0. Shader types include spatial and canvas_item (particles, sky and fog are named). Uniforms with hints, global uniforms from Project Settings and per-instance uniforms are supported.
capabilities.inputs: shader_type, uniform hints (source_color, hint_range), group_uniforms, instance uniform, global uniforms

capabilities.does: VisualShader is a node graph assigned to a ShaderMaterial, with Vertex, Fragment and Light modes, an Expression node for code, a Fresnel node and a generated-code view.
capabilities.inputs: Shader Editor, Expression node, Reroute, If, Switch, Mesh Emitter

capabilities.does: DirectionalLight3D, OmniLight3D and SpotLight3D with energy, indirect energy, volumetric fog energy, negative light, cull mask, bake mode, projector texture and physical light units.
capabilities.inputs: Color, Energy, Indirect Energy, Volumetric Fog Energy, Negative, Specular, Cull Mask, Bake Mode, Projector texture

capabilities.does: AreaLight3D gives a rectangular light controlled by area size and energy normalisation (shown in the Godot 4.7 stable docs).
Directional shadows use orthogonal or parallel-split (2 or 4 splits) shadow maps with blend splits, pancake size, fade start and maximum distance.
capabilities.inputs: Max Distance, Blend Splits, Pancake Size, Fade Start

capabilities.does: Contact-hardening soft shadows (PCSS) use light size or angular distance; shadow filter modes run from Soft Very Low to Soft Ultra.
capabilities.inputs: Angular Distance, Size, Blur, shadow filter mode

capabilities.does: Positional shadows use a four-quadrant atlas (default 4 + 4 + 16 + 64 = up to 88 lights) with bias, normal bias, caster mask and distance fade; omni lights use Dual Paraboloid or Cube mapping.
capabilities.inputs: Bias, Normal Bias, Transmittance Bias, Reverse Cull Face, Caster Mask, Positional Shadow atlas size

capabilities.does: MSAA 3D at 2x, 4x or 8x works in all renderers and smooths geometry edges only.
TAA (Forward+ only) uses frame history; it adds blur and can ghost behind moving objects.
FSR2 (Forward+) can run at native resolution as AA or upscale a lower render scale; Scaling 3D scale above 1.0 with bilinear mode gives supersampling.
FXAA and SMAA 1x are screen-space filters for Forward+ and Mobile, and can combine with TAA or FSR2 (SMAA). A screen-space roughness limiter reduces specular aliasing.
capabilities.inputs: Screen Space AA = FXAA or SMAA; Screen Space Roughness Limiter

capabilities.does: Automatic mesh LOD generated on import for glTF, .blend, Collada and FBX scenes. Switching uses a screen-space threshold in pixels (default 1) with a per-node LOD Bias.
capabilities.inputs: Rendering > Mesh LOD > LOD Change > Threshold Pixels, LOD Bias, mesh_lod_threshold

capabilities.does: The meshoptimizer library decimates meshes on import to create LOD levels. Generation can be turned off per scene or per mesh and can cause problems on skinned meshes.
CPU occlusion culling rasterizes occluders with Embree into a low-resolution buffer and tests occludee bounding boxes. OccluderInstance3D bakes or uses Quad, Box, Sphere, Polygon or Array occluders.
capabilities.inputs: Use Occlusion Culling, Bake > Simplification, Bake > Cull Mask, BVH Build Quality, Occlusion Rays Per Thread

capabilities.does: MultiMeshInstance3D draws many copies of a mesh; the editor Populate Surface tool scatters instances over a surface with random rotation, tilt and scale.
capabilities.inputs: Target Surface, Source Mesh, Mesh Up Axis, Random Rotation, Random Tilt, Random Scale, Amount

capabilities.does: The Compositor resource on WorldEnvironment or Camera3D holds CompositorEffect scripts that run compute shaders at a chosen stage of the 3D pipeline. Mobile and Forward+ only.

GPUParticles3D processes particles on the GPU with custom particle shaders; CPUParticles3D runs on older hardware with fewer options. Particle attractors (box, sphere, vector field) and collision nodes (box, sphere, SDF, heightfield) add forces and contacts.
capabilities.inputs: GPUParticles3D, CPUParticles3D, process material, attractors, collision nodes

capabilities.does: Jolt Physics is an alternative 3D physics engine since Godot 4.4 and the default for new projects. It is selected under Physics > 3D > Physics Engine and has settings for margins, stabilisation and sleeping.
capabilities.inputs: Physics > 3D > Physics Engine = Jolt Physics, Collision Margin Fraction, Baumgarte Stabilization Factor, Temporary Memory Buffer Size

capabilities.does: Jolt supports PinJoint3D, HingeJoint3D, SliderJoint3D, ConeTwistJoint3D and Generic6DOFJoint3D, with many soft-limit properties unsupported.
SoftBody3D works with Area3D under Jolt, including overlap signals for soft bodies.

AnimationNodeStateMachine in an AnimationTree switches states by transition with switch mode (Immediate, Sync, At End), crossfade time and curve, priority and advance by condition or expression. travel() finds a path with A*.
capabilities.inputs: Switch Mode, Xfade Time, Xfade Curve, Reset, Priority, Advance Mode, Advance Condition, Advance Expression

capabilities.does: Blend tree nodes Blend2, Blend3, OneShot, TimeScale and Transition, plus BlendSpace1D and BlendSpace2D, combine clips from an AnimationPlayer, with filters for layering.
A skeleton bone can be set as the root motion track; the tree then returns position, rotation and scale deltas to drive character movement, for example through move_and_slide.

Movie Maker mode records non-real-time video and audio to OGV, AVI (MJPEG) or a PNG sequence with WAV audio, or to a custom MovieWriter. Settings include FPS, quality, speaker mode; command line flags set file, resolution, FPS and frame count.
glTF 2.0 (.gltf and .glb) is the recommended 3D import format. A .blend file is imported by calling Blender to export glTF first (Blender 3.0 or later).
FBX import uses ufbx by default from Godot 4.3; FBX2glTF is optional. Collada (older) and OBJ (no skeletons or PBR) are also read.
GridMap places meshes from a MeshLibrary on a grid, with per-tile collision shapes and navigation regions.

GDScript is an indentation-based, gradually typed language for Godot with signals, @export annotations, await coroutines, lambdas, single inheritance, class_name, enums, typed Array and Dictionary, match with guards and @tool scripts.
C# is shown beside GDScript in the introduction; C++ is mentioned for engine modules.

scripting: GDExtension (named on the Movie Maker page)
outcomes: interactive scenes exported to desktop, mobile, web and consoles
offline video from Movie Maker mode

rea.restrictions: MIT licence per README; full licence text not read.
rea.notes: Documentation pages read are the stable branch, which showed Godot 4.7 content on the environment, lighting and AA pages. The GDExtension docs index and what_is_gdextension page returned 404, so GDExtension appears only as named on the Movie Maker page. Several pages were thin: MultiMesh (no per-instance data), Compositor (callback list not shown), AnimationTree (no IK).

entries.name: Bevy

licence.name: MIT or Apache-2.0, at the user's choice (README)

engines.name: Bevy ECS
engines.does: Data-driven entity component system at the center of the engine.

engines.name: bevy_pbr / bevy_light
engines.does: PBR materials, lights, shadows, fog, atmosphere, probes, decals and experimental meshlets.

engines.name: bevy_core_pipeline
engines.does: Core 2D and 3D pipelines, prepass, OIT, tonemapping and skybox.

engines.name: bevy_render
engines.does: wgpu-based render backend with phases, extraction, storage buffers and GPU occlusion culling.

engines.name: bevy_post_process and bevy_anti_alias
engines.does: Bloom, DOF, motion blur, chromatic aberration; TAA, FXAA, SMAA.

engines.name: bevy_animation
engines.does: Clips, players, animation graph and transitions.

engines.name: bevy_gltf
engines.does: glTF 2.0 loader.

engines.name: Solari
engines.does: Experimental raytraced lighting.

capabilities.does: StandardMaterial is the PBR material: base color, metallic (0 to 1), perceptual roughness and a non-metal reflectance control. Lighting sets up through PbrPlugin and MaterialPlugin.
A thin top layer with its own roughness and normal texture, for painted surfaces. Optional textures need a cargo feature.
Stretches specular highlights along a direction, with strength, rotation and texture controls.

Specular transmission refracts the scene behind a surface and needs ScreenSpaceTransmission on the camera. Thickness, index of refraction (default 1.5) and attenuation distance and color shape the result.
Diffuse transmission scatters light through a material, as in leaves or wax, at lower cost than specular transmission.
Normal map needs UVs, tangents and normals on the mesh; a flip option handles DirectX-style maps. An occlusion texture darkens crevices.
A grayscale depth map shifts texture coordinates for apparent depth, tuned by a depth scale, a mapping method and a maximum layer count.
Emissive color and texture, with an exposure weight so camera exposure can change its strength. Bright values can drive bloom.
Alpha mode sets how the base color alpha is used; the default is opaque. A uv_transform, cull mode, double_sided, depth_bias and an unlit flag are also on the material.
capabilities.inputs: alpha_mode, uv_transform, cull_mode, double_sided, depth_bias, unlit, fog_enabled

capabilities.does: ExtendedMaterial extends a base material with extra shaders and data through a MaterialExtension; MaterialPlugin registers a new Material type.

PointLight, SpotLight and DirectionalLight in bevy::light, plus AmbientLight and GlobalAmbientLight. Texture masks (DirectionalLightTexture, PointLightTexture, SpotLightTexture) shape light intensity like cookies.
RectLight is a rectangular area light.
CascadeShadowConfig sets how cascaded shadow maps split the view for directional lights, built with CascadeShadowConfigBuilder.
ShadowFilteringMethod on a camera controls how shadow edges are filtered. NotShadowCaster and NotShadowReceiver opt meshes out. ContactShadows adds screen-space ray-marched contact shadows.

Atmosphere simulates a planet sky around an entity: inner and outer radius, ground albedo and a ScatteringMedium asset (Earth or Mars presets). Cameras carry AtmosphereSettings and can use LookupTexture or Raymarched modes; a SunDisk shapes the solar disk.

EnvironmentMapLight is a pair of cubemaps for the surroundings; GeneratedEnvironmentMapLight filters one at runtime; AtmosphereEnvironmentMapLight lets the atmosphere supply reflections and ambient light. Skybox shows a cubemap.
LightProbe marks a cuboid region giving global illumination; IrradianceVolume provides voxel indirect lighting data.
The Lightmap component applies baked indirect diffuse lighting to a mesh; lightmap_exposure on the material sets its brightness.
VolumetricFog on a camera, VolumetricLight on a shadow-casting directional light, and FogVolume cube regions give fog and light shafts. DistanceFog configures distance fog on StandardMaterial meshes.
ScreenSpaceAmbientOcclusion is a camera component that applies SSAO.
ScreenSpaceReflections is a camera component that enables screen-space reflections.
ClusteredDecal projects a decal onto surfaces within its bounds; ClusteredDecalPlugin adds the support.
Bloom module in bevy::post_process, added by PostProcessPlugin.
Depth of field module simulates camera focus as a postprocessing effect.
Per-object, per-pixel motion blur.
PostProcessPlugin adds chromatic aberration along with bloom, motion blur and depth of field. An auto_exposure module is also listed.
A tonemapping module in the core pipeline; the tonemapping_luts cargo feature supplies lookup tables that some methods need, otherwise output may render pink.
bevy::anti_alias holds temporal anti-aliasing (taa), FXAA, SMAA and contrast adaptive sharpening modules, all added by AntiAliasPlugin, which also offers optional DLSS support.
Order independent transparency for 3D, enabled by OrderIndependentTransparencyPlugin.
A prepass renders depth, normal and motion vector textures before the main pass. A deferred module and a per-material deferred lighting pass id also exist.

Experimental meshlet renderer for high-poly meshes: MeshletMesh splits a mesh into small triangle clusters (MeshletMesh::from_mesh), drawn as MeshletMesh3d through MeshletPlugin. Needs the meshlet cargo feature.
Experimental Solari plugin set for raytraced lighting, with pathtracer and realtime submodules; needs the bevy_solari cargo feature.
The Bevy site lists a Render Graph among its engine features, next to a 2D renderer and a 3D renderer. The page gives no further detail.

In bevy::render, the render phase module queues, prepares, sorts and draws entities; Core2d and Core3d (bevy::core_pipeline) are schedule labels for the 2D and 3D pipelines; extraction copies main-world data to the render world.

Clustered forward rendering: the cluster module groups objects (point lights, spot lights, decals, light probes) into spatial clusters. ClusterConfig sets the strategy, ClusterZConfig the depth slicing and ClusterFarZMode the far plane handling.
A render module provides GPU occlusion culling.

bevy::render::batching has separate paths for GPU preprocessing and for no GPU preprocessing. NoAutomaticBatching on a mesh entity opts it out of automatic batching. Instancing is not named on the page.
GpuMeshPreprocessPlugin builds mesh uniforms on the GPU.
The default rendering backend is wgpu. Cargo features webgpu and webgl2 target Wasm builds; webgpu overrides webgl2. Linux windowing features are wayland and x11.
capabilities.inputs: RenderPlugin, features webgpu, webgl2, wayland, x11

capabilities.does: A mip_generation module downsamples textures into mipmap levels.

AnimationClip holds curves and target ids; AnimationPlayer plays them; AnimatedBy links animated entities to the player; glTF curves load through gltf_curves. Animation events can trigger observers during playback.
The animation graph module blends animations together and a transition module handles transitions.

GltfPlugin loads glTF 2.0 with GltfAssetLabel for scenes and parts, loader settings, name and extras components, and morph target names. Extensions include lights_punctual, anisotropy, clearcoat, emissive_strength, ior, specular, transmission, unlit, volume and texture_transform. Draco, meshopt, dispersion, iridescence and sheen are not supported.
Cargo features add KTX2 (with zstd decoding), Basis Universal, DDS, EXR and HDR texture loading.
capabilities.inputs: features ktx2, zstd_rust, basis-universal, dds, exr, hdr

capabilities.does: Bevy ECS is a data-oriented Entity Component System that runs logic in parallel where possible; the engine is modular so parts can be replaced.

rea.restrictions: Dual MIT or Apache-2.0 per README; licence texts not read.
rea.notes: API pages are docs.rs latest, which showed Bevy 0.20.1 on the light, gltf and meshlet pages.

entries.verified: 2026-11-02, how: docs.rs API pages and the repository README read via WebFetch

entries.name: Filament

licence.name: Apache-2.0 (README)

engines.name: Material system
engines.does: PBR shading models lit, subsurface, cloth, unlit and specularGlossiness compiled from .mat files.

engines.name: matc
engines.does: Material compiler that turns .mat files into material packages.

engines.name: cmgen
engines.does: Command-line generator for prefiltered IBL cubemaps and spherical harmonics.

engines.name: gltfio
engines.does: glTF loader library producing Filament objects.

engines.name: Post-processing options
engines.does: Bloom, DOF, SSAO, SSR, TAA, MSAA, dynamic resolution, fog, vignette.

capabilities.does: Standard material model with baseColor, metallic, perceptual roughness (squared to alpha, clamped near 0.089), reflectance (dielectric F0 = 0.16 x reflectance squared), emissive and per-pixel ambient occlusion.
capabilities.inputs: baseColor, metallic [0..1], roughness, reflectance [0..1], emissive, ambientOcclusion

capabilities.does: Second specular layer with fixed index of refraction 1.5 (F0 of 4 percent). Controlled by strength and its own roughness; a material flag controls whether the coat changes the base IOR.
Anisotropic specular with a value from -1 to 1: positive stretches along the tangent, negative along the bitangent. Tangent and bitangent roughness derive from roughness and anisotropy.
Cloth shading model with a sheen color for two-tone fabric and a subsurface tint. It omits metallic and reflectance. The lit model also lists sheenColor and sheenRoughness.

Subsurface shading model (shadingModel subsurface) approximates light passing through thin surfaces with a thickness, a tint color and a power term. The design document marks its theory section as unfinished.
The lit model lists iridescence properties for thin-film color shifts.
Refraction is switched on by refractionMode (none, cubemap, screenspace) and refractionType (solid, thin). Properties set index of refraction, transmission, absorption and thickness.
capabilities.inputs: refractionMode, refractionType, ior (1.5), transmission (1.0), absorption, thickness, microThickness

capabilities.does: Dispersion property splits refracted light by wavelength; not available with refractionType thin.

Blending modes opaque, transparent, fade, add, masked, multiply, screen and custom (blendFunction with srcRGB, srcA, dstRGB, dstA). Transparency can use two passes. Premultiplied alpha is used for transparent blending.
Masked blending discards pixels below a threshold; alphaToCoverage can smooth edges under MSAA.
Material outputs normal, bentNormal and clearCoatNormal. The design document compares reoriented normal blending (accurate) with UDN blending (cheaper).
Specular anti-aliasing keeps highlights from breaking up on glossy surfaces at distance.

Materials are written in .mat files with a material() function and compiled by the matc tool. The shader API offers getUV0() and getWorldPosition(), and prepareMaterial() must be called before material() returns. Attributes, up to 5 interpolants and vertex domains are declared.
capabilities.inputs: requires, variables, vertexDomain (object, world, view, device), interpolation, featureLevel

capabilities.does: Directional lights use illuminance in lux; point and spot lights use luminous power in lumens, with inner and outer spot cone angles; photometric lights use candela; image lights use cd/m2.
The direct lighting section covers area lights, with luminous power in lumens.

IBL types are distant and local light probes, planar reflections and screen-space reflections. Diffuse uses an irradiance cubemap or 2 or 3 bands of spherical harmonics; specular uses a roughness-indexed prefiltered cubemap and a DFG lookup table.
capabilities.inputs: prefiltered cubemap, SH coefficients (4 or 9), DFG LUT

capabilities.does: cmgen turns an equirectangular or cross cubemap (PNG, HDR, PSD, EXR) into a roughness-prefiltered cubemap, spherical harmonics and a skybox. Outputs cubemap, equirect, octahedron or KTX in several formats.
README lists several shadow techniques: cascaded shadows, contact shadows, transparent shadows and colored penumbra.
Variance shadow maps (VSM) and soft shadow (PCSS-style) options control light bleed, anisotropy, mipmapping and penumbra size.
capabilities.inputs: VsmShadowOptions: anisotropy, mipmapping, msaaSamples, lightBleedReduction (0.15); SoftShadowOptions: penumbraScale, penumbraRatioScale, maxPenumbraRatio, maxSearchRadius

capabilities.does: Screen-space cone tracing adds contact shadows as part of the ambient occlusion options.
capabilities.inputs: ssct: lightConeRad, shadowDistance, contactDistanceMax, intensity, lightDirection, depthBias, depthSlopeBias, sampleCount, rayCount

capabilities.does: Screen-space ambient occlusion with SAO or GTAO types, optional bent normals and bilateral filtering. The design document describes micro, medium and large-scale occlusion combined by minimum.
capabilities.inputs: aoType (SAO, GTAO), radius (0.3), power, bias, resolution (0.5), intensity, bilateralThreshold, quality, bentNormals

capabilities.does: Materials can turn on multi-bounce ambient occlusion and specular ambient occlusion; the design document gives a specular AO formula and a horizon occlusion term for indirect specular.
Screen-space reflections with thickness, bias, maximum distance and stride; materials choose reflections default or screenspace.
capabilities.inputs: thickness (0.1), bias (0.01), maxDistance (3.0), stride (2.0), material reflections

capabilities.does: HDR bloom with strength, levels, resolution, blend mode, threshold, highlight and an optional lens dirt texture.
capabilities.inputs: strength (0.10), levels (6), resolution (384), blendMode (ADD), threshold, highlight (1000), dirt, dirtStrength

capabilities.does: Bloom options include screen-space lens flare with starburst, ghosts and halo controls.
capabilities.inputs: lensFlare, starburst, ghostCount (4), ghostSpacing, ghostThreshold, haloThickness, haloRadius, haloThreshold

capabilities.does: Bloom options hold a chromatic aberration amount for color fringing.
Depth-of-field bokeh with circle-of-confusion scale, a median or other filter, ring counts for foreground, background and fast gather, and maximum blur size.
capabilities.inputs: cocScale, cocAspectRatio, maxApertureDiameter, filter (MEDIAN), foregroundRingCount, backgroundRingCount, maxForegroundCOC, maxBackgroundCOC

capabilities.does: Vignette with mid point, roundness, feather and color.

Physically based camera with aperture in f-stops, shutter speed and ISO giving EV100; exposure compensation, and automatic exposure by log-luminance or histogram with spot, center-weighted and matrix metering.
capabilities.inputs: aperture N, shutter t, sensitivity S, EV100

capabilities.does: README lists several tone mappers and color grading in the post-processing chain.
Temporal anti-aliasing with feedback, sharpness, LOD bias, jitter pattern, history filtering, anti-flicker, disocclusion handling and optional upscaling.
capabilities.inputs: feedback (0.12), sharpness, lodBias (-1), upscaling, jitterPattern (HALTON_23_X16), preventFlickering, historyReprojection, depthDisocclusion

capabilities.does: MSAA option with sample count (default 4) and a custom resolve flag.
FXAA is listed among the anti-aliasing options in the README.
Dynamic resolution scales the render target between a minimum and maximum, with sharpness and quality settings; README mentions AMD FSR support.

Fog options give a height-falloff exponential fog with density, start distance, cut-off distance, maximum opacity, in-scattering start and size and an option to take color from the IBL or a sky texture.
capabilities.inputs: distance, cutOffDistance, maximumOpacity, height, heightFalloff, color, density, inScatteringStart, inScatteringSize, fogColorFromIbl

capabilities.does: The light path section of the design document covers clustered forward rendering.
Backends listed in the README are OpenGL, OpenGL ES, Metal, Vulkan, WebGPU and WebGL 2.0, used from C++, Java/JNI or JavaScript.
View options include a stereoscopic option block with an enabled flag.
A motion vector option block with an enabled flag supports temporal effects.

gltfio reads glTF and glb and creates Filament objects. A MaterialProvider is either UbershaderProvider (precompiled .uberz) or JitShaderProvider (runtime build with filamat); a TextureProvider is StbProvider (PNG, JPEG) or Ktx2Provider (BasisU).
README lists Draco compression among supported glTF extensions.
README lists glTF transform, morph and skin animation.
The gltfio Ktx2Provider reads KTX2 textures through BasisU.

outcomes: real-time PBR viewers and apps on Android, iOS, desktop and web

entries.name: bgfx

licence.name: BSD-2-Clause (README)

engines.name: Renderer backends
engines.does: Direct3D, Metal, OpenGL, OpenGL ES, Vulkan, WebGL and WebGPU back ends behind one API.

engines.name: shaderc
engines.does: Shader compiler for the bgfx shader language.

engines.name: texturec
engines.does: Texture converter and cubemap filter.

engines.name: geometryc
engines.does: OBJ and glTF mesh converter.

capabilities.does: One API over Direct3D 11 and 12, Metal, OpenGL 4.3+, OpenGL ES 3.0+, Vulkan, WebGL 2.0 and WebGPU (Dawn Native only), plus GNM for licensed PS4 developers. getSupportedRenderers and getRendererType report the choice.
Views are ordered render passes. Each view has a name, rect, scissor, clear, mode, frame buffer, transform and order; draw submissions target a view id.
capabilities.inputs: setViewName, setViewRect, setViewScissor, setViewClear, setViewMode, setViewFrameBuffer, setViewTransform, setViewOrder

capabilities.does: An Encoder collects draw state from several threads: begin and end, then setState, setTransform, setUniform, setTexture, buffers, setInstanceCount and submit. The multithreaded renderer can be disabled with BGFX_CONFIG_MULTITHREADED=0.
capabilities.inputs: bgfx::begin, setState, setStencil, setScissor, submit, BGFX_CONFIG_MULTITHREADED

capabilities.does: shaderc compiles bgfx shader language (GLSL-based, with a C preprocessor) to HLSL, GLSL, GLSL ES, Metal, PSSL or SPIR-V for vertex, fragment or compute stages. Inputs and outputs are declared in varying.def.sc.
texturec converts BMP, DDS, EXR, GIF, JPG, HDR, KTX, PNG, PSD, PVR and TGA to DDS, EXR, HDR, KTX or PNG in formats such as BC1 to BC5 or ETC1, with a quality setting, mipmaps and normal-map mode.
texturec handles equirectangular and cross-strip cubemap input and can filter cubemaps with a lighting model (Phong, PhongBrdf, Blinn, BlinnBrdf or GGX).
geometryc converts Wavefront OBJ and glTF 2.0 meshes into a bgfx-optimized format, with scaling, winding, UV flip, packed normals and UVs, tangent and barycentric generation and index compression.
Per-instance data (i_data attributes in shaders) is allocated in instance data buffers and bound with setInstanceDataBuffer.
Frame buffers are created from textures and attached to a view for off-screen rendering; a texture can be fetched from a frame buffer.
Occlusion queries return a visibility result for a draw, and setCondition makes a later draw conditional on it.
Shaders can be compiled for the compute stage, and an indirect buffer type exists for GPU-driven draws; blit copies between textures.
Static, dynamic and transient vertex and index buffers, with vertex layouts, update calls and transient allocation per frame.
Screenshot request writes the rendered frame; readTexture reads texture data back.
C and C++ API with community bindings listed in the README for Beef, C#, C3, Python, D, Go, Haskell, LWJGL3, Java, Lua, Nim, Pascal, Rust, Swift and Zig.
Debug text printing and debug flags are built in; RenderDoc integrates with the DX11 and OpenGL renderers, loaded from renderdoc.dll in the working directory (F11 captures a frame).

outcomes: cross-platform renderers inside a custom engine or framework

rea.restrictions: BSD-2-Clause per README; licence text not read.
rea.notes: bgfx is a rendering layer, not a full renderer; it has no PBR or post-process stack of its own beyond what examples show.

entries.name: Diligent Engine

licence.name: Apache-2.0 (README); Metal backend for commercial clients only per DiligentCore page

engines.name: DiligentCore
engines.does: Graphics API abstraction with D3D, Vulkan, OpenGL and WebGPU back ends.

engines.name: DiligentTools
engines.does: Texture and asset loaders, ImGui support, render state notation parser and packager.

engines.name: DiligentFX
engines.does: High-level rendering components: PBR, shadows, post-processing, Hydrogent.

engines.name: DiligentSamples
engines.does: Tutorials and demo applications.

capabilities.does: Core runs on Direct3D 11 and 12, OpenGL, OpenGL ES, Vulkan and WebGPU; the README also lists Metal, but the Core page says the Metal backend is for commercial clients only. Platforms include Windows, UWP, Linux, Android, macOS, iOS, tvOS and Web.
Shader variables are grouped as static, mutable or dynamic. Mutable and dynamic ones are bound through Shader Resource Binding objects, by name through a resource mapping, or as immutable samplers.
capabilities.inputs: Shader Resource Binding, resource mapping, immutable samplers

capabilities.does: One monolithic pipeline state object holds all shader stages and render states, for graphics and compute pipelines. States can be created from JSON render state notation and packed by a Render State Packager.
capabilities.inputs: Pipeline State Object, render state notation, Render State Packager

capabilities.does: Immediate and deferred contexts, created at engine initialization, allow multithreaded command recording. Resource state transitions can be automatic or explicit.

Shaders come as HLSL, GLSL, verbatim GLSL or Metal Shading Language source, or as bytecode. HLSL is converted to GLSL for OpenGL and compiled to SPIR-V for Vulkan using glslang, SPIRV-Cross and DirectXShaderCompiler. WGSL and DXBC are also named in the README.
README lists ray tracing, mesh shaders, variable rate shading, bindless resources and sparse resources as advanced features. The Core page does not describe them.
capabilities.outputs: hardware ray tracing and related features

capabilities.does: DiligentFX has a physically based renderer with image-based lighting, in its PBR folder.
A glTF 2.0 loader lives in DiligentTools AssetLoader and feeds the PBR renderer.
Hydrogent is a Hydra render delegate for Diligent Engine, used by the USD Viewer sample.
Shadows are a DiligentFX component with a sample image; the page does not state the technique.
Screen-space ambient occlusion post-process effect.
Screen-space reflections post-process effect.
Depth of field post-process that blurs parts of the image outside the focal plane.
Bloom post-process effect adding glow around bright areas.
Temporal anti-aliasing post-process using data from previous frames.
Shader utilities for tone mapping under Shaders/PostProcess/ToneMapping.
Epipolar light scattering produces light shafts (god rays).

outcomes: cross-API real-time renderers inside custom applications

rea.restrictions: Apache-2.0 per README; licence text not read.
rea.notes: Ray tracing, mesh shaders, VRS and bindless are named in the main README but not described on the Core page.

entries.name: wgpu

licence.name: Apache-2.0 or MIT (README)

engines.name: wgpu
engines.does: Main Rust API following WebGPU.

engines.name: naga
engines.does: Shader translation library for WGSL, SPIR-V, GLSL, MSL and HLSL.

engines.name: wgpu-native
engines.does: C bindings for wgpu.

capabilities.does: Native backends are Vulkan, Metal, D3D12 and OpenGL. On wasm it targets WebGL2 or the browser WebGPU. Vulkan needs MoltenVK on Apple platforms; GL ES on some systems needs ANGLE. Backends are cargo features.
capabilities.inputs: features dx12, metal, vulkan, gles, webgpu, angle, vulkan-portability, webgl
capabilities.outputs: one API over native and web back ends

capabilities.does: wgpu implements the WebGPU standard as a native Rust library, and the README names it as the base of WebGPU support in Firefox, Servo and Deno. Coordinate conventions follow D3D and Metal, with depth in [0, 1].

Instance creates Adapters, Devices and Surfaces; Queue submits work; CommandEncoder records RenderPass and ComputePass; Buffer, Texture, TextureView, Sampler, BindGroup and ShaderModule are the resources. Handles are reference-counted.
capabilities.inputs: Instance, Adapter, Device, Queue, Surface, CommandEncoder, BindGroup

capabilities.does: ComputePipeline and ComputePass run compute work alongside RenderPipeline and RenderPass graphics work.
Shaders are written in WGSL, enabled by default. SPIR-V, GLSL and naga IR inputs are optional cargo features. On WebGPU, non-WGSL shaders are converted automatically.

Naga reads SPIR-V, WGSL and GLSL (440+, Vulkan semantics) and writes SPIR-V, MSL, HLSL (Shader Model 5.0+), GLSL (330+ and ES 300+), WGSL and DOT. It validates shaders and has a command-line tool for conversion.
naga-cli validates one file or converts between two formats, such as SPIR-V to Metal or WGSL to GLSL, can dump the IR and sets options like the GLSL profile.
SurfaceConfiguration color_space selects HDR and wide-gamut output; the default Auto never picks HDR.
Ray tracing and mesh shading are available but experimental, and misuse may cause undefined behavior.
capabilities.outputs: ray tracing and mesh shader access

capabilities.does: A Features type lists optional device capabilities (PASSTHROUGH_SHADERS is one example on the page). Immediate data is set with set_immediates.
wgpu-native provides C bindings, with a list of libraries for other languages; the README also points C++ developers to the Learn WebGPU resource.
capabilities.outputs: wgpu from C and other languages

capabilities.does: A noop backend performs no computation, for testing. Optional cargo flags include serde, trace, counters and static-dxc. The workspace includes wgpu-info and a CTS runner.

outcomes: native and web GPU applications in Rust
WebGPU in Firefox, Servo and Deno

rea.restrictions: Dual Apache-2.0 and MIT per README; licence texts not read.
rea.notes: docs.rs latest page read; MSRV 1.87 stated there.

entries.name: Dawn

licence.name: BSD 3-Clause (landing page); not an officially supported Google product

engines.name: dawn_native
engines.does: Native WebGPU implementation with frontend validation and D3D12, Metal, Vulkan and OpenGL backends.

engines.name: dawn_wire
engines.does: Client-server serialization of WebGPU commands.

engines.name: Tint
engines.does: WGSL compiler with SPIR-V, HLSL, GLSL and MSL writers.

capabilities.does: Dawn implements webgpu.h, a one-to-one mapping of the WebGPU IDL, and is the WebGPU implementation inside Chromium. Ships C/C++ headers and a C++ wrapper.
dawn::native translates WebGPU to D3D12, Metal, Vulkan and OpenGL. A frontend does state tracking and validation; per-API backend folders do the translation. SPIR-V is checked with spirv-val.
dawn::wire is a client-server layer for sandboxed apps: the client serializes WebGPU commands, the server validates and calls dawn_native, and returns messages for callbacks.
dawn_native and dawn_wire fill a dawnProcTable of function pointers; the dawn_proc library forwards calls so native or wire can be chosen at runtime.

Tint compiles WGSL. Readers parse WGSL and SPIR-V into a Program; writers emit SPIR-V, WGSL, HLSL, GLSL and MSL; a Resolver validates semantics; an Inspector extracts data such as specialization constants.
capabilities.inputs: WGSL or SPIR-V input; target language

capabilities.does: Tint transforms clone a valid Program, change it and return a new valid Program; examples named are Vertex Pulling and Robust Buffer Access.

PixelLocalStorage gives shaders per-pixel data that lasts a render pass, in tile storage on tiler GPUs or by fragment interlock plus read-write storage textures elsewhere. Coherent and non-coherent modes exist; the shader uses var<pixel_local>.

Subgroup matrix types spread a matrix across a subgroup for machine-learning style matrix multiplies, using the chromium_experimental_subgroup_matrix WGSL extension. Vulkan uses cooperative matrix; Metal needs Apple7+; Direct3D is not supported.
One command issues many indirect draws with a count read from a buffer, for GPU-driven rendering. Needs the MultiDrawIndirect feature and an Indirect-usage buffer.
SharedTextureMemory imports texture memory allocated outside the API (AHardwareBuffer, DMA-buf, DXGI handles, IOSurface and others) with BeginAccess, EndAccess and shared fences for synchronization.

The features folder holds 37 documents on Dawn features and extensions, including multi_planar_formats, framebuffer_fetch, transient_attachments, static_samplers, timestamp_query_inside_passes, shared_buffer_memory, shared_fence and host_mapped_pointer.
API headers, the C++ wrapper, proc tables and parts of the wire code are generated from dawn.json with Jinja2 templates in generator/.
The repository documents a standalone WebGPU CTS runner and rolling the CTS; tests are split into end-to-end, unit, white-box and benchmark groups.

rea.restrictions: BSD 3-Clause per the landing page; licence text not read.
rea.notes: Landing page lists D3D12, Metal, Vulkan and OpenGL; bgfx README mentions Dawn Native as its WebGPU route. The Tint README and a features.md page returned 404 and were not used.
