entries.name: Panda3D

licence.name: Modified BSD

engines.name: Scene graph
engines.does: Tree (really a directed acyclic graph) of nodes with transforms, render state and effects; NodePath objects address one place in it and carry per-instance data.

engines.name: Render pipeline
engines.does: GraphicsEngine, GraphicsPipe, GraphicsStateGuardian and GraphicsOutput classes create windows and offscreen buffers and draw display regions; an optional multithreaded pipeline overlaps stages.

engines.name: Shader generator
engines.does: Builds shaders on the fly for nodes marked for automatic shading, so lighting, maps and shadows work without hand-written shader code.

engines.name: Collision system
engines.does: Built-in solid-based collision tests run by a traverser with handler objects; separate from the Bullet integration.

engines.name: Bullet integration
engines.does: Python bindings to the Bullet library for rigid bodies, soft bodies, vehicles and a kinematic character controller.

engines.name: Particle system
engines.does: Effects built from a factory, an emitter and a renderer, using the physics module for forces.

engines.name: PStats
engines.does: Profiler with a separate viewer program that graphs per-frame time and counters.

capabilities.does: Calling setShaderAuto on a node (or on render for the whole scene) makes the engine generate shaders that handle lights, materials, textures, vertex colours and fog for that subtree. An explicit setShader on a child overrides it.
capabilities.outputs: per-pixel lit, textured geometry from fixed-function style state

capabilities.does: Normal maps assigned to a texture stage in the modelling tool are picked up by the shader generator and used for per-pixel lighting once automatic shading is on.
capabilities.inputs: normal map on a texture stage; setShaderAuto()

capabilities.does: Gloss maps scale specular strength and glow maps add self-lit areas; both come from texture stages set in the modelling program and are applied by the shader generator.
capabilities.inputs: gloss map and glow map texture stages

capabilities.does: Skinning can run on the GPU when two Config.prc variables are set: hardware-animated-vertices true and basic-shaders-only false. The shader generator then uses up to four joint weights per vertex and up to 120 active joints.

GLSL compute shaders load with Shader.load_compute and run through a ComputeNode with add_dispatch(x, y, z) workgroup counts, or through GraphicsEngine.dispatch_compute for a one-off. They read and write texture images and need OpenGL 4.3 class hardware.
capabilities.inputs: Shader.load_compute(SL_GLSL, file); ComputeNode.add_dispatch(x, y, z); set_shader_input
capabilities.outputs: texture images written by the GPU

capabilities.does: Textures bound to compute shaders appear as image2D, read with imageLoad and written with imageStore. They need a sized format such as F_rgba8, expose only mip level 0, and allow atomics only on F_r32i. Memory barriers between shaders are automatic.
capabilities.inputs: Texture.F_rgba8 and other sized formats; clearImage; setClearColor

capabilities.does: Four light classes: PointLight (position and attenuation matter), DirectionalLight (orientation only, default direction +Y), AmbientLight (flat fill) and Spotlight (cone from a PerspectiveLens). Colour defaults to white and may exceed 1 for bright lights.
capabilities.inputs: light.color (r,g,b,a); attenuation (constant, linear, quadratic) default (1,0,0); setColorTemperature in kelvin
capabilities.outputs: lights attached to the scene graph and enabled per subtree with setLight

capabilities.does: Shadow casting is switched on per light with setShadowCaster(True, width, height); receivers need the shader generator. The light lens near/far and, for directional lights, film size tune the depth range, and setDepthOffset(1) reduces self-shadowing on thin geometry.
capabilities.inputs: setShadowCaster(flag, xsize, ysize); lens setNearFar; setFilmSize; setDepthOffset

capabilities.does: LightRampAttrib replaces the two colour clamps in lighting with tone-mapping curves: makeHdr0, makeHdr1 and makeHdr2 map 0 to infinity into 0 to 1 with decreasing contrast. Needs per-pixel lighting from the shader generator.
Light ramps can quantise diffuse light into bands: makeSingleThreshold(t0, l0) and makeDoubleThreshold(t0, l0, t1, l1) set threshold and level pairs. Applies to directional lights only.
capabilities.inputs: LightRampAttrib.makeSingleThreshold(t0, l0); makeDoubleThreshold(t0, l0, t1, l1)

capabilities.does: CommonFilters wraps a set of ready post-process passes with set and del methods: bloom, cartoon ink, volumetric lighting, inversion, blur/sharpen, ambient occlusion, gamma, sRGB encode, HDR, exposure and MSAA.
capabilities.inputs: CommonFilters(win, cam); setBloom, setCartoonInk, setVolumetricLighting, setInverted, setBlurSharpen, setAmbientOcclusion, setGammaAdjust, setSrgbEncode, setHighDynamicRange, setExposureAdjust

capabilities.does: The bloom filter takes bright pixels above a trigger range, desaturates them and blurs them back onto the image.
capabilities.inputs: blend (0.3,0.4,0.3,0.0), mintrigger 0.6, maxtrigger 1.0, desat 0.6, intensity 1.0, size "medium"

capabilities.does: Screen-space ambient occlusion filter with sample count, radius, strength and falloff controls.
Radial light-shaft filter driven by a caster node: samples along the screen-space ray towards the light.
Edge-detection filter that draws ink outlines at silhouettes and depth steps.
CommonFilters can enable multisample anti-aliasing for the filtered render (added in 1.10.13).

FilterManager redirects scene rendering into textures (renderSceneInto with colortex, depthtex, auxtex) and builds intermediate quads (renderQuadInto with mul, div, align) so custom multi-stage full-screen shader passes can be chained.
capabilities.inputs: FilterManager(win, cam); renderSceneInto; renderQuadInto; quad.setShader; setShaderInput; AuxBitplaneAttrib

capabilities.does: makeCubeMap on a window creates six cameras and a cube texture at a point; applied with a world cube-map texgen it gives live reflections. Near/far planes limit cost and the buffer can be paused.
capabilities.inputs: window.makeCubeMap(name, size, rig, cameraMask, toRam); setTexGen(stage, MWorldCubeMap); buffer.setActive

capabilities.does: The Moguri simplepbr add-on gives a forward-rendered metal-roughness PBR shader for all Panda3D light types, with normal, emission and occlusion maps, diffuse and specular IBL, filmic tone mapping with an optional LUT, and basic shadows for directional lights and spotlights.
capabilities.outputs: PBR-shaded scenes on OpenGL 2.1 or newer

capabilities.does: The panda3d-gltf add-on loads glTF 2.0 and binary glTF through a Python file loader and supports KHR_lights_punctual and BLENDER_physics. Options include collision_shapes (builtin or bullet), flatten_nodes, legacy_materials, no_srgb, skip_animations, skip_axis_conversion.
capabilities.inputs: PRC variables gltf-<option>; gltf2bam source.gltf output.bam
capabilities.outputs: Panda3D scene graph or BAM file

capabilities.does: LODNode holds model variants as children; addSwitch(far, near) gives each variant a distance range. Switches must be added in the same order as the children.

NodePath.instanceTo places one node under many parents without copying it. Each instance has its own transform and bounding volume, is culled separately, and is still drawn once per instance; an animated actor animates once.
Actor play, loop (restart, fromFrame, toFrame), stop and pose control playback; setPlayRate scales speed (negative plays backward); getNumFrames, getCurrentFrame and getAnimControl query state.
capabilities.inputs: play(name, fromFrame); loop(name, restart, fromFrame, toFrame); pose(name, frame); setPlayRate(rate, name)

capabilities.does: enableBlend lets several animations run together with per-animation weights from setControlEffect (default 0.0). makeSubpart(name, include, exclude) splits joints into body parts so an animation plays on only that part. setBlend(frameBlend=True) interpolates between frames.
capabilities.inputs: enableBlend(); setControlEffect(name, weight); makeSubpart(name, include, exclude); play(name, partName)

capabilities.does: Built-in solids: sphere, capsule, inverse sphere, plane, polygon, box, ray, line, segment, parabola. Ray, line, segment and parabola are "from" solids only; plane and polygon are "into" only; sphere and box work as both.
Handlers turn traverser hits into behaviour: CollisionHandlerQueue (collect), Event (send events), Pusher (push apart), PhysicsCollisionHandler, Floor (follow ground) and Gravity.
capabilities.inputs: CollisionTraverser; CollisionHandlerQueue / Event / Pusher / Floor / Gravity; bitmasks

capabilities.does: The panda3d.bullet module exposes Bullet rigid bodies, collision shapes, filtering, continuous collision detection, ghost trigger volumes, queries and a debug renderer.
capabilities.outputs: simulated rigid bodies bound to scene nodes

capabilities.does: Constraint types: hinge, slider, spherical, cone twist and generic six-degrees-of-freedom, built from two bodies with local frames or from one body and the world. Cone twist has setLimit(swing1, swing2, twist).
capabilities.inputs: BulletConeTwistConstraint(nodeA, nodeB, frameA, frameB); setLimit; setDebugDrawSize

capabilities.does: Raycast vehicle with a chassis rigid body and per-wheel set-up: createWheel, chassis connection point, direction, axle, radius, suspension stiffness, damping, friction slip, roll influence, steering, engine force and brake per wheel index.
capabilities.inputs: BulletVehicle(world, chassis); createWheel; setSteeringValue; applyEngineForce; setBrake

capabilities.does: Kinematic capsule character controller: setLinearMovement, setAngularMovement, jump height and speed, doJump, isOnGround. The page calls it early-stage.
BulletSoftBodyNode simulates ropes, patches (cloth or inflated shapes) and tetrahedral volumes, built with factory methods.

Particle effects combine a factory (Point or ZSpin), an emitter (Box, Disc, Line, Arc, Point, Rectangle, Ring, SphereSurface, SphereVolume, TangentRing) and a renderer (Point, Line, Sparkle, Sprite, Geom).

DirectGUI widgets: button, check button, radio button, dialog, entry, frame, label, option menu, scrolled list, wait bar, slider, scroll bar, scrolled frame. Frames use relief styles and frameSize, frameColor, borderWidth.

PStats connects over a network to a viewer program. Enable with want-pstats 1, PStatClient.connect() or shift-S in pview. Shows time strip charts (App, Cull, Draw), value charts and piano-roll charts; optional GPU timing and Python profiler.
Display regions, buffers and windows are created through the graphics classes; stereo display regions, 2D display regions, cull bins and render order allow multi-pass and multi-view rendering.
The manual lists supported model formats, Egg text models and BAM binary files, conversion from Blender, Maya and 3ds Max, glTF files and the pview previewer.
capabilities.inputs: egg and bam converters; exporter plug-ins

rea.notes: Manual cited is the 1.10 Python edition. Modified BSD per repository README.

entries.name: OGRE / OGRE-Next
entries.vendor: OGRECave community (Torus Knot Software Ltd copyright)

licence.name: MIT

engines.name: HLMS material system
engines.does: Material layer that builds shaders from templates plus per-material property sets; implementations are PBS, Unlit and Terra (plus mobile variants).

engines.name: Compositor
engines.does: Node-graph frame description: a workspace connects nodes made of passes (scene, quad, compute, copy, clear) over declared textures.

engines.name: Terra
engines.does: Heightmap terrain drawn without vertex buffers, with LOD rings and a compute shadow pass.

engines.name: ParticleFX2
engines.does: Second particle plug-in built for large counts, with shared quota and shader-generated quads.

engines.name: Global illumination set
engines.does: Several indirect-light options: ambient, spherical harmonics, parallax-corrected cubemaps, instant radiosity, irradiance volume, voxel cone tracing, irradiance field.

engines.name: Render systems
engines.does: Backends for Direct3D 11, OpenGL 3.3+, Metal and Vulkan.

capabilities.does: HLMS keeps GLSL or HLSL shader templates and expands them with a preprocessor per datablock and mesh combination, so unused code (for example skinning on an unskinned mesh) is removed. Identical property sets share a hash and one compiled shader.
capabilities.outputs: compiled shader variants per material and mesh

capabilities.does: Render state is split into shared immutable blocks: macroblock (depth test and write, culling, polygon mode), blendblock (blend factors and operations) and samplerblock (filtering, addressing, LOD bias, anisotropy, border colour). Changing one means assigning a new block.
capabilities.outputs: state-sorted draw calls with few state changes

capabilities.does: A datablock is the mutable material: properties plus references to the three state blocks. Implementations subclass it (HlmsPbsDatablock holds roughness and fresnel). Created through createDatablock with a macroblock, blendblock and parameter vector.
capabilities.inputs: createDatablock(name, humanName, macroblock, blendblock, HlmsParamVec, visibleToManager)

capabilities.does: Hlms::setPrecisionMode picks shader float precision: PrecisionFull32 (default), PrecisionMidf16 or PrecisionRelaxed, each with fallbacks. Only the Vulkan and Metal backends use the reduced modes.
HlmsTextureManager packs textures into array textures on desktop and atlas textures on mobile, driven by texture type (diffuse, normals and others) and settings such as maxTexturesPerArray.
capabilities.outputs: packed texture arrays or atlases with an index and divisor

capabilities.does: The PBS datablock has a metallic workflow with a monochrome metalness map and roughness map; roughness value is above 0 with no upper bound and metalness is 0 to 1.
capabilities.inputs: workflow metallic; roughness value/texture; metalness value/texture
capabilities.outputs: physically based metal and dielectric surfaces

capabilities.does: Two specular workflows are offered: specular_ogre (default, coloured or grey specular texture) and specular_fresnel (the common specular workflow of other engines). Neither uses the metalness setting.
capabilities.inputs: workflow specular_ogre | specular_fresnel; specular value; fresnel

capabilities.does: The brdf keyword selects the lighting model: default, cook_torrance, blinn_phong, default_uncorrelated, three separate-diffuse-fresnel variants for glass-like surfaces, and two legacy Blinn-Phong modes for porting Ogre 1.x content.
capabilities.inputs: brdf default | cook_torrance | blinn_phong | *_separate_diffuse_fresnel | blinn_phong_legacy_math | blinn_phong_full_legacy
capabilities.outputs: BRDF matched to fabric, glass or legacy content

capabilities.does: Fresnel can be given as a coefficient, derived from index of refraction, or set as per-channel colour, with matching coloured_ior mode. IOR modes are not for the metallic workflow.
capabilities.inputs: fresnel mode coeff | ior | coloured | coloured_ior; value

capabilities.does: Normal map strength is a single value defaulting to 1. Each map can choose a UV set from 0 to 7.
capabilities.outputs: bump detail with per-map UV set choice

capabilities.does: Up to four detail diffuse layers and four detail normal layers, each with offset, scale and weight, blended with 12 modes (Add, Multiply, Overlay, Screen and others); detail_weight masks the four slots by RGBA channel.
capabilities.inputs: detail_diffuse0..3 (mode, offset, scale, value); detail_normal0..3; detail_weight
capabilities.outputs: repeating surface detail over a base map

capabilities.does: PBS transparency has four modes: None, Fade (plain alpha), Refractive (alpha plus refraction, drawn in its own compositor pass) and Transparent (keeps specular reflections, for glass and plastic). A value from 0 to 1 sets opacity.
capabilities.inputs: transparency value; mode None | Fade | Refractive | Transparent; use_alpha_from_textures; refraction_strength (0.075)

capabilities.does: alpha_test takes a compare function (less, greater, always and others), a threshold and an optional shadow-only flag, for cut-out materials.
Emissive colour is a vec3 with no physical basis; an emissive texture can instead act as a light map multiplying diffuse when lightmap is true.
A cubemap slot supplies reflections for a PBS material; its coordinates are generated, so the uv setting has no effect.

The Unlit datablock has no lighting and supports 16 diffuse map layers; each layer has a blend mode, a 4x4 animation matrix for UV transforms, a sampler and a UV set. Used for GUI, billboards and particles.
capabilities.inputs: diffuse_map0..15 (texture, blendmode, animate, sampler, uv); diffuse colour

capabilities.does: A workspace is the top-level frame definition: it chooses nodes, connects their channels, declares global textures (names start with global_), picks the SceneManager and sets the final target (window or texture). Several can run at once.
capabilities.inputs: workspace; compositor_node; in/out channels; global_ textures

capabilities.does: Nodes declare textures with size (absolute or relative to the target), pixel format, MSAA, depth pools, UAV use, array, 3D and cubemap types, mip count, reinterpretable views and explicit resolve.
capabilities.inputs: texture name w h [d] format; target_width_scaled; msaa; depth_pool; uav; cubemap; mipmaps

capabilities.does: Pass kinds: clear, generate_mipmaps, render_quad, render_scene, shadows, stencil, uav_queue, compute, texture_copy/depth_copy and custom. Shared keywords include load/store actions, viewport, execution masks and profiling_id.
capabilities.inputs: pass clear | render_scene | render_quad | compute | stencil ...; load; store; expose

capabilities.does: The render_scene pass takes a render-queue range, visibility masks, camera, LOD and cull cameras, Forward+ switch, prepass and normals G-buffer flags, refraction use, UV baking and instanced stereo.
capabilities.inputs: rq_first; rq_last; enable_forwardplus; is_prepass; use_prepass; gen_normals_gbuffer; use_refractions; uv_baking; instanced_stereo
capabilities.outputs: configured scene render passes, including baking to UV space

capabilities.does: A shadow node produces depth maps by uniform, focused or pssm (cascaded) technique, with split count, split blend and fade, lambda, constant and normal-offset bias, and light-to-shadow-map assignment into atlas regions.
capabilities.inputs: technique uniform | focused | pssm; num_splits; pssm_lambda; normal_offset_bias; constant_bias_scale; shadow_map
capabilities.outputs: shadow maps for directional, point and spot lights

capabilities.does: The README lists Forward Clustered rendering among the engine features.

Terra makes terrain geometry from the vertex ID in the shader with no vertex buffers: grid cells read heights from a texture, LOD rings halve tessellation per ring, adjacent cells merge into fewer draws, and skirts hide LOD seams.
For directional lights Terra runs a compute shader that ray-marches the heightmap into a shadow texture, then blurs it; point and spot lights use ordinary shadow maps.
capabilities.inputs: compute shadow texture (red opacity, green height)

capabilities.does: Ambient light options: flat colour, hemisphere (upper and lower colour), rim modes, and 3rd-order spherical harmonics supplied by the caller (monochrome option available).

Parallax-corrected cubemaps treat a probe as a box room to correct reflections, with automatic or manual probe assignment, a per-pixel blending variant that needs Forward+, and a grid placement helper.
capabilities.inputs: envFeatures; ibl_specular pass; per-pixel PCC; pccVctMinDistance / pccVctMaxDistance
capabilities.outputs: localised reflections and fake diffuse GI

capabilities.does: Instant Radiosity traces rays from lights and places virtual point lights; an irradiance volume stores the result in a 3D grid saved to disk. Both need rebuilds when lights or static geometry change.
capabilities.inputs: virtual point lights; irradiance volume grid size

capabilities.does: VCT voxelises the scene and traces cones for bounce light and rough reflections. Settings include cone count, anisotropic voxels, specular SDF quality, thin-wall counter and an ambient sky fake. Needs DX11 or GL4 class hardware.
capabilities.outputs: dynamic-object GI with emissive light sources

capabilities.does: A grid of octahedral probes with depth data (similar to DDGI) gives diffuse GI, generated from VCT voxels or rasterisation, with probes updated over several frames.
capabilities.outputs: diffuse indirect light with less leaking

capabilities.does: Image-based VCT voxelises each mesh once (about 2-3 MB for a 64 cubed volume), stitches the volumes into a scene voxel each frame and shifts camera-centred cascades by revoxelising only new rows. Marked alpha in the page.
capabilities.outputs: faster GI rebuilds for large scenes

capabilities.does: ParticleFX2 shares one quota across instances, gives emit priority by camera distance, generates quads in the vertex shader, supports shadows, PBS lighting and normal maps, and uses alpha hashing instead of sorting. No local_space.
The README lists area lights among the rendering features.
The README lists background texture streaming among the engine features.
The README lists OpenVR integration among the engine features.
The classic OGRE repository lists hardware and software skeletal animation among its features.

The classic OGRE repository lists PBR material workflows, stencil and texture shadows, compositor post-effects such as bloom and HDR, multi-layer terrain with LOD, volume rendering with CSG, Dear ImGui and Bullet integration.

outcomes: real-time 3D scenes on desktop and mobile

rea.notes: MIT per repository pages. Manual pages cited are the Docs/src/manual markdown files and the built API pages hlms.html and compositor.html.

entries.name: Flax Engine

licence.name: Flax Engine End User License Agreement (source on GitHub is governed by this EULA; terms not read)

engines.name: Renderer
engines.does: Deferred opaque pass plus forward pass for transparent materials, with backends for Direct3D 11/12, Vulkan and others; HLSL shaders compiled at cook time.

engines.name: Physics
engines.does: PhysX 5.1 for rigid bodies, colliders, joints, character controller and vehicles; NvCloth for cloth.

engines.name: Particles
engines.does: Graph-authored emitters simulated on the CPU (up to 200k particles) or the GPU (up to 5,000k).

engines.name: Anim Graph
engines.does: Graph-based animation with state machines, blending, skeleton masks, IK and retargeting.

engines.name: Scripting
engines.does: C#, C++ and visual scripting that attach to scene actors, plus behaviour trees for AI.

capabilities.does: Material domain selects use: Surface, Post Process, Decal, GUI, Terrain, Particle or Deformable. Each domain exposes its own inputs and options.
capabilities.inputs: Domain (Surface | Post Process | Decal | GUI | Terrain | Particle | Deformable)
capabilities.outputs: material assets for each render purpose

capabilities.does: Five shading models: Unlit (emissive output), Lit (default; roughness, AO, specular), Subsurface (subsurface colour and opacity as thickness), Foliage (thin leaves) and Custom Lit for own lighting code such as cel shading.
capabilities.inputs: Shading Model; Roughness; Specular; Subsurface Color; Opacity; Emissive
capabilities.outputs: lit, scattering, unlit or custom-shaded surfaces

capabilities.does: Blend modes: Opaque (deferred path), Transparent (uses Opacity), Additive and Multiply, all forward-rendered. Additional options include Opacity Threshold and Mask Threshold for clipping.
capabilities.inputs: Blend Mode; Opacity; Opacity Threshold; Mask Threshold
capabilities.outputs: opaque, glass-like, glowing and tinting surfaces

capabilities.does: Transparent materials can use two lighting modes, Surface (directional diffuse and specular) or Surface Non-Directional (diffuse only, for smoke and dust), and a refraction option driven by pixel versus vertex normals.
capabilities.inputs: Transparent Lighting Mode; Pixel Normal Offset Refraction; Enable Distortion

capabilities.does: Render state options: Cull Mode, Wireframe, Depth Test, Depth Write, Enable Reflections, Enable Screen Space Reflections, Enable Fog, Enable Global Illumination, Use Input World Space Normal and dithered LOD transition.
capabilities.inputs: Cull Mode; Depth Test; Depth Write; Enable Fog; Use Dithered LOD Transition

capabilities.does: Surface materials can tessellate with None, Flat, PointNormal or Phong modes, capped by Max Tessellation Factor (default 15).
Decal-domain materials choose a blending mode: Translucent, Stain (multiplies surface colour), Normal (normal only) or Emissive.
Post Process materials run at a chosen point: after or before the post pass, before forward pass, after custom post effects, before reflections, or after anti-aliasing.
capabilities.outputs: custom full-screen effects at a chosen stage

capabilities.does: Materials hold typed named parameters with defaults; code reads them and Material Instances override them. Attributes such as Tooltip, Range, Slider and Editor Group shape the editor UI.
The Materials section lists a material editor, inputs, functions, layered materials, instanced materials and shader code embedded in materials.
capabilities.inputs: material editor; material functions; layered materials; instanced materials

capabilities.does: Shaders are written in HLSL in .shader files (shared code in .hlsl) and compiled to target APIs at cook time with editor hot reload. Stage macros META_VS, META_HS, META_DS, META_GS, META_PS, META_CS mark functions; minFeatureLevel can be ES2, SM4, SM5 or SM6.

META_PERMUTATION_1 to _4 declare macro-driven shader variants statically in one source file; the engine compiles only those and runtime code picks one by index. META_CB_BEGIN and META_CB_END define constant buffers.
Four light types: Directional, Point, Spot and Sky Light, each with its own page and property set.
capabilities.inputs: Directional Light; Point Light; Spot Light; Sky Light

capabilities.does: Point light properties: Radius, Source Radius and Source Length for area-style highlights, Color, Brightness, View Distance and Minimum Roughness.
capabilities.inputs: Radius; Source Radius; Source Length; Color; Brightness; View Distance; Minimum Roughness

capabilities.does: Point lights can use physically based inverse-square falloff, where Radius only clamps the range, or a Fall Off Exponent otherwise.
capabilities.inputs: Use Inverse Squared Falloff; Fall Off Exponent

capabilities.does: Lights accept an IES Texture; Use IES Brightness takes intensity from the profile and Brightness Scale adjusts it.
capabilities.inputs: IES Texture; Use IES Brightness; Brightness Scale

capabilities.does: Classic shadow mapping with a shared atlas: spot lights use 1 projection, point lights 6, directional lights one per CSM Count. Filtering follows quality: 1x1, 2x2 or 3x3 PCF, and 32-tap PCSS on Ultra.

Per-light shadow controls: Mode (None, Static Only, Dynamic Only, All), Sharpness, Strength, Distance, Fade Distance, Depth Bias, Normal Offset Scale, Resolution, Contact Shadows Length, Update Rate and Update Rate At Distance.
capabilities.inputs: Mode; Sharpness; Strength; Distance; Depth Bias; Normal Offset Scale; Update Rate
capabilities.outputs: tunable shadows with cached static parts

capabilities.does: Global illumination can be baked into lightmap textures in the editor; the manual has pages on lightmap UVs, lightmapping and lightmap settings. A realtime GI approach is also listed.
Lighting section lists Sky and Skybox, Sky Light, Environment Probe for reflections, IES profiles and colour space pages.

Exponential Height Fog actor has a Volumetric Fog switch with Density, Albedo and Emission. Lights add Volumetric Scattering Intensity and Cast Volumetric Shadow. Particles with a Volumetric Fog Rendering module act as local fog volumes with a per-particle radius.
capabilities.inputs: Density; Albedo; Emission; Volumetric Scattering Intensity; Cast Volumetric Shadow

capabilities.does: Post effect with Enabled, Intensity, Power, Radius and Fade Out Distance (world units).
capabilities.inputs: Intensity; Power; Radius; Fade Out Distance

capabilities.does: Modes: FXAA, SMAA and TAA (needs motion vectors; Jitter Spread, Sharpness, Stationary Blending, Motion Blending). A CAS sharpening pass can follow FXAA or SMAA.
capabilities.inputs: Jitter Spread; Sharpness; Stationary Blending; Motion Blending; Sharpening Amount; Edge Sharpening

capabilities.does: DoF with Blur Strength, Focal Distance, Focal Region, near and far transition ranges, Depth Limit; bokeh shape (Hexagon, Octagon, Circle, Cross, Custom texture), size, brightness threshold, falloff and depth cutoff.
capabilities.inputs: Focal Distance; Focal Region; Blur Strength; Bokeh Shape; Bokeh Size; Bokeh Brightness Threshold

capabilities.does: Bloom with Intensity, Threshold, Threshold Knee, Clamp, Base Mix and High Mix to weight wide versus tight glow.
capabilities.inputs: Intensity; Threshold; Threshold Knee; Clamp; Base Mix; High Mix

capabilities.does: Tone Mapping has a Mode setting; the Filmic Tone Mapper follows ACES, with White Temperature (default 6500) and White Tint (default 0).

Three-way grading with Master, Shadows, Midtones and Highlights groups, each with Saturation, Contrast, Gamma, Gain and Offset, plus Shadows Max and Highlights Min. A custom 256x16 LUT texture can be blended in after tonemapping.
capabilities.inputs: Saturation; Contrast; Gamma; Gain; Offset; custom LUT with weight

capabilities.does: SSR settings: Intensity (0-1), Depth and Ray Trace and Resolve resolution (full or half), BRDF Bias 0.82, Roughness Threshold 0.45, World Anti Self Occlusion Bias 0.1, Resolve Samples 4, Edge Fade Factor 0.1, colour-buffer mips and temporal smoothing.
capabilities.inputs: Intensity; Roughness Threshold; Resolve Samples; Temporal Scale; Temporal Response
capabilities.outputs: scene reflections on rough and smooth surfaces

capabilities.does: Camera artifact effects: vignette (intensity default 0.8, colour, shape factor 0.125), film grain (amount 0.005, particle size 1.6, speed), chromatic aberration distortion, and a screen fade colour tint.
capabilities.inputs: Vignette Intensity; Grain Amount; Chromatic Distortion; Screen Fade Color

capabilities.does: Motion blur with Scale, Sample Count and Motion Vectors Resolution, and a Per Bone Motion Blur option for skeletal meshes.
capabilities.inputs: Scale; Sample Count; Motion Vectors Resolution; Per Bone Motion Blur

capabilities.does: Lens flare effect with Ghosts, Halo Width, Halo Intensity, Ghost Dispersal, Distortion, threshold bias and scale, plus lens dirt, lens colour and lens star textures.
capabilities.inputs: Intensity; Ghosts; Halo Width; Ghost Dispersal; Lens Dirt; Lens Star

capabilities.does: Auto exposure modes: None, Manual, Automatic Histogram (compute shader) and Automatic Average Luminance; Speed Up and Speed Down, Pre and Post Exposure, Minimum and Maximum Brightness, histogram low and high percent.
capabilities.inputs: Mode; Speed Up; Speed Down; Pre Exposure; Post Exposure; Histogram Low Percent

capabilities.does: Models carry up to 6 LODs chosen by screen size percentage; Generate LODs on import builds them. Dithered LOD transition on materials, view.ModelLODBias, per-instance LOD Bias and Forced LOD.
capabilities.inputs: Generate LODs; Use Dithered LOD Transition; LOD Bias; Forced LOD

capabilities.does: Instances sharing a model and materials are batched into one draw call by default on supported platforms.
Physics uses PhysX 5.1. Colliders: box, sphere, capsule and mesh; the section also covers rigid bodies, triggers, physical material, physics settings, raycasting and collisions.
capabilities.inputs: BoxCollider; SphereCollider; CapsuleCollider; MeshCollider; physical material

capabilities.does: Joint types: Fixed, Distance, Hinge, Slider, Spherical and D6.
capabilities.inputs: FixedJoint; DistanceJoint; HingeJoint; SliderJoint; SphericalJoint; D6Joint

capabilities.does: Cloth actor simulates a mesh on the CPU through NvCloth. Vertices are painted as locked or free (Max Particle Distance). Settings include gravity scale, damping, drag, inertia, wind via air drag and lift, collisions, self-collision, fabric stiffness for vertical, horizontal, bending and shearing.
capabilities.inputs: Max Particle Distance; Gravity Scale; Wind Velocity; Self Collision Distance; Stiffness; Stretch Limit
capabilities.outputs: cloth on static or animated models

capabilities.does: Wheeled Vehicle actor on the PhysX vehicle SDK: Drive Type, up to 20 wheels with radius, width, Max Steer Angle and brake torques, engine, differential and gearbox groups, and script calls SetThrottle, SetSteering, SetBrake, SetHandbrake.
capabilities.inputs: Drive Type; Wheels; Engine; Differential; Gearbox; GetWheelState

capabilities.does: Particle systems use sprite, mesh and ribbon particles, authored in an emitter graph. CPU mode handles up to 200k particles; GPU mode up to 5,000k, samples scene textures, supports depth-buffer collisions, and does not support ribbons.
capabilities.inputs: Particle Emitter asset; Particle System asset; Particle Effect actor

capabilities.does: Anim Graph with parameters, functions, animation slots, state machines, blending, skeleton masks, inverse kinematics, retargeting, root motion and bone sockets.
capabilities.inputs: Anim Graph; Skeleton Mask; Animation Retargeting; Bone Socket

capabilities.does: Scripts in C# (.NET, C# 14), C++ or visual scripts; visual scripts can inherit C++ or C# classes, hot reload, and use the whole engine API. Script events, properties, attributes, serialization, custom editors and plugins are covered.
capabilities.inputs: Script; Actor; visual script; plugin project

capabilities.does: Artificial intelligence section provides behaviour trees with knowledge, behaviour, nodes, decorators and custom nodes.
capabilities.inputs: Behavior Tree; custom node; custom decorator

rea.notes: Source repository is public but governed by the Flax EULA, which was not read. Several manual pages returned 404 or 503 and are not cited.

entries.name: Wicked Engine

licence.name: MIT

engines.name: Renderer
engines.does: C++ renderer with DirectX 12, Vulkan and Metal back ends, tiled forward rendering and a RenderPath3D post-process chain.

engines.name: Entity-component system and scene
engines.does: Data-oriented scene made of components for meshes, materials, lights, armatures, animation, physics, sound and scripts, updated by a job system.

engines.name: Path tracer
engines.does: GPU ray and path tracing render path with a denoiser, also used for lightmap baking.

engines.name: Editor
engines.does: Standalone 3D editor with a Lua console.

engines.name: Lua scripting
engines.does: Lua environment for loading models, moving entities, playing sounds and reading input; startup.lua runs on launch.

capabilities.does: Tiled forward (Forward+) rendering with 2.5D culling, reversed Z-buffer, gamma-correct HDR rendering and multithreaded command recording.
Occlusion culling with GPU queries; the documentation lists an Occlusion Culling section under the Renderer.
Tiled decals applied in the forward pass; Decals have their own Renderer documentation section.
Variable rate shading is listed among supported rendering features.
Texture atlas packing, virtual textures and texture streaming are listed.
Impostor system for far objects, plus a procedural terrain generator and splines.
Gaussian splat rendering is in the feature list.
H.264 video decoding is listed for playing video textures.
Physically based rendering with normal mapping, displacement, parallax occlusion mapping, animated texturing and stochastic alpha-test transparency.
Tessellation for silhouette smoothing and displacement; hull and domain shader stages are in the shader stage list.
Directional, spot and point lights, plus translucent coloured shadows and light shafts.
Directional lights use cascaded shadow maps, spot lights use shadow maps and point lights use cube maps; PCF soft shadows, screen-space contact shadows and translucent coloured shadows are added.
The Renderer documentation has a Shadow Maps section for 2D and cube maps, configured with SetShadowProps2D and SetShadowPropsCube.
Hardware ray tracing (DXR and Vulkan) can render ambient occlusion, shadows and reflections; a compute-based software path exists for hardware without it.
Static and real-time cube map reflections, planar reflections, parallax-corrected environment maps and stochastic screen-space reflections.
Refraction caustics and volumetric light scattering are listed.
Indirect lighting options: screen-space GI, voxel GI, surfel GI and dynamic diffuse GI (DDGI). DDGI is noted as usable with software ray tracing.
capabilities.inputs: SSGI; Voxel GI; Surfel GI; DDGI

capabilities.does: Screen-space AO variants SSAO, HBAO and MSAO.
The documentation lists RenderPath3D_Pathtracing with a denoiser, and a Lightmap baking section under the renderer; the feature list adds GPU path tracing for lightmap baking.
Scene BVH built on the GPU with compute (GPUBVH) for ray queries without the hardware ray tracing API.
Anti-aliasing options: MSAA, FXAA, TAA and supersampling.
Post effects: bloom, edge outline, motion blur, lens flare, bokeh depth of field, chromatic aberration, colour grading, sharpen filter and eye adaptation.
GPU particles emitted from a point, mesh or animated mesh, with soft particles, depth-buffer collisions and force fields; Smooth Particle Hydrodynamics fluid simulation is also listed.
GPU hair particle system attached to mesh surfaces, used for grass and vegetation, affected by force fields.
FFT ocean rendered relative to the camera as an infinite water plane.
Rigid bodies use RigidBodyPhysicsComponent with BOX, SPHERE, CAPSULE, CONVEX_HULL and TRIANGLE_MESH shapes and KINEMATIC or DISABLE_DEACTIVATION flags.
SoftBodyPhysicsComponent works with a mesh; simulated positions go into vertex_positions_simulation, and pinned vertices follow object transform or skinning.
Physics list adds ragdoll, vehicle, character, springs and colliders.
Skeletal animation, morph targets with sparse accessors, inverse kinematics, humanoid rig, animation retargeting and expressions.
Imports OBJ, FBX, glTF/GLB, VRM/VRMA and PLY and saves to the native WISCENE format.

glTF extension support includes unlit, transmission, specular-glossiness, sheen, clearcoat, specular, anisotropy, IOR, emissive strength, punctual lights and image-based lights; VRM 0.0 and 1.0 add spring bones, blend shapes, expressions and humanoid rigs.
Audio classes Sound, SoundInstance and SoundInstance3D, with submix types and reverb presets.
Lua scripting for loading models, moving entities, playing sounds and reading input; startup.lua runs on launch; the editor has a Lua console toggled with the Home key.
UDP networking and 3D path finding are listed in the feature list.

rea.notes: MIT per repository README. Console extension files are private according to the README.

entries.name: Cocos Creator / cocos-engine

licence.name: MIT (engine repository); editor terms not read

engines.name: Render pipeline
engines.does: Built-in forward pipeline (default) and a trial deferred pipeline, built from flows and stages; a custom pipeline API and per-camera post-process settings sit on top.

engines.name: Effect and shader system
engines.does: Effect assets describe passes; surface shaders, legacy shaders and compute shaders are supported, with built-in PBR, toon and unlit effects.

engines.name: Physics 3D
engines.does: Selectable back end among Bullet, cannon.js, PhysX 4.1 and a built-in collision-only engine.

engines.name: Marionette animation
engines.does: Graph-based skeletal animation with state machines and procedural pose graphs.

engines.name: Particle system
engines.does: Module-based 3D particle system with emitter, influencers and renderer.

engines.name: Native renderer
engines.does: C++ renderer using Vulkan on Windows and Android and Metal on macOS and iOS, with WebGL on the web.

capabilities.does: Default builtin-forward pipeline: ShadowFlow with ShadowStage, then ForwardFlow with ForwardStage drawing opaque, lighting, transparent, then UI. Only one directional light takes effect and up to 16 lights are supported per the page.

Trial builtin-deferred pipeline: GBufferFlow writes opaque objects to a GBuffer, LightingFlow runs screen-space lighting then transparents, then a PostProcessStage copies to screen. Needs multiple render targets.
capabilities.inputs: builtin-deferred; deferred pass in effect files

capabilities.does: A BuiltinPipelineSettings component on a camera enables MSAA, shading scale, bloom, colour grading, FXAA and FSR when the matching builtin materials and textures are assigned.
MSAA at 2X or 4X on native platforms (WebGL antialias on web), FXAA, and FSR upscaling that only helps when Shading Scale is below 1.
Bloom blurs bright areas and blends them back; the settings are Bloom Iterations and Bloom Threshold.
Tone mapping is integrated with colour grading, which applies a LUT texture.
Physically based lighting uses photometric units: luminous flux (lm), luminance (cd/m2) and illuminance (lx); sunlight uses illuminance. Colour temperature and light size contribute.
capabilities.inputs: luminous flux; luminance; illuminance; colour temperature; size

capabilities.does: Two shadow types: Planar and ShadowMap. ShadowMap size options Low 256, Medium 512, High 1024 and Ultra 2048; MaxReceived defaults to 4 lights. PCF modes HARD, SOFT, SOFT_2X, SOFT_4X (1, 4, 9, 16 samples).

Directional light shadows use cascaded shadow maps when FixedArea is off; FixedArea mode sets ShadowNear, ShadowFar and ShadowOrthoSize. ShadowDistance limits range and ShadowInvisibleOcclusionRange casts shadows from off-screen objects.
capabilities.outputs: sun shadows over a camera range

capabilities.does: Light Probe Group nodes generate a uniform probe grid inside an editable box (Number Of Probes X/Y/Z); probes are baked in the Light-Probe panel with up to 4 bounces and applied to movable nodes with Use Light Probe.
capabilities.inputs: Generating Min Pos / Max Pos; Number Of Probes; Bake To Light Probe; Use Light Probe
capabilities.outputs: baked indirect light for dynamic objects

capabilities.does: Reflection Probe (v3.7+) has CUBE (baked cube map at 256, 512 or 768 per face) and PLANNAR (real-time, needs a Source Camera) types, with Size, Clear Flag, Visibility mask and a Bake button.
capabilities.inputs: Probe Type; Resolution; Size; Source Camera; Clear Flag; Visibility

capabilities.does: Static lights and meshes bake into lightmaps; needs a second non-overlapping UV set. Panel parameters: MSAA 1/2/4/8, Resolution 128-2048, Gamma, GIScale, GISamples, AOLevel, AOStrength, AORadius, AOColor; output is RGBE8.

builtin-standard effect: albedo, albedoScale, normalMap and normalStrength, packed pbrMap (R occlusion, G roughness, B metallic) or metallicRoughnessMap, occlusion, roughness and metallic constants (0-1), emissive with emissiveScale, alphaThreshold.
capabilities.inputs: mainColor; roughness; metallic; pbrMap; occlusionMap; emissive; USE_PBR_MAP

capabilities.does: Built-in toon effect with optional outline pass (lineWidth, depthBias, baseColor) and two shade steps: shadeColor1/2, baseStep, baseFeather, shadeStep, shadeFeather, shadowCover, specular, emissive and optional maps.

Surface Shader writes material data in short code and picks a lighting model; shared environment lighting and a rendering debug view come with it. builtin-standard uses it from v3.7.2; older shaders live in a legacy folder.
capabilities.inputs: surface shader; lighting models; macro remapping
capabilities.outputs: shaders without writing the full pipeline

capabilities.does: Compute shaders run on Vulkan, Metal and GLES 3.1 inside a custom render pipeline: effect pass with compute entry and local_size layout, addComputePass, addStorageTexture, addStorageImage and addQueue().addDispatch(x, y, z, material).
capabilities.inputs: pipeline.addComputePass; addStorageTexture(name, format, w, h); addDispatch(x, y, z, material)

capabilities.does: Global fog types Linear (FogStart, FogEnd), Exponential and Exponential Squared (FogDensity 0-1, FogStart, FogAtten) and Layer Fog (FogTop, FogRange, FogAtten), with an Accurate per-pixel option.
capabilities.inputs: Type; FogColor; FogDensity; FogStart; FogEnd; FogAtten; FogTop; FogRange

capabilities.does: The 3D particle system has Main, Shape, Velocity, Force, Size, Rotation, Color over lifetime, Texture Animation, Limit Velocity, Trail and Renderer modules.

Back end selectable per project: Bullet (ammo.js, about 1.5 MB, default), cannon.js (about 141 KB), PhysX 4.1 (about 5 MB, native-oriented) or Builtin collision-only. PhysX constraints are experimental.

Marionette (3.5+) uses Animation Graph assets run by an Animation Controller component: states from clips, state machines, transitions, layers, masks and variants, and procedural pose graphs with blend, modify and sample nodes. Skeletal clips from fbx, gltf and glb only.

Debug-draw interface: addLine, addDashedLine, addTriangle, addQuad, addBoundingBox, addCross, addFrustum, addCapsule, addCylinder, addCone, addCircle, addArc, addPolygon, addDisc, addSector, addSphere, addTorus, addOctahedron, addBezier, addSpline, addMesh, addIndexedMesh. Must be re-added each frame.

Terrain asset and cc.Terrain component edited with Manage, Sculpt (Bulge, Sunken, Smooth, Flatten, Set Height), Paint and Select tabs; up to 4 texture layers; Tile Size, Weight Map Size, Light Map Size; LOD toggle and bias. No rotation or scale.
capabilities.inputs: Tile Size; Weight Map Size; Lod Bias; brush size, strength, falloff

capabilities.does: The engine is half C++, half TypeScript; native builds use Vulkan (Windows, Android) and Metal (macOS, iOS), the web uses WebGL. Targets include HarmonyOS and several mini-game platforms.
capabilities.outputs: builds for desktop, mobile, web and mini-games

capabilities.does: The manual documents glTF models, MeshRenderer, SkinnedMeshRenderer, vertex animation textures, texture compression and render textures.

outcomes: games and apps for web, mobile and desktop

entries.name: jMonkeyEngine

licence.name: New BSD (3-clause)

engines.name: Render pipeline
engines.does: Per-viewport RenderPipeline objects, with a default ForwardPipeline in jme3-core; custom pipelines are registered on a ViewPort or the RenderManager (3.8).

engines.name: Material system
engines.does: j3md material definitions with parameters, techniques, defines and world parameters; built-in definitions for unshaded, Phong, terrain, particles and sky.

engines.name: Shader nodes
engines.does: Shaders assembled at run time from small node definitions wired in a material technique.

engines.name: Physics
engines.does: Bullet-based PhysicsSpace with rigid bodies, ghosts, vehicles, characters and ragdolls.

engines.name: SpiderMonkey networking
engines.does: Server and client classes sending serialised messages over TCP or UDP.

engines.name: TerraMonkey
engines.does: Quad-tree terrain with GeoMipMapping LOD and texture splatting.

capabilities.does: Pipelines implement RenderPipeline with fetchPipelineContext, hasRenderedThisFrame, startRenderFrame, pipelineRender and endRenderFrame; shared state sits in a PipelineContext registered with the RenderManager. viewPort.setPipeline or renderManager.setPipeline assigns them.

Light classes in com.jme3.light: PointLight (colour, radius, position), DirectionalLight, SpotLight (inner angle, outer angle, spot range) and AmbientLight. Lights are added with rootNode.addLight; Lighting.j3md needs a directional, point or spot light.
capabilities.inputs: setColor; setRadius; setSpotRange; setSpotInnerAngle; setSpotOuterAngle; LightControl

capabilities.does: Each light type has a shadow renderer and a shadow filter (DirectionalLightShadowRenderer, PointLightShadowRenderer, SpotLightShadowRenderer and matching filters). Directional ones take shadow map size and count; setLambda, setShadowIntensity and setShadowZextend tune splits and range.
capabilities.outputs: cascaded sun shadows and point and spot shadows

capabilities.does: Lighting.j3md parameters: DiffuseMap, NormalMap (LATC flag), SpecularMap, Shininess, ParallaxMap, AlphaMap, AlphaDiscardThreshold, ColorRamp, GlowMap, GlowColor, VertexLighting, UseMaterialColors with Diffuse, Ambient and Specular colours.
capabilities.inputs: DiffuseMap; NormalMap; SpecularMap; Shininess; ParallaxMap; GlowMap

capabilities.does: Unshaded.j3md (ColorMap, Color, VertexColor, LightMap, GlowMap), Sky.j3md (Texture, SphereMap), reflect.j3md (environment-mapped glass) and ShowNormals.j3md for debugging.

Render state blend modes via setBlendMode: Off, Alpha, Additive, AlphaAdditive, Color, Modulate, ModulateX2 and PremultAlpha; setDepthWrite, setAlphaTest with alpha fall-off and face culling modes Back, Off, Front and FrontAndBack.

The wiki describes the image-based lighting theory used for PBR: an irradiance cube map from nine spherical-harmonic coefficients and a prefiltered specular map with roughness in the mip levels plus a BRDF lookup (split-sum).
capabilities.inputs: irradiance map; prefiltered environment map; BRDF lookup texture

capabilities.does: Shader Node system builds a shader at run time from vertex and fragment node definitions (.j3sn), wired in a Technique through InputMappings (MatParam, WorldParam, Attr, Global, previous node) and OutputMappings, with Conditions that compile to defines.

Custom GLSL shaders are declared per technique in a .j3md with MaterialParameters, WorldParameters and Defines. Uniform prefixes g_ (world) and m_ (material); attribute names inPosition, inNormal, inColor, inTexCoord.
FilterPostProcessor holds filters in com.jme3.post.filters: WaterFilter, DepthOfFieldFilter, FogFilter, LightScatteringFilter, BloomFilter, SSAOFilter, CartoonEdgeFilter and FadeFilter.
SSAOFilter adds screen-space ambient occlusion shading, including with transparency, on a viewport.

WaterFilter simulates ocean water: setWaterHeight, setMaxAmplitude, setWaveScale (0.005), setWindDirection, setSpeed, setNormalScale, foam (setUseFoam, setFoamHardness, setFoamExistence), shore (setShoreHardness, setUseHQShoreline), colours, setWaterTransparency, setColorExtinction, refraction and reflection map size (512).
capabilities.outputs: animated water with foam and reflections

capabilities.does: ParticleEmitter settings: mesh type (Triangle or Point), particle count, particles per second (20), start and end size (0.2, 2), start and end colour, low and high life (3, 7), velocity variation (0.2), gravity, facing, random angle, rotate speed, sprite-sheet frames, emitter shape (point or sphere).
capabilities.inputs: setParticlesPerSec; setStartSize; setLowLife; setHighLife; setVelocityVariation; setImagesX; setShape

capabilities.does: TerrainQuad builds a GeoMipMapping tree of TerrainPatch tiles (example: 65 tile size, 513 total, up to 1025) with TerrainLodControl; texture splatting uses alpha maps and per-layer normal maps; 16 sampler limit constrains layer counts.
capabilities.inputs: new TerrainQuad(name, patchSize, totalSize, heightMap); TerrainLodControl; LodCalculator

capabilities.does: Terrain.j3md uses three diffuse maps with an alpha map; HeightBasedTerrain.j3md has four height regions plus slope map; TerrainLighting.j3md supports many layers with normal maps and triplanar mapping (11 map limit).
LodGenerator (a Java port of the Ogre generator) bakes reduced index buffers with COLLAPSE_COST, PROPORTIONAL or CONSTANT methods; LodControl picks the level from camera distance.

AnimComposer plays named actions, chains them with actionSequence and tweens, and makes layers with armature masks (makeLayer, ArmatureMask.createMask) for upper and lower body motion. Animations are authored elsewhere.
capabilities.inputs: AnimComposer; SkinningControl; setCurrentAction(name, layer); makeLayer; ArmatureMask

capabilities.does: Cinematic (an AppState) schedules events on a timeline: MotionEvent along a MotionPath with LookAt, Path, PathAndRotation or Rotation direction modes, SoundEvent, GuiEvent, AnimationEvent and custom events; bindCamera and activateCamera switch cameras.
capabilities.inputs: Cinematic; MotionEvent; SoundEvent; AnimationEvent; bindCamera; activateCamera

capabilities.does: BulletAppState runs a PhysicsSpace; RigidBodyControl (dynamic, static, kinematic), GhostControl, and collision shapes (box, sphere, cylinder, capsule, plane, simplex, compound, mesh, hull, GImpact, heightfield). Space tuning: setGravity, setAccuracy (1/60), setMaxSubSteps, world bounds.

VehicleControl with PhysicsVehicleWheel, CharacterControl and BetterCharacterControl, and RagDollControl are provided; PhysicsCollisionListener and PhysicsTickListener handle events and per-step forces.

Network.createServer(port) and Network.connectToServer(host, port); Message classes annotated @Serializable, reliable (TCP) or unreliable (UDP) per message; listeners for messages, connections and client state; server name and version must match.

The 3.8 documentation lists camera and multiple views, render buckets, input handling and combo moves, mouse picking, Nifty GUI, HUDs, virtual reality, and an SDK with scene composer, terrain editor, material editor and filter editor.
The how-to list covers Blender export as glTF or Ogre XML, 3ds Max, MakeHuman and Mixamo animation workflows; models load through the asset manager.

outcomes: desktop and mobile 3D games and applications

rea.notes: New BSD per repository README; v3.8.0 stated as latest stable. Docs 3.8 pages cited.

entries.name: UNIGINE

licence.name: Community SDK free; Sim SDK and Academic Research SDK by contact or academic pricing (terms not read)

engines.name: Deferred renderer
engines.does: Deferred opaque pass with a G-buffer and screen-space lighting, then a forward pass for water, clouds and transparents, then post effects.

engines.name: Material system
engines.does: Base materials (shader-backed, *.basemat) and user materials (*.mat) in an inheritance tree, with a node-based material graph editor.

engines.name: Light and probe objects
engines.does: World, omni and projected lights plus environment, voxel and planar probes, each with dynamic or static (baked) modes.

engines.name: Image Generator
engines.does: Simulation rendering with out-the-window and sensor views, double-precision terrain, ephemeris, weather and multi-channel sync.

engines.name: Effect objects
engines.does: Particle systems, volumetrics, fields acting on grass and water, and physical force fields.

capabilities.does: Opaque geometry fills a G-buffer (depth, albedo, shading data, normals with roughness, velocity, material mask, lightmap data); decals blend into it; a deferred light pass accumulates diffuse and specular light, then composites with environment reflections and ambient.
capabilities.inputs: G-buffer; deferred light pass; deferred composite

capabilities.does: Documented frame order: common pass, calculations (culling, sorting, batching), shadow maps, dynamic reflections, deferred pass, transparent forward pass, exposure, TAA, camera effects, tone mapping, post materials, GUI.
capabilities.outputs: a known pass order for custom work

capabilities.does: World light uses up to four orthographic cascades; omni lights use six perspective cameras; projected lights use one. The render docs name Parallel-Split Shadow Mapping.
capabilities.inputs: cascade count; shadow map per light

capabilities.does: LightWorld (sun), LightOmni (point) and LightProj (projected cone); omni and proj have static modes with prebaked shadow cubemap or 2D depth texture.
capabilities.inputs: LightWorld; LightOmni; LightProj; dynamic or static mode

capabilities.does: LightEnvironmentProbe captures a cubemap each frame (dynamic) or uses a prebaked one; LightPlanarProbe renders mirror-like reflections each frame. Priority: omni, proj and world light, then voxel probe, then environment probe.
capabilities.outputs: reflections and ambient light from probes

capabilities.does: LightVoxelProbe bakes indirect diffuse light into a 3D texture inside a box volume (Box Size, Voxel Size, bake quality presets Draft to Ultra, normal and tangent bias, three blend modes). Dynamic objects inside are shaded when Bake Internal Volume is Full or Half.
capabilities.inputs: Box Size; Voxel Size; Bake Quality; Bake Internal Volume

capabilities.does: SSRTGI produces SSAO, SSGI and bent normals from screen-space data; SSR runs with or without importance sampling, and a separate SSAO/SSGI step fills in when SSRTGI did not.
Shading data includes translucency and microfibre; SSS is applied as an exponential blur over the deferred result.
Volumetric clouds render into an RGBA16F texture; global water builds height and shoreline fields, a W-buffer and underwater or overwater modes with water decals, shafts and water depth of field.
capabilities.outputs: clouds and ocean in the forward pass

capabilities.does: Anti-aliasing options listed in the render section: FXAA, TAA, SRAA and supersampling.

DLSS (up to version 4) and FSR 3 (up to 3.1.3) upscaling. Settings render_upscale_mode (1 FSR, 2 DLSS), render_upscale_order and context limits dlss_max_contexts and fsr_max_contexts; TAA is disabled when upscaling is on.

Camera effects stage: motion blur from the velocity buffer, depth of field with chromatic aberration, bloom from up to eight lower-resolution textures, cross and lens effects with lens dirt, shadow shafts; adaptive or static exposure and filmic tone mapping with a LUT.
capabilities.inputs: Motion Blur; Depth of Field; Bloom; Lens; adaptive exposure

capabilities.does: Output modes: stereo rendering, multi-monitor rendering including SpiderVision and Surround plugins, and panoramic rendering; dynamic resolution scale is listed.

Base materials hold shaders and cannot be edited in the Materials Editor; user materials override their properties, form hierarchies by GUID and are editable. Manual and internal (runtime) materials are distinguished.

Node-based material graph with about 30 sample materials (Glass, Ice, Dissolve, Fresnel Effect, Vertex Animation) and node categories Misc, Input, Parameters, Logical, Decal, Math, Matrix, Trigonometry, Textures, Procedural.

Graph parameters cover Bool, Combobox, Static Int, Color, float and int vectors, Slider, Group and 2D, 2D array, 2D int, 3D, cube and ramp textures; custom parameters, surface IDs and material buffers can be set from C# or C++.
Built-in base materials cover billboards, clouds, decals, grass, GUI, landscape and terrain, meshes (including PBR), particles, sky, water, volumetric effects, post-processing and debugging.

Effect objects: particle systems (emitter, particles, force), volumetric objects for fog, clouds, light beams and halos, fields that hide or animate selected grass and water areas, and physicals with a force field.
capabilities.outputs: fire, smoke, fog and force effects

capabilities.does: Simulation Image Generator with out-the-window, EO, IR and night-vision views, double-precision whole-Earth terrain, ephemeris, weather, Simplifier, Adaptive Quality System, Syncker multi-IG sync, CIGI/HLA/DIS connectors. Needs the Sim SDK.

Release highlights listed on the product page: NavMesh generation (experimental), Cesium integration, LiDAR, radar and fisheye sensors, improved Gaussian splatting, a Sequencer tool, an AI toolkit for editor assistance.
The API index lists skeletal animation and timeline animation class groups under animations.

rea.notes: The docs site needs JavaScript; this entry uses the vendor Markdown mirror on GitHub (ai-docs), whose licence was not shown. EULA not read.

entries.name: Torque 3D

licence.name: MIT

engines.name: GFX layer
engines.does: Graphics abstraction with Direct3D 11, OpenGL and Null device back ends, plus texture, shader, state-block, vertex-buffer and occlusion-query classes.

engines.name: Lighting manager
engines.does: Basic (forward) and advanced (deferred) lighting back ends with a shadow-map manager.

engines.name: PostFx system
engines.does: PostEffect objects chained by a manager, scripted in TorqueScript.

engines.name: T3D game classes
engines.does: Players, vehicles, projectiles, lights, scenes, decals, physics zones and AI classes in the T3D source folder.

engines.name: Physics plug-in layer
engines.does: Simple built-in physics that can be swapped for PhysX or Bullet through a wrapper.

capabilities.does: The feature list names a forward-rendering basic lighting mode and a deferred-rendering advanced lighting mode; the source tree has separate basic and advanced lighting folders.
Per-pixel lighting with normal and parallax mapping; materials built in a high-level editor or written in GLSL or HLSL; shaders for water, sky, sun and common material types.
Version 4.0 moved lighting and materials to PBR with ORM texture packing, corrected BRDF handling and emissive fixes.

Material objects use mapTo to bind to a model material target, diffuseMap[n], normalMap[n], specular[n] (colour) and specularPower[n]; a material can inherit another with a colon; skin names retarget materials per instance.
capabilities.inputs: mapTo; diffuseMap[0]; normalMap[0]; specular[0]; specularPower[0]; skin

capabilities.does: Built-in PostFX effects: HDR with light adaptation, depth of field, lens flare and sun rays, SSAO, FXAA, refraction, reflection and glow; levels can change their post effects.
Version 4.0 reworked reflection probes with an active probe list, re-implemented a dynamic cubemap probe mode, cleaned up IBL and allowed ambient light injection into IBL.
The T3D source folder has light base, point light, spot light, light description, light flare data and light animation data classes.
capabilities.outputs: scene lights with flares and animation

capabilities.does: Version 4.0 notes mention fade, max-light and shadow options for shapes, a preference for whether local lights cast shadows, further light preferences, and spotlight cookie projection fixes.
GFX includes D3D11, OpenGL and Null devices; version 4.0 switched from Direct3D 9 to Direct3D 11 and raised OpenGL to 4.0.
capabilities.outputs: rendering on Windows, Linux and macOS

capabilities.does: Terrain editor to import or sculpt terrain; 4.0 added height-based terrain texture blending and an asset-based terrain loader.
Plug-in physics: a simple built-in implementation swappable with PhysX or Bullet. Listed capabilities include rigid bodies, cloth, destructible objects, destroyable joints and fluid buoyancy.
The T3D fx folder has particle emitters and nodes, explosions, splashes, precipitation, lightning, ribbons, wind emitters, ground cover and foliage or shape replicators.
Built-in server-authoritative networking with local game-state prediction, interpolation and datablocks for time-invariant data sent at join.
Documented editors: scene, ConvexShape, terrain editor and painter, material, spline-based mesh road, river and decal road, datablock, particle, decal, forest, navmesh, shape and GUI editors.
capabilities.inputs: World Editor; Mesh Road Editor; River Editor; Forest Editor

capabilities.does: The feature list names plug-in based editor modes, automatic reload of externally changed assets, and Collada DAE shape import.
Version 4.0 moved the engine to assets and modules and added an Assimp shape importer and a legacy project importer.

TorqueScript is a custom C-like language with variables, types, operators, control structures, functions, objects and module interop calls (queueExec, callOnModules, moduleExec). A C interface is documented for other languages.
AI pages cover navmesh generation, AI objects and AI scripting; the source tree includes a navigation folder and the editor has a navmesh editor.

rea.notes: MIT per repository page. Several documentation pages (lighting, terrain, shaders, GFX, render bins) were stubs and are not cited for content.

entries.name: Verge3D

licence.name: Paid licence per seat/edition; Enterprise and Ultimate add source access (prices not read)

engines.name: Exporter and App Manager
engines.does: DCC add-ons for Blender, 3ds Max and Maya export glTF 2.0 with Verge3D extensions; the App Manager creates and runs web apps from templates.

engines.name: Runtime renderer
engines.does: WebGL 1/2 PBR renderer with a three.js-partially-compatible JavaScript API.

engines.name: Puzzles
engines.does: Visual logic editor with more than 300 blocks covering events, materials, animation, physics, post-processing, AR/VR, e-commerce and SCORM.

engines.name: Physics module
engines.does: Ammo.js (Bullet) build used by physics puzzles and JavaScript.

capabilities.does: Content comes from Blender 4.5-5.2, 3ds Max 2024-2027 and Maya 2024-2027 add-ons that export glTF 2.0 with Verge3D extensions; glTF 2.0 can also come from any suite. USDZ export is available through Puzzles.

Blender: Eevee and Cycles shader nodes plus a glTF-compliant Principled BSDF. 3ds Max: Physical, OpenPBR, Standard, glTF and USD Preview Surface. Maya: Standard Surface, OpenPBR, aiStandardSurface, approximated Lambert/Phong/Blinn and glTF-compliant nodes.
Procedural textures can be written in Open Shading Language; custom shaders use GLSL ES 2.0 (WebGL 1) or 3.0 (WebGL 2).

Blender lights supported: Point, Sun, Spot and Area (square or rectangle). Settings: Temperature, Color, Power or Strength, Exposure, spot beam size and blend, Custom Distance; disk and ellipse area shapes are unsupported.
capabilities.inputs: Temperature; Color; Power; Exposure; Beam Shape; Custom Distance

capabilities.does: Light types per suite: 3ds Max photometric (point, rectangle) and standard lights (spot, direct, omni); Maya ambient, directional, point, spot, area and Arnold area lights.
capabilities.outputs: lights carried from Max and Maya

capabilities.does: A single HDR world texture can light the scene and form the background; a Light Path node (Is Camera Ray) can separate them. IBL Env. Mode options: PMREM (best), Light Probe (diffuse only, fast) and None. Env. Map Size 256 to 1024.
capabilities.inputs: World nodes; IBL Env. Mode; Env. Map Size

capabilities.does: Reflection cubemap probes (sphere or box influence, intensity, custom parallax, visibility and influence collections) and planar reflection probes (distance, clipping offset, falloff); one probe per object; each planar probe adds N+1 draw calls.
capabilities.inputs: Probe Type; Custom Parallax; Visibility Collection; Distance; Clipping Offset

capabilities.does: Shadow filters: Basic, Bilinear, PCF (default, Poisson disk) and ESM (softest, light leaks possible). Global Cube Size and Cascade Size set map resolution; per light Blur Radius, Clip Start, Bias and ESM Bias.
capabilities.inputs: Cube Size; Cascade Size; Blur Radius; Bias; ESM Distance Scale

capabilities.does: Sun light cascades: Count, Fade, Max Distance, Distribution and Cascade Margin; per object Cast Shadow via Ray Visibility and Receive Shadows toggles.
capabilities.inputs: Count; Fade; Max Distance; Distribution; Cascade Margin

capabilities.does: Blend modes Auto, Opaque, Alpha Clip, Alpha Hashed (alpha to coverage), Alpha Blend; Clip Threshold; transparency hacks Nearest Layer (depth prepass) and Two-Pass; per-object render order; order-independent transparency needs WebGL 2.
capabilities.inputs: Blend Mode; Clip Threshold; Render Order; Depth Write

capabilities.does: Anti-aliasing options: Auto, MSAA 4x, 8x or 16x, FXAA or None.

View Transform options Standard, Khronos PBR Neutral, AgX and Filmic; ACES and others fall back to Standard. Look supports None and Punchy; Exposure scales brightness. HDR rendering uses 16-bit float buffers.
capabilities.inputs: View Transform; Look; Exposure; Use HDR Rendering

capabilities.does: Ambient occlusion is enabled in the Verge3D Settings panel with Distance, Factor, Trace Precision and Bent Normals; an outline effect has edge strength, glow, thickness, pulse period and hidden-edge colours.
capabilities.inputs: Distance; Factor; Trace Precision; Edge Strength; Edge Thickness

capabilities.does: Puzzle-enabled post effects with parameters: Afterimage (level), Bloom (threshold, strength, radius), Brightness/Contrast, Depth of Field (focus, aperture, maxblur), Grayscale, Simple Refraction, and Screen Space Reflection/Refraction (steps, max distance, resolution, stride, jitter).

Skeletal animation, object transform animation, node value animation, shape keys, and constraints such as Copy Location/Rotation/Scale, Limit Distance, Damped Track, Track To and Floor in Blender (equivalents in Max and Maya).

Ammo.js (Bullet) physics with dynamic, static, kinematic and ghost bodies, a capsule character setup, continuous collision detection (ccd motion threshold, ccd swept sphere radius); puzzles create bodies, apply params, snap bodies, set state and detect collisions.
capabilities.inputs: create physics body; apply body param; detect collisions; on simulation tick

capabilities.does: The physics module covers collision detection, dynamic objects, characters and vehicles, springs, ropes and cloth through Puzzles or JavaScript.

WebXR VR on Meta Quest 1-3 and HTC Vive, AR in Chrome for Android (ARCore) and WebXR Viewer on iOS, and Safari USDZ Quick Look; puzzles enter VR/AR mode, detect horizontal surfaces and handle sessions. WebXR needs HTTPS.
capabilities.inputs: enter VR mode; enter AR mode; detect horizontal surface AR; export to USDZ

capabilities.does: Export can convert JPEG and PNG textures to KTX2 with Basis Universal: Auto (UASTC), UASTC (all types), ETC1S (smallest) or Disable; NPOT textures are skipped; HDR images use lossless LZMA.
Scene files can be LZMA-compressed to .xz (about 20x for .gltf, 6x for .bin); enabled in export settings and the configure application puzzle.
Publishing to own server, Verge3D Network, SCORM LMS, mobile app stores through wrapping, and desktop apps via Electron; progressive web app creation; WordPress and WooCommerce integration.
capabilities.outputs: web, mobile, desktop and LMS deliverables

capabilities.does: Puzzles reference spans initialization, events, selectors, objects, materials, animation, cameras and lights, scenes, time, HTML, AR/VR, audio and video, physics, post-processing, logic, loops, lists, dictionaries, variables, procedures, e-commerce and SCORM.
HTML5 audio for music, WebAudio for short samples, a basic synthesiser with 100+ instruments and MIDI files, and Blender speaker support with distance and cone properties.
JavaScript programming against a three.js-partially-compatible API; HTML-based UI, text rendering and custom HTML/CSS layouts.

rea.notes: Source code access is stated as part of Enterprise and Ultimate editions; licence text not read. Manual describes features only.

entries.name: Needle Engine

licence.name: Not stated on the pages read; licences are managed through Needle Cloud

engines.name: Web runtime on three.js
engines.does: TypeScript component runtime that draws with three.js and loads glTF scenes exported from Unity or Blender, or built in code.

engines.name: Rapier physics
engines.does: Built-in rigid bodies, colliders, raycasts and character controllers.

engines.name: Networking layer
engines.does: Rooms, synced transforms, per-user avatars, voice chat and screen share.

engines.name: Needle Mesh Baker
engines.does: Browser tool that reduces geometry and bakes materials for heavy models.

engines.name: Needle Cloud
engines.does: Hosting, asset management and licence management service.

capabilities.does: Scenes are authored in Unity or Blender with an editor integration, or written in plain three.js with TypeScript; a Vite plug-in and instant web deployment (URL or QR code) are provided.
capabilities.inputs: Unity package; Blender add-on; Vite plugin

capabilities.does: Renderer components: MeshRenderer (lightmapping, instancing), SkinnedMeshRenderer, SpriteRenderer (sprite animation), ParticleSystem and VideoPlayer (streams including M3U8).
capabilities.outputs: meshes, sprites, particles and video in the scene

capabilities.does: Light component for directional, point and spot lights with shadows and baking; ContactShadows adds realtime contact shadows and ShadowCatcher an invisible shadow receiver.
Reflection probes and improved lightmapping arrived in the Blender integration 1.0.0; Unity and Blender both pass lightmaps and materials.
MaterialX materials with vertex displacement, realtime shadows, displacement animation and alpha-mode detection; OpenUSD files are supported in the browser.

A Volume component hosts post effects (pmndrs postprocessing; Unity needs URP): Antialiasing, Bloom, ChromaticAberration, ColorAdjustments, DepthOfField, Vignette, TiltShift, ToneMapping, Pixelation, Sharpening, SSAO, with custom effects supported.
GroundProjection projects an environment texture onto the ground; SeeThrough fades objects blocking the view; XRFlag and DeviceFlag switch visibility by XR mode or device.
Camera component (perspective or orthographic), OrbitControls (orbit, zoom, pan) and ViewBox for visible bounds.

WebXR for VR and AR with passthrough and avatars; native iOS WebXR, Meta Quest and Apple Vision Pro; XRRig, controller models, controller movement and teleport, image and plane tracking, WebARSessionRoot, USDZExporter for iOS Quick Look.
Animator (state machine with controller, transitions, conditions), Animation (single clip) and PlayableDirector (timelines for animation, audio and state).
DragControls, Duplicatable, SmoothFollow, Deletable and DeleteBox, DropListener, SpatialTrigger, CursorFollow, ScrollFollow and HoverAnimation provide ready interactions.

Rapier physics: Rigidbody (gravity, mass, drag; dynamic, kinematic or static), Box, Sphere, Capsule and Mesh colliders, physics materials for friction and bounce, Attractor, triggers, raycasting and character controllers.

SyncedRoom turns on multiplayer; SyncedTransform syncs position, rotation and scale; SyncedCamera shares views; PlayerSync spawns an object per user; Voip gives spatial voice chat over WebRTC; ScreenCapture shares screens; Networking configures a custom backend.
AudioListener on the camera and AudioSource with spatial audio playback.
Canvas (screen or world space), Text with custom fonts, Button, Image, RawImage and InputField render a UI in 3D scenes; SceneSwitcher loads scenes, prefabs and glTF with preload and URL navigation.
GltfExport can export a glTF at runtime (experimental) and DropListener receives dropped files.
Needle Mesh Baker reduces geometry, bakes materials and produces PBR textures; its example cuts 880,000 triangles to 6,000. A compression pipeline built on glTF supports delivery.
Debug helpers GridHelper, BoxGizmo and AxesHelper plus static Gizmos methods for debug drawing in code.

entries.name: Wonderland Engine

licence.name: Standard plan free up to $120k annual revenue, 10% royalty above; seated and enterprise plans by quote; API code is MIT; runtime and editor under a separate EULA (text not read)

engines.name: WebAssembly runtime
engines.does: C++ engine compiled to WebAssembly (about 580 kB gzipped) with SIMD and threads when available, a dual-quaternion scene graph and runtime batching.

engines.name: Wonderland Editor
engines.does: Desktop editor with an integrated live-reload web server, packaging that converts assets to a binary format, CLI, views and plug-ins.

engines.name: JavaScript API
engines.does: TypeScript and JavaScript API (MIT) with component classes, resources and managers, used to write custom components.

engines.name: Wonderland Cloud
engines.does: Hosting with servers, pages, cloud APIs and subscriptions.

capabilities.does: Meshes that share a shader are joined at runtime so many objects draw in one call, with a material list to vary parts; textures are combined into atlases automatically. The page claims tens of thousands of objects in under 10 draw calls.
capabilities.outputs: few draw calls for large scenes

capabilities.does: Compressed GPU textures plus streaming of texture pieces based on what the camera sees, to fit high-resolution textures on memory-limited devices.
Basis Universal: images compress to one intermediate format that is transcoded to each device GPU format at load; Basis files load at runtime but cannot be imported into the editor.
The editor converts glTF, OBJ and other text formats to a compact binary format at packaging time, with mesh property quantisation, animation quantisation and removal of redundant keyframes.

Well-supported scene imports: FBX, glTF/GLB, OBJ and PLY (skinned meshes only from FBX, glTF, GLB); also COLLADA, 3ds Max, STL, BVH. Images: WebP, JPEG, PNG, BMP, PSD, TGA, HDR, GIF; video plays at runtime in browser-supported formats.
capabilities.inputs: FBX; glTF; OBJ; PLY; image formats

capabilities.does: LightComponent with lightType, color, intensity, spot innerAngle and outerAngle (degrees), shadows flag, shadowBias, shadowNormalBias, shadowRange, shadowTexelSize and cascadeCount for sun shadows.
capabilities.inputs: lightType; intensity; innerAngle; outerAngle; shadowBias; cascadeCount

capabilities.does: GI probe volumes arrived in release 1.4.0.
Release 1.6.0 (March 2026) introduced meshlets and screen-space ambient occlusion; 1.4.0 added reverse-Z depth.

Custom fragment shaders (no vertex shader API) in GLSL with a Material struct that drives packed inputs and the editor UI: float, uint, int, vec2-4, ivec2-4 with lowp/mediump precision; FEATURE_ defines become pipeline toggles; USE_ symbols enable fragment inputs.
capabilities.inputs: Material struct; FEATURE_<name>; USE_<input>; viewIndex uniform

capabilities.does: PhysXComponent: flags allowQuery, allowSimulation, simulate, gravity, kinematic, static, trigger, sleepOnActivate; linearDamping, angularDamping, staticFriction, dynamicFriction, bounciness, mass, inertia tensor, axis locks, shapes (Sphere, Capsule, Box, Plane, TriangleMesh, ConvexHull), groupsMask and blocksMask, offsets.
capabilities.inputs: shape; mass; linearDamping; groupsMask; blocksMask; addForce(f, mode); onCollision(cb)

capabilities.does: Designed for WebXR with VR and AR, controller input and WebXR Device API; integrations with 8th Wall and AR.js.
Custom reusable components in JavaScript or TypeScript, integration of JS/TS libraries and any browser functionality, and properties exposed to the editor.

Native components: AnimationComponent, CollisionComponent, InputComponent, LightComponent, MeshComponent, ParticleEffectComponent, PhysXComponent, TextComponent, ViewComponent; resources include AnimationGraph, MorphTargets, Skin, Material, Pipeline, Texture and Font.
Editor features: integrated web server, fast packaging with file watching and automatic reload, prebuilt components configurable through the UI; runs on Windows, macOS and Linux.
Release and deploy pages plus Wonderland Cloud (servers, pages, cloud APIs, subscriptions, development flow); projects are shared by URL.

rea.notes: JS API repository is MIT per its README summary; runtime and editor are under the Wonderland Engine EULA, which was not read. docs.wonderlandengine.com failed to load (socket closed), so pages on wonderlandengine.com were used.

entries.verified: 2026-11-02, how: site pages, API pages and news page read

entries.name: Spline
