licence.name: Free tier plus Hobby, Pro and Max subscriptions; AI credits metered (prices not read)

engines.name: 3D editor
engines.does: Browser editor for modelling, sculpting, materials, lighting, cameras, particles, physics and animation.

engines.name: Hana
engines.does: Companion 2D canvas for interfaces and animated graphics sharing the same interaction model.

engines.name: Web runtime
engines.does: @splinetool/runtime and react-spline run published scenes in the browser on WebGPU or WebGL.

engines.name: State, event and action system
engines.does: No-code interactivity: events such as mouse, key, scroll, collision and variable change drive actions such as transitions, sound, camera switch and object creation.

capabilities.does: Materials are stacks of layers: colour, vertex colour, gradient, image, video, pattern, noise, rainbow, lighting, toon, matcap, fresnel, glass, reflection, depth, normal, bump and roughness maps, displace, cavity, dust and outline, with layer masking.

A library of hundreds of materials in stylised categories (gradient, subsurface scattering, patterns, noise, cartoon and outline, colourful metal) and real-world categories (metal, ceramic, marble, transparent, concrete, stone, wood, fabric, nature); full access needs a paid plan.
Glass layer with three settings: Blur (frosted look), Thickness (bending and distortion) and Refraction (clarity or distortion of objects behind).
Directional, Point and Spot lights are added from the toolbar; new scenes start with an Ambient light and a Directional light, and the ambient light is edited in the Environment panel.
capabilities.inputs: Directional Light; Point Light; Spot Light; Ambient Light

capabilities.does: Depth of Field effect with Focus Distance (set with a focus point tool), Depth of Field (width of the sharp zone) and Blur strength.
capabilities.inputs: Focus Distance; Depth of Field; Blur

capabilities.does: Scene effects panel: Depth of Field, Pixelation, Aberration, Bloom, Hue, Brightness, Vignette and Noise; the page warns that stacking effects reduces exported-scene performance.

Physics is enabled in the Simulation panel (gravity setting) and per object: Body Type (Positioned or Dynamic), Collider (Precise or simpler), Weight, Gravity Scale, Friction, Damping, Bounce, and translation and rotation locks; groups can have Separate child physics.
capabilities.inputs: Body Type; Collider; Weight; Gravity Scale; Friction; Damping; Bounce

capabilities.does: Emitters (Plane, Box, Sphere, Torus, Cone, Custom Shape) with Emit Time (Infinite, Loop, One Time), colour A and B, size and fades, birth rate, lifetime, speed, orientation, image, gravity, noise (Curl, Simplex, Fbm) and particle forces Collider, Attractor and Vortex.
capabilities.inputs: Birth Rate; Lifetime; Noise type; Attractor; Vortex; Particle Control Action

capabilities.does: Cloner modifier with Radial, Linear, Grid and Object modes (count, radius, spacing, spread by polygon centre, edge or vertex, alignment) and Randomness (strength, Perlin or Simplex noise, transform, seed, movement); all parameters can be animated through states.
capabilities.inputs: Count; Radius; Spread; Randomness Strength; Seed

capabilities.does: Hair system grows simulated strands from a surface for hair, fur, grass or carpet, with length, curl, clumping, tip spread, root colour, stiffness, wind and damping; renders on WebGPU only.
capabilities.inputs: Hair Shape; Physics (stiffness, wind, damping); root/mid/tip colour

capabilities.does: Events include start, mouse, key, scroll, look at, follow, distance, state or variable change, collision, drag and drop, trigger area, webhook. Actions include transition, sound, video, open link, camera switch, create or destroy object, scene transition, particles control, variable set, conditional, API request.
capabilities.inputs: Start Event; Collision Event; Transition Action; Switch Camera Action; Conditional Action

capabilities.does: The web packages @splinetool/runtime (vanilla JS) and react-spline (React wrapper) can read and update scene variables, change object properties such as position, scale and rotation, trigger transitions and listen to real-time events.

Publish to a public URL, Spline Viewer embed, exported code, self-hosted project; native 3D embeds and generated app projects for iOS (SwiftUI) and Android (Jetpack Compose, APK, AAB); Spline Mirror for visionOS.
capabilities.inputs: Export as Public URL / Viewer / Code / Self-Hosted
capabilities.outputs: shipping interactive 3D to web and apps

capabilities.does: glTF/GLB export carries geometry plus either a default grey material or the colour layer and textures on primitives (paid plans), and only position, rotation and scale timeline animation; physics, states, post-processing, lighting and fog are not exported.
The index lists Variables, a Real-time API, Webhooks, AI text (OpenAI) and AI voice assistant APIs, a Code tab, and code APIs for web, SwiftUI and Kotlin.
capabilities.inputs: Variables; Real-time API; Webhooks; Code Tab
capabilities.outputs: scenes connected to data and services

capabilities.does: File export pages cover image, video, image sequences, glTF/GLB, USDZ and STL (3D printing).

Guidance: fewer than 3 lights per scene, at most 3 subdivision levels, fewer sides on parametric shapes, image compression in Play Settings (up to 4x smaller files), geometry compression with Performance quality, one to three embeds per page.
AI 3D generation and prompt-based scene building in the editor, plus an MCP server that lets external agents such as Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor or Codex read and write the scene and render views.
capabilities.inputs: AI agent; AI 3D generation; Spline MCP server

capabilities.does: Timeline animation plus state-based animation: the index lists pages on timeline animation, how state-based animation works and animatable properties, with transitions triggered by events.

rea.notes: Editor is a closed web application; docs cover use and export. Entered as kind engine as the task asked; it is a design tool with a runtime.

entries.verified: 2026-11-02, how: documentation pages and llms.txt index read

entries.name: Armory3D (Armory Engine)

licence.name: Zlib

engines.name: Blender add-on
engines.does: Blender integration where scenes, materials, logic nodes, traits and render settings are authored and exported.

engines.name: Render path
engines.does: Scriptable forward and deferred render paths built at compile time; unused passes are removed.

engines.name: Physics
engines.does: Bullet through Haxebullet, or the lighter Oimo engine.

engines.name: Logic nodes and traits
engines.does: Visual logic trees and Haxe, bundled or UI traits attached to objects and scenes.

engines.name: Navmesh
engines.does: Recast-based navigation mesh generation through a bundled trait.

capabilities.does: Forward and deferred renderers are supported out of the box; the render path is built at game compile time; extra passes use path.setTarget, path.bindTarget and path.drawShader; a custom RenderPathCreator.hx replaces the internal path and iron.RenderPath.setActive swaps paths at runtime.

Materials use Blender EEVEE and Cycles nodes. Supported: Mix Shader, Add Shader, Diffuse, Glossy, Emission, Transparent; partial: Principled BSDF, Glass, Holdout, Anisotropic (as Glossy), Translucent, Velvet, Subsurface, Refraction; unsupported: Toon, Specular, volume nodes.

Armory Props per material: Blending (additive), Alpha Test, Read Depth (soft particles), and exposed RGB, Value and Image Texture parameters driven at runtime. A Shader Data node reads engine uniforms such as _pointPosition.
capabilities.inputs: Blending; Alpha Test; Read Depth; Parameters

capabilities.does: Render path Displacement setting: Off, Vertex or Tessellation; tessellation subdivides before moving vertices along normals, detail set by Mesh and Shadow properties; smooth shading recommended.

Voxel cone tracing GI and voxel AO need OpenGL 4.4 or Direct3D 11. Settings: Dimensions (default 16 units), Resolution (128 or below), Resolution Z, Revoxelize, Dynamic Camera, Temporal Filter, Cones, Occlusion, Step, Range, Offset.
capabilities.inputs: Render Path > Voxel AO; Dimensions; Resolution; Revoxelize

capabilities.does: Screen-space ray-traced AO (RTAO with Rays, Step, Max Steps, Strength), contact shadows (SSRS with Step) and reflections (SSR with Step).
Static scenes can bake lightmaps through the Armory Bake tool using Cycles; set the preset to 2D/Baked. Cubemap and plane probes are supported.
Options: none, MSAA (1 to 16, forward path), FXAA (fastest, blurs), SMAA, TAA (needs velocity buffer) and supersampling.

Screen effects: auto exposure (strength 0.7), bloom (threshold 1, strength 3.5, radius 3), film grain, fish-eye, lens flares, lens textures, letterboxing, LUT colour grading (512x512), motion blur (object and camera), SSRS, SSR, tonemapping (Filmic, ACES, Reinhard, Uncharted), vignette, volumetric fog and light.

Bullet via Haxebullet by default or Oimo; rigid bodies are Dynamic, Static or Kinematic with Mass, Friction, Bounciness and shapes Box, Sphere, Capsule, Cylinder, Cone, Mesh and Convex Hull. Physics objects should have scale 1.0; Bullet can become unstable below about 50 Hz.
capabilities.inputs: Physics Engine property; Rigid Body panel

capabilities.does: Rigid body constraints restrict axes or attach two bodies, added in the Logic node editor or the Physics tab; the page also lists sections for triggers, raycasts, vehicles, soft bodies and cloth.

Experimental particle support: Emitter or Hair type, Number, frames, Lifetime, Seed, Emit From (vertices, faces, volume), Newtonian physics with size and mass, render as Object, GPU simulation by default (CPU optional) and GPU instancing.
Terrain generator in Scene Properties makes sectors from greyscale heightmap PNGs named heightmap_<n>.png with Sectors, Sector Size and Height Scale; each sector gets a Bullet height-field shape.

Traits: Haxe scripts, WebAssembly, UI canvas, Bundled (for example character controllers) and Nodes. Callbacks notifyOnAdd, notifyOnInit, notifyOnRemove, notifyOnUpdate, notifyOnRender, notifyOnRender2D.
Navigation uses Recast (haxerecast) by default; the Navmesh bundled trait has a Generate Navmesh button; the module is left out when the scene has none.
The wiki lists build pages for Windows, Linux, macOS, HTML5, Android, iOS and consoles, plus an APK tutorial.

outcomes: games and interactive apps from Blender scenes

rea.notes: Zlib licence per repository page. Haxe and Kha used; Kha/Iron engine repositories not separately read. Wiki pages cited are GitHub wiki.

entries.verified: 2026-11-02, how: GitHub README and wiki pages read

entries.name: LayaAir

licence.name: MIT

engines.name: Rendering
engines.does: TypeScript renderer on WebGL, WebGPU, OpenGL and Vulkan paths with programmable pipelines, PBR streams, ClusterLighting and Forward+.

engines.name: d3 module
engines.does: The 3D module with animation, component, core, depth map, graphics, loaders, physics, post-process, shader, shadow map, WebXR and UI3D folders.

engines.name: LayaAir IDE
engines.does: Editor with 3D scene, material, particle, blueprint, animation, physics and UI editors, a plug-in store and AI generation tools.

engines.name: Post-process effects
engines.does: Bloom, colour grading, Gaussian depth of field, scalable AO, temporal AA, lens flares and material-based effects.

capabilities.does: The README lists programmable render pipelines, a new PBR rendering stream, ClusterLighting multi-light support and Forward+ rendering, on WebGL, WebGPU, OpenGL and Vulkan.

Core materials in the d3 module: BlinnPhongMaterial, PBRStandardMaterial, PBRMaterial (with PBRRenderQuality), UnlitMaterial, EffectMaterial, ExtendTerrainMaterial and sky materials (SkyBox, SkyPanoramic, SkyProcedural).
Light component classes cover directional, point, spot and area lights, with ShadowMode and ShadowCascadesMode settings and a LightQueue.
The shadowMap folder holds ShadowCasterPass, ShadowLightType and ShadowSliceData for per-light and per-slice shadow rendering.
Scene3D support files include Lightmap and AmbientMode alongside the scene render manager.

BloomEffect: intensity (1.0), threshold (1.0), softKnee (0.5, 0-1), diffusion (7, range 1-10), anamorphicRatio (-1 to 1), clamp (65472), colour tint, fastMode, lens dirt texture with dirtIntensity, resolutionScale (0.125-2).
capabilities.inputs: intensity; threshold; softKnee; diffusion; anamorphicRatio; dirtTexture

capabilities.does: ScalableAO is a screen-space AO effect with aoColor, intensity (0.12), radius (0.15) and aoQuality High, MEDIUM or LOWEST; it needs depth and depth-normals textures and blurs horizontally then vertically.

ColorGradEffect bakes settings into a 32x32x32 LUT: ACES tone mapping, white balance (temperature, tint), split toning, shadows/midtones/highlights with limits, lift/gamma/gain, post exposure, contrast, colour filter, hue shift and saturation. Custom LUT is marked TODO.
capabilities.inputs: toneMapping None | ACES; temperature; tint; lift; gamma; gain; contrast; saturation

capabilities.does: GaussianDoF blurs only the far field: farStart (10), farEnd (30), maxRadius (0-2, default 1); a circle-of-confusion pass, half-resolution prefilter and separable Gaussian blur. Near-field blur is not supported.

TemporalAAEffect blends the frame with a history texture using depth, motion and view-projection matrices; quality VeryLow to VeryHigh (five shader variants); RCAS sharpening through camera TAA settings.
LensFlares folder and LensFlareSettingsLoader provide a lens flare post effect loaded from settings.

Physics: Rigidbody3D, PhysicsCollider, CharacterController, WheelCollider and PhysicsVehicleComponent; shapes Box, Capsule, Compound, Cone, Cylinder, HeightField, Mesh and Sphere; HitResult and ContactPoint for queries.
Constraint classes: FixedConstraint, HingeConstraint, SpringConstraint and ConfigurableConstraint on a ConstraintComponent base.

The animation folder has AnimationClip with parser versions 03 and 04, AnimationEvent, AnimatorStateScript and KeyframeNode lists; skinned meshes use SkinnedMeshRenderer and SimpleSkinnedMeshRenderer.

LayaAir IDE has 3D scene, material, particle, blueprint, animation, physics and UI editors; users can upload plug-ins to a resource store; an AIGC framework covers AI generation, AI control of the IDE and AI customer service.
Build targets: HTML5 web, native apps for Android, iOS, Mac, Windows and Linux, and mini-games for WeChat, ByteDance, Alipay, OPPO, vivo and Xiaomi.

rea.notes: MIT per repository page. The official documentation site renders with scripts and returned no table of contents, so this entry relies on the repository README and source files (LayaAir_3.4 branch).

entries.verified: 2026-11-02, how: repository README, source tree pages and post-effect source files read

entries.name: Cycles

licence.name: Apache-2.0 for the Cycles code (cycles-renderer.org and the standalone repository page); the surrounding Blender application is GPL 2-or-later, binaries GPL 3-or-later (blender.org licence page)

engines.name: Path-tracing core
engines.does: Physically based path tracer used by Blender for final renders and the Rendered viewport; one engine for CPU and several GPU backends.

engines.name: Compute backends
engines.does: CPU plus CUDA, OptiX, HIP, oneAPI and Metal device backends, selectable in preferences or on the command line.

engines.name: Sampling and denoising
engines.does: Adaptive sampling, light tree, path guiding, and OpenImageDenoise or OptiX denoisers, all set in the Sampling panel.

engines.name: Shading system
engines.does: Node-based shaders (Principled BSDF and friends) plus optional Open Shading Language script nodes.

engines.name: Light and world sampling
engines.does: Light objects, emissive meshes, sky and environment lighting with importance sampling, portals and light linking.

engines.name: Baking
engines.does: Bakes shading, lighting and geometry data (combined, AO, normal, position, UV and more) into image textures or vertex colours.

engines.name: Standalone application and Hydra delegate
engines.does: The Cycles repository builds as a standalone command-line renderer reading XML scenes, or as a Hydra render delegate.

capabilities.does: Cycles is a physically based path tracer for final renders and the Rendered viewport; it is chosen as the render engine in Render properties, and GPU devices are enabled in preferences.
Hardware ray tracing: always on with OptiX on RTX cards, on HIP for Radeon RX 6000 or newer (a preference toggle), with oneAPI on Intel Arc and with Metal on Apple Silicon.
capabilities.outputs: Faster ray traversal on supported GPUs

capabilities.does: Renders on the CPU. This is the only device that supports every Cycles feature; thread count is set in the Performance panel or on the command line.
capabilities.inputs: Device = CPU; Threads mode (Auto-Detect or Fixed), Threads
capabilities.outputs: Frames rendered on all or a fixed number of cores

capabilities.does: CUDA backend for NVIDIA GPUs of compute capability 5.0 or higher on Windows and Linux; ships precompiled kernels.
capabilities.inputs: Preferences > System > Cycles Render Devices = CUDA
capabilities.outputs: GPU path tracing on NVIDIA cards without hardware ray tracing

capabilities.does: OptiX backend for NVIDIA RTX cards. Uses hardware ray-tracing units, supports GPU Open Image Denoise on compute 7.0+, and is the only GPU backend that runs Open Shading Language.
capabilities.inputs: Cycles device = OptiX; driver 575 or newer
capabilities.outputs: Hardware-accelerated GPU rendering and OSL on GPU

capabilities.does: HIP backend for AMD RDNA1-or-newer GPUs and APUs on Windows and Linux; hardware ray tracing needs RX 6000 or newer and is switched on in preferences.
capabilities.inputs: Cycles device = HIP; optional hardware ray tracing toggle
capabilities.outputs: GPU path tracing on AMD cards

capabilities.does: oneAPI backend for Intel Arc (Xe HPG) GPUs on Windows and Linux, with hardware ray tracing and GPU denoising.
capabilities.outputs: GPU path tracing on Intel Arc cards

capabilities.does: Metal backend for Apple Silicon Macs, with GPU ray tracing and denoising; macOS 13.0 or newer for all features.
capabilities.outputs: GPU path tracing on Apple Silicon

capabilities.does: Several GPUs can render together; NVLink-linked NVIDIA cards can pool memory, and CUDA, OptiX, HIP and Metal fall back to system memory when GPU memory is full.
capabilities.inputs: Compute device list; Distributed Memory Across Devices option
capabilities.outputs: Larger scenes than one card holds, at some speed cost

capabilities.does: The --cycles-device switch picks CPU, CUDA, OPTIX, HIP, ONEAPI or METAL for a headless run; adding +CPU to a GPU name uses both together.
capabilities.outputs: Device choice without opening the UI

capabilities.does: Sets the number of paths traced per pixel, with separate counts for the Rendered viewport (0 means keep sampling) and the final render.
capabilities.outputs: Noise level traded against render time

capabilities.does: Ends the render once a time budget is used up, whatever the sample count; zero turns the limit off, and scene preparation time is excluded.
Stops sampling a pixel once its estimated noise falls below a threshold, with a minimum sample count before the test starts.
capabilities.inputs: Noise Threshold (typical 0.1 to 0.001, 0 = automatic), Min Samples (0 = automatic)
capabilities.outputs: Fewer samples spent on clean areas

capabilities.does: Chooses which light to sample with a tree that weighs distance and estimated brightness. Cuts noise in scenes with many emitters, costs more per sample, and makes light linking efficient.
Skips light samples whose contribution would fall under a cut-off value; zero turns the test off.
Chooses the random number pattern: Automatic, Classic (precomputed Owen-scrambled Sobol) or Blue-Noise.
Cuts pixel-to-pixel randomness to speed up GPU rendering at the risk of artifacts. Modes are Automatic, Viewport and a Multiplier below one; not usable with Blue-Noise.
Seed value changes the noise pattern; an animated-seed option changes it every frame so animation noise does not stay fixed.
Minimum number of light bounces before Russian roulette may end a path, and a matching minimum for transparent bounces.
capabilities.inputs: Min Light Bounces, Min Transparent Bounces
capabilities.outputs: Less noise at some render-time cost

capabilities.does: View layers can override the scene sample count: use the layer value, cap it at the scene count, or ignore it.
Renders only part of the sample range, so one frame can be split over several machines and the results combined.
capabilities.inputs: Sample Subset offset (0-based start index), length

capabilities.does: CPU-only learning of good light directions during the render, for surfaces and optionally volumes. Not supported on any GPU.
capabilities.inputs: Training Samples (0 = until end; about 128 to 256 usual), Surface, Volume

capabilities.does: Removes render noise after sampling. Viewport and render denoising are toggled separately; denoiser is Automatic, OpenImageDenoise or OptiX (NVIDIA only).
Chooses extra data the denoiser reads next to colour: none, Albedo, or Albedo plus Normal.
capabilities.outputs: Better edge and texture detail after denoising

capabilities.does: OpenImageDenoise can clean its albedo and normal inputs first: None keeps most detail, Fast and Accurate trade speed for cleaner inputs.
capabilities.outputs: Control of detail against input noise

capabilities.does: OpenImageDenoise quality level for the whole denoise pass.
Denoising can run on the GPU (more GPU memory used), and viewport denoising can be delayed until a chosen sample.
Writes the noisy image with denoising albedo, specular albedo, normal, roughness and depth, so denoising can be run later in compositing.
capabilities.inputs: Denoising Data pass in View Layer
capabilities.outputs: Multi-channel EXR for external or later denoise

capabilities.does: Compositor Denoise nodes get their own device (Auto, CPU, GPU) and preview and final quality (High, Balanced, Fast) in Performance settings.
capabilities.inputs: Denoising Device, Preview Quality, Final Quality
capabilities.outputs: Denoise node speed and quality control

capabilities.does: Caps path length overall and per interaction type; zero total gives direct light only.
capabilities.inputs: Max Bounces: Total, Diffuse, Glossy, Transmission, Volume, Transparent
capabilities.outputs: Balance of realism against noise and time

capabilities.does: Limits the brightness a single sample adds to a pixel to suppress fireflies, separately for direct and indirect light; zero disables it.
capabilities.outputs: Fewer bright outlier pixels, slightly dimmer highlights

capabilities.does: Blurs sharp glossy reflections after a blurry bounce to cut noise; any value above zero turns it on and 1.0 is a starting point.
Switches off reflective or refractive caustic paths to remove their noise, at the cost of some real light.
After a chosen bounce count, swaps global illumination for ambient occlusion (Replace) or adds AO on diffuse surfaces (Add).
capabilities.inputs: Method, AO Factor, AO Distance, Viewport Bounces, Render Bounces

capabilities.does: Default volume rendering uses an unbiased null-scattering method; a Biased option switches to ray marching with step controls.
Global step-size multipliers for biased ray marching, separate for renders and the viewport; per object, material or world step sizes override the automatic value.
capabilities.inputs: Step Rate Render, Step Rate Viewport, Step Size

capabilities.does: Caps the number of marching steps through one volume so large objects or tiny step sizes cannot stall a render.
Renders hair strands as rounded ribbons (fastest), true 3D curves with automatic subdivision, or linear 3D curves with straight segments (CPU and GPU may differ).
capabilities.inputs: Shape = Rounded Ribbons | 3D Curves | Linear 3D Curves

capabilities.does: For rounded ribbons, sets a power-of-two subdivision count for intersecting cardinal curves; a viewport shape (Strand or Strip) and extra subdivisions are set separately for Material Preview.
capabilities.inputs: Curve Subdivisions, Viewport Shape, Additional Subdivisions

capabilities.does: Dices subdivision-surface meshes into micropolygons sized by a dicing rate, with a coarser rate off-screen and a cap on subdivision level.
capabilities.inputs: Dicing Rate Render/Viewport, Offscreen Scale, Max Subdivisions
capabilities.outputs: Detail only where the camera sees it

capabilities.does: Names a camera used as the reference for dicing, so tessellation does not crawl when the scene camera moves.
Scene-wide limits for speed and memory: cap on subdivision level, share of child particles shown, and texture size limit with texture downscale.
capabilities.inputs: Max Subdivision, Child Particles, Texture Resolution, Texture Size Limit
capabilities.outputs: Lighter scenes for preview or render

capabilities.does: Viewport-only simplification: lower volume object resolution (percentage) and skip custom normal computation.
Hides objects outside the camera view, and optionally objects beyond a set distance from it.
capabilities.inputs: Camera Cull + Margin, Distance Cull + Distance
capabilities.outputs: Fewer objects loaded for large scenes

capabilities.does: Blurs moving objects and camera over a shutter interval placed at the start, centre or end of the frame.
capabilities.inputs: Position = Start | Center | End on Frame; Shutter (frames)
capabilities.outputs: Blur from object, camera and deformation motion

capabilities.does: Simulates a rolling shutter that scans top to bottom; a duration slider mixes pure rolling shutter (0) with pure motion blur (1).
capabilities.inputs: Rolling Shutter = None | Top-Bottom; Rolling Shutter Duration

capabilities.does: A custom curve describes how open the shutter is over time (x is time, y from closed to open); default is an instant open and close.
Per-object option to blur deforming meshes such as characters and hair, with a step count that sets accuracy and memory use. Topology-changing modifiers can break it.
Brightens or darkens the data itself in the film settings, separate from the colour-management exposure that only changes the view transform.
Reconstruction filter that softens edges and reduces aliasing: Box, Gaussian or Blackman-Harris (the default), with a width control.
Renders the background as transparent for compositing; Transparent Glass also makes glass see-through, except surfaces above a roughness threshold.
Renders large images in tiles to save memory; the tile size defaults to 2048 pixels and smaller sizes help when memory runs out.
Keeps scene data in memory between frames or re-renders so animations restart faster, using extra memory; only one view layer is kept.
BVH options: spatial splits for scenes mixing big and small polygons, a dedicated curves BVH, motion BVH time steps, and a compact BVH that saves RAM (hidden with OptiX).
capabilities.inputs: Use Spatial Splits, Use Curves BVH, BVH Time Steps, Use Compact BVH
capabilities.outputs: Speed against build time and memory

capabilities.does: Converts textures to .tx files to cut memory use and start-up time in texture-heavy scenes, with auto-generate, generate-all and clear actions.
capabilities.inputs: Use Texture Cache, Auto Generate, Generate, Clear

capabilities.does: Three presets for the performance panel: Default, Faster Render (more memory) and Lower Memory (slower), plus viewport pixel size to lower preview resolution.
capabilities.outputs: Quick tuning of speed against memory

capabilities.does: The manual lists practical noise fixes: fewer bounces, lower colour values, no caustics, filter glossy, light falloff smooth, material and world importance sampling, an optimised glass shader, portals, denoising and clamping.

Before rendering, shader graphs are simplified: constant folding, removal of no-op math and mix nodes, merging duplicate nodes, dropping unused nodes, and skipping unused Mix Shader branches at run time.
Principled BSDF core inputs: base colour, metallic blend (dielectric to metal), microfacet roughness, IOR (default 1.5), alpha, a thin-wall switch and a normal input.
capabilities.inputs: Base Color, Metallic, Roughness, IOR, Alpha, Thin Wall, Normal

capabilities.does: Cycles-only diffuse roughness: zero gives Lambertian reflection, higher values switch to Oren-Nayar.
Light scatters under the surface with a per-channel radius and scale; methods are Christensen-Burley, Random Walk, Random Walk (Skin) and Random Walk (Legacy, to be removed).
capabilities.inputs: Method, Weight, Radius, Scale, IOR, Anisotropy (-0.9 to 0.9)
capabilities.outputs: Skin, wax, marble and leaf looks

capabilities.does: Standalone Subsurface Scattering node with colour, scale, radius, IOR, anisotropy and a roughness for the glossy layer above; the Random Walk methods and the three extra inputs are Cycles only.
capabilities.inputs: Color, Scale, Radius, IOR, Anisotropy, Roughness, Normal; Subsurface Method

capabilities.does: Specular layer controls: GGX or Multiscatter GGX distribution, IOR Level that scales reflectivity (0.5 neutral), and a specular tint colour.
Stretches highlights along the tangent, with a rotation input (add 0.25 to match the Glossy BSDF) and a Tangent input for direction. Cycles only.
Transmission weight blends from opaque to fully refractive using the base colour, roughness and IOR.
Clear coat layer with its own weight, roughness, IOR, absorption tint and normal.
capabilities.inputs: Coat Weight, Roughness, IOR, Tint, Normal

capabilities.does: Soft rim reflection layer for cloth, with weight, roughness and tint.
Emission node with colour and strength; a strength of 1.0 on a material shows the colour unchanged, and emissive meshes light the scene (surface strength in W/m2).
Thin-film interference tints specular reflection by view angle; thickness in nanometres (0 disables) and film IOR (default 1.33). Cycles only, also on the Glass BSDF.
capabilities.inputs: Thin Film Thickness, Thin Film IOR

capabilities.does: Glass BSDF with colour, roughness, IOR and normal, and a distribution choice of GGX, Multiscatter GGX or Beckmann (Cycles only).
Principled Hair colour setups: direct RGB, melanin concentration with redness and tint, or an absorption coefficient, plus randomisation of colour and roughness per strand.
capabilities.inputs: Color Parametrization, Melanin, Melanin Redness, Tint, Absorption Coefficient, Random Color, Random Roughness

capabilities.does: Two hair scattering models: Chiang with roughness, radial roughness and coat, and Huang with aspect ratio, roughness and scale factors for reflection, transmission and secondary reflection.
capabilities.inputs: Roughness, Radial Roughness, Coat, IOR, Offset; Aspect Ratio, Reflection, Transmission, Secondary Reflection

capabilities.does: Single volume shader with scattering colour and density (or grid attributes), anisotropy, absorption colour, emission with blackbody, and temperature from a grid.
capabilities.inputs: Color, Density, Anisotropy, Absorption Color, Emission Strength/Color, Blackbody Intensity/Tint, Temperature, Attribute names

capabilities.does: Volume Scatter node with five phase functions: Henyey-Greenstein, Fournier-Forand (underwater), Draine (dust), Rayleigh and Mie (clouds, fog); the last four are Cycles only.
capabilities.inputs: Color, Density, Anisotropy, IOR, Backscatter, Alpha, Diameter

capabilities.does: Volume Absorption node that darkens and tints light passing through, with colour and density.
Material volume settings: sampling method (Distance, Equiangular, Multiple Importance), interpolation (Linear or Cubic) and biased step rate.
capabilities.inputs: Sampling Method, Interpolation, Step Rate Biased

capabilities.does: Displacement node moves the surface along the normal from a height texture, with midlevel, scale and object or world space; the material chooses bump only, true displacement, or both.
capabilities.inputs: Height, Midlevel (0.5), Scale, Normal, Space; Material Displacement method

capabilities.does: Vector Displacement node pushes the surface in any direction from a three-axis map, in object space for static meshes or tangent space for deforming ones.
Per-material choice of Displacement Only (moves vertices), Bump Only (changes normals, no silhouette change) or both; includes a bump map correction option to reduce shadow terminator artifacts.
capabilities.inputs: Displacement = Displacement Only | Bump Only | Displacement and Bump; Bump Map Correction

capabilities.does: Material setting that lets an emissive surface be sampled as a light: None, Auto, Front, Back or Front and Back.
Transparent BSDF materials can let shadows respect transparency; switching it off is faster and less accurate.
Holdout shader cuts a zero-alpha hole in the render so other footage shows through; it has no inputs or properties.
IES Texture node reads a photometric profile (embedded text block or external file) and outputs a factor that drives an Emission shader strength for real-lamp light patterns.

Open Shading Language: Script nodes run internal text or external .osl/.oso files; output parameters become sockets. Runs on CPU, or on GPU only with OptiX, with limits on texture lookups and noise functions.
capabilities.inputs: Shading System = Open Shading Language; Script node mode

capabilities.does: The Shader to RGB node converts shader output to a colour and lights it like a Blended material. The page marks it EEVEE only, so Cycles has no equivalent.
Point and spot lights have power, radius (soft shadows), soft falloff, and for spots an angle (1 to 180 degrees), blend and a cone display.
capabilities.inputs: Power, Radius, Soft Falloff, Spot Angle, Blend, Show Cone

capabilities.does: Area lights take a rectangle, square, disk or ellipse shape, with size values per shape.
capabilities.inputs: Shape, Size / Size X / Size Y

capabilities.does: Sun light with strength in W/m2 and an angular diameter that sets shadow softness.
Every light has blackbody temperature, colour, exposure (scales by 2^exposure) and a Normalize switch that keeps total power constant when size changes.
Spread narrows or widens how far an area light fans out: wider spread gives softer shadows, narrower acts like a gridded soft box.
Area lights can act as portals placed on windows or doors; they guide environment-light sampling into interiors and cut noise indoors.
Per-light Cycles settings: Max Bounces for that light, Cast Shadow off for speed, and Multiple Importance Sample to combine light and BSDF sampling.
capabilities.inputs: Max Bounces, Cast Shadow, Multiple Importance
capabilities.outputs: Noise and speed control per light

capabilities.does: A light can be marked as a refractive caustic caster, which pairs with the object-level caustic settings.
Objects can be marked as shadow-caustic casters or receivers, which uses an MNEE-based caustics speed-up with many limits.
capabilities.inputs: Cast Shadow Caustics, Receive Shadow Caustics (object)

capabilities.does: Limits which objects a light or emissive mesh lights by naming included or excluded receivers in a collection; emissive meshes support it in Cycles only, and it is most efficient with the light tree.
Limits which objects block a light and cast shadows from it through a blocker collection; costs extra rays.
World surface accepts a Background node; an Environment Texture node gives equirectangular or mirror-ball image lighting.
World sampling settings: multiple importance sampling (Auto, Manual or None), importance map resolution, max bounces, shadow caustics and whether the world casts shadows.
capabilities.inputs: Sampling, Map Resolution, Max Bounces, Cast Shadow
capabilities.outputs: Less noise from bright sky spots

capabilities.does: A world volume shader fills all space, useful for night or dark scenes; with it set, the world surface shader and sun lights have no effect.
Sky Texture node with Single Scattering and Multiple Scattering atmosphere models, sun disc (Cycles only), sun size, intensity, elevation and rotation.
capabilities.inputs: Sky Type, Sun Disc, Sun Size, Sun Intensity, Sun Elevation, Sun Rotation

capabilities.does: Atmosphere controls of the sky texture: altitude, air, aerosols and ozone densities, with legacy Preetham and Hosek/Wilkie models (turbidity, ground albedo) marked for removal.
capabilities.inputs: Altitude, Air, Aerosols, Ozone, Turbidity, Ground Albedo
capabilities.outputs: Sky colour from haze to clear

capabilities.does: Mist pass maps camera distance to 0 to 1 with start, depth and a falloff curve (Quadratic, Linear, Inverse Quadratic).
Camera lens controls: sensor fit (Auto, Horizontal, Vertical), sensor size, lens shift that keeps verticals straight, and clip start and end.
capabilities.inputs: Sensor Fit, Size/Width/Height, Shift X/Y, Clip Start/End

capabilities.does: Perspective lens type mimics normal vision, with zoom set by focal length in millimetres or by a field-of-view angle.
capabilities.inputs: Lens Type = Perspective, Focal Length / Field of View

capabilities.does: Orthographic lens keeps parallel lines parallel; Orthographic Scale sets apparent size.
Camera depth of field from a focus object or distance, f-stop, aperture blade count (minimum 3), blade rotation and anamorphic ratio.
capabilities.inputs: Focus Object, Focus Distance, F-Stop, Blades, Rotation, Ratio

capabilities.does: Cycles panoramic lens in Equirectangular (360 by 180 degrees, with latitude and longitude limits) or Equiangular Cubemap Face, which spreads detail more evenly for VR.
capabilities.inputs: Panorama Type, Min/Max Latitude and Longitude

capabilities.does: Fisheye Equisolid (focal length, field of view, sensor aware), Fisheye Equidistant (uses full sensor, dome projection) and Mirror Ball projections.
capabilities.inputs: Lens, Field of View (can exceed 360 degrees)

capabilities.does: Fisheye Lens Polynomial models a real lens with a fourth-degree polynomial mapping sensor position to view direction.
A Custom camera type is written in OSL (Cycles only), so any projection can be scripted.
Data passes: Combined, Depth, Mist, Position, Normal, Vector, UV, Grease Pencil, Denoising Data, plus an Alpha Threshold setting controlling which surfaces they record.
Direct, indirect and colour passes for diffuse, glossy and transmission, direct and indirect for volume, plus Emission, Environment, AO and Shadow Catcher.
Object Index and Material Index passes for ID masks, and debug passes Render Time (not on GPU) and Sample Count for checking adaptive sampling.
capabilities.inputs: Object Index, Material Index, Render Time, Sample Count

capabilities.does: Compositor Cryptomatte node builds mattes from a render layer or a multilayer EXR: pick objects or materials by name, get Image, Matte and Pick outputs. Sidecar files, node groups and volume objects are unsupported.
capabilities.inputs: Source, Scene/Image, Cryptomatte Layer, Matte ID; outputs Image, Matte, Pick

capabilities.does: Cryptomatte passes store Object, Material or Asset ID masks, with a Levels setting for how many objects can share a pixel.
Shader AOVs write custom colour or value passes from materials, and light groups give one Combined-like pass per group that sum back in compositing.
capabilities.inputs: AOV Output node, Light Group names

capabilities.does: Marks an object as a shadow catcher so it receives only shadows, to blend CG over footage; output depends on the Shadow Catcher pass being enabled.
Per-object ray visibility for Camera, Diffuse, Glossy, Transmission, Volume Scatter and Shadow rays; faster than doing the same with shader nodes.
capabilities.outputs: Objects hidden from selected ray types

capabilities.does: Geometry Offset and Shading Offset reduce shadow terminator artifacts on low-poly smooth meshes; Geometry Offset is preferred because it keeps energy.
capabilities.inputs: Shadow Terminator: Geometry Offset, Shading Offset

capabilities.does: Bake types: Combined, Ambient Occlusion, Shadow, Position, Normal, UV, Roughness, Emit, Environment, Diffuse, Glossy and Transmission, with a View From option for reflections.
Combined and pass bakes can include direct and indirect lighting and each contribution (diffuse, glossy, transmission, emit), with or without colour.
Normal bakes are written in tangent space (default, works for animation) or object space, with swizzle controls for each colour channel.
High-poly to low-poly baking with an optional cage object, cage extrusion or a maximum ray distance.
capabilities.inputs: Cage, Cage Object, Cage Extrusion, Max Ray Distance

capabilities.does: Bake output target is image textures or the active colour attribute; margin type (Extend or Adjacent Faces) and pixel size avoid seam artifacts.
capabilities.inputs: Target, Clear Image, Margin Type, Margin Size

capabilities.does: Bakes normals, displacement or vector displacement by comparing viewport and render levels of a Multiresolution modifier.
Background mode renders without the UI; frames can be set with -f, -a, -s, -e and -j, and output path and format with -o and -F; arguments run in the order given.
Python API gives access to blender data, read-only context and operators; scripts can be run with --python or --python-expr to set up scenes and render.
capabilities.outputs: Automated scene setup and batch jobs

capabilities.does: The Cycles repository builds a standalone renderer that reads example XML scenes, with command-line options for samples, output and an OSL shading system.
The Cycles repository can also be built as a Hydra render delegate for USD-based viewers.

rea.notes: Repository page lists Apache-2.0 and is public; licence text itself not read. Facts are from the Blender manual that was titled 5.2 LTS when fetched. Not shown by the pages read: Bump node page and Shader to RGB page (old URLs 404), an overscan setting on the Film page, and stereoscopy or VR camera settings (the camera pages were read from the middle of the body).

entries.verified: 2026-11-02, how: Blender manual (latest, titled 5.2 LTS) pages read, cycles-renderer.org and repository page read; entry url not opened in this sweep (official domain, unchecked)

entries.name: EEVEE (Next)

licence.name: Part of Blender: GPL 2-or-later, binary builds GPL 3-or-later (blender.org licence page)

engines.name: Rasterised real-time renderer
engines.does: GPU rasteriser for PBR materials that shows results in the 3D viewport and can also produce final renders; uses the same shader nodes as Cycles.

engines.name: Ray tracing and Fast GI
engines.does: Screen-space or light-probe based ray tracing for reflections, refraction and indirect light, with a cheaper Fast GI path for rough surfaces.

engines.name: Virtual shadow maps
engines.does: Shadow-map ray tracing with resolution focused where needed and cached results, used by all light types.

engines.name: Light probes
engines.does: Sphere, plane and baked volume probes that store light for indirect lighting and reflections.

engines.name: Volumetrics
engines.does: Volume rendering with resolution, step and depth range controls; single scattering only.

capabilities.does: Chooses how scene intersections are found: Light Probe uses placed probes only (cheapest), Screen-Trace traces the depth buffer and falls back to probes off-screen. A resolution value trades speed for blur.
Screen-Trace tuning: precision (accuracy against distance), assumed surface thickness, back-face hits as valid hits to cut leaks, and a radiance scale for back-face hits.
capabilities.outputs: Fewer ray artifacts and light leaks

capabilities.does: Ray-trace denoising stages: spatial reuse of neighbour rays, temporal accumulation by reprojection (adds colour bias), and a bilateral filter.
capabilities.inputs: Spatial Reuse, Temporal Accumulation, Bilateral Filter

capabilities.does: Surfaces rougher than a threshold use a cheaper Fast GI instead of ray tracing; method is Ambient Occlusion (fastest) or Global Illumination. A threshold of 1 ray-traces everything.
capabilities.inputs: Threshold, Method = Ambient Occlusion | Global Illumination, Resolution

capabilities.does: Fast GI sampling controls: rays per pixel, screen steps per ray, intersection precision and an optional maximum distance.
capabilities.outputs: Noise against cost for Fast GI

capabilities.does: Fast GI occlusion tuning: near and far thickness to reduce leaks or lost occlusion, and a shading-normal bias against self-intersection.
Viewport sample count (0 resamples forever) and final-render sample count, with temporal reprojection to reduce noise while moving the view.
capabilities.inputs: Viewport Samples, Render Samples, Temporal Reprojection

capabilities.does: Shadow sampling per light: number of rays traced and shadow-map samples per ray (more steps give softer shadows), plus a shadow map resolution percentage.
Jitter produces softer and more precise shadows but prevents shadow-map caching, so it is costly; final renders always use it and the viewport toggle is off by default.
Approximates absorption of light by surrounding volumes for volumetric shadows; very costly and limited, with its own step count.
Global minimum light intensity for a light to affect the scene; a per-light custom distance overrides it. Lower values improve performance.
Shadow-map ray tracing that concentrates resolution where needed and caches results, working with any render method.
capabilities.outputs: Soft, high-detail shadows for all light types

capabilities.does: Shadow filter smooths aliasing with a circular blur (above 1 pixel increases leaking); overblur traces shadows per jittered sample, blurring beyond physical accuracy.

Smallest shadow-map pixel size; higher values save memory and speed, lower values add detail but more leaking. An absolute variant measures it at one unit from the light and does not apply to Sun lights.

Per-light influence distance where the light fades to zero, replacing the global light threshold; not for Sun lights. Separate factors scale a light for diffuse, glossy, transmission and volume scatter.
capabilities.inputs: Custom Distance; Diffuse, Glossy, Transmission, Volume Scatter factors

capabilities.does: Sphere light probes capture reflections and light with a sphere or box influence volume, percentage falloff, capture clip range and optional separate parallax shape; resolution is set in Scene settings.
capabilities.inputs: Type, Radius/Size, Falloff, Clipping Start/End, Custom Parallax

capabilities.does: Plane probes capture mirror-like reflections on flat surfaces; they need Screen-Trace, take an influence distance, parallax and a clipping offset, and affect surfaces aligned to the plane normal.

Baked volume probe grids store indirect light on a regular grid of capture points; resolution X/Y/Z, surfel resolution and bake samples set the quality, and the data lives in the object so it can be moved or linked.
capabilities.inputs: Resolution X/Y/Z, Surfel Resolution, Bake Samples

capabilities.does: Volume probe capture options: extend the captured area, include world, indirect and emission contributions, clamp direct and indirect light, and offset capture points from surfaces.
capabilities.inputs: Capture Distance, Contributions, Clamping, Surface Offset, Search Distance

capabilities.does: Volume probe interpolation controls: normal, view and facing bias, a validity threshold that ignores points inside closed geometry, and dilation with a search radius to fill invalid points.
capabilities.inputs: Normal Bias, View Bias, Facing Bias, Validity Threshold, Dilation Threshold, Radius

capabilities.does: World lighting is stored in a world light probe with its own resolution; bright parts above a threshold can be extracted into a sun light with an angle and optional shadows.
capabilities.inputs: World Resolution, Sun Threshold, Sun Angle, Use Shadow
capabilities.outputs: Environment lighting with a real sun shadow

capabilities.does: One scene-level setting sets the resolution of every sphere probe in the scene.

Volume rendering quality: resolution, number of steps along view depth, a linear-to-exponential distribution that favours near samples, a maximum surface-intersection depth, and an optional custom start and end range.
capabilities.inputs: Resolution, Steps, Distribution, Max Depth, Custom Range Start/End

capabilities.does: Material volume boundary method: Fast treats every face as a boundary (closed meshes only), Accurate handles complex meshes with much more memory.
Thickness drives subsurface, translucency and refraction approximations; modes are Sphere, Slab (panels, grass blades) and From Shadow (shadow-map based). Zero turns it off.
Post-process depth of field with a maximum blur size in pixels (0 switches to sample-based), sprite brightness threshold, neighbour rejection, camera jitter for sample-based blur, and over-blur.
capabilities.inputs: Max Size, Sprite Threshold, Neighbor Rejection, Jitter Camera, Over-blur

capabilities.does: Shutter position (start, centre or end on frame) and length in frames, with accumulation steps, a max blur in pixels, a bleeding bias against background blur over foreground, and a custom shutter curve.
capabilities.inputs: Position, Shutter, Bleeding Bias, Max Blur, Steps, Shutter Curve

capabilities.does: Pixel filter size softens the image to cut aliasing; lower is crisper, higher is softer.
Transparent film renders a see-through background for compositing; overscan adds a percentage of the render size to the buffer to fix screen-edge glitches, at a large performance cost.
capabilities.outputs: RGBA output and cleaner screen-space edges

capabilities.does: Clamps direct and indirect light separately for surfaces and for volumes to remove fireflies; 0 disables. Indirect clamping also limits world light.
Scales direct and indirect lighting strength after clamping without changing light energy, ray depth or performance.
Uses higher-precision normals and tangents for dense meshes with high-frequency textures, at a memory cost.
Texture anisotropic filtering at oblique angles from Off to 16 samples, sharpening distant floors and roads.
GPU memory pools for shadows and light probe volume grids; a bigger pool allows more of them but may not fit in GPU memory (fixes the shadow buffer full error).
capabilities.inputs: Shadow Pool, Light Probes Volume Pool

capabilities.does: Viewport pixel size lowers preview resolution; the compositor can run on CPU or GPU with auto or full precision, and Denoise nodes get device and preview/final quality.
capabilities.inputs: Pixel Size; Compositor Device, Precision GPU; Denoising Device, Preview/Final Quality

capabilities.does: Material transparency method: Dithered (grey hashed transparency; works with passes and ray tracing) or Blended (coloured transparency, no passes or ray tracing, per-object sorting) with an overlap switch.
capabilities.inputs: Render Method, Transparency Overlap, Raytraced Transmission

capabilities.does: Hides back faces for the camera, for shadow casting and for light-probe volume baking separately.
capabilities.inputs: Backface Culling: Camera, Shadow, Light Probe Volume
capabilities.outputs: Faster rendering and fewer probe leaks

capabilities.does: Bump Only changes normals; Displacement and Bump moves vertices at render time (costly with many samples); Displacement Only falls back to both. Max Distance limits vertex movement.
Accurate shadows for Transparent BSDF materials; turning it off renders faster with less accurate shadows.
Curves and hair draw as Strand (about one pixel wide, ignores diameter) or Strip (flat ribbon with rounded normals), plus extra subdivisions over the hair system resolution.
Normal Offset and Geometry Offset shift shadow position to hide shadow-break artifacts on low-poly smooth meshes.
capabilities.inputs: Shadow Terminator: Normal Offset, Geometry Offset

capabilities.does: Per-object visibility for camera rays, shadow casting and the Raycast node, and separate switches for volume, sphere and plane light-probe capture.
capabilities.inputs: Ray Visibility: Camera, Shadow, Raycast; Light Probes: Volume, Sphere, Plane

capabilities.does: Receiver and shadow blocker collections limit which objects a light affects and which block it.
Mist pass with start, depth and a falloff curve (Quadratic, Linear, Inverse Quadratic) for distance fades.
Shader to RGB converts BSDF output to a colour and lights it like a Blended material; the node is available in EEVEE only.

EEVEE node limits compared with Cycles: Random Walk SSS, SSS IOR/anisotropy and Principled anisotropy are unsupported, sheen is approximate, Bevel, Light Falloff, Hair BSDF and Toon are not supported.
capabilities.outputs: Know which nodes render the same

capabilities.does: Volumes support single scattering only, appear to camera rays but not in reflections, refractions or probes, and do not cast shadows on solid objects.

Screen-space effects only see on-screen front surfaces. EEVEE is GPU-only with no CPU mode, no multi-GPU, no headless Windows, perspective and orthographic cameras only, 128 sphere and 16 plane probes in view.
Most calculations use 16-bit floats, shader node evaluation is 32-bit, render output is 16-bit, and negative values in Combined and Light passes clamp to zero.

outcomes: Stills and animations at interactive speed

rea.notes: Source is part of Blender under GPL; the repository itself was not opened. Terms virtual shadow maps and Fast GI come from the manual; the manual pages opened do not use the term horizon scan.

entries.verified: 2026-11-02, how: Blender manual (latest, titled 5.2 LTS) EEVEE pages read; shadows render-settings page returned 404

entries.name: Mitsuba 3
entries.vendor: EPFL Realistic Graphics Lab (Wenzel Jakob and contributors)

licence.name: BSD-style 3-clause licence with an added clause about contributed enhancements (LICENSE file read; copyright Wenzel Jakob, 2017)

engines.name: Retargetable renderer core
engines.does: One code base compiled into variants for scalar CPU, LLVM-vectorised CPU and CUDA/OptiX GPU, in mono, RGB, spectral and polarised modes.

engines.name: Dr.Jit just-in-time layer
engines.does: Compiler that fuses array code into kernels and supplies automatic differentiation; Mitsuba is built on it.

engines.name: Plugin system
engines.does: Integrators, BSDFs, emitters, sensors, films, samplers, filters, media, phase functions, shapes, textures and volumes are plugins; Python subclasses can be registered too.

engines.name: Differentiable rendering
engines.does: Path replay backpropagation and projective-sampling integrators give gradients of images with respect to scene parameters for inverse rendering.

engines.name: Scene description
engines.does: XML scene files and Python dictionaries describe the scene; parameters can be substituted from the command line or keyword arguments.

capabilities.does: A variant name starts with a backend: scalar (CPU, one ray at a time, easy to debug), llvm (CPU, JIT-compiled parallel kernels) or cuda (NVIDIA GPU with OptiX ray tracing).
capabilities.outputs: CPU or GPU execution from the same scene

capabilities.does: Colour mode of a variant: mono (grayscale), rgb, or spectral over roughly 360 to 830 nm.
The _ad part of a variant name turns on automatic differentiation for inverse problems.
The _polarized suffix tracks full light polarisation; it costs roughly 1.5 to 2 times the render time.
The _double suffix runs computation in 64-bit precision; Embree and OptiX ray tracing still run in single precision.
The pip package ships 13 variants (scalar_rgb, scalar_spectral, scalar_spectral_polarized and llvm_ad / cuda_ad in mono, rgb, spectral, with polarised forms); all others need a source build.
Release 3.9.0 (June 2026) adds Metal variants (metal_*, metal_ad_*) for Apple Silicon and a redesigned ray-tracing core.
Path integrator: unidirectional path tracer, the recommended general default, without participating media.
Volpath integrator: volumetric path tracer for participating media with multiple importance sampling of phase function and direct light; not forward-mode differentiable.
capabilities.outputs: Images with fog, smoke and subsurface media

capabilities.does: Volpathmis integrator: volumetric path tracer with spectral MIS for media whose extinction changes with wavelength; not forward-mode differentiable.
Direct integrator: direct lighting only, combining BSDF and emitter sampling; no media, no indirect light.

AOV integrator: writes arbitrary variables (albedo, depth, position, uv, geo_normal, sh_normal, dp_du, dp_dv, duv_dx, duv_dy, prim_index, shape_index) next to nested integrators, each into separate images.
Depth integrator: debugging integrator that returns camera-to-hit distance, or 0 on a miss.
Moment integrator: records the second moment of the samples a nested integrator produces, for variance estimates.
Stokes integrator: outputs the full Stokes vector at the sensor; first channel is radiance, the other three describe polarisation.
Particle tracer: starts rays at emitters and connects them to the sensor at every bounce; high variance, no media.

PRB integrator: path replay backpropagation for differentiable rendering; no projective sampling, so shape gradients are incomplete and ideal specular properties cannot be optimised; not for polarised variants.
prb_basic: a minimal PRB written in Python for illustration; no emitter sampling, MIS, Russian roulette or projective sampling, so gradients are noisy.
prbvolpath: volumetric PRB using differentiable delta tracking for free-flight sampling; no projective sampling.
prb_projective: PRB with projective sampling, so discontinuous visibility changes give correct gradients; builds paths outward from boundary segments.
capabilities.inputs: max_depth (-1), rr_depth (5), sppc, sppp, sppi, guiding, guiding_proj, guiding_rounds

capabilities.does: direct_projective: direct illumination with projective sampling for visibility gradients; equals prb_projective at max_depth 2. Guiding structure is none, grid or octree (default).
capabilities.inputs: sppc, sppp, sppi, guiding (octree), guiding_proj (true), guiding_rounds (1)

capabilities.does: Release 3.7.0 added a volprim_rf_basic integrator; the ellipsoid shapes added with it are designed for volumetric primitive integrators.
Diffuse BSDF: ideal Lambertian surface.
Dielectric BSDF: smooth interface between two dielectrics such as air and glass, with reflection and refraction.
Thin dielectric BSDF: reflects and transmits through a thin sheet without bending the light; same parameters as dielectric, no polarised variant.
Rough dielectric BSDF: microfacet model of ground glass, Beckmann or GGX distribution with visible-normal sampling.
capabilities.inputs: distribution (beckmann), alpha / alpha_u / alpha_v (0.1), sample_visible (true), IORs

capabilities.does: Conductor BSDF: perfectly smooth metal from a named material preset or explicit complex IOR.
Rough conductor BSDF: microfacet metal with Beckmann or GGX distribution and visible-normal sampling.
capabilities.inputs: material, eta, k, specular_reflectance, distribution, alpha, alpha_u, alpha_v, sample_visible

capabilities.does: Plastic BSDF: smooth diffuse base under a smooth dielectric coating; nonlinear option models colour shift from internal scattering.
Rough plastic BSDF: diffuse base under a rough microfacet coating.
capabilities.inputs: diffuse_reflectance, nonlinear, distribution, alpha (0.1), sample_visible, IORs

capabilities.does: Polarisation-aware plastic: microfacet specular lobe plus diffuse lobe.
capabilities.inputs: diffuse_reflectance, specular_reflectance, int_ior, distribution, alpha, sample_visible

capabilities.does: Principled BSDF: artist-friendly multi-lobe model after Burley's Disney BRDF; no subsurface scattering. Separate sampling-rate weights for diffuse, specular and clearcoat lobes.
capabilities.inputs: base_color, roughness, anisotropic, metallic, spec_trans, eta or specular, spec_tint, sheen, sheen_tint, flatness, clearcoat, clearcoat_gloss, sampling rates

capabilities.does: Thin principled BSDF: principled-style model for thin translucent materials, with diffuse transmission and separate sampling rates for diffuse and specular reflection and transmission.
capabilities.inputs: base_color, roughness, anisotropic, spec_trans, eta (1.5), spec_tint, sheen, sheen_tint, flatness, diff_trans (0 to 2)

capabilities.does: Hair BSDF: Chiang et al. near-field hair and fur model for bsplinecurve shapes, using pigments or a direct absorption coefficient.
capabilities.inputs: eumelanin (1.3), pheomelanin (0.2), sigma_a, scale, int_ior (amber 1.55), longitudinal_roughness (0.3), azimuthal_roughness (0.3), scale_tilt (2)

capabilities.does: Measured BSDF: loads a measured material from a .bsdf file; spectral files need spectral variants, RGB files need RGB variants.
Measured polarimetric BRDF from a .pbsdf file; works in spectral polarised variants only.
capabilities.inputs: filename, alpha_sample (0.1), wavelength (-1 = all, or 450 to 650 nm)

capabilities.does: Ideal linear polariser optical element; can also act as a neutral density filter.
Ideal linear retarder (wave plate) with fast-axis angle and retardance in degrees.
capabilities.outputs: Wave plate in the light path

capabilities.does: Ideal circular polariser, right-handed unless left_handed is set.
Bump map adapter: perturbs the shading normals of a nested BSDF from a height texture.
capabilities.inputs: scale (1), flip_invalid_normals (true), use_shadowing_function (true); nested texture and bsdf

capabilities.does: Normal map adapter: perturbs shading normals of a nested BSDF from a normal-map texture given in the local shading frame; same flip and shadowing options.
Blend BSDF: linear mix of two nested BSDFs by a weight (0 first, 1 second).
capabilities.inputs: weight (0.5, float or texture); two nested bsdfs

capabilities.does: Mask BSDF: blends a nested BSDF with full transparency by an opacity value.
Two-sided adapter: makes a one-sided BSDF act on both faces, or takes separate front and back BSDFs.
Null BSDF: invisible surface that does not interact with light, used mainly to enclose participating media.
Point light radiating equally in all directions from one position.
Area emitter: diffuse light from the outside surface of any shape it is attached to.
Spot light with a cone, linear falloff between beam width and cutoff angle, and an optional projected texture.
capabilities.inputs: intensity (1), cutoff_angle (20), beam_width (cutoff x 3/4), texture, to_world

capabilities.does: Distant light from one fixed direction with set irradiance; its adjoint is the distant sensor.
Area light that emits only along the surface normal; renders correctly only with a particle tracer.
Constant environment emitter: uniform light surrounding the scene.
Environment map emitter built from a latitude-longitude image, with scale and optional MIS compensation.
capabilities.inputs: filename or bitmap, scale (1), to_world, mis_compensation (false)

capabilities.does: Projector emitter: projects a texture into the scene; the reciprocal of a perspective camera and takes the same field-of-view parameters.
capabilities.inputs: irradiance texture, scale, fov or focal_length, fov_axis, to_world

capabilities.does: Sun and sky emitter at one fixed moment using the Hosek-Wilkie models; place and time or a sun direction set the sun.
capabilities.inputs: turbidity (3, 1 to 10), albedo (0.3), latitude, longitude, timezone, date and time, sun_direction, sun_scale, sky_scale, sun_aperture (0.5338), complex_sun

capabilities.does: Timed sun and sky emitter averaged over a time window, or varying over the sensor shutter, for multi-day or yearly lighting studies.
capabilities.inputs: window_start_time (7), window_end_time (19), start and end dates, shutter_open, shutter_close, plus sunsky parameters

capabilities.does: Perspective pinhole camera with field of view or 35mm-equivalent focal length, clip planes, principal point offset and a sensor response function.
capabilities.inputs: fov, focal_length (50mm), fov_axis (x), near_clip (0.01), far_clip (10000), principal_point_offset_x/y, srf, to_world

capabilities.does: Thin-lens perspective camera with a circular aperture and focus distance for depth of field.
capabilities.inputs: aperture_radius, focus_distance (0), focal_length, fov, fov_axis, near_clip, far_clip, srf

capabilities.does: Orthographic camera with no perspective distortion.
Radiance meter measures radiance along one ray, like a perspective camera with a field of view near zero; used with 1 by 1 pixel films.
Irradiance meter measures incident power per area over the shape it is attached to; for meshes it covers all triangles.
Distant radiance meter records radiance leaving the scene in one direction; adjoint of the directional emitter, with an optional target point or shape.
Batch sensor groups several sub-sensors to render many viewpoints together with less overhead; film width must be a multiple of the sensor count; path-tracing integrators only.
HDR film writes linear radiance without post-processing to OpenEXR (default), RGBE or PFM, with crop window and border sampling.
capabilities.inputs: width 768, height 576, file_format (openexr), pixel_format (rgb), component_format (float16), crop_offset_x/y, crop_width/height, sample_border, rfilter (gaussian)

capabilities.does: Spectral film saves one or more user-defined sensor-response bands as a multichannel spectral OpenEXR; bands need not be visible light.
capabilities.inputs: width, height, component_format, crop options, sample_border, rfilter, nested spectrum plugins as bands

capabilities.does: Independent sampler: unstratified uniform pseudorandom numbers from PCG32; simplest, converges slowest.
Stratified sampler: one sample per stratum to cut clumping; sample count should be a square.
Correlated multi-jittered sampler after Kensler: stratified in 2D and in each 1D projection.
Orthogonal array sampler: extends multi-jittered sampling to higher dimensions; sample count must be a prime square, strength 2 recommended.
Low-discrepancy sampler: quasi-Monte Carlo sequence mixed with a pseudorandom generator, after Kollig and Keller.
Box reconstruction filter: fastest, often gives strong aliasing.
Tent reconstruction filter: triangular, avoids ringing and usually aliases less than box.
Gaussian reconstruction filter (windowed): the default; no ringing, can over-blur.
Mitchell-Netravali cubic filter: balances sharpness and ringing.
Catmull-Rom filter: keeps sharp features at the cost of more ringing.
Lanczos filter: windowed approximation of the ideal low-pass filter; sharp, slowest, can ring at edges.
Homogeneous medium with constant extinction and spatially varying albedo; any phase function; turning off emitter sampling can cut time up to half inside dielectrics.
Heterogeneous medium: albedo and extinction come from nested volume plugins, constant, procedural or grids.
Isotropic phase function: uniform scattering in all directions.
Henyey-Greenstein phase function: forward, isotropic or backward scattering by one asymmetry value.
Rayleigh phase function: unpolarised scattering by particles much smaller than the wavelength.
SGGX microflake phase function: anisotropic scattering for fibres or surface-like structures, from six matrix values supplied as a volume.
Tabulated phase function: isotropic function from a user table over cos theta, normalised automatically.
Blended phase function: linear mix of two nested phase functions, such as aerosols plus Rayleigh air.
OBJ loader for triangle and quad meshes with normals and UVs; the docs call it a last resort because of size, memory and precision.
PLY loader, binary preferred, with UVs, normals and custom vertex or face attributes; prefixed attributes group into multi-dimensional ones.
Serialized loader: Mitsuba's compact gzip-compressed indexed triangle format; one file can hold several meshes.
Analytic sphere with a low-variance area-light sampling strategy.
Analytic cylinder without end caps; inside is absorbing unless wrapped in a twosided BSDF.
Rectangle covering -1 to 1 in XY with normal along +Z; for ground planes and area lights.
Analytic unit disk in XY with normal along +Z.
Cube spanning -1 to 1 on each axis, one UV square per face.
Cubic B-spline curves modelled as open hollow tubes with per-point radii from a text file; backfaces culled.
capabilities.inputs: filename (x y z radius per line, at least 4 points per curve), to_world

capabilities.does: Linear-segment curves with spherical joints and end caps, from the same text format; at least 2 points per curve.
Signed distance field on a grid over the unit cube, with smooth or analytic normals; no UVs, cannot be an area emitter.
Shape group: container of shapes prepared for instancing; invisible on its own.
Instance places a shape group with a transform; material comes from the group, and groups cannot hold emitters, sensors or subsurface shapes.
Point cloud of anisotropic ellipsoids with closed-form ray intersection, for volumetric primitive integrators.
capabilities.inputs: filename or data / centers / scales / quaternions, scale_factor (1), extent (3), extent_adaptive_clamping, to_world

capabilities.does: Same ellipsoid cloud, tessellated so hardware ray-triangle intersection can be used.
capabilities.inputs: ellipsoids parameters plus shell (ico_sphere | box | uv_sphere | mesh)

capabilities.does: Bitmap texture from JPEG, PNG, OpenEXR, RGBE, TGA or BMP with interpolation, wrap modes, storage format and raw (no colour conversion) mode.
capabilities.inputs: filename, bitmap, data, filter_type (bilinear), wrap_mode (repeat), format (auto), raw (false), to_uv, accel

capabilities.does: Procedural two-colour checkerboard.
Exposes a mesh attribute (name starts with vertex_ or face_), such as vertex colour, as a texture.
Volume texture looks up a 3D volume at each surface point in world space; useful without UVs or for 3D procedural textures.
Raw constant texture returns the same value in every colour mode, without colour conversion (added in 3.7.0).
Grid volume: 3D grid data with trilinear or nearest interpolation and wrap modes, loaded from a binary file, a VolumeGrid or a tensor.
capabilities.inputs: filename, grid, data, use_grid_bbox (false), filter_type (trilinear), wrap_mode (clamp), raw, to_world, accel

capabilities.does: Constant volume with one scalar or spectrum value everywhere.
Uniform spectrum: one constant value over a wavelength range (default 360 to 830 nm).
Regular spectrum: linear interpolation of evenly spaced samples.
Irregular spectrum: linear interpolation of samples at arbitrary wavelengths.
sRGB spectrum: smooth spectrum upsampled from an sRGB colour in spectral modes; constant in RGB and mono modes.
D65 spectrum: CIE D65 daylight illuminant, the default emission spectrum in spectral modes, optionally tinted or textured.
Blackbody spectrum at a temperature in kelvin; emission only and spectral modes only.
XML scene format: scene root with versioned plugin tags, typed properties, nested objects, ref and alias reuse, default parameters with $name substitution, include files and resource paths.
capabilities.inputs: integer, float, boolean, string, point, vector, rgb, spectrum, transform, ref; <default>, <include>, <path>

capabilities.does: Dictionary scene format for mi.load_dict: type key per object, nested dictionaries as nested objects, ref entries with ids, resources entries for search paths.
Transform composition in scene files: translate, rotate (axis and degrees), scale, matrix (3 by 3 or 4 by 4) and lookat, each left-multiplied onto the result.
Python API: mi.load_file, mi.render(scene, spp), result as a tensor in linear RGB, mi.util.write_bitmap to PNG or EXR, mi.variants() to list installed variants.
Custom renderers can be written with array code: build rays on a grid, intersect with scene.ray_intersect, test occlusion with scene.ray_test, draw numbers with mi.PCG32 inside dr.syntax loops.
capabilities.outputs: Ambient occlusion and other custom renders

capabilities.does: Differentiable workflow: AD variant, mi.traverse(scene) to name parameters, params.update(), mi.render with tracked parameters, loss, dr.backward, optimiser step.
capabilities.inputs: mi.traverse, params.update(opt), mi.render(scene, params, spp=...), dr.backward, mi.ad.Adam

capabilities.does: Optimisers SGD (with or without momentum) and Adam act like a dictionary of variables, with per-parameter learning rates, masked updates and a step that resets gradients.
capabilities.inputs: lr, momentum, params, mask_updates, set_learning_rate(), step(), reset(key)

capabilities.does: Projective-sampling integrators target gradients from shadows and reflections; the tutorial optimises a 3D curve so its shadow matches a reference, and guided estimates match finite differences.
capabilities.inputs: direct_projective, prb_projective; sppc, sppp, sppi, guiding

capabilities.does: Python plugins: subclass mi.BSDF (or other plugin bases) with sample, eval, pdf, traverse and parameters_changed, register with mi.register_bsdf and similar calls; JIT variants run the Python only a few times per wavefront.
capabilities.outputs: Custom materials and components in Python

capabilities.does: Mesh handling: load OBJ, PLY, serialized; mi.Mesh with fixed vertex and face counts; edit buffers through mi.traverse; add vertex_ or face_ attributes; write PLY with Mesh.write_ply.

Recent releases: 3.7.0 added the sunsky emitter, ellipsoid shapes and the rawconstant texture; 3.7.1 added invalid-normal flipping and shadowing to bump and normal maps; 3.8.0 gave pplastic spatially varying roughness and IOR and moved to Dr.Jit 1.3.1.
Polarised transport uses 4-component Stokes vectors and 4 by 4 Mueller matrices with reference frames; exact treatment is limited to specular reflection and refraction.
A mitsuba command-line tool exists (release notes mention its parallel scene loading); the pages read here document only -D parameter substitution and search paths for scene files.

formats.name: PNG / JPEG / TGA / BMP (bitmap textures, PNG output)

rea.notes: LICENSE page read: BSD-style 3-clause licence with an added clause on contributed enhancements. Docs are the stable branch; release 3.9.1 is cited in the README.

entries.verified: 2026-11-02, how: Mitsuba 3 stable docs (plugin reference, key topics, tutorials, release notes), GitHub README and LICENSE read

entries.name: pbrt v4
entries.vendor: Matt Pharr, Wenzel Jakob, Greg Humphreys

licence.name: Apache-2.0 (repository page)

engines.name: Spectral CPU renderer
engines.does: Reference renderer from the fourth edition of the book; light transport uses point-sampled spectra and RGB appears only in scene input and image output.

engines.name: GPU path tracer
engines.does: OptiX-based GPU rendering switched on with --gpu; supports the full volumetric path integrator feature set.

engines.name: Scene description parser
engines.does: Text scene format with directives, named objects, includes and typed parameters for every plugin-like component.

engines.name: Book companion
engines.does: The online book documents the same system chapter by chapter, including a chapter on wavefront rendering on GPUs.

capabilities.does: All light transport uses point-sampled wavelengths; colours as RGB appear only in scene files and the final image.
capabilities.inputs: Scene description; film sensor and colour space

capabilities.does: GPU rendering through CUDA 11+ and OptiX 7.1+ on Linux or Windows, enabled with --gpu and PBRT_OPTIX_PATH; supports the full VolPathIntegrator features.
A wavefront integrator can also run on the CPU, switched on with an Option setting.
Path integrator: unidirectional path tracer; optional regularisation roughens specular vertices after non-specular scattering to cut caustic noise.
Volpath integrator: path tracer that handles participating media.
Bidirectional path tracing integrator, with options to save one image per (s,t) strategy and the MIS weight images.
Metropolis light transport: Markov chains with bootstrap samples, large-step probability and small-mutation sigma.
Stochastic progressive photon mapping integrator with photons per iteration, initial search radius and seed.
capabilities.inputs: photonsperiteration (-1 = one per pixel), radius (1), seed (0)

capabilities.does: Ambient occlusion integrator with cosine or uniform hemisphere sampling and a maximum occlusion distance.
Simple integrators for study and comparison: simplepath (toggle BSDF and light sampling), simplevolpath, lightpath and randomwalk.
The README lists light BVHs, solid-angle sampling for triangles and quads, and portal sampling for environment lights among the v4 light sampling improvements.
capabilities.inputs: lightsampler (bvh default, per the file format page)

capabilities.does: Point light with intensity I, position from, power and scale.
Spot light with axis from/to, full-intensity cone angle and a falloff delta angle.
Goniometric light driven by an octahedral emission image for measured light distributions.
Projection light that shines an image with a spread angle along the shorter axis.
Distant light with radiance L and arrival direction from/to; accepts illuminance.
Infinite light: uniform radiance, or an environment map; an optional portal quad limits where light is sampled.
Diffuse area light attached to shapes, with emitted radiance L, optional emission image and a two-sided switch.
Diffuse material with a reflectance texture, 0 to 1.
Coated diffuse: diffuse base under a dielectric coat with optional scattering medium between layers; Monte Carlo layer evaluation.
capabilities.inputs: reflectance (0.5), albedo (0), g (0), maxdepth (10), nsamples (1), thickness (0.01)

capabilities.does: Coated conductor: metal under a dielectric coat with separate roughness for the interface and the conductor.
capabilities.inputs: interface.roughness, conductor.roughness, conductor.eta / conductor.k (copper), reflectance, albedo, g, maxdepth, nsamples, thickness

capabilities.does: Conductor material from wavelength-dependent eta and k, or from an average reflectance; roughness controls with remap.
capabilities.inputs: eta, k (copper), reflectance, roughness, uroughness, vroughness, remaproughness (true)

capabilities.does: Dielectric material with an index of refraction (float or spectrum, default 1.5) and optional roughness.
Diffuse transmission material: diffuse reflection plus diffuse transmission, with a scale.
Hair material from absorption, an RGB reflectance or melanin pigments, with longitudinal and azimuthal roughness and cuticle scale angle.
capabilities.inputs: sigma_a, reflectance, eumelanin (1.3), pheomelanin, eta (1.55), beta_m (0.3), beta_n (0.3), alpha (2)

capabilities.does: Measured BRDF material from a data file (the README mentions Dupuy and Jakob style measured BRDFs).
Mix material blends two named materials by an amount texture.
Subsurface material from scattering and absorption coefficients, mean free path, measured preset names or reflectance.
capabilities.inputs: eta (1.33), g, mfp, name, reflectance, sigma_a, sigma_s, scale

capabilities.does: Interface material marks a surface as ignored by intersection, used for medium boundaries.
All materials except interface and mix accept a displacement texture and a normal map.
Perspective camera with field of view along the shorter axis, optional thin-lens radius and focal distance, and shutter times.
