capabilities.inputs: fov (90), lensradius (0), focaldistance (1e30), frameaspectratio, screenwindow, shutteropen (0), shutterclose (1)

capabilities.does: Orthographic camera with optional lens radius and focal distance.
Realistic camera traces rays through a lens system file with aperture diameter in mm, focus distance in metres and a circular or image aperture shape.
Spherical camera with equal-area (default) or equirectangular mapping.
Samplers halton, sobol, paddedsobol and zsobol (the default) take a pixel sample count and a randomisation method (fastowen by default; permutedigits for Halton).
Independent sampler (random, for comparison) and stratified sampler with x and y strata and jitter.
Filters box, gaussian (default, radius 1.5, sigma 0.5), mitchell (B, C), sinc (tau) and triangle, each with x and y radius.
capabilities.inputs: xradius, yradius, sigma, B, C, tau

capabilities.does: Films: rgb (default), gbuffer (adds geometry channels in camera or world space, EXR only) and spectral (bins over a wavelength range, EXR only). Shared options set resolution, sensor, ISO, white balance and 16-bit saving.
capabilities.inputs: xresolution (1280), yresolution (720), iso (100), whitebalance, sensor (cie1931), savefp16, nbuckets (16), lambdamin 360, lambdamax 830

capabilities.does: Homogeneous medium with absorption, scattering, Henyey-Greenstein asymmetry, emission and measured presets.
capabilities.inputs: sigma_a (1), sigma_s (1), scale, g (0), Le, Lescale, preset

capabilities.does: Uniform grid medium from nx*ny*nz densities with bounds p0/p1 and optional blackbody temperature grid for emission.
capabilities.inputs: density, nx, ny, nz, p0, p1, temperature, temperatureoffset, temperaturescale

capabilities.does: RGB grid medium with separate RGB absorption, scattering and emission grids.
capabilities.inputs: sigma_a, sigma_s, Le, Lescale, p0, p1, scale

capabilities.does: Procedural cloud medium with density scale, frequency and wispiness.
capabilities.inputs: density (1), frequency (5), wispiness (1), sigma_a, sigma_s, p0, p1

capabilities.does: NanoVDB medium reads a volume file with scaling for absorption, scattering and temperature-based emission.
capabilities.inputs: filename, sigma_a, sigma_s, scale, Lescale, temperatureoffset, temperaturescale

capabilities.does: Quadric shapes: sphere (radius, zmin, zmax, phimax), cylinder along z, and disk (height, radius, innerradius, phimax).
capabilities.inputs: radius, zmin, zmax, phimax, height, innerradius

capabilities.does: Triangle meshes from indices, P, N, S, uv; plymesh with optional displacement; bilinear patch meshes; loop subdivision with levels.
capabilities.inputs: indices, P, N, S, uv, filename, displacement, edgelength, levels

capabilities.does: Curve shape from control points with basis, degree, type, width at ends and split depth.
capabilities.inputs: P, basis, degree, type, N, width, width0, width1, splitdepth

capabilities.does: Textures: constant, scale, mix, directionmix, bilerp, checkerboard (2D or 3D) and dots.
capabilities.inputs: value, tex, tex1, tex2, amount, dimension, inside, outside

capabilities.does: Noise textures fbm, wrinkled, windy and marble with octaves, roughness, scale and variation.
Image map texture with wrap, anisotropy limit, filter, encoding, scale and invert; ptex texture with encoding and scale.
capabilities.inputs: filename, wrap, maxanisotropy, filter, encoding, scale, invert

capabilities.does: Acceleration structures: bvh (max primitives per node 4, SAH split by default) and kdtree with cost and depth controls.
capabilities.inputs: maxnodeprims, splitmethod, intersectcost, traversalcost, emptybonus, maxprims, maxdepth

capabilities.does: ColorSpace statement selects srgb (default), rec2020, dci-p3 or aces2065-1 for scene and output colour.
Option statement: disablepixeljitter, forcediffuse, wavefront and rendercoordsys (cameraworld default, camera or world).
Scene file directives: AttributeBegin/End state stacks, ObjectBegin/ObjectInstance, Include (also gzip), Import for parallel parsing, MakeNamedMedium, CoordinateSystem, ReverseOrientation.
Command-line tools: pbrt --upgrade converts v3 scenes, --toply converts meshes to binary PLY, imgtool makeequiarea converts environment maps, and assimp can export other formats to pbrt.
imgtool denoise-optix runs the OptiX denoiser on rendered images.
The --display-server option streams progressive output to the tev or hdrview image viewers, on port 14158 by default.

The online fourth edition covers radiometry and spectra, cameras, shapes, BVHs, sampling, reflection models, textures, volume scattering, light sampling, path tracing, volume rendering and wavefront GPU rendering in 16 chapters.

rea.notes: Repository page shows Apache-2.0. Book terms were not read. The v4 scene format page does not describe an aov integrator.

entries.name: appleseed

licence.name: MIT (repository page and GitHub API); site assets CC BY-SA 4.0 (site page)

engines.name: Rendering kernel
engines.does: Lighting engines in source folders for path tracing (pt), bidirectional path tracing (bdpt), light tracing and SPPM, with direct and volume lighting integrators.

engines.name: Scene model
engines.does: Modeling folders for AOVs, BSDFs, BSSRDFs, cameras, EDFs, environment, lights, materials, objects, post-processing stages, shader groups, surface shaders, textures and volumes.

engines.name: Standalone tools and plugins
engines.does: C++ library with C++ and Python APIs, standalone applications for Windows, Linux and macOS, and plugins for Maya, 3ds Max and Blender.

capabilities.does: Lighting engine folders: pt (path tracing), bdpt (bidirectional), lighttracing, sppm (stochastic progressive photon mapping) and a null engine.
Forward and backward light samplers and a light tree, with direct-lighting and image-based-lighting integrators.
The site describes partial participating-media support and lists heterogeneous volumes and OpenVDB as upcoming.
The lighting kernel has a volume lighting integrator, and the scene model has a volume folder.
Light path recorder and stream sources allow recording and visualising light paths.
Final and progressive frame renderers with timed and serial renderer controllers and tile callbacks.

BSDF sources: Ashikhmin, Blinn, Disney, Kelemen, Lambertian, Oren-Nayar, glossy, glossy layer, metal, plastic, sheen, specular BRDF and BTDF, diffuse BTDF, glass, hair, blend, mix and null, plus energy compensation and OSL BSDFs.
Open Shading Language shaders can be compiled on the fly, with a set of OSL materials described on the site.
Camera sources: pinhole, perspective, orthographic, thin lens, fisheye lens, multi-lens, spherical and a generic lens camera.
A BCD denoiser was added in release 1.9.0 and Intel Open Image Denoise can be used on renders, per the site.
Python bindings, a Python console and Python plugins are described on the site; the library has C++ and Python APIs.
appleseed.studio is a standalone lookdev application described on the site.
Plugins exist for Blender (blenderseed), Maya and 3ds Max, and Gaffer integrates appleseed.

rea.notes: Status check: GitHub API shows the repository is not archived, last push 2026-06-11, updated 2026-10-29. The site newest post is appleseed 2.1.0-beta from September 2019 with a 2010-2020 footer. Treat the project as low-activity.

entries.name: LuxCoreRender

licence.name: Apache-2.0 (repository page and GitHub API); BlendLuxCore add-on is GPL-3.0 (its README)

engines.name: SLG render engines
engines.does: Engine directories for CPU and OpenCL path tracing, bidirectional with vertex merging, light tracing, tile path, real-time path and baking.

engines.name: Film and image pipeline
engines.does: Film with output channels, pixel filters, denoisers and a chain of image-pipeline plugins that turn raw radiance into a final image.

engines.name: Scene library
engines.does: Materials, textures, lights, cameras, shapes and volumes defined in the scene description and evaluated on CPU and OpenCL kernels.

engines.name: C++ and Python API
engines.does: LuxCore v2.x exposes a C++ and Python API; a make target builds the pyluxcore module.

capabilities.does: Path tracing engines in separate CPU (pathcpu) and OpenCL (pathocl) source directories, sharing a common base for the OpenCL variants.
capabilities.outputs: Unbiased path-traced images on CPU or GPU

capabilities.does: Bidirectional CPU engines in two directories, bidircpu and bidirvmcpu (vertex merging); release notes mention BIDIRCPU can use the PhotonGI caustic cache for SDS paths.
capabilities.inputs: bidircpu, bidirvmcpu directories; BIDIRCPU named in release notes
capabilities.outputs: Better caustics and difficult light transport

capabilities.does: A light-tracing engine directory (lightcpu) traces from light sources toward the camera.
Tile-based path tracing engines on CPU and OpenCL (tilepathcpu, tilepathocl).
Real-time path engines on CPU and OpenCL (rtpathcpu, rtpathocl) with a dedicated sampler header, aimed at interactive preview.
A bakecpu engine directory handles texture baking.
A filesaver engine directory exports a scene description to files.
The engines folder has a caches directory; release notes name a PhotonGI caustic cache used by the bidirectional engine.
Sampler sources include random, Sobol, Metropolis, a tile-path sampler and a real-time path sampler.
Film pixel filters: Blackman-Harris, box, Catmull-Rom, Gaussian, Mitchell, Mitchell (supersampled variant), none and sinc.
Denoiser plugins for Intel Open Image Denoise, BCD and OptiX, plus a film denoiser module; release notes say OIDN 1.4.0 added auxiliary-buffer prefiltering and better albedo and normal AOV support.
The film folder holds noise-estimation and convergence-test modules for deciding when a render is clean.

Image pipeline plugins include bloom, vignetting, colour aberration, gamma, white balance, camera response, colour LUT, gaussian blur, contour lines, mist, background image, object-ID mask, patterns, premultiply alpha, output switcher, bake margin and a tone map folder.
Release 2.6 added OpenColorIO 2.0 and an OCIO tone mapper; colour space options apply to textures, materials and lights.

Material types: archglass, carpaint, cloth, Disney, glass, glossy2, glossycoating, glossytranslucent, matte, mattetranslucent, metal2, mirror, mix, null, roughglass, roughmatte, roughmattetranslucent, thinfilmcoating, twosided and velvet.
Light types: point, spot, sphere, distant, sharp distant, sun, sky2, constant infinite, infinite (image), laser, projection, mapped point, mapped sphere and triangle (mesh) lights.
Camera sources: perspective, orthographic, environment (panoramic) and stereo, over a projective base.

Texture sources include band, bevel, bilerp, blackbody, Blender textures, bombing, brick, brightness/contrast, checkerboard, cloud, colour depth, density grid, distort, dots, fBm, fresnel approximation, HSV, image map, irregular data, lamp spectrum, marble, normal map, object ID, triplanar, UV, windy, wireframe and wrinkled.
Volume types: clear, homogeneous and heterogeneous.
Release 2.6 added texture resize policies and a film-only out-of-core mode for CUDA GPUs, plus faster mesh-light parsing.
capabilities.inputs: texture resize policies, film out-of-core mode

capabilities.does: LuxCore v2.x provides a C++ and Python API; a make target builds pyluxcore.
BlendLuxCore integrates the engine into Blender 4.5 LTS and 5.2 LTS (v2.11.x), installed as a zip extension; the README advertises accelerated indirect light and efficient caustics.

rea.notes: luxcorerender.org and its wiki returned HTTP 403 to the fetcher, so manual pages were not read. Capabilities come from the repository source tree listings, release notes and READMEs; descriptions of each directory are inferred from file names and marked basis source.

entries.name: Hydra and USD Storm (HdStorm)

licence.name: OpenUSD; the API index page names the TOST licence (text not read); the repository README links a License file without naming it

engines.name: Hydra (Hd)
engines.does: Framework that connects scene graphs to renderers; Hydra 2.0 centres on scene indices and renderers, with a legacy render delegate and render index kept for emulation.

engines.name: Storm (HdSt)
engines.does: Hydra renderer for GPU rasterisation; reads scene data, builds command buffers that share GPU resources, and suits changing scenes and cached playback.

engines.name: UsdImaging
engines.does: Layer that turns a USD stage into Hydra data through a stage scene index and prim adapters; UsdImagingGLEngine is the application entry point.

engines.name: Third-party render delegates
engines.does: Renderers such as RenderMan (hdPrman) and Arnold plug into Hydra to render USD stages.

capabilities.does: Hd links many scene graphs to many renderers; scene processing, rendering and the application are kept separate so each can be reused.
Hydra 2.0 scene representation: HdSceneIndexBase gives prims on request and sends PrimsAdded, PrimsRemoved, PrimsDirtied and PrimsRenamed notices to observers.
Filtering scene indices transform an input scene lazily; core filters include merging, flattening, prefixing, notice batching and dependency forwarding.
capabilities.outputs: Scene edits without touching the source

capabilities.does: Filters are bundled as HdSceneIndexPlugin and registered per renderer with a phase and order, so renderer-specific filters run after application filters before the terminal scene index.
Container, vector and sampled data sources with locators address prim data; sampled sources return values at shutter offsets for motion blur.
Schemas for meshes (topology, subdivision scheme, geom subsets, double-sided), basis curves, volumes with field bindings, volume fields (OpenVDB and Field3D) and instancers.
capabilities.inputs: mesh, basisCurves, volume, volumeField, instancer schemas

capabilities.does: Material schema holds per-render-context networks of nodes, terminals and interface parameters, plus material overrides.
Light schema marks lights and carries light-link, shadow-link and light-filter-link data; lights expect a light terminal on their material.
Camera schema carries projection, apertures, focal length, clipping, f-stop and focus distance, shutter and exposure, split diopter and lens distortion.
capabilities.inputs: fStop, focusDistance, focalLength, shutter, splitDiopter, lensDistortion

capabilities.does: Render settings schema stores settings per renderer name (such as ri or storm), colour space, included purposes, and render products with render variables, camera and resolution.
Render buffer schema describes AOV buffers by dimensions, format and multisampling.
Hydra 1.0 style: HdRenderDelegate with HdRenderIndex and Rprim, Sprim and Bprim types, synced in tier order from a scene delegate; Hydra 2.0 keeps adapters for it.
New renderers derive from HdRendererPlugin, created through HdRendererPluginRegistry; a pure Hydra 2.0 renderer overrides _CreateRenderer, otherwise a legacy delegate is wrapped.

UsdImaging turns a stage into Hydra data with a stage scene index and prim adapters for prim types and API schemas; one USD prim can expand into several subprims; UsdImagingGLEngine is the entry point.
HdSt is the core of the HdStorm renderer: it reads scene data from the render index and builds command buffers that share GPU resources, for scenes that change often or play back from cache.
Storm turns MaterialX networks into shaders through the MaterialX GLSL generator (a Metal generator is also named); shaders compile once and are shared by draw batches.
usdMtlx reads MaterialX files into USD material prims; some MaterialX features do not convert, and edits to external .mtlx files do not refresh the stage.
hdPrman is a third-party USD Imaging plugin that renders USD with RenderMan 25 or newer, built opt-in with --prman; it supports colour, depth, primId, instanceId and elementId AOVs.

arnold-usd provides an Arnold Hydra render delegate covering meshes, volumes, point instancers, materials, lights, cameras, motion blur, AOVs and render settings, plus a USD procedural and Sdr node plugin.
A Hydra Scene Debugger and usdview can visualise scene indices and filters.
Default build covers core, Imaging and UsdImaging; it is developed mainly on Linux, built and supported on macOS and Windows, with embeddable builds for iOS, visionOS and WebAssembly.

outcomes: Pluggable final renders through third-party delegates

rea.notes: Storm feature pages (shadows, transparency, MSAA, GPU backends) were not found: the HdSt overview page is short and the Hgi and Karma pages returned 404. Capabilities cover Hydra structure, schemas, MaterialX in Storm and named delegates only.

entries.verified: 2026-11-02, how: OpenUSD Hydra getting-started guide, prim schema, MaterialX and HdSt pages, hdPrman page, arnold-usd and OpenUSD READMEs read

entries.name: AMD Radeon ProRender

licence.name: license.txt in the SDK repository (terms not read); GitHub API labels the licence Other

engines.name: Northstar
engines.does: Main path-tracing backend; since 3.01.00 it runs on HIP by default with precompiled kernels, OpenCL stays optional.

engines.name: HybridPro
engines.does: Hybrid rendering backend with D3D12 support, software ray tracing and procedural curve tracing, per the release notes.

engines.name: SDK and API
engines.does: C API (RPR) with headers, tutorials and Python bindings for integrating the renderer in applications.

engines.name: HdRpr Hydra delegate
engines.does: Plug-in that renders USD and Hydra scenes with ProRender, buildable for usdview or Houdini.

capabilities.does: Physically based path tracing on CPUs, GPUs or both through the RPR SDK, usable by developers directly or by artists through plug-ins.
SDK page lists OpenCL 1.2 GPUs (tuned for AMD), Metal 2 on macOS and CPU rendering, on Windows, macOS, Ubuntu and CentOS.

HIP became the default Northstar compute backend in 3.01.00 (February 2023); the OpenCL backend remains available but AMD does not recommend it long term. Missing kernels return RPR_ERROR_SHADER_COMPILATION.
HybridPro backend: Hybrid mode and D3D12 arrived in 2.02.16, software ray tracing in 2.02.17, and procedural curve tracing and a shadow catcher followed.

Single multipurpose material with weighted layers for diffuse, reflection, refraction, coating, sheen, emissive, subsurface, transparency, normal and displacement; supports metallic/roughness and specular/glossiness workflows.
capabilities.outputs: Most surface looks from one node

capabilities.does: Further material nodes arrived over releases: toon shader, ramp node, Voronoi texture, blackbody, triplanar UV and rounded-corner bevel.
MaterialX displacement arrived in 3.01.00, tessellation-free displacement for ray tracing and bump-map nodes in 3.01.03, and MaterialX SSS in HybridPro 3.01.04 Beta 2.
Light BVH and IES lights (2.02.16 and 2.02.17), spot light falloff, light layer filtering, and light linking for toon shading.
Camera motion transform API, post-scale, lens shift and camera UV distortion (3.01.00).
ASVGF denoiser improvements and FSR 2 upscaling in 2.02.16 and 2.02.17; the SDK page links Radeon Image Filters and Radeon Machine Learning as companion libraries.
AOVs added over time: mesh ID, volume, SSS, direct and indirect diffuse and reflection, extended Cryptomatte, and ambient occlusion (3.01.04).
Fog and atmosphere volume (2.02.9) and heterogeneous volumes on CPU (2.02.5) and GPU (2.02.6).
Curve primitives were introduced in release 1.320 (October 2018) and procedural curve tracing in HybridPro 2.02.16.
Shadow catcher (HybridPro from 2.02.17) and reflection catcher (from 1.34.0) for compositing CG into plates.
The SDK repository ships tutorial samples and Python bindings built with nanobind, premake build files and a trace player folder.
HdRpr renders USD and Hydra scenes on OpenCL 1.2 hardware as a usdview or Houdini plug-in; Windows is supported, Linux and macOS experimental.
Plug-ins are documented for Blender, Maya, 3ds Max, Unreal Engine, Houdini and Inventor, plus a material library; the documentation footer is dated 2022.
Related AMD libraries in the docs: Radeon Image Filters, Radeon Machine Learning, RadeonRays, HIP RT and AMD RenderStudio.

outcomes: Photoreal stills and animations in host DCCs

The SDK repository publishes headers, binaries, samples and docs; licence terms in license.txt were not read, GitHub API labels the licence Other. entries.name: Arnold

licence.name: commercial; bundled with Maya and 3ds Max per Wikipedia; the arnold-usd plug-ins are Apache-2.0

engines.name: CPU path tracer
engines.does: Unbiased Monte Carlo path tracing for physically based images; runs on x86 and Apple M-series processors.

engines.name: Arnold GPU
engines.does: GPU rendering on CUDA-capable NVIDIA cards through OptiX, added in 2019 according to Wikipedia.

engines.name: Hydra render delegate and USD procedural (arnold-usd)
engines.does: Open-source components that render USD scenes through Arnold, either from Hydra viewers or by loading USD into Arnold as a procedural.

capabilities.does: standard_surface is the main physically based material. It layers diffuse, specular with complex Fresnel for metals, specular transmission, subsurface, thin scattering, a second specular coat, sheen, thin film and emission, mixed in a stated order.
capabilities.inputs: component groups: Base, Specular, Transmission, Subsurface, Coat, Sheen, Emission, Thin Film, Geometry, Matte, AOV ids, Advanced, Bump and Normal Mapping

capabilities.does: Default values suit plastic, wood and stone. Pushing one key weight to 1 moves toward other material classes: Metalness for gold, silver, iron and car paint; Transmission for glass and water; Subsurface for skin, wax and leaves; Thin Walled for paper and bubbles.
capabilities.inputs: Metalness, Transmission, Subsurface, Thin Walled (0 to 1)

capabilities.does: standard_surface conserves energy by default: as specular or metallic share grows, diffuse share drops. Weights or colours above 1 break this and are discouraged because results vary with lighting and add noise.
capabilities.inputs: layer weights and colours kept at or below 1
capabilities.outputs: light out never above light in

capabilities.does: Diffuse surfaces only shade correctly when mesh normals face outward; a flipped sphere renders wrongly. The page documents this as an input requirement.

Arnold is a commercial unbiased, physically based Monte Carlo path tracer. It was started in 1997 and developed with Sony Pictures Imageworks; the Wikipedia page lists version 7.5.1.1 from April 2026.
GPU rendering was added in March 2019 using NVIDIA OptiX on CUDA-enabled cards. The CPU renderer runs on x86 and Apple M-series.
Geometry instancing lets Arnold hold very large scenes in memory. Texture input uses OpenImageIO so many high-resolution textures can be used.
Shaders can be written in C++ or Open Shading Language, and the programmable API is a core part of the product according to Wikipedia.
Plug-ins connect Arnold to Maya, 3ds Max, Houdini, Cinema 4D and Katana; the Autodesk help home lists separate user guides for each. Softimage is named in Wikipedia as an earlier host.

arnold-usd ships a Hydra render delegate. It supports Mesh, Volume and Points, point instancers (also nested), USD Skel, basis curves, UsdPreviewSurface translation, pause and resume, and CPU/GPU switching with defaults set by environment variables.
capabilities.inputs: USD stage in a Hydra viewer

capabilities.does: The Hydra delegate maps USD lights to Arnold: distant, sphere, disk, rect, cylinder and dome lights plus shaping parameters, with light and shadow linking.
Light and shadow linking is supported in the Hydra delegate; the USD procedural also reads light linking.
The Hydra delegate offers Color, Depth and PrimID AOVs, plus raw, primvar and LPE rendervars with SourceName and DataType, filter choice by arnold:filter_type, and deep render products.
capabilities.outputs: extra image channels and deep output

capabilities.does: Hydra delegate supports deformation and transformation motion blur, and motion vectors on points.
capabilities.inputs: time samples on transforms and points

capabilities.does: In the Hydra delegate the camera prim supports perspective projection only.

The Arnold USD procedural loads USD scenes into Arnold. It reads meshes, curves, points, primitive shapes, point instancers, volumes, cameras, UsdLux lights (textured dome, rect, geometry lights), UsdPreviewSurface and UsdUVTexture; NURBS are unsupported.
capabilities.outputs: USD content inside an Arnold render

capabilities.does: Arnold schemas describe Arnold nodes and scenes in USD, with Python bindings, and a node registry plug-in exposes built-in and custom Arnold shaders to Sdr. The registry has no nodes for shapes, lights, filters, drivers or options.

rea.notes: Arnold core is closed. The arnold-usd repository (Hydra delegate, procedural, schemas) is public under Apache-2.0 (LICENSE.md read). Most Arnold user-guide pages on help.autodesk.com returned Page Not Found to the fetch tool; only the standard_surface page opened, and docs.arnoldrenderer.com redirects to it.

entries.verified: 2026-11-02, how: one Autodesk help page, Wikipedia and the arnold-usd README read; most guide pages could not be opened

entries.name: Chaos Corona

licence.name: commercial; interface and render-node licences for distributed rendering; free GUI-less Standalone edition for plug-in developers per Wikipedia

engines.name: CPU renderer
engines.does: CPU-based engine that does unbiased path tracing and also biased rendering with a precomputed secondary solver; modes Progressive, Bucket and BiDir/VCM per Wikipedia.

engines.name: Interactive rendering
engines.does: Image refreshes while the scene is edited; runs fully on the CPU and denoises with the NVIDIA AI denoiser by default.

engines.name: Corona VFB and LightMix
engines.does: Frame buffer with a LightMix tab that rebalances light contributions after rendering.

capabilities.does: CPU renderer with unbiased path tracing and optional biased precomputation; Wikipedia lists Progressive, Bucket and BiDir/VCM modes and optional GPU-based AI denoising.
capabilities.outputs: physically based images on the CPU

capabilities.does: Interactive Rendering refreshes the image as objects, materials, lights, cameras or the environment change, without restarting. It runs on the CPU only. Related entries: floating window or active viewport, Render Selected, Render Regions, DOF focus point from the VFB.
NVIDIA AI denoiser is on by default for interactive and regular rendering and keeps cleaning after rendering stops. A supported GPU is needed and the installer detects it.

Corona Physical Material uses Metalness (0 non-metal, 1 metal), Color, Roughness, IOR (about 1.52 typical glass), Bump, Edge color for grazing metal reflection, Roughness mode (roughness or glossiness) and IOR mode (direct or from a Disney Specular value).
capabilities.inputs: Metalness, Color, Roughness, IOR, Edge color, Bump, Roughness mode, IOR mode, Use complex IOR for metals

capabilities.does: Anisotropy Amount stretches the highlight along perpendicular axes (-1 to 1, 0 isotropic); Rotation turns it in degrees; Anisotropy Orientation selects local axis or UVW.

Refraction Amount blends plastic (0) to glass (1); Thin shell (no inside) models zero-volume panes; Caustics (slow) switches physical caustics versus faster transparent shadows; Thin absorption for thin glass.
capabilities.inputs: Refraction Amount, Thin shell, Caustics (slow), Thin absorption

capabilities.does: Dispersion takes an Abbe number to spread colour; the page says 30 to 60 is typical and below 10 looks unrealistic.
Clearcoat layer with Layer Amount (0 off, 1 full), its own IOR, Roughness, Absorption colour and Bump.
capabilities.inputs: Layer Amount, IOR, Roughness, Absorption, Bump

capabilities.does: Thin Film layer: Amount, thickness texture, Min and Max thickness in nm (typical 10 to 2000), film IOR (lower gives more colour fringing).
capabilities.inputs: Amount, Texture, Min thickness, Max thickness, IOR

capabilities.does: Sheen layer with Layer Amount, front reflection Color and Roughness; it shows at grazing angles even when the colour is black.

Subsurface Scattering with Amount (1 means no diffuse part), Radius and Scatter colour. Volumetric Scattering adds Absorption color and Distance, Scattering color, Directionality (-1 backward to 1 forward) and Single bounce only for god rays.
capabilities.inputs: Amount, Radius, Scatter color, Absorption color/Distance, Scattering color, Directionality

capabilities.does: Glints layer for sparkling flakes: Layer Amount (default 0), Color, Roughness, Anisotropy, Density, Sharpness, Scaling U/V, Glint size, UVW or triplanar mapping and a colour ramp.
capabilities.inputs: Density, Sharpness, Scaling U/V, Glint size, Mapping mode, Color Ramp

capabilities.does: Normals filtering has None, Linear and Roughness Modulation modes; Roughness Modulation has been the default since Corona 11. Base tail lengthens GGX falloff.

Corona Layered Material stacks materials on a base using a Mask per layer. Displacement blends as Blend all layers (default), Only from base material, or Add all layers. No layer cap is stated, but many layers cost render time.
capabilities.inputs: Base mtl, Layer N: Mtl and Mask, Displacement mode

capabilities.does: The documentation index lists Corona material types: Physical, Layered, Legacy, Toon, Skin, Hair, Scanned, Select, Slicer, Shadow Catcher, Volume, Fabric, Light, Light Override, Outline and Rayswitch.

LightMix saves each light or group in its own render channel so intensity and colour can be changed in the VFB without re-rendering, including for interactive renders. Setup groups: Instanced, Individual, Grouped lights, or Layers. Layers composite with an add blend.
capabilities.inputs: CShading_LightMix, CShading_LightSelect, Included light sources, Include Environment Light

capabilities.does: Tone mapping operators: Simple Exposure (-20 to 20), Photographic Exposure, Contrast, White Balance (2000 to 99999 K), Green-Magenta Tint, Saturation, Vignette, Lift Gamma Gain, Filmic mapping with toe and shoulder controls, Tone Curve, Reinhard highlight compression, ACES output transform, LUT.
capabilities.inputs: operator list with Highlight compression, Rich Shadows, Toe/Shoulder Strength and Length

capabilities.does: Several LAN machines render one frame together; master plus render nodes with the Corona DR Server. Master settings: Enable, Search LAN during render, node list, Synchronization interval, Max pixels to transfer at once. Needs interface and render-node licences.
capabilities.inputs: Enable, Search LAN during render, Synchronization interval [s], Max pixels to transfer at once

capabilities.does: Plug-in for 3ds Max (since 2009) and Cinema 4D (since 2019) per Wikipedia; a free Standalone edition without GUI is aimed at plug-in developers.

rea.notes: EULA page listed in the index, not read. Corona Light, Sun, Camera, Volume Material, Render Settings and Supported Features pages came back as stubs when fetched.

entries.verified: 2026-11-02, how: Chaos Corona for 3ds Max pages on documentation.chaos.com read (.md pages) plus Wikipedia

entries.name: D5 Render

licence.name: account and plans exist (docs list Account and Purchase, D5 for Teams); tier terms not read

engines.name: Real-time path tracing GI
engines.does: D5 default global illumination: light bounces are cached by path tracing before rendering; accumulation mode adds samples until the preview matches final output.

engines.name: D5 SR
engines.does: Super-resolution sampling that combines multi-channel feature maps with a neural network to speed up still images; needs at least 1440 by 1440 output.

engines.name: Unreal Engine and NVIDIA RTX base
engines.does: The About page says D5 Render is built on Unreal Engine and NVIDIA RTX technology.

capabilities.does: Real-time path tracing is the default GI. Custom parameters, used only for accumulation, final renders and video: GI Precision (three levels), Refl. Depth, SPP and Roughness limit (default 0.5). Defaults when custom is off: GI Precision 1, Reflection Depth 2, SPP 64.
capabilities.inputs: GI Precision, Refl. Depth, SPP, Roughness limit, Accumulate (F4)

capabilities.does: Accumulate mode keeps adding pixel samples until the preview matches final quality; moving the camera or pressing Esc stops it.
D5 SR is a proprietary super-resolution method for stills at 1440 by 1440 or larger. It does not support EXR output, is not advised with depth of field or foam post effects, and loses some detail.

Caustics must be on for both material and light. Custom templates give reflective caustics; Transparent and Water give reflective and refractive ones. Light controls: Caustics Intensity and Softness (needs light radius above 0). At most 64 lights at once.
capabilities.inputs: Caustics on material and light, Caustics Intensity, Softness

capabilities.does: Ray tracing uses DXR on Windows. Supported cards: NVIDIA GTX and RTX, workstation RTX, AMD Radeon RX and PRO, Intel Arc. Several GPUs are not combined. Output is the same on every card that passes the hardware test.
AI Model Generation, in beta: Text to 3D from a prompt, with a Use a Fixed Seed option to reproduce results. Ten free attempts, then credits.
capabilities.inputs: text prompt, Use a Fixed Seed

capabilities.does: Image to 3D takes a main-view image (.jpg, .jpeg or .png, up to 10 MB, above 1040 by 1040 recommended) and up to three extra angles, with Model Name and Use a Fixed Seed settings. Output formats are not stated.
capabilities.inputs: main-view image, Multi-angle Views, Model Name

capabilities.does: The About page states D5 has self-developed high-precision GI and denoise technology tuned for RTX cards. No settings were shown.

outcomes: architectural stills, video and real-time walkthroughs

rea.notes: www.d5render.com returned 403. Only docs.d5render.com pages were read. Platforms beyond Windows DXR were not stated; Windows is inferred from the DXR sentence. Roadmap and plan pricing not read.

entries.verified: 2026-11-02, how: D5 help centre pages read

entries.name: Enscape

licence.name: commercial plug-in; terms not read

engines.name: Enscape renderer
engines.does: Own real-time renderer for architecture on OpenGL 4.4 and Vulkan; combines path tracing, screen-space techniques and BVH-based global data structures for indirect light and reflections.

capabilities.does: Indirect lighting and reflections come from a mix of path tracing, screen-space techniques and BVH-based global data structures, with physically based materials meant to keep lighting cost mostly independent of project size.
Supports OpenGL 4.4 and Vulkan.
Real-time rendering linked to the live host model: changes in the host or in Enscape update both ways.
Hosts named: Revit, SketchUp, Rhinoceros 3D, ArchiCAD, Vectorworks and ReluxDesktop.
AI tools named: a Veras integration for creative exploration, AI-enhanced scene enrichment, and an upscaler for drafts up to 16K.
VR support for interactive design reviews.

entries.name: Karma

licence.name: part of Houdini; commercial licence (edition terms not read)

engines.name: Karma CPU
engines.does: Physically based path tracer in software; USD scene description, acts as a Hydra render delegate and is meant to replace Mantra for new projects.

engines.name: Karma XPU
engines.does: Engine that uses CPU (Embree) and NVIDIA GPU (OptiX) devices together; faster than CPU but with fewer features. Needs NVIDIA driver 570 or later and compute capability 5.0.

engines.name: Solaris viewport delegate
engines.does: The viewport can draw the Solaris view with Karma; snapshots do not carry all AOVs.

capabilities.does: Karma is the path tracer of Houdini, built on USD and Hydra. Karma CPU and Karma XPU are selectable engines; Principled-shader Object scenes can be rendered directly or after a Scene Import LOP.
capabilities.inputs: USD stage, Karma LOP / Karma ROP, Camera path
capabilities.outputs: rendered frames to MPlay or disk

capabilities.does: XPU runs on Embree (CPU) and OptiX (GPU) devices, each GPU a separate device with no pooled memory; if one device fails, the others finish the frame. Shaders compile on first use (1 to 2 minutes). Control by environment variables such as KARMA_XPU_DEVICES.
capabilities.inputs: Rendering Engine = XPU Engine, KARMA_XPU_DEVICES, KARMA_XPU_DISABLE_OPTIX_DEVICE

capabilities.does: XPU limits: 4 custom trace sets, 4 shadow-linking groups, UDIM up to 10 by 10, dome lights only lat-long maps, SSS only on Polymesh and Points, Gaussian splats get no lighting, Principled shader is converted to USD Preview Surface.
capabilities.outputs: knowledge of what XPU can render

capabilities.does: Sampling is ordered: Pixel Samples (primary) first, then Min/Max Secondary Samples, then quality multipliers for Diffuse, Reflection, Refraction, Volume and SSS. A pixel oracle with a Variance Threshold limits primary samples; Secondary Noise Level sets the indirect threshold.
capabilities.inputs: Pixel Samples, Min/Max Secondary Samples, Secondary Noise Level, Diffuse/Reflection/Refraction/Volume/SSS Quality, Variance Threshold, Path Traced Samples

capabilities.does: Indirect Guiding is a machine-learning feature that speeds up secondary sampling, mainly useful when rendering multiple frames in one process.

Karma samples each light once by default. Light Sampling Quality samples lights more often for cleaner direct light and shadows; each light has its own Sampling Quality multiplier and a light-tree Sampling Mode (uniform sampling excludes a light from the tree).

A Denoiser, for example NVIDIA OptiX, is chosen on the Render Settings Filters tab; the AOVs field lists render vars to denoise and a Tone Map dropdown applies a curve to them. XPU also lists an Enable Denoising setting.
capabilities.inputs: Denoiser, AOVs, Tone Map, Enable Denoising

capabilities.does: AOVs are set in the Karma Render Settings LOP. Category checkboxes toggle passes; custom AOVs have Source Type Raw, Primvar, LPE or Intrinsic. A Karma AOV VOP makes material-based AOVs. Per-AOV filter, colour space and 16 or 32 bit precision.
capabilities.inputs: Source Type, Source Name, AOV Name, Split per LPE Tag, Ordered Render Vars

capabilities.does: Karma writes Cryptomatte AOVs; IDs come from primitives, bound materials, or constant/uniform string or integer primvars. Per-instance IDs need a unique string primvar per instance.

Karma blurs motion from time samples authored on the stage. Settings: Motion Samples from Stage (on), Transform Time Samples (2), Geometry Time Samples (2), Velocity Blur (None, Velocity, Acceleration), Instance Velocity Blur, Instance Motion Samples. Acceleration blur needs three or more samples to curve.
capabilities.inputs: Motion Blur LOP, Cache LOP, velocities, accelerations, angularVelocities

capabilities.does: Karma lights: UsdLux Cylinder, Disk, Distant, Dome, Point, Portal, Rect, Sphere, plus KarmaSkyDomeLight and Karma Physical Sky. Properties include Intensity, Exposure, Color, colour temperature (1000 to 10000 K), Diffuse/Specular Multiplier, shadow controls with falloff, and Spread for rect and disk lights.
capabilities.inputs: Intensity, Exposure, Color, Color Temperature, Normalize Power, Shadow Enable/Color/Falloff Start Distance/Falloff Gamma, Radius, Width, Height, Angle

capabilities.does: KarmaSkyDomeLight takes Solar Altitude, Solar Azimuth and Turbidity; Karma Physical Sky and a Sky Atmosphere LOP are listed as XPU-supported.

Geometry Light LOP turns meshes, points, curves or volumes into lights through LightAPI, MeshLightAPI (meshes only) or VolumeLightAPI. Material Sync Mode: No Material Response, Material Glow Tints Light, or Independent; Diffuse Multiplier preferred over raising intensity.
capabilities.inputs: Primitives, Material Sync Mode, Intensity, Exposure, Color, Diffuse Multiplier, width, pscale

capabilities.does: Light filters are VOP nodes built in a Light Filter Library: Gel (tint, intensity, diffuse/specular), Gobo (projects a texture) and Barndoor (shapes output). Added through a light's Light filters parameter. A Karma Light Projection node makes UVs.
capabilities.inputs: Light filters, Gel Tint, Gobo texture, Barndoor

capabilities.does: Portal lights are transformable; Render Geometry Settings marks a prim as a portal source and can name the dome lights it affects. Portal geometry must not overlap polygons in XPU.
capabilities.outputs: faster interior sampling of dome light

capabilities.does: XPU lists point, rectangle, sphere, disk, cylinder, distant, dome and physical sky lights as supported along with light linking, shadow linking, portal lights and light filters.
capabilities.inputs: light link and shadow link collections

capabilities.does: Houdini provides VOP nodes matching MaterialX. Builders: USD MaterialX Builder and Karma MaterialX Builder in the Material Library LOP. MtlX Standard Surface is the recommended uber shader; BSDF nodes include Conductor, Dielectric, Sheen and Subsurface; layer and mix nodes combine them.
capabilities.inputs: MtlX Standard Surface, MtlX Layer, MtlX Mix, MtlX Image, MtlX Triplanar Projection, MtlX Normalmap
capabilities.outputs: node-based materials; .mtlx import via Reference LOP

capabilities.does: Karma terminal shaders under XPU: MtlX Standard Surface, MtlX OpenPBR Surface, MtlX Surface Unlit, USD Preview Surface, Karma Hair and Karma Fur (fur with medulla support). Both Standard and OpenPBR can emit light.
capabilities.inputs: Karma Material Builder, Material Library LOP

capabilities.does: Karma Fur is a physically based hair and fur material with medulla support; Karma Hair is a Karma-specific shader whose patterns MaterialX nodes can drive.
Displacement shaders are best finished with a Collect VOP; Dicing Quality sets the subdivision resolution for smooth and displaced surfaces.

Karma Volume node builds MaterialX volume shaders for XPU; MtlX Volume plus MtlX Geompropvalue binds fields by name. Volume materials apply only to volume prims (VDBs) and read constant primvars on density.
capabilities.inputs: MtlX Volume, Karma Volume, field names

capabilities.does: Meshes render as subdivision surfaces when subdivisionScheme is set; catmullClark is fully supported, loop and bilinear are not.

Karma renders BasisCurves as rounded tubes, ribbons or oriented ribbons; Points as spheres or discs; and Volume, Houdini Field, OpenVDB and Field3D primitives. Native instances and PointInstancers are supported.
capabilities.inputs: prim types, Render Visibility category expression

capabilities.does: Lens shaders can be enabled with Use Lens Shader; the Karma Physical Lens VOP gives common lens effects, Lens Bokeh VOP generates circular, polygon or butterfly bokeh. Custom lens shaders are Karma CPU only, while XPU lists Physical Lens Shader support.
capabilities.inputs: Use Lens Shader, Karma Physical Lens VOP, Lens Bokeh VOP

capabilities.does: XPU renders Gaussian splats; they receive no lighting. A KARMA_XPU_GSPLATS_RENDER_MODE variable selects stochastic (0) or depth peeling (1).

rea.notes: Houdini licence text not read. Karma documentation is in the public Houdini docs (22.0 per the geometry lights page).

entries.verified: 2026-11-02, how: SideFX Houdini Solaris and Karma documentation pages read

entries.name: KeyShot

licence.name: subscription; editions KeyShot Studio, Studio VR, Studio Web, Cloud and Network Rendering; Studio Business licence needed for network rendering

engines.name: Real-time ray tracing renderer
engines.does: Ray-traced viewport preview with physically based materials and lighting; renders on CPU, GPU or both, with NVIDIA and AMD hardware ray tracing and Apple GPU support from 2026.2.

engines.name: KeyShot Studio AI
engines.does: Local AI tools included with a subscription: Restyle, Background, Imagine, Transform and Replace, all driven by text prompts.

engines.name: Network Rendering
engines.does: Worker machines on a network share render jobs; CPU jobs scale with core count and each GPU counts as 16 licensed cores.

capabilities.does: Physically based rendering with global illumination and physically accurate caustics, plus a real-time ray-traced preview in the viewport.
Rendering on CPU, GPU, or both together; NVIDIA and AMD GPUs with hardware-accelerated ray tracing are supported. Apple GPU support is named for 2026.2.
AI Denoise is listed for faster renders.
Cryptomatte and OpenPBR support are listed for professional pipelines.
A drag-and-drop material system with scientifically accurate base materials, and a Material Graph for procedural texturing.
Partner-certified libraries are listed: Pantone, RAL, Mold-Tech, Sorensen, Coloro, INTERPON and Axalta.
Physical lights and a patented HDRI editor, plus Light Layers and advanced lighting control.
One-click animations: turntables, exploded views, colorway transitions and product reveals. Studio Switch animations and camera flythroughs are also named on the home page.

Native import for 34 or more 3D and CAD formats (the page also gives 36 and 50+ extensions), 14 CAD plug-ins, and LiveLinking that syncs CAD changes while keeping views, materials, textures and animations.
capabilities.outputs: scene kept in sync with CAD

capabilities.does: Web and marketing export to GLB, USD and interactive 3D for e-commerce and AR is listed on the home page.

KeyShot Studio AI: Restyle changes finishes from a text prompt, Background places a product in a described scene, Imagine makes new directions without 3D geometry, Transform redirects a rendering, Replace edits an isolated part. Runs locally.

Computers on a network act as Workers for render jobs on macOS, Windows or Linux. CPU time falls roughly with core count. A Studio Business licence is required; GPU jobs need no separate licence and each GPU uses 16 of the licensed cores.
Assembly-aware exploded views are listed on the home page.

entries.name: OctaneRender

licence.name: commercial; standalone and slave licences, subscriptions, offline USB dongles; tier details not read

engines.name: CUDA path tracer
engines.does: Unbiased, spectrally correct GPU renderer; needs an NVIDIA CUDA GPU, RT cores speed up some scenes.

engines.name: Octane X (Metal)
engines.does: Metal version of Octane for Apple hardware, per Wikipedia; its listed stable release with 2022.1 CUDA is dated June 2023.

engines.name: AI denoiser and AI light
engines.does: Spectral AI denoiser and an AI Light system shown cleaning a render at 50 samples.

capabilities.does: Octane is described as an unbiased, spectrally correct GPU render engine.

Out-of-core support puts geometry and textures in system memory so scenes can exceed GPU memory, which also frees VRAM for the denoiser. Devices cannot be toggled while it is active (FAQ page, older text).

Several GPUs scale linearly, but VRAM is not pooled and the smallest card limits scene size. NVLink is supported from 2018.1 on supported RTX setups. Networked rendering supports up to 40 GPUs depending on licence tier (FAQ page, older text).
RTX acceleration is claimed at 2 to 5 times on RTX GPUs, with larger gains in complex scenes and multi-GPU setups.
Spectral AI denoiser; it needs extra memory: about 5 GB for a 4K render, 20 GB for 8K, plus about 450 MB of VRAM per device.
An AI Light system works with the denoiser; the product page shows it in a demo but gives no settings.
Layered material: a base layer with up to 8 layers on top. Node types include layered material, diffuse, specular, sheen, metallic and layer group.
The FAQ lists glossy, diffuse, specular (glass), mix, metallic, toon and universal layered materials.
Spectral random-walk SSS uses a Random Walk medium for skin and other absorbing or scattering materials.
Spectral hair material with several colouring modes and roughness parameters along a strand.
Procedural and OSL vertex displacement, height or vector, computed before rendering, with a displacement mixer node to layer maps. The older system is now called Texture Displacement.
OSL shaders can be volume textures that drive absorption, scattering and emission instead of fixed colours.
VECTRON makes vector-polygon geometry for procedural scenes and volumes on the GPU; SPECTRON makes procedural volumetric lights such as spots with blockers, barn doors and gels.
A scene graph powered by Brigade is claimed to give 10 to 100 times faster scene updates and real-time movement of high-poly objects.
Lighting options named in the FAQ: sun and sky, environment maps, and area or IES lights.
Realistic camera model with real-time depth of field and integrated post-processing.
Import formats named: OBJ, Alembic (.abc), FBX and VDB. Host plug-ins exist, for example Cinema 4D and 3ds Max.
Octane is a CUDA 12 application: Windows needs NVIDIA driver 572.x or higher, macOS needs 15.x or later on Apple M1 or newer, Linux needs glibc 2.11.1 or later; cuDNN is required.

rea.notes: The standalone manual (docs.otoy.com/standaloneSE) has no readable table of contents for the fetch tool; only the cover, installation, hardware and software pages were read. Kernels (direct light, path tracing, PMC, info-channel), RenderTarget and the node reference could not be verified. ORBX is named in OTOY site navigation but its spec was not read. FAQ text is older (mentions CUDA 10). EULA not read.

entries.name: NVIDIA Omniverse RTX Renderer

licence.name: part of Omniverse Kit-based applications; the Licenses page was not read

engines.name: RTX - Real-Time 2.0 mode
engines.does: Physically based path-tracing mode that reaches real-time rates with DLSS neural rendering; some effects (subsurface scattering, depth of field, volumes) may differ from the Interactive mode.

engines.name: RTX - Interactive (Path Tracing) mode
engines.does: Higher-fidelity path tracer with progressive sample accumulation and an OptiX denoiser, at some cost in speed.

engines.name: Omniverse (platform)
engines.does: The docs front page describes Omniverse as libraries and microservices for physical-AI simulation applications, built on OpenUSD; Kit SDK is the application framework and ovrtx is a pre-release RTX rendering and sensor library.

capabilities.does: RTX Real-Time 2.0 is a path-tracing based mode that uses DLSS neural rendering for real-time speed. It needs DLSS Ray Reconstruction on supported GPUs; without it images look much noisier. Eco Mode stops rendering after a number of unchanged frames.
DLSS settings: Super Resolution (3 = DLSS, 4 = DLAA), Mode (Performance, Balanced, Quality, Auto) and Frame Generation (Ada Lovelace and newer).
capabilities.outputs: higher-resolution output from a lower-resolution render

capabilities.does: Real-Time path settings: Max Bounces (3), max specular and transmission bounces (3), SSS volume bounces (15), fractional cutout opacity, a reflection cache controlled by a Roughness Threshold (0.3; 1.0 disables it).

Interactive mode accumulates samples: Samples per Pixel per Frame (1 to 32, default 1), Total Samples per Pixel (512; 0 = no limit), Max Bounces 4, Max Specular and Transmission Bounces 6, Max SSS Volume Scattering Bounces 64, Max Fog Scattering Bounces 2.
Interactive mode has optional adaptive sampling with a Target Error (default 0.001).
Firefly Filtering clamps per-ray intensity: Max Ray Intensity Glossy and Diffuse both default to 3200 in Interactive mode; Real-Time mode also has an emissive limit.
OptiX denoiser only: Denoising (on by default), Temporal Mode, Blend Factor (0 denoised only, 1 none) and Denoise AOVs. The listed Real-Time page has no general denoiser switch.
Anti-aliasing sample pattern: Box, Triangle (default), Gaussian or Uniform, with a filter radius (default 1.0).

Path-tracing AOV toggles: Background, Diffuse Filter, Direct Illumination, Global Illumination, Illuminance, Luminance, Motion Vectors, Reflections, Reflection Filter, Refractions, Refraction Filter, Self-Illumination, Subsurface Filter, View and World Normal, Volumes, World Position, Z-Depth, with depth range and 32-bit option.
LPEs are configured through USD RenderVars with sourceType set to lpe rather than through RTX settings.
Multi Matte writes ID matte channels: a Channel Count and a Multimatte ID Index for each of Red, Green and Blue.

Non-uniform volumes: transmittance by Biased Ray Marching or Ratio Tracking, Max Collision Count 1024, Max Light Collision Count 32, Max Non-Uniform Volume Scattering Bounces 2. Rayleigh atmosphere option with scale and Skip Background.
Multi-GPU rendering with automatic load balancing, per-GPU weights, and compression of radiance, albedo and normals; the overview states up to 16 GPUs in one system.
Real-Time SSS is off by default with a per-frame sample cap of 32, firefly filtering, and a transmission sub-block with BSDF sample counts and an optional ReSTIR switch.
capabilities.outputs: translucent skin and wax in real time

capabilities.does: Simple Fog (colour, height start, density and falloff, distance start and end) and Global Volumetric Effects (atmosphere height, max distance, density multiplier, transmittance colour, single-scattering albedo, anisotropy -1 to 1, detail noise with octaves).
NVIDIA Flow fire and smoke can be rendered with ray-traced shadows, reflections, translucency and path tracing, each a separate switch; all are off by default.

Geometry and texture streaming with GPU budgets (geometry budget 64000 MB default, texture priority 0.5), block-compression quality (Fastest to Highest), mip generation for normal maps and a maximum mip count.
Subdivision surfaces through OpenSubdiv with refinementLevel (each step multiplies triangles by 4) and an adaptive refinement switch; curves use a split count.

Materials are NVIDIA MDL and UsdPreviewSurface. The docs list MDL search path, MDL Distill and Bake and MDL language pages, plus OmniPBR, OmniGlass, OmniSurface, OmniSurface Blend, OmniEmissive, OmniHair and OpenPBR templates.

OmniPBR parameters: diffuse_color_constant (0.2 grey), reflection_roughness_constant (0.5), metallic_constant (0), specular_level (0.5), ORM packed texture switch, albedo desaturation, brightness and tint, detail normal map.
OmniPBR emission: enable_emission, emissive_color, emissive_intensity (default 1.0), emissive colour and mask maps.
OmniPBR opacity: opacity_constant, opacity map, mono source mode (alpha, average, luminance, maximum) and opacity_threshold (above 0 gives cutout).
OmniPBR clearcoat layer: tint, transparency, roughness (0), weight, flatten, IOR (1.56) and its own normal map and strength.
OmniPBR normal maps with bump_factor strength, detail normal map (strength 0.3), U and V tangent flip switches (V flip is on by default; DirectX format recommended).

OpenPBR Base follows the MaterialX reference implementation translated to MDL. In Real-Time 2.0 mode sheen and thin film are not supported and subsurface needs enabling; refraction may need more bounces.

Light types: Distant, Sphere, Rect, Disk, Cylinder, Dome. Properties: Intensity, Exposure, Color Temperature, Normalize Power, shaping with Focus, Cone and IES (inputs:shaping:ies:file), dome Texture File and Format, projector direction texture.
capabilities.inputs: Intensity, Exposure, Color Temperature, Normalize Power, Focus, Cone, IES file

capabilities.does: Light Linking selects which objects a light illuminates and Shadow Link selects which objects receive its shadow.
Dome light handling: strategy Image-Based Lighting, Approximated or Limited, baking resolution 4096. Background can be none, texture or colour with texture mode, colour space and luminance scale.
A camera-attached light with Distant or Spot type, colour, intensity (3000), angle, radius, cone angle and softness, for headlight-style lighting.

Cameras use UsdGeomCamera pinhole with Perspective or Orthographic projection, focalLength, focusDistance and fStop for depth of field, aperture and offset, clipping, and an exposure API with fStop, iso, time and responsivity.
Lens distortion schemas: OpenCV pinhole and fisheye, Kannala-Brandt K3, RadTanThinPrism, fTheta, look-up-table based, and omnidirectional stereo.
Stereo Role (left eye, right eye, mono, non-stereo) and omnidirectional stereo with an interpupillary distance default of 0.064 m.
Global shutter by default or rolling shutter with a per-pixel exposure texture, and shutter:open and shutter:close for motion blur.

Tone mapping operators: Clamp, Linear, Reinhard, Modified Reinhard, HejiHableAlu, HableUC2, ACES, Iray, with Camera Exposure, Film ISO, F-stop and White Point. Auto Exposure adds a histogram filter (Median or Average) and adaptation speed.
capabilities.inputs: operator choice, Film ISO, F-stop, White Point, Adaptation Speed

capabilities.does: Colour Correction with mode (ACES pre-tone or standard post-tone), output space (sRGB Linear or AcesCG), Saturation, Contrast, Gamma, Gain, Offset.
capabilities.inputs: Mode, Output Color Space, Saturation, Contrast, Gamma, Gain, Offset

capabilities.does: Post DOF overrides: Enable DOF, Subject Distance, Focal Length, F-stop, Anisotropy.
capabilities.inputs: Subject Distance, Focal Length, F-stop, Anisotropy

capabilities.does: Motion Blur with Blur Diameter Fraction, Exposure Time Fraction and Number of Samples.
capabilities.inputs: Blur Diameter Fraction, Exposure Time Fraction, Number of Samples

capabilities.does: FFT Bloom built from an aperture model: Blades, Aperture Rotation, Sensor Diagonal, F-stop, Focal Length; or non-physical halo and flare falloff and weight controls. There is no separate lens flare effect.
capabilities.inputs: Scale, Cutoff Point, Cutoff Fuzziness, Blades, Halo Radius, Anisotropic Flare Weight

capabilities.does: Chromatic Aberration with per-channel strength (red, green, blue), Radial or Barrel algorithm per channel, and a Lanczos sampler option.
capabilities.inputs: Strength Red/Green/Blue, Algorithm Red/Green/Blue, Use Lanczos Sampler

capabilities.does: TV Noise and Film Grain: grain amount, colour amount, luminance amount, grain size; TV controls for scanlines, vignetting, ghost flicker, wavy distortion, vertical lines, random splotches.
capabilities.inputs: Grain Amount, Color Amount, Luminance Amount, Grain Size

capabilities.does: Matte Object, Shadow Catcher, Fade Out, Composite Shift and Composite Contrast let CG sit on a background; Compositing outputs alpha and black background options.
capabilities.inputs: Matte Object, Shadow Catcher, Output Alpha in Composited Image

scripting: Kit SDK application framework and extensions (named on the docs front page)
USD render settings paths such as /rtx/pathtracing/*

rea.notes: Licenses page listed on the docs front page, not read. ovrtx is shown on the front page as a pre-release GitHub library; its licence was not read. Kit-based apps USD Composer and Explorer are listed as legacy.

entries.name: RenderMan

licence.name: commercial licence, floating (licence server) or node-locked; the licensing page read does not describe a non-commercial edition

engines.name: RIS
engines.does: The path-tracing renderer with CPU integrators (PxrPathTracer, PxrVCM, PxrUnified) and plug-in C++ patterns and BxDFs.

engines.name: XPU
engines.does: Data-parallel renderer that runs on CPU and GPU with the same scene; supports PxrPathTracer, OSL patterns, Lama and MaterialX nodes, but not PxrVCM or PxrUnified.

engines.name: Denoiser
engines.does: Machine-learning image filter from Disney Research that cleans partly converged renders; runs from the command line, a UI, or the host applications.

engines.name: Stylized Looks
engines.does: Display-filter and shader toolset that turns rendered output into toon, line, hatching and painterly images.

capabilities.does: Forward path tracer integrator for final frames. Direct light uses multiple importance sampling over light and BxDF samples; indirect rays are allocated by sampleMode ("bxdf" or "manual").
capabilities.inputs: PxrPathTracer: maxIndirectBounces (8), sampleMode, numLightSamples (2), numBxdfSamples (1), numIndirectSamples, numDiffuseSamples, numSpecularSamples, numSubsurfaceSamples, numRefractionSamples, allowCaustics (off), accumOpacity

capabilities.does: Controls how deep and how bright indirect paths may get: Russian roulette termination plus per-ray luminance clamping, in both PxrPathTracer and PxrVCM.
capabilities.inputs: rouletteDepth, rouletteThreshold (0.2), clampDepth (2), clampLuminance (10.0, large value disables), maxIndirectBounces
capabilities.outputs: bounded path length and fewer fireflies

capabilities.does: PxrVCM combines bidirectional path tracing with progressive photon mapping (vertex merging) and direct lighting, weighted together. Helps interiors with strong indirect light and caustics. Not available in XPU.
capabilities.inputs: connectPaths (on), mergePaths (on), mergeRadius (5.0 px), timeRadius (1.0), maxIndirectBounces (10), photonGuiding (0 to 1), photonGuidingBBoxMin/Max
capabilities.outputs: image with better caustics and indirect convergence

capabilities.does: PxrUnified is one integrator that switches between unidirectional, bidirectional and photon-mapping modes with a traceLightPaths setting. Marked experimental; not in XPU. Several features such as holdout workflows are listed as unsupported.
capabilities.inputs: traceLightPaths (Off, On, Photons Only, UPS/VCM), maxIndirectBounces (8), useTraceDepth, maxRayDistance, catchAllLights, emissionMultiplier, directClamp, indirectClamp, causticClamp, sssOversampling
capabilities.outputs: beauty image from the chosen sampling mode

capabilities.does: Manifold walk finds caustic light paths through specular interfaces and is cheaper than photon tracing. Lights and materials can opt in; volume caustics are a separate costly switch.
capabilities.inputs: manifoldWalk, maxIterations, maxInterfaces, walkThreshold, enableVolumeCaustics; light-side Manifold Walk and Manifold Walk Exclude Group

capabilities.does: Two learned-guidance methods steer indirect rays toward the places where light comes from: RIS path guiding (a switch) and PPG guiding that trains on a number of early samples.
capabilities.inputs: risPathGuiding (0 or 1); indirectTrainingSamples (minimum 64, at most 10 to 20 percent of max samples), indirectSpatialBlurRadius, indirectDirectionalBlurRadius, indirectOversampling
capabilities.outputs: less indirect noise at the same sample count

capabilities.does: Adaptive sampling spends samples per pixel between a minimum and maximum, driven by an error metric. Pixel Variance sets the target noise; 0 turns it off. Error metrics are variance (default), contrast and a legacy contrast-v22.
capabilities.inputs: Pixel Variance (default 0.015 for the variance metric), min samples, max samples, Relative pixel variance (per object, default 1.0)

capabilities.does: Incremental mode renders the whole frame in rounds and refines it over time; the default batch mode finishes buckets one after another. Bucket order can be swaths or spiral, and crop windows limit the region.
capabilities.inputs: incremental mode, bucket order (swaths default, spiral), crop window

capabilities.does: Machine-learning denoiser developed with Disney Research and studio partners. It cleans partly converged renders while trying to keep detail and frame-to-frame consistency. Runs from a command line, a UI, or the host applications.
capabilities.inputs: noisy beauty plus auxiliary passes (the page read does not list the passes)

capabilities.does: AOVs are extra images written next to the beauty, each to its own driver and filter. RIS groups them as built-in, integrator, custom and light path expression outputs. Built-ins include Ci, a, id, z, P, Nn, dPdtime, motionBack, motionFore, curvature, cpuTime, sampleCount.
capabilities.inputs: AOV name (built-in, __Pworld, __Nworld, __depth, __st, __Pref and others), per-AOV filter mode (zmin, sum)

capabilities.does: A light group name on each light lets light path expressions write per-light AOVs, so lighting can be rebalanced in compositing. The setting appears on dome, env-day and mesh lights.

Batch incremental renders can write checkpoints on an interval or a time limit, then resume with a recover flag. Only TIFF and OpenEXR drivers support it; recovery is OpenEXR only. Signals HUP and USR1 trigger a checkpoint on Linux and macOS.
capabilities.inputs: prman -checkpoint interval,exit; Option "checkpoint" interval, asfinal, command; prman -recover 1
capabilities.outputs: resumable frames and time-boxed draft renders

capabilities.does: An intersect priority attribute makes refraction between touching transparent objects correct without remodelling them. XPU supports nested dielectrics.

XPU runs the same scene on CPU, GPU, or both. It processes ray packets in staged kernels with queues between them. Large scenes can exceed GPU memory and crash, so an XPUCPU variant exists. Mixed GPUs are not supported; macOS is not supported.
capabilities.outputs: final frames or interactive renders from one scene

capabilities.does: XPU supports PxrPathTracer, PxrSurface, PxrLayerSurface, PxrDisneyBsdf, PxrMarschnerHair, Lama and MaterialX nodes, OSL patterns, analytic and mesh lights, light filters, light linking, subdivision, curves, points and aggregate volumes. NURBS, procedurals and photon mapping are unsupported.
capabilities.outputs: knowledge of which scene features move to XPU

capabilities.does: PxrSurface is a layered material with diffuse, subsurface, specular, rough specular, clearcoat, iridescence, fuzz, single scatter and glass lobes. Global controls cover bump, presence, shadow mode and colour, utility pattern, and a user colour lobe for compositing AOVs.
capabilities.inputs: Bump, Presence, Presence Cached, Shadow Mode, Shadow Color, Utility Pattern, Specular Curvature Clamp, User Color, Enable Manifold Walk

capabilities.does: PxrDisneyBsdf follows the extended Disney principled model: base colour, metallic, roughness, anisotropic, index of refraction, specular tint and a specular reflection scale in one compact material.
capabilities.inputs: Base Color, Emit Color, Metallic (0 to 1), Specular Tint, Roughness, Anisotropic (0 to 1), Index of Refraction, Specular Reflection Scale (0 to 1)

capabilities.does: Disney BSDF clearcoat adds a second specular lobe for a varnish layer. Clearcoat Gloss is the inverse of roughness, 0 blurry to 1 tight.
Sheen adds a grazing-angle diffuse component, meant for cloth. A tint control moves it from achromatic toward the base colour.
Disney BSDF transmission covers diffuse and specular transmission, a thin-surface switch (IOR becomes 1), and coloured absorption defined by colour plus a distance.
capabilities.inputs: Diffuse Transmission (0 to 2), Specular Transmission, Thin Surface, Transmission Color, Transmittance Distance, Transmission Behavior

capabilities.does: Subsurface amount, colour, per-channel scattering distances and anisotropy (-1 to 1) in the Disney BSDF. At zero distance it reverts to diffuse.
capabilities.inputs: Subsurface, Subsurface Color, Scattering Distances, Subsurface Anisotropy

capabilities.does: Presence is a mask that cuts geometry out where it is 0, for leaves and thin shapes. The Disney page asks for 0 or 1 because grey values add noise; PxrSurface can cache presence per micropolygon.
A control on the Disney BSDF hides the shadow terminator line that strong bump or normal maps can produce.
capabilities.outputs: clean shadow edge on bumped surfaces

capabilities.does: OSL shaders compiled with oslc to .oso files act as pattern nodes. No closures; outputs connect to BxDF and displacement inputs. Batched evaluation is the default and is switched with an osl:batched option. Builtins differ between RIS and XPU.

PxrMeshLight turns any mesh into a light, for neon tubes, panels and deforming shapes. It follows the mesh visibility; an automatic black material stops self-scattering. Deformation motion blur is not supported.
capabilities.inputs: Color, Intensity, Exposure, Texture Color, Enable Temperature, Temperature (6500 K), Specular Amount, Diffuse Amount, Intensity/Specular/Diffuse Near Dist, Area Normalize, Light Group, Importance Multiplier
capabilities.outputs: emitting geometry that is sampled as a light

capabilities.does: PxrDomeLight lights from an environment image as if infinitely far, so only rotation matters. Float formats such as EXR, HDR or TIFF are advised. It has shadow, visibility and manifold walk controls.
capabilities.inputs: Color Map, Map Gamma, Map Saturation, Exposure, Color Temperature, Primary Visibility, Enable Shadows, Shadow Max Distance, Shadow Falloff, Trace Subset, Thin Shadow, Light Samples

capabilities.does: PxrEnvDayLight is a daylight sky and sun based on the Preetham, Shirley and Smits model. Sun position comes from a direction or from date, time, zone, latitude and longitude. Haziness runs 1.7 to 10.
capabilities.inputs: Direction, Haziness (1.7 to 10), Sky Tint, Sun Tint, Sun Size, Ground Mode (Legacy, Horizon Clamping, Diffuse Ground), Month, Day, Year, Hour, Zone, Latitude, Longitude

capabilities.does: PxrVolume renders constant fog, smoke, fire and clouds. Scattering and emission colour, density by float or colour, primary and secondary anisotropy, and optional multiple scattering. Surface effects need a PxrSurface with the volume as interior.
capabilities.inputs: Diffuse Color, Emit Color, Multiple Scattering, Density Float/Color, Extinction Distance, Max Density, Primary Anisotropy (-1 to 1), Secondary Anisotropy, Lobe Blend Factor, Equiangular Weight, Velocity

capabilities.does: Built-in perspective, orthographic, sphere, torus and cylinder projections work with the ray tracing hider; projection plugins trace rays through custom curved surfaces. XPU lists PxrPerspective, PxrOrthographic, PxrSphereCamera and partly PxrCamera.

Stylized Looks is a per-pixel post-process through display filters: PxrStylizedToon, PxrStylizedLines, PxrStylizedHatching, plus XPU versions and painterly brush and canvas filters. Controls cover toon quantising, line width and colour, hatching, texture sets. Commercial customers only.
capabilities.inputs: PxrStylizedControl on PxrSurface or LamaSurface; PxrStylizedLightControl, PxrStylizedLinesControl, PxrStylizedHatchControl
capabilities.outputs: toon, line, hatching and painterly images; stylised AOVs

scripting: C++ pattern and BxDF plug-ins (named in the XPU limits list)
outcomes: layered AOV EXR sets for compositing

rea.notes: The wiki says the Disney BSDF source is among the bxdf code examples; the RenderMan renderer itself is not open. EULA text not read.

entries.verified: 2026-11-02, how: RenderMan 27 wiki pages read (rmanwiki-27.pixar.com .md pages)

entries.name: Twinmotion

licence.name: licence terms not read; Wikipedia notes an Epic and Autodesk partnership making it available to Revit subscribers (2022)

engines.name: Render modes
engines.does: Standard, Lumen and Path tracer modes in Render settings; MegaLights shadows apply to Standard and Lumen only and need hardware ray tracing.

engines.name: Interchange importer
engines.does: Single import pipeline in 2026.2 Preview for FBX, OBJ, glTF/GLB and SKP.

capabilities.does: MegaLights is a Shadows mode for the Standard and Lumen render modes; it needs hardware ray tracing (NVIDIA RTX or Apple Silicon M3 and later). The Path tracer mode does not use it.
A Path tracer rendering mode exists beside Standard and Lumen; path-traced media made on Windows cannot switch to Lumen after opening on macOS.
Cryptomatte EXR export keyed on Object ID, Material ID, Container ID, Mesh section ID or Render layer ID, with a High precision option that smooths jagged edges.

Dynamic sky in Realistic mode with Night sky settings: true moon position, moon phases, Milky Way and air traffic, plus an aurora borealis with animation, intensity and colour controls. Sun location accepts latitude and longitude in three notations.
capabilities.inputs: Env > Ambience > Dynamic sky > Realistic > Night sky

capabilities.does: Ambience Settings is the reference page for settings that control scene atmosphere; Fog Cards add atmospheric effects and Parallax Windows add depth to windows.
capabilities.inputs: Ambience panel, Fog Cards, Parallax Windows

capabilities.does: Animator Tools animate scene elements. Scalers (2026.2 Preview) give procedural growing, shrinking and pulsing; Custom paths animate several objects, including imported or animated ones, with placement options.
capabilities.inputs: Library > Tools > Animators, Scalers, Custom paths

capabilities.does: Populating Scenes covers adding assets, animated paths and real-life urban context; downloaded Megascans assets work offline in 2026.2 Preview.

Interchange import supports FBX, OBJ, glTF/GLB and SKP with Reset transform, Reset material and Reimport deleted objects. 3DS, C4D, DAE, DXF and STL are no longer supported; the legacy importer was removed.
Known-issue text mentions SketchUp Direct Link sync and Datasmith for Rhino; the docs index adds importing Twinmotion projects into Unreal Engine.
Working with Media creates media and shares it as presentations and panorama sets; Cloud Presentations and Cloud content are mentioned.

outcomes: architectural stills, videos, panoramas and presentations

rea.notes: twinmotion.com returned 403. Release-note index pages gave titles only; features come from the 2026.2 Preview notes. Path tracer and Lumen details beyond mode names were not shown. Platforms listed come from the Apple Silicon and macOS mentions in the release notes.
