entries.name: V-Ray

licence.name: commercial; academic and render-node licences exist; each distributed-rendering server needs a V-Ray Render Node licence

engines.name: V-Ray CPU
engines.does: The production renderer with bucket and progressive image samplers and several global illumination engines (brute force, light cache, irradiance map).

engines.name: V-Ray GPU
engines.does: GPU renderer with brute-force primary GI and a choice of none, brute force or light cache as secondary engine.

engines.name: V-Ray Denoiser
engines.does: Post-render noise removal with three engines: V-Ray own, NVIDIA AI and Intel Open Image Denoise.

engines.name: Chaos Cloud rendering
engines.does: Submits V-Ray for 3ds Max jobs to Chaos servers, still or animation, GPU jobs in RTX mode by default.

engines.name: Chaos Vantage live link
engines.does: Real-time ray-traced engine shown in the 3ds Max viewport through a Live Link (7 update 4).

capabilities.does: VRayMtl is the general material. Diffuse and Reflect colours (Reflect filters Diffuse), reflection Glossiness and Max depth, Fresnel Reflections with Fresnel IOR, Refract colour with its own Glossiness, Max depth and IOR, displacement slots, coat, energy preservation mode and opacity mode.
capabilities.inputs: Diffuse, Reflect, Glossiness, Fresnel IOR, Refract, IOR, Coat Color, Energy preservation mode, Opacity mode
capabilities.outputs: general opaque, metal and glass surfaces

capabilities.does: VRayMtl displacement slot takes an image with Water Level, Amount and Shift controls; the example page treats 1.0 as subtle and 2.5 to 5 as strong.

Light Cache traces camera paths (Subdivs squared, default 1000) and stores indirect light. Retrace default 2.0 for stills, about 8.0 for animation. Modes: Single frame, From file, Save to file. Path guiding is experimental and CPU-only.
capabilities.inputs: Preset, Subdivs, Sample size, Store direct light, Retrace, Path guiding, Mode, File, Don't delete, Auto save

capabilities.does: Irradiance map is a sparse-sample GI cache, described as deprecated. Presets run from Very low to Very high; passes run from Min rate to Max rate; interpolation and sample lookup have several types; modes include multiframe incremental and animation prepass.
capabilities.inputs: Current preset, Min rate, Max rate, Subdivs, Interp. samples, Color/Distance/Normal thresholds, Detail enhancement, Interpolation type, Sample lookup, Mode

capabilities.does: In V-Ray GPU the primary engine is always Brute Force. The secondary engine is None, Brute force or Light cache, and GI depth sets secondary bounce count when brute force is selected.
capabilities.inputs: GI engine (None, Brute force, Light cache), GI depth

capabilities.does: Image sampler is Progressive or Bucket. Progressive refines the whole image over time; Bucket varies samples per pixel by neighbour difference. Max Subdivs default 24; also Noise threshold, Min shading rate, Lock noise pattern, Adaptivity clamp.
capabilities.inputs: Type, Max Subdivs, Noise threshold, Min shading rate, Lock noise pattern, Adaptivity clamp

capabilities.does: Image sampler render mask limits which pixels are computed: None, Texture (black not rendered), Selected, Include/Exclude list, Layers, or Object IDs.
capabilities.inputs: Render mask mode and its object list or IDs

capabilities.does: Denoiser works after rendering, so settings can be changed without re-rendering. Engines: default V-Ray, NVIDIA AI, Intel Open Image Denoise. Presets Mild, Default, Strong set Strength and Radius; temporal mode and AI upscale exist on the NVIDIA engine. Standalone vdenoise blends frames.
capabilities.inputs: Denoising engine, Preset, Strength, Radius, Denoise alpha, Temporal mode, NVidia AI upscale, Denoise light cache, Hardware acceleration

capabilities.does: Photon-map caustics: a larger search distance blurs them, more Max photons smooths them, and a light Caustics Multiplier scales them. A VRaySun photon emit radius also changes them.
capabilities.inputs: Caustics method (Photon map), Search distance, Max photons, Light Caustics Multiplier

capabilities.does: Version 7 update 3 adds a simpler caustics setup for common cases such as pools, documented under VRayMtl, without the traditional photon setup.
capabilities.inputs: VRayMtl quick caustics option (name not shown on the page read)

capabilities.does: LPE syntax starts at C (camera), uses spawn and scattering events such as <RD>, ends at L, O or B, and allows regular-expression symbols. Example C<RD>.*[LO] gives indirect diffuse lighting.
capabilities.inputs: expression string; tokens C, R, D, L, O, B, labels
capabilities.outputs: render element for chosen light paths

capabilities.does: VRayLight shapes: Plane, Disc, Sphere, Mesh and Dome. Units can be image-based, luminous power, luminance, radiant power or radiance; colour or Kelvin temperature mode; Directional cone and strength for Plane and Disc; decay rollout with near and far start and end.
capabilities.inputs: Type, Units, Mode, Multiplier, Directional, Directional strength, Double-sided, Invisible, Affect diffuse/specular/reflections/atmospherics, Shadow bias, Cutoff (0.001, CPU only), Tex resolution

capabilities.does: A Mesh light type converts the surface of an object into a light, for string lights or lanterns.
capabilities.outputs: emissive object that lights the scene

capabilities.does: Dome light lights from an HDR map. Options: Spherical (full dome), Affect alpha, Lock texture to icon, Adaptive dome for faster sampling, Tex resolution for importance sampling.
capabilities.inputs: Map, Spherical (full dome), Affect alpha, Lock texture to icon, Adaptive dome, Tex resolution

capabilities.does: VRayProxy loads .vrmesh or Alembic .abc files as render-time geometry; files can be dragged into the viewport when V-Ray is the current renderer.
capabilities.outputs: light viewport objects with heavy render geometry

capabilities.does: VRayFur makes fur at render time on a source mesh. Length, Radius, Gravity, Bend, Taper, Knots, curl, direction and length variation, distribution per face or per area, level of detail, dynamic tessellation and texture maps for density and length.
capabilities.inputs: Source object, Length, Radius, Gravity, Bend, Taper, Knots, Curl radius, Number of curls, Per face, Per area, Generate W-coordinate

capabilities.does: VRayVolumeGrid renders grid volumes from OpenVDB (.vdb), Field3D (.f3d) and Phoenix (.aur) caches. Parameter groups: grid parameters, volumetric options (lighting, intensity, opacity for fire and smoke), atmosphere settings.
capabilities.inputs: cache file, effect type, display resolution, surfacing, displacement type
capabilities.outputs: smoke and fire from simulation caches

capabilities.does: USD content loads through the VRayScene object or the USD Stage node (V-Ray 6 update 1 or later). Supports meshes, particles, UsdPreviewSurface, V-Ray materials and lights, displacement, user attributes, MaterialX through maxUSD.
capabilities.inputs: USD Stage node, VRayScene, Assign USD Materials

capabilities.does: Export uses the MAX USD Exporter with V-Ray materials and the V-Ray chaser (or V-Ray plug-in configuration from 6 update 1.1). Writes V-Ray shaders, lights, displacement, VRayInstancer, VRayProxy and the physical camera. Render settings and object properties are not exported.

Jobs are sent to Chaos Cloud from a toolbar button or menu; still and animation jobs; GPU jobs default to RTX Render Mode, with CUDA-only and CUDA CPU modes. Changed resubmissions upload only the differences. Billing uses Chaos Credits.
capabilities.inputs: Submit to Chaos Cloud, RTX Render Mode, CUDA-only Mode, CUDA CPU

capabilities.does: One frame is split into regions across networked machines over TCP/IP. DR1 connects client to servers directly; DR2 adds an optional dispatcher and scales further. Bucket rendering is the main method; progressive also works. Each server needs a Render Node licence.
capabilities.inputs: Distributed Rendering settings, dispatcher selection, Check for missing files, VRAY_ASSETS_CACHE_PATH

capabilities.does: Version 7 update 3 adds object-based autofocus that locks focus distance on a selected object or 3D point, and per-camera inclusion or exclusion of objects, both under VRayPhysicalCamera.
capabilities.inputs: VRayPhysicalCamera focus target, per-camera include/exclude lists

capabilities.does: Chaos Vantage, a real-time ray-traced engine, runs in the 3ds Max viewport through Live Link so scene changes appear without re-export (V-Ray 7 update 4). Veras, an AI visualisation add-in, was added in the same update.
Version 7 update 3 lets Gaussian Splats be relit to match the scene by rebalancing baked light, documented under VRayGaussiansGeom.
capabilities.outputs: splat scene matched to V-Ray lighting

capabilities.does: VRayParallaxTex fakes interior depth and lighting behind windows in exterior renders without modelling the room, adjustable per window.

scripting: V-Ray SDK and App SDK (listed in the documentation index)

rea.notes: EULA page exists in the documentation index but was not read. Several VMAX pages (VRayPhysicalCamera, VRaySun, OpenPBR Shading Mode, V-Ray GPU Supported Features, Cameras) were stubs when fetched.

entries.verified: 2026-11-02, how: V-Ray for 3ds Max help pages on documentation.chaos.com read (.md pages)

entries.name: Indigo Renderer

licence.name: terms not read (vendor site unreachable); the Blender exporter is GPL-2.0

engines.name: CPU bidirectional and Metropolis renderer
engines.does: Light transport selected by render mode: bidirectional path tracing, bidirectional with Metropolis, plain CPU path tracing.

engines.name: GPU path tracer
engines.does: OpenCL path tracing with its own bounce limit and a list of render devices.

engines.name: Material system
engines.does: Nine material types: Diffuse, Phong, Specular, Coating, DoubleSidedThin, Blended, External, Null, Fast SSS, each with spectrum, texture or shader channels.

engines.name: Scene file format
engines.does: Scenes are written as .igs files that the Indigo program renders; meshes can be referenced as external proxies.

capabilities.does: Render mode presets: bidirectional (default), bidirectional with Metropolis, CPU path, GPU path, shadow and custom. Flags bidir, metro, hybrid and gpu set the algorithm. Metropolis has large mutation probability (0.4), max_change (0.01) and a consecutive rejection limit that adds bias if finite.
capabilities.inputs: render_mode, bidir, metro, hybrid, max_depth (10000), large_mutation_prob, max_change, max_num_consec_rejections
capabilities.outputs: unbiased image by chosen light transport

capabilities.does: GPU switch with its own maximum bounce depth (default 8, minimum 4, maximum 100) and a device list where each entry carries id, platform, device, vendor and a use flag.

Renders until a time limit (halttime, seconds) or a sample count per pixel (haltspp) is reached; -1 disables each. Saves outputs every period_save seconds (default 1800). Contribution clamping (max_contribution, default 10) limits fireflies.
capabilities.inputs: halttime, haltspp, period_save, clamp_contributions, max_contribution (1 to 64)

capabilities.does: Network mode off, master or working_master, with a slave host name and a port (default 7100) so several machines render one scene.
Denoise switch that runs on every image update; an optimise mode writes albedo and normal channels, renders in buckets and decorrelates sampling; denoiser memory limit defaults to 6000 MB.

Light layers and channels: direct and indirect diffuse, specular reflection, refraction, transmission, emission, participating media, subsurface scattering, normals (with and without bump), depth, beauty, albedo, position, material and object IDs, alpha, material and object masks.

Separate splat and downsize filters (Mitchell, Gaussian, box, fastbox, radial, sharp) with blur, ring and radius controls, presets default, crisp, strong, custom, and a supersample factor from 1 to 10.
capabilities.inputs: filter_preset, splat_filter, ds_filter, ds_filter_radius (1 to 3), supersample

capabilities.does: Camera with f-stop (1 to 128, default 8), exposure as 1/x seconds (default 125), film ISO (25 to 10000), white balance by illuminant or chromaticity, and autofocus. Aperture diffraction shapes: image, generated blades (3 to 20) or circular.
capabilities.inputs: fstop, exposure, iso, whitebalance, autofocus, ad_type, ad_blades, ad_offset, ad_curvature, ad_angle, ad_image, ad_obstacle
capabilities.outputs: physically based exposure, depth of field and bokeh shape

capabilities.does: Diffuse material with optional Oren-Nayar roughness (sigma 0 to 20), transmitter and shadow catcher flags; Phong material with exponent (default 1000) or roughness, fresnel scale, IOR (default 1.3) and measured n-k data.
capabilities.inputs: sigma, exponent, roughness, fresnel_scale, ior, nk_data_type

capabilities.does: Specular material in two types, specular and glossy_transparent, with exponent or roughness, a medium, arch glass and single face switches, and a precedence value from 1 to 100 for overlapping media.
capabilities.inputs: type, medium_chooser, exponent, roughness, arch_glass, single_face, precedence

capabilities.does: Coating material over a substrate material with thickness in micrometres (default 1), roughness, fresnel scale, IOR and an interference switch for thin-film colour.
capabilities.inputs: thickness, roughness, fresnel_scale, ior, interference, substrate_material

capabilities.does: Fast SSS material plus media with a subsurface switch, uniform or Henyey-Greenstein phase function, IOR, Cauchy B dispersion term and skin presets (dermis, epidermis) driven by haemoglobin, melanin and eumelanin sliders.
capabilities.inputs: medium_type, sss, fast_sss, sss_phase_function, medium_ior, medium_cauchy_b, medium_melanin

capabilities.does: Emission on most material types: RGB, blackbody or uniform spectrum, power (default 1500), gain, scale in lumens, candela, nits or lux, IES profile, back face emission, emission sampling multiplier and a light layer name.
capabilities.inputs: emit_power, emit_gain_val, emission_scale_measure, emit_ies_path, backface_emit, em_sampling_mult, emit_layer

capabilities.does: Per-material map channels for bump, normal, displacement, roughness, fresnel scale and blend; textures have brightness, scale and offset controls (A, B, C), a UV set, smoothing, and an image gamma defaulting to 2.2.
capabilities.inputs: bumpmap, normalmap, displacement, roughness map, blendmap, texture A B C, gamma
capabilities.outputs: surface detail from images or shaders

capabilities.does: Colour channels take spectra: RGB, RGB with gain, uniform, peak, blackbody (1000 to 10000 K, default 6500) or tabulated, so lights and materials are not limited to RGB triples.
capabilities.inputs: spectrum type, rgb, rgb_gain, blackbody_temp, uniform value

capabilities.does: Sun and sky lamp with turbidity 1 to 10 (default 2), sunsky model original, extra_atmospheric or captured-simulation, separate sun and sky light layers, plus a hemisphere lamp as background colour or HDRI environment map (spherical or spherical_environment) with gain.
capabilities.inputs: turbidity, model, sunlayer, skylayer, env_map_path, env_map_type, env_map_gain_val

capabilities.does: Tone mapping types Reinhard (pre 4, post 1.2, burn 6), linear scale, camera response function from preset or file with EV adjust, and Filmic with a scale; gamma defaults to 2.2.
capabilities.inputs: tonemap_type, reinhard_pre, reinhard_post, reinhard_burn, linear_unit, camera_response_preset, camera_ev, filmic_scale, gamma

capabilities.does: Mesh options for view-dependent subdivision (0 to 20 levels, pixel threshold 4, curvature threshold 0.1), displacement error threshold, external mesh proxies, section planes, exit portals, sphere primitives and invisible-to-camera objects.
capabilities.inputs: max_num_subdivisions, subdivide_pixel_threshold, displacement_error_threshold, mesh_proxy, exit_portal, section_plane

outcomes: denoised images with albedo and normal channels

rea.notes: indigorenderer.com returned 503 on every page tried, so no vendor documentation or EULA was read. The Blender exporter source is public under GPL-2.0 and its Changelog shows Blender 5.0 support in version 5.0.0.

entries.verified: 2026-11-02, how: Blender exporter source files read; vendor site unreachable (503); entry url not opened in this sweep (official domain, unchecked)

entries.name: NVIDIA Iray

licence.name: SDK licensed through NVIDIA partners; terms not read

engines.name: Iray Photoreal
engines.does: Final-quality progressive renderer; the Daz Studio host lists CPU and GPU devices for it separately.

engines.name: Iray Interactive
engines.does: Interactive render mode with its own device list; the product page describes interactive previews cleaned by an AI denoiser.

engines.name: MDL
engines.does: Material Definition Language that describes materials and lights; Iray materials, measured materials and hair or fur use it.

capabilities.does: Two render modes, Photoreal and Interactive; the host lets you pick CPU and GPU devices for each mode separately and offers an OptiX Prime acceleration option for photoreal.
capabilities.inputs: Render Mode, Photoreal Devices, Interactive Devices

capabilities.does: Progressive controls named in the Daz Studio host: minimum update samples, update interval in seconds, minimum and maximum samples, maximum time, a rendering quality switch with a quality value, and a rendering converged ratio.
capabilities.inputs: Min Update Samples, Update Interval, Min Samples, Max Samples, Max Time, Rendering Quality, Rendering Converged Ratio
capabilities.outputs: image that refines until a stop rule

capabilities.does: The 2019 SDK uses NVIDIA RTX hardware ray tracing in all render modes; any number or mix of GPUs and CPUs in one machine can render, with control over which devices are used.
AI denoiser running on Tensor Cores cleans both final frames and interactive previews.

Image filters: firefly filter (nominal luminance), noise filter with degrain radius and blur difference, bloom with radius, threshold and brightness scale, and a pixel filter (box, triangle, Gaussian, Mitchell, Lanczos) with radius.
capabilities.inputs: Firefly Filter, Noise Degrain Radius, Bloom Filter Threshold, Pixel Filter, Pixel Filter Radius

capabilities.does: Optimization group named in the Daz Studio host: Max Path Length, Architectural Sampler on or off, Caustic Sampler on or off, and instancing optimization set to Memory or Speed. The page gives no descriptions.
capabilities.inputs: Max Path Length, Architectural Sampler, Caustic Sampler, Instancing Optimization
capabilities.outputs: settings only; effects not described on the page

capabilities.does: Spectral rendering is listed as a feature of the renderer alongside caustics.
Light path expressions are listed as a feature on the product page; no detail is given.
Materials are written in MDL: surface colour, reflection, refraction and emission, plus measured materials and hair or fur.

The open MDL SDK parses and validates modules, builds material instances from call graphs, compiles them, distills them to simpler renderer models and bakes textures; code backends target CUDA PTX, LLVM IR, HLSL, GLSL and native CPU.
Light sources include emissive geometry, photometric lights built from measured data, and a Sun and Sky system.

Sun-Sky controls: sun node direction, latitude, day, time, sun disk intensity and scale (default 4.0), glow, haze 0 to 15, blue-red tint, saturation, horizon height and blur, night colour, multiplier, ground colour.
capabilities.inputs: SS Sun Node, SS Haze, SS Sun Disk Scale, SS Horizon Height, SS Night Color, SS Ground Color

capabilities.does: Environment mode (Dome and Scene, Dome Only, Sun-Sky Only, Scene Only); dome as infinite or finite sphere or box, with or without a ground; map, intensity, lighting resolution, blur, scale, radius, origin and rotation.
capabilities.inputs: Environment Mode, Dome Mode, Environment Map, Environment Lighting Resolution, Dome Rotation

capabilities.does: Ground plane that catches shadows, positioned automatically at the scene bottom or by hand, with a texture scale and a shadow intensity (0 none, 1 regular, above 1 darker).
capabilities.inputs: Draw Ground, Ground Position Mode, Ground Shadow Intensity, Ground Texture Scale
capabilities.outputs: shadows on a transparent or mapped ground

capabilities.does: Tone mapper with exposure value from shutter speed, f-stop and film ISO (ISO 0 switches to arbitrary scaling), cm^2 factor, vignetting, white point, burn highlights (0 to 1), crush blacks, saturation and gamma.
capabilities.inputs: Shutter Speed, F/Stop, Film ISO, Vignetting, White Point, Burn Highlights, Crush Blacks, Gamma

capabilities.does: Texture compression thresholds named Medium Threshold and High Threshold appear in the advanced settings.
The Iray SDK is available through NVIDIA partners; plug-ins exist for Maya, 3ds Max and Rhino; listed products using Iray include Daz Studio, CATIA, SOLIDWORKS Visualize and Siemens NX.

rea.notes: The Iray programmer's manual host (raytracing-docs.nvidia.com) failed the certificate check and was not read, so renderer internals and the licence were not checked. The MDL SDK repository states BSD-3-Clause. The Daz Studio pages list setting names only for several groups, with no descriptions. Capabilities with basis observed come from the NVIDIA product page, not hands-on use.

entries.verified: 2026-11-02, how: NVIDIA product page, Daz Studio reference pages and MDL-SDK README read; programmer's manual unreachable

entries.name: Chaos Vantage

licence.name: commercial product; price and EULA not read

engines.name: Real-time ray-traced renderer
engines.does: Draws a loaded scene with ray tracing and global illumination on a DXR-capable GPU, up to two GPUs.

engines.name: Denoiser and upscaler stack
engines.does: Vantage denoiser, NVIDIA OptiX AI denoiser, DLSS Ray Reconstruction and frame generation, chosen in the viewport bar.

engines.name: Scene import
engines.does: Opens .vrscene files from V-Ray, Enscape and Corona, and USD and MaterialX content from other tools.

engines.name: Animation Editor
engines.does: Timeline for camera clips, transitions, pauses and imported scene animation, in time mode or shot mode.

engines.name: High Quality Render mode with queue
engines.does: Renders stills and sequences in one batch with per-item camera, resolution, samples and render elements.

capabilities.does: Renders the full scene by ray tracing at interactive rates; needs a discrete DXR-capable NVIDIA, AMD or Intel GPU and can use two. Windows 10 2004 or newer, AVX2 CPU, RAM at least equal to GPU memory.
capabilities.inputs: scene, one or two DXR GPUs

capabilities.does: Viewport quality preset (Low, Medium, High, Ultra, Custom) and resolution scale (25, 50 or 100 percent of camera or viewport size); presets live in a JSON file in the user's app data folder; rendering can be paused and resumed.
capabilities.outputs: viewport at chosen cost and noise

capabilities.does: Denoiser switch plus an amount slider from 0 (raw) to 100 (fully denoised) for the Vantage denoiser; an NVIDIA OptiX AI primary denoiser needs driver 535 or newer. View modes other than Beauty need the denoiser on.
capabilities.inputs: denoiser toggle, amount 0 to 100, primary and secondary denoiser

capabilities.does: NVIDIA upscaling denoiser renders at half resolution and upscales. DLSS levels Performance (4X), Balanced (3X), Quality (2.25X) and a 1X level pair with DLSS Ray Reconstruction. Frame Generation multiplies displayed frames 2x to 6x; 3x to 6x need an RTX 50 GPU.
capabilities.inputs: DLSS quality level, frame generation factor

capabilities.does: Display correction modes Auto, Raw, sRGB, HDR (Rec.2100-PQ) and OpenColorIO with input colour space, display, view and look; HDR display toggle on HDR monitors; separate colour correction post step.
capabilities.inputs: display mode, OCIO input space, display, view, look

capabilities.does: Camera tab simulates a real camera with physical settings such as f-stop and ISO; a separate Color Corrections tab covers exposure, hue and saturation and colour balance as post-processing.
Camera rollout groups: resolution, type and lens, exposure, depth of field, tilt and shift, lens distortion, and near and far clipping.
capabilities.inputs: camera type, lens mode, tilt, shift, distortion, clip planes

capabilities.does: Pick Focus Point tool (key T) sets focus by clicking in the viewport; the viewport bar also has auto-exposure, which ignores the camera exposure and has a maximum range, and an exposure bias value.
capabilities.inputs: focus point, auto exposure, exposure bias

capabilities.does: Sun light with colour modes Filter, Direct and Override, intensity, sun size multiplier, shadow offset; position by manual, altitude and azimuth, geolocation or animated geolocation (date, time, zone, DST), plus Moon size, phase, glow and brightness.
capabilities.inputs: mode, altitude, azimuth, latitude, longitude, date, time, time zone

capabilities.does: Light kinds in the lister: Sun, Sphere, Rect, IES, Point, Spot, Direct, Mesh and Cylinder. The lister shows compact, basic or advanced parameter sets, and right-click resets a value.

Render elements: Lighting, Specular, Global Illumination, Reflection, Refraction, Self-Illumination, Atmosphere, Background, Diffuse Filter, Bumped Normals, Z-Depth, Velocity, Object and Material masks, Raw RGBA, and Multi Matte RGBA masks by ID or include list. Elements are not denoised.
capabilities.inputs: element selection, PNG, JPEG or EXR output

capabilities.does: Layered texture stacks foreground over background layers with 25 blend modes, including Normal, Multiply, Screen, Overlay, Difference and Hue; Blend, Multi, Override and CarPaint materials also exist.
Toon outline effect on the Materials tab with line colour brightness and line strength, plus a clay mode display.
capabilities.inputs: line colour brightness, line strength, clay mode

capabilities.does: Beta node-based Material Node Editor for creating and editing materials and textures, including Chaos Cosmos assets; opens from the Materials tab, main toolbar, Tools menu or key M.

Animation Editor with time and shot modes; camera, sun and imported scene tracks; recorded cameras; transitions (Linear, In/Out Quad, In Quad, Out Quad); pauses; FPS; forced resolution; trim markers; linear or smooth camera paths.
capabilities.inputs: cameras, transitions, pauses, FPS, width, height, aspect

capabilities.does: Render queue collects stills and sequences, each with camera, resolution, samples, presets and elements; items can be edited, skipped by checkbox, deleted, then started together.
capabilities.inputs: still or sequence, camera, resolution, samples, elements

capabilities.does: Live Link sends a 3ds Max scene (V-Ray or Corona) to Vantage and renders animation frames there; Cinema 4D with Corona has a one-click export that creates no live link.
Free look, collision with eye height, step height ratio, height tolerance and gravity, orbit around cursor hit, target or selection, and move speed in metres per second.
capabilities.inputs: navigation mode, eye height, move speed

Render graphs connect passes by edges; scripts call loadRenderPassLibrary, createPass, addPass, addEdge and markOutput; the API adds removePass, updatePass, getPass, removeEdge, unmarkOutput and getOutput.
A pass library exports registerPlugin to register pass classes; input and output fields can be Optional or Persistent; create() reads a dictionary and getScriptingDictionary() serialises the pass.

Mogwai scripts use object m: loadScene(path, buildFlags), renderFrame, clock, profiler, addGraph, getGraph, resizeFrameBuffer; the falcor Python module exposes Renderer, Clock, Scene, Camera, RenderGraph, RenderPass and Texture. The API page is no longer updated.

entries.name: Radiance

licence.name: Radiance open-source licence (LBNL); licence text not read

engines.name: rpict
engines.does: Renders a picture from a scene octree for a chosen view type, resolution and sampling.

engines.name: rtrace
engines.does: Traces individual rays read from input and prints values such as radiance, irradiance, hit point and normal.

engines.name: oconv
engines.does: Builds an octree from scene descriptions for the tracers.

engines.name: rcontrib and rfluxmtx
engines.does: Compute ray contribution coefficients and flux transfer matrices for named modifiers.

capabilities.does: Indirect diffuse light by Monte Carlo sampling with interpolation: -ab bounces, -ad divisions, -as super-samples, -ar resolution and -aa accuracy (0 means no interpolation).
Direct light controls: -dj jitter, -ds source subdivision ratio, -dt shadow test threshold, -dc certainty, -dr virtual source relays and -dp virtual source presampling density.
Ray weight limit -lw and reflection limit -lr with Russian roulette; specular sampling threshold -st and specular sample factor -ss for highlights on rough materials.

rtrace -o picks output fields per ray: origin, direction, value, weight, lengths, uv, hit point, perturbed and unperturbed normals, surface, modifier and material names, mirrored and unmirrored parts; -I computes irradiance; formats a, f, d, c.

View types set with -vt: perspective v, parallel l, cylindrical panorama c, hemispherical fisheye h, angular fisheye a, planisphere s; options for view point, direction, up, size, fore and aft clipping, shift and lift.
Aperture diameter -pd in world units gives depth of field; focal distance comes from the length of the view direction.
Pixel sampling controls: -pj sample jitter, -ps sample spacing for adaptive subdivision and -pt tolerance that triggers a third sample.
rpict sets resolution (-x, -y, -pa), recovers interrupted renders (-r, -ro), writes depth files (-z), renders a view sequence from stdin (-S) and runs in persistent mode (-P, -PP).

gensky writes CIE sky descriptions: sunny with or without sun, intermediate, cloudy and uniform; location (-a, -o, -m), date and time with solar or zone time, turbidity -t, zenith brightness, solar radiance, ground reflectance -g and direct solar angles.

oconv builds an octree with limits -n (surfaces per voxel, default 6) and -r (maximum resolution, default 16384), optional bounding cube -b, incremental -i, and frozen octrees -f that embed the scene; inputs can be commands.

mkillum replaces windows and skylights with secondary sources that carry precomputed light distributions; settings for samples per direction, colour handling, minimum radiance and light or illum mode.
capabilities.inputs: mkillum variables d, s, c, b, l, m, f, o

capabilities.does: rcontrib computes ray coefficients for objects whose modifiers are named with -m or -M; -b and -bn split results into bins, -V sets coefficient or contribution output, -c averages rays, -o routes output files.
rfluxmtx samples a sender surface and records arrival on receivers as a matrix; hemisphere bases u, kf, kh, kq (Klems), rN (Reinhart), cie and scN (Shirley-Chiu); bin jitter -bj and sample count -c.
capabilities.inputs: sender and receiver files, h= basis, -bj, -c

capabilities.does: rtrace has a photon mapping mode in which -ab (diffuse indirect bounces) defaults to 1; the project site lists a separate Photon Map Manual.

rad controls lighting parameters and automates most of the rendering process; trad is a Tcl/Tk interface to rad; ra_* programs convert pictures; holodeck programs (rholo), glrad and ranimove are also shipped.

engines.does: Fits a set of 3D Gaussians to posed photographs with gradient descent, with density control that adds and removes Gaussians during the run.

engines.name: Differentiable Gaussian rasteriser
engines.does: Sorts and blends projected anisotropic Gaussians per screen tile on the GPU, in forward and backward passes; reusable in other projects.

engines.name: SIBR viewers
engines.does: Two desktop viewers: one attaches to a running training job, the other loads a finished model and renders it interactively.

engines.name: COLMAP converter (convert.py)
engines.does: Runs COLMAP on a folder of photos and writes the undistorted images and sparse model the optimiser reads.

capabilities.does: Optimises a scene made of 3D Gaussians from photos with known camera poses. Input is a COLMAP or NeRF-synthetic dataset; the run lasts 30000 iterations by default and writes the model to a folder.
capabilities.outputs: trained Gaussian scene in the model folder

capabilities.does: Expects images in an images folder and a COLMAP sparse model in sparse/0 with cameras.bin, images.bin and points3D.bin; the sparse SfM points are the starting set.
convert.py runs feature matching and mapping through COLMAP, undistorts the images, and can write half, quarter and eighth resolution copies.
capabilities.outputs: undistorted images plus sparse model; originals kept in distorted/

capabilities.does: The --eval flag holds out test views using the MipNeRF360 split rule, so quality numbers refer to unseen cameras.
capabilities.outputs: L1 and PSNR on test views at the listed iterations

capabilities.does: Chooses the image size used in training: a divisor of 1, 2, 4 or 8, or a target width. Without a value, images wider than 1.6K pixels are scaled down automatically.
Stores view-dependent colour per Gaussian as spherical harmonic coefficients, up to degree 3. A flag moves the SH evaluation into PyTorch instead of the CUDA kernel.

Grows and prunes the Gaussian set during training. Densification starts at iteration 500, ends at 15000, runs every 100 iterations, and uses a gradient threshold of 0.0002; opacity is reset every 3000 iterations.
capabilities.outputs: Gaussian count adapted to the scene

capabilities.does: Separate learning rates per Gaussian attribute, with an exponentially decaying schedule for position.
Sets the weight of the structural-similarity term that is mixed with the L1 image loss.
capabilities.outputs: balance of L1 and D-SSIM loss

capabilities.does: Selects the optimiser: the standard Adam or a sparse variant; the README reports faster training with it together with a drop-in faster rasteriser branch.
Uses monocular depth maps as an extra training signal; a helper script computes the scale and offset between depth maps and the SfM scene. The README suggests Depth Anything V2 for the depth maps.
capabilities.outputs: better geometry in poorly covered regions

capabilities.does: Learns a per-image exposure correction so photos taken with changing camera exposure give a consistent scene.
Adds an elliptical weighted average filter taken from the Mip-Splatting work.
Saves the Gaussian model at chosen iterations and stores resume checkpoints inside the model folder.

Options to fit smaller GPUs: keep images on the CPU, stop densifying earlier, densify less often, raise the gradient threshold, and skip test passes. The README gives about 8 GB as an untested estimate.
A debug mode dumps rasteriser inputs on failure from a chosen iteration; covariance can also be computed in PyTorch for checking.
render.py draws the training and test views of a finished model; settings are read back from the model folder and can be overridden.
capabilities.outputs: rendered images of train and test cameras

capabilities.does: metrics.py scores renders of one or more models against held-out photos; full_eval.py repeats the paper evaluation on the MipNeRF360, Tanks and Temples and Deep Blending sets.
SIBR_remoteGaussian_app connects to a training process over a socket and shows the scene as it improves, with an option to show source images in a top view.

SIBR_gaussianViewer_app loads a trained model and renders it interactively, with FPS and trackball navigation, snap-to-camera, scaling modifier, ellipsoid and point-cloud display modes, and fast culling.
An OpenXR extension, contributed by Orange Labs, lets a headset view trained scenes; it lives on a separate branch of the repository.
capabilities.outputs: VR view of a splat scene

capabilities.does: The scene is a cloud of anisotropic 3D Gaussians with position, covariance, opacity and colour, started from the sparse SfM points; the paper says this avoids computing in empty space.
A visibility-aware splatting rasteriser renders the Gaussians; the abstract claims 30 frames per second or more at 1080p for unbounded scenes after training.

scripting: Python scripts (train.py, render.py, metrics.py, convert.py, full_eval.py)

rea.restrictions: Licence page read: software is for research and evaluation use; commercial use or distribution needs the licensors' prior explicit consent; redistribution must carry the licence; derivative works may add own terms only if the research-only limit is kept for them.
rea.notes: The README as fetched does not name the file format of the saved model, so none is claimed here. The 3DGS reference code is not under a commercial-use licence; a commercial Studio must not embed it.

entries.name: gsplat

licence.name: Apache-2.0

engines.name: CUDA rasteriser
engines.does: GPU kernels that project, sort and blend 3D or 2D Gaussians into images, with PyTorch autograd bindings; CUDA code builds on first run when installed from PyPI.

engines.name: Densification strategies
engines.does: Classes that decide when to duplicate, split, prune or relocate Gaussians during training.

engines.name: Compression module
engines.does: Packs trained splats into quantised PNG, k-means and NPZ files and reads them back.

engines.name: Example trainers and viewer
engines.does: Scripts for fitting COLMAP captures, single images and large scenes, plus a browser viewer built on Viser and nerfview.

capabilities.does: rasterization() renders batches of 3D Gaussians for several cameras at once. It returns colour images, alpha images and a meta dict of intermediate tensors (radii, means2d, depths, conics, isect ids).
capabilities.inputs: means, quats, scales, opacities, colors, viewmats [..., C, 4, 4], Ks [..., C, 3, 3], width, height

capabilities.does: Chooses what is rendered: colour, depth, or both. Depth can be accumulated (D) or expected (ED), and lower-case variants exist for the raw channel.
capabilities.outputs: image tensors with colour and or depth channels

capabilities.does: Switches between the classic projection and an antialiased variant; eps2d is added to the eigenvalues of the projected 2D covariance (0.3 gives a minimum of about 3 pixels).
Projects through several camera types and lens distortions, including rolling shutter between two poses.
capabilities.inputs: camera_model: 'pinhole','ortho','fisheye','ftheta','lidar'; radial_coeffs, tangential_coeffs, thin_prism_coeffs, ftheta_coeffs, lidar_coeffs, rolling_shutter, viewmats_rs
capabilities.outputs: render under the chosen lens model

capabilities.does: Skips Gaussians outside the near and far plane or whose projected radius is at or below a pixel threshold; the large-scene example uses a 3 pixel threshold to stay real-time.
Packed mode stores only visible Gaussian-camera pairs; sparse_grad returns COO gradients for means, quats and scales, and absgrad exposes absolute 2D-mean gradients for densification.
Evaluates view-dependent colour from SH coefficients when sh_degree is given; separate functions handle degree 0 and degree 1 or higher.
capabilities.inputs: sh_degree; spherical_harmonics(degrees_to_use, means, viewmats, coeffs), spherical_harmonics_l0(sh0), spherical_harmonics_l1_plus(shN)

capabilities.does: Optional 3DGUT-style projection and per-ray evaluation of the Gaussian response in 3D, allowing distorted cameras; can return normals.
capabilities.inputs: with_ut, ut_params, with_eval3d, return_normals (needs with_eval3d), global_z_order
capabilities.outputs: render with distortion-aware splats and optional normals

capabilities.does: Selects how batches of cameras are rasterised in eval3d mode: serial forward with parallel backward, or parallel in both passes.
A flag turns on multi-GPU rasterisation of a splat set across devices.
Renders arbitrary per-Gaussian feature channels, processed in channel chunks; extra signals can carry their own SH degree.
capabilities.inputs: colors with N-D channels, channel_chunk (32), extra_signals, extra_signals_sh_degree, backgrounds

capabilities.does: rasterization_2dgs() renders 2D Gaussian surfels and returns normals, depth-derived surface normals, a distortion map and median depth, with optional distortion loss.
capabilities.outputs: colour, alpha, render_normals, surf_normals, render_distort, render_median

capabilities.does: DefaultStrategy duplicates small high-gradient Gaussians, splits large ones, prunes by opacity and scale, and resets opacity on a schedule; AbsGS-style absolute gradients and a 2DGS gradient key are options.
capabilities.inputs: prune_opa 0.005, grow_grad2d 0.0002, grow_scale3d 0.01, grow_scale2d 0.05, prune_scale3d 0.1, prune_scale2d 0.15, refine_start_iter 500, refine_stop_iter 15000, reset_every 3000, refine_every 100, absgrad, revised_opacity, key_for_gradient

capabilities.does: MCMCStrategy keeps a fixed cap on Gaussians, relocates low-opacity ones to high-opacity places, adds samples by opacity, and injects noise into positions.
capabilities.inputs: cap_max 1000000, noise_lr 500000, min_opacity 0.005, refine_start_iter 500, refine_stop_iter 25000, refine_every 100, noise_injection_stop_iter, noise_opacity_t, noise_opacity_k

capabilities.does: Each strategy is driven by three calls around the backward pass and a sanity check on parameter and optimiser dictionaries.
PngCompression writes a splat dictionary as quantised, optionally sorted PNG images; SH coefficients go through k-means and extra attributes through NPZ. It needs imageio, plas and torchpq.
Reports which Gaussians land on each pixel: counts, all contributor ids with weights, or the top contributors ranked by alpha times transmittance.
The projection, tile intersection and pixel blending steps are exposed as separate functions, including a fused covariance, transform and projection kernel.
capabilities.inputs: quat_scale_to_covar_preci, proj, world_to_cam, fully_fused_projection, isect_tiles, isect_offset_encode, rasterize_to_pixels
capabilities.outputs: radii, 2D means, depths, conics, tile ids, images

capabilities.does: Rotations are quaternions in (w, x, y, z) order, and the view matrix is world-to-camera with camera z as depth.
A 9 by 9 copy of a scene (about 30 million Gaussians) renders in real time by dropping far, small Gaussians; the viewer can switch between the gsplat and Inria backends.
capabilities.outputs: interactive view of very large splat scenes

capabilities.does: simple_trainer.py fits a COLMAP capture and writes checkpoints and results to a folder; the example passes a positional config name (default) that the page does not explain.
simple_viewer.py serves a browser view of a checkpoint using Viser and nerfview and lowers resolution when the frame rate drops.
An optional install extra adds LiDAR sensor rasterisation.
Wrapper functions call the original Inria 3DGS and 2DGS CUDA backends so results can be compared to gsplat; they need the external packages installed and carry their own licence.

outcomes: depth and normal maps from splats

rea.notes: Apache-2.0 per the repository page. The Inria wrapper functions depend on separately licensed packages.

entries.name: Nerfstudio

licence.name: Apache-2.0

engines.name: ns-train
engines.does: Trains a chosen radiance-field or splat method on a dataset; the method, then the dataparser, are given as sub-commands with their own options.

engines.name: ns-process-data
engines.does: Turns images, video or another capture app's export into a nerfstudio dataset with camera poses.

engines.name: Web viewer
engines.does: Browser viewer on port 7007 that shows training live, builds camera paths and exports from the EXPORT tab.

engines.name: ns-export and ns-render
engines.does: Writes point clouds, meshes and splats from a trained model, and renders videos along camera paths.

engines.name: Modular pipeline
engines.does: Dataparsers, datamanagers, fields, models and pipelines are separate pieces, so a new method plugs in by replacing some of them.

capabilities.does: The default method for real captures of static scenes. It joins pose refinement, per-image appearance conditioning, proposal sampling, scene contraction and hash encoding.
Pushes the image loss back into the input poses so errors from phone captures are reduced, which lowers cloudy artefacts.
A piecewise sampler spends half its samples uniformly within distance 1, then widens steps; proposal networks (two density fields work best) concentrate samples near the first surface.
capabilities.inputs: density fields built from hash encoding and a small fused MLP (tiny-cuda-nn)
capabilities.outputs: fewer, better placed samples per ray

capabilities.does: Size and speed variants of the method with different memory use, plus a depth-supervised one.

The original NeRF idea: a fully connected network maps a 5D coordinate (position plus viewing direction) to density and view-dependent radiance; classic volume rendering along camera rays makes images, and images with known poses are the only training input.
The original NeRF is available as a method for reference runs.
Instant-NGP rebuilt on NerfAcc multiscale occupancy grids, fully fused networks and a hash grid of L levels with up to T entries of F features; hash collisions are not handled.
capabilities.inputs: ns-train instant-ngp; hash table size T, feature size F, levels L

capabilities.does: Gaussian splatting trained through the gsplat library. It starts from COLMAP points or ns-process-data output and uses an image datamanager that undistorts and caches the photos. Only perspective cameras work.

Culling and regularisation switches: lower the alpha cull threshold for quality, stop culling after densification, or add a scale regulariser against long spiky Gaussians. splatfacto-big uses more Gaussians for higher quality at about twice the memory.

The docs list further methods that run in the same framework, including Splatfacto-W, Mip-NeRF, K-Planes, TensoRF, Zip-NeRF, LERF, Generfacto, Instruct-NeRF2NeRF, Instruct-GS2GS, SIGNeRF and Nerfbusters.
capabilities.outputs: one trainer for many research methods

capabilities.does: ns-process-data images or video runs COLMAP and FFmpeg to produce poses; video input samples frames, and a separate evaluation image folder can be supplied.
Splits 360 images or video into perspective views before pose estimation and can crop edges.
capabilities.inputs: --camera-type equirectangular, --images-per-equirect (8 or 14, default 8), --crop-factor top bottom left right, --crop-bottom

capabilities.does: Imports exports of other tools: Polycam zip (LiDAR iPhone, developer mode), Record3D with optional point cloud, Metashape XML, RealityCapture CSV, ODM output, and Project Aria VRS plus MPS data. KIRI Engine output trains directly.
capabilities.inputs: polycam --data zip; record3d --ply --voxel-size (0.8); metashape --xml; realitycapture --csv; odm; aria --vrs-file --mps-data-dir

capabilities.does: Holds out files by name for evaluation through the dataparser.
Poisson surface reconstruction from a trained model; it needs a model that predicts normals, which nerfacto does when told to.
Extracts a surface by TSDF fusion of rendered depth maps; works with all models.
Writes a PLY point cloud, also from the viewer EXPORT tab, with a crop box so only the region inside it is saved.
texture.py textures an existing mesh using the trained model, unwrapping with xatlas and reducing faces with PyMeshLab.
Exports a trained splat as a PLY that other splat viewers can open; mesh and point cloud export are not offered for splats.
ns-export offers six sub-commands.
capabilities.inputs: pointcloud, tsdf, poisson, marching-cubes, cameras, gaussian-splat

capabilities.does: Training starts a browser viewer (default port 7007); ns-viewer opens saved runs. Remote use works by SSH port forwarding or a share link, and the port can be changed.
capabilities.inputs: --viewer.websocket-port, --viewer.make-share-url True, --vis viewer_legacy for the old viewer

capabilities.does: ns-render turns a camera path into a video or frames and needs FFmpeg installed; four sub-commands choose the path source.

A Blender add-on converts a Blender camera into a nerfstudio camera-path JSON and imports a nerfstudio path as a baked camera, so NeRF renders can be composited with Blender renders; supports perspective, equirectangular, VR180 and omni stereo cameras for NeRFs.
capabilities.inputs: Nerfstudio Path Generator panel, Nerfstudio Camera Generator panel, --rendered-output-names accumulation for a matte

capabilities.does: A Volinga extension trains a nerfacto-based model whose checkpoint is converted by Volinga Suite into an NVOL file for Unreal Engine.
Developer guides describe adding a method, custom viewer GUI elements and a Python viewer control; a plugins API page exists.

rea.notes: Apache-2.0 per the repository page. Splatfacto uses the Apache-licensed gsplat library. CLI reference pages list sub-commands but their flags have to be read with --help; the flags above come from guide pages.

entries.name: instant-ngp

licence.name: NVIDIA Source Code License for instant neural graphics primitives: research or evaluation use only; NVIDIA may use it commercially; business use goes through the research licensing form named on the README

engines.name: Hash-grid encoding and fused MLP (tiny-cuda-nn)
engines.does: Multi-resolution hash encoding and small fully fused networks that make fitting a scene fast on an NVIDIA GPU.

engines.name: GUI testbed
engines.does: Desktop window where a dataset is trained live and viewed, with camera-path, snapshot and mesh-conversion tools.

engines.name: pyngp Python module
engines.does: Python binding of the testbed, used by scripts/run.py for headless runs and snapshot handling.

capabilities.does: Fits a neural radiance field from a folder of posed images. Starts from a dataset path given on the command line, e.g. data/nerf/fox.
Learns a signed distance field from a triangle mesh, such as data/sdf/armadillo.obj; OptiX 7.6 or newer speeds up mesh SDF training.
Fits a network to a single image including gigapixel ones; large images are first converted to a .bin file by scripts/convert_image.py.
Fits a network to a NanoVDB volume such as the example wdas_cloud_quarter.nvdb.

Keyboard control of the viewport and training: WASD move, Space and C up and down, E and Shift+E exposure, T toggle training, R reload network, Shift+R reset camera, bracket keys step through training views.
capabilities.inputs: keys W A S D Space C E T R Tab [ ] { }

capabilities.does: Number keys 1 to 8 switch render modes (2 is the normal one); other keys show the error map, the ground truth and a multi-view layer view.
capabilities.inputs: keys 1-8, O, G, M, comma, period

capabilities.does: Add keyframes from the current camera, play them, render an .mp4, or export the keyframes to JSON.
capabilities.inputs: GUI: Add from cam, render mp4, export keyframes json

capabilities.does: The GUI converts a trained NeRF or SDF into a triangle mesh.
Renders with NVIDIA DLSS upscaling (needs the Vulkan SDK at build time); sharpening of 1.0 and render-crop settings are recommended.
capabilities.inputs: GUI Rendering: DLSS, DLSS sharpening, Crop size, Crop aabb

capabilities.does: Connects to OculusVR, SteamVR or any OpenXR headset from a GUI button, with stick movement, grab dragging and two-handed grab for rotate and zoom; multiple GPUs are only used for VR, one per eye.
Models are saved and loaded as snapshots from the GUI or from the pyngp module; headless runs use --no-gui or scripts/run.py.
The GUI can optimise camera poses and lens parameters while training; a mask file excludes moving objects (dynamic_mask_<name>.png beside each image).
scripts/colmap2nerf.py can extract frames from a video, run COLMAP, and write transforms.json; it can mask categories such as person or car with Detectron2.
Global fields of the dataset file control the scene box and appearance codes.
capabilities.inputs: aabb_scale (power of two up to 128), scale (0.33), offset ([0.5,0.5,0.5]), n_extra_learnable_dims (16 suggested)

capabilities.does: Helper scripts convert Record3D captures and live NeRFCapture streams to datasets.
The tips page advises 50 to 150 sharp images, notes that most convergence happens in the first seconds, and links exposure variation to floaters.
capabilities.inputs: Debug visualization: Visualize cameras, Visualize unit cube

rea.restrictions: Licence page read: use of the work and derivatives is limited to research or evaluation; NVIDIA and affiliates may use it commercially; redistribution needs the licence text; suing a licensor over patents ends your rights.
rea.notes: Not usable inside a commercial product without a separate licence from NVIDIA.

entries.name: COLMAP
entries.vendor: COLMAP contributors (copyright also held by ETH Zurich and UNC Chapel Hill)

licence.name: New BSD (BSD-3-Clause style); dependencies are licensed separately and can change the licence of a build

engines.name: Feature extraction and matching
engines.does: Detects keypoints and descriptors per image and finds correspondences between image pairs, writing everything into a SQLite database.

engines.name: Incremental and global mappers
engines.does: Build a sparse camera and point model, either by adding images one by one (mapper) or by solving all poses together (global_mapper).

engines.name: Multi-view stereo
engines.does: Computes depth and normal maps per image with patch-match stereo, fuses them into a coloured point cloud, then meshes it.

engines.name: GUI and CLI
engines.does: One executable offers both a graphical interface and command-line sub-commands; options can come from arguments or a project .ini file.

capabilities.does: SIFT is the default extractor, on GPU (CUDA works headless) or CPU. Cancelled runs resume, so images can be added later.
Optional learned extractors ALIKED (two variants) and LoMa (two descriptor sizes) run ONNX models; the build needs ONNX enabled and one database should not mix extractor types.
Matcher types pair with the extractor: brute force with ratio test for SIFT, cosine brute force for learned descriptors, LightGlue networks, and dedicated LoMa matchers.

Pair selection by exhaustive (best for a few hundred images), sequential with loop detection, vocabulary tree (thousands of images), spatial (GPS or location priors), transitive, or a custom pair list; re-runs only match new pairs.
Matches are verified geometrically and the result is stored per pair as fundamental, essential and homography matrices; reconstruction uses only this table.
The mapper starts from an initial image pair, registers further images, triangulates points and refines with bundle adjustment, shown live in the GUI; several models can result and be merged.
capabilities.inputs: mapper --database_path --image_path --output_path; Reconstruction options > Init for a manual pair; model_merger

capabilities.does: global_mapper solves all camera poses at once instead of incrementally; the repository names it a global SfM pipeline (GLOMAP).

Many intrinsic models: pinhole, radial, OpenCV, full OpenCV, several fisheye models, FOV, division, EUCM, skewed pinhole and spherical. Guidance: pinhole for undistorted images, simple radial for unknown intrinsics, OpenCV for known calibration.
capabilities.inputs: SIMPLE_PINHOLE, PINHOLE, SIMPLE_RADIAL, RADIAL, OPENCV, FULL_OPENCV, OPENCV_FISHEYE, FOV, EUCM, SKEWED_PINHOLE, ...
capabilities.outputs: camera parameters per image or shared

capabilities.does: Intrinsics come from EXIF, a camera database, or manual values; images from one camera can share intrinsics, and the database tool can set the camera of selected images with a GUESS, EXIF or USER source flag.

Groups cameras with fixed relative poses into rigs and frames. A JSON file names the reference camera and relative rotation and translation; unknown rig poses can be estimated from a first reconstruction.
capabilities.inputs: rig_configurator --database_path --rig_config_path; rig_config.json: image_prefix, ref_sensor, cam_from_rig_rotation, cam_from_rig_translation; --Mapper.ba_refine_sensor_from_rig; --FeatureMatching.rig_verification

capabilities.does: bundle_adjuster refines a whole reconstruction; the solver backend is selectable.
point_triangulator triangulates points for an existing model with known poses, and image_registrator adds new database images to a model without adjustment.
Align a model to a frame given by camera centres, merge two models that share images, crop to a bounding box, orient axes under a Manhattan assumption, and convert formats.
Undistorts images, runs patch-match stereo for depth and normal maps (optionally with geometric consistency), then fuses them to a point cloud with normals.
Poisson surface reconstruction or a Delaunay graph-cut mesher turn the fused cloud into a mesh; the workspace also lists an advancing-front result. mesh_simplifier reduces faces.
mesh_texturer writes a mesh with per-face UV coordinates and a texture atlas image.
One command or one GUI dialog runs the sparse and dense pipeline from a folder of images.

The 3D viewer rotates, shifts, zooms, changes point and camera size, moves the clipping plane and selects points or cameras by double click; Extras can grab an image or assemble a movie from added viewpoints.
capabilities.inputs: mouse and scroll modifiers; Render > Render options; Extras > Grab image, Grab movie

capabilities.does: Sparse models are stored as binary or text files for rigs, cameras, frames, images and points3D; export covers NVM, Bundler, PLY and VRML, and plain PLY point clouds can be imported.
capabilities.inputs: File > Export model, Export model as text, Export as...; model_converter
capabilities.outputs: COLMAP model, NVM, Bundler, PLY, VRML

capabilities.does: Undistorted output can be exported in layouts for CMVS/PMVS and CMP-MVS together with run scripts; Line3D++ is also supported.

All extracted data lives in one SQLite file with tables for rigs, frames, cameras, images, keypoints, descriptors, matches and two-view geometries, so it can be edited or filled by other programs; features and matches can be imported from text.
The repository publishes pycolmap on PyPI, including CUDA 12 wheels, and Docker images.

outcomes: sparse point cloud with camera poses
poses for splat or NeRF training

rea.restrictions: Licence page read: new BSD terms; keep notices in source and binary redistributions; the names of ETH Zurich, UNC Chapel Hill and contributors may not be used to promote derived products without permission; dependencies are separately licensed. No statement on study or reverse engineering.
rea.notes: Version shown on the docs landing page: 4.3.0.dev0 (2026-10-30).
