entries.name: Meshroom (AliceVision)

licence.name: MPL-2.0 (Meshroom, per the repository and alicevision.org)

engines.name: AliceVision framework
engines.does: C++ computer-vision library behind the nodes: 3D reconstruction, camera tracking, HDR and panoramas; related libraries are CCTag for markers and PopSift for GPU SIFT.

engines.name: Meshroom node graph
engines.does: Desktop app that edits and runs a graph of nodes; results are cached on disk, and a change recomputes only the nodes downstream of it.

engines.name: Photogrammetry pipeline template
engines.does: Ready graph: CameraInit, feature extraction and matching, SfM, depth maps, meshing, filtering and texturing.

engines.name: Command-line tools
engines.does: Headless entry points to run, batch, submit and inspect graphs.

capabilities.does: The default template reads cameras, finds and matches keypoints, solves cameras and a sparse cloud, computes dense depth maps on the GPU, and builds a textured mesh.
capabilities.inputs: CameraInit, FeatureExtraction, ImageMatching, FeatureMatching, TracksBuilding, SfMBootStrapping, SfMExpanding, DepthMap, DepthMapFilter, Meshing, MeshFiltering, Texturing

capabilities.does: Every node writes cached output; changing an attribute recomputes only downstream nodes. Graphs can be saved as templates, run locally or on a render farm with per-node CPU, RAM and GPU rules.
New nodes can be written in Python or wrap an external command-line tool; optional plugins add segmentation, depth estimation, dense matching (RoMa), Gaussian splatting, MicMac and geolocation.
Reads image metadata and a sensor database, groups images into intrinsics by camera serial and focal length, and writes cameraInit.sfm and viewpoints.sfm.
capabilities.inputs: viewpoints, intrinsics (Camera Type pinhole | radial1 | radial3 | brown | fisheye4, Initial Focal Length, Focal Length, Principal Point, Locked), Sensor Database, Default Field Of View (45 deg)

capabilities.does: Detects keypoints and descriptors per image on the GPU (CUDA) or CPU, with several describers and quality presets.
capabilities.inputs: Describer Types: sift, sift_float, sift_upright, akaze, akaze_liop, akaze_mldb, cctag3, cctag4, sift_ocv, akaze_ocv; Describer Preset: low, medium, normal, high, ultra; Force CPU Extraction; Max Nb Threads

capabilities.does: Photometric matching proposes pairs, then geometric filtering with RANSAC removes outliers.
capabilities.inputs: Photometric Matching Method: BRUTE_FORCE_L2, ANN_L2, CASCADE_HASHING_L2, FAST_CASCADE_HASHING_L2, BRUTE_FORCE_HAMMING; Geometric Filter Type: fundamental_matrix, essential_matrix, homography_matrix, homography_growing, no_filtering; Distance Ratio 0.8; Max Iteration 2048; Guided Matching

capabilities.does: Incremental SfM builds a two-view start, then adds cameras one at a time; options cover RANSAC-family localisation, triangulation thresholds, local bundle adjustment for large sets, rig constraints and locking known intrinsics. GlobalSfM is the global alternative.
capabilities.inputs: Localizer Estimator (acransac, ransac, lsmeds, loransac, maxconsensus), Min Angle For Triangulation 3.0, Max Reprojection Error 4.0, Local Bundle Adjustment, Use Rig Constraint, Lock Scene Previously Reconstructed, Initial Pair A and B

capabilities.does: Estimates a depth value per pixel for every solved camera with semi-global matching plus a sub-pixel refinement step; needs CUDA.
capabilities.inputs: Downscale (1 to 16), Min/Max View Angle, SGM: Nb Neighbour Cameras, WSH, GammaC, GammaP; Refine: samples, depths, iterations, neighbour cameras, WSH, Sigma, GammaC, GammaP

capabilities.does: Removes depth values that disagree with neighbouring cameras to enforce consistency before meshing.
capabilities.inputs: Number of Nearest Cameras 10, Min Consistent Cameras 3, Min Consistent Cameras Bad Similarity 4, Filtering Size in Pixels

capabilities.does: Fuses depth maps into a dense point cloud and mesh; without depth maps it makes a quick draft mesh from the sparse cloud.
capabilities.inputs: Max Input Points, Max Points, Max Points Per Voxel, Partitioning (singleBlock | auto), Repartition (multiResolution | regularGrid), angleFactor 15, simFactor 1, Add Landmarks To The Dense Point Cloud, Colorize Output

capabilities.does: Drops large triangles and, optionally, everything except the biggest connected piece; smooths the mesh.
capabilities.inputs: Filter Large Triangles Factor 60, Keep Only the Largest Mesh, Nb Iterations 5, Lambda 1

capabilities.does: Reduces vertex count by removing vertices, so the remaining ones already exist in the source mesh.
capabilities.inputs: Simplification factor 0.5, Fixed Number of Vertice, Min Vertices, Max Vertices, Flip Normals

capabilities.does: Creates UVs when the mesh has none and projects photo textures with visibility- and resolution-weighted multi-band blending.
capabilities.inputs: Texture Side 1024 to 16384 (8192), Texture Downscale (2), Texture File Type png | jpg | tiff | exr, Unwrap Method Basic | LSCM | ABF, Fill Holes, Padding, Max Nb of Images For Fusion, Visibility Remapping Method

capabilities.does: Moves, rotates and scales a reconstruction by a given transform, from cameras, landmarks, a single camera, markers or EXIF GPS, so it can be set to real-world size.
capabilities.inputs: Transformation Method: transformation, auto_from_cameras, auto_from_landmarks, from_single_camera, from_markers, from_gps; Additional Scale; transformation string X,Y,Z;R;S

capabilities.does: The manual lists 44 nodes, including camera calibration and localisation, rig calibration, keyframe selection, HDR merging, panorama stitching, image processing, SfM alignment and transfer, and export or upload nodes (animated camera, Maya, coloured point cloud, Sketchfab).
Six command-line programs run, batch, submit and inspect graphs without the GUI.
capabilities.inputs: meshroom_compute, meshroom_batch, meshroom_submit, meshroom_status, meshroom_statistics, meshroom_newNodeType

capabilities.does: Panes for images, a 2D viewer (features, depth map in 3D, SfM statistics, metadata), a 3D viewer with render modes and media library, a graph editor and its properties, plus start, pause, stop and submit controls.
capabilities.inputs: Images Pane, Image Viewer Pane, 3D Viewer Pane, Graph Editor Pane

capabilities.does: The Images pane has import, augment-reconstruction and live-reconstruction functions.
capabilities.inputs: Images Pane: Import Images, Augment Reconstruction, Live Reconstruction

capabilities.does: Besides photogrammetry, the AliceVision plugin ships pipelines for camera tracking, HDR fusion from bracketed photos, panorama stitching (including fisheye and motorised heads), photometric stereo and multi-view photometric stereo.
Meshes can go to Blender, ZBrush or Maya for retopology and retexturing; integrations exist for Blender and Houdini (SideFX Labs).

rea.notes: MPL-2.0 per the repository page. The manual "latest" pages show labels, not internal attribute names; some defaults (for example the largest-mesh switch) are tied to older releases named on the pages.

entries.verified: 2026-11-02, how: alicevision.org, repository page and manual node, GUI and CLI index pages read via WebFetch

entries.name: RealityScan (formerly RealityCapture)

licence.name: Free for students, educators and anyone under US$1M revenue in the past 12 months; above that, paid seats (licence page shows US$1,250 per seat per year); desktop app installed through the Epic Games Launcher

engines.name: Alignment (registration)
engines.does: Detects features in images, scans and other inputs, solves camera poses into components, and uses control points and camera priors.

engines.name: Reconstruction
engines.does: Computes depth maps and builds a mesh at preview, normal or high detail, with separate settings for LiDAR input.

engines.name: Colouring and texturing
engines.does: Colours vertices (F8) or unwraps and bakes texture images (F9) from the input photos.

engines.name: Command line and RealityScan Node
engines.does: Scripted runs through RealityScan.exe commands and a REST-like service for custom applications.

capabilities.does: Registers images into components by detecting features. Settings cover detection quality, features per megapixel or per image, expected image overlap, downscale before detection, and a reprojection error limit (3 px recommended).
capabilities.inputs: Feature detection quality, Max features per mpx, Max features per image, Image overlap, Image downscale factor, Max feature reprojection error

capabilities.does: Extra switches for alignment: GPU use, auto reconstruction region, forced rematch of components, background feature detection at low priority, preselector features, detector sensitivity from Low to Ultra, and merging georeferenced components without overlap.
capabilities.inputs: GPU acceleration, Force component rematch, Preselector features, Detector sensitivity, Merge georeferenced components, Distortion model

capabilities.does: Uses recorded image positions and orientations as soft constraints; accuracy and hardness values set how closely the result follows them.
capabilities.inputs: Use camera priors for georeferencing, Position accuracy, Position prior hardness, Yaw/Pitch/Roll accuracy, Orientation prior hardness

capabilities.does: A quick alignment mode with its own overlap level (Low, Medium, High), downscale factor and an optional final bundle adjustment.
capabilities.inputs: Draft: Image overlap, Image downscale factor, Final model optimization

capabilities.does: Three point types: tie points link images, ground control points add known coordinates in several coordinate systems, and ground test points are held out to check georeferencing. Each has weight, accuracy and an alignment report.
capabilities.inputs: Type, Weight, Coordinate system, Position accuracy, Converted position, Actual position

capabilities.does: Depth maps are computed at preview or normal quality with an image downscale factor and a pixel cap; high detail always works at full size.
capabilities.inputs: Image downscale, Maximal depth-map pixel count, Depth map algorithm version

capabilities.does: Controls mesh density and smoothness: minimum vertex distance, grouping and noise factors for default and low-texture areas, smoothing, detail decimation, marginal triangle removal and a preview strategy by sparse cloud or vertex count.
capabilities.inputs: Minimal distance between two vertices, Default/Low-texture grouping factor, Default/Low-texture noise factor, Smoothing, Detail decimation factor, Adaptive blending start (0.45), Max vertex count

capabilities.does: LiDAR points can be thinned by distance, cropped by scanner radius, cut by intensity and filtered by classification. Photos and scans join one project without special steps; scans are converted to an internal .lsp format.
capabilities.inputs: Minimal distance between two points, Point-cloud cropping radius, Minimal intensity, Filtering based on classification
capabilities.outputs: meshes from combined photos and scans

capabilities.does: Accepts photos, LiDAR scans, structured-light scanners and depth cameras in one project without special steps; each scan converts to an internal .lsp file that is added like an image.

Coloring paints vertices and gives a smaller model; texturing unwraps the mesh and computes texture images. Existing unwraps are reused; the Unwrap tool makes a new one. Single images can be switched on or off per camera.
capabilities.inputs: Colorize F8, Texture F9, Tx toggle per image

capabilities.does: Exports to many mesh and point formats and can write a .rsinfo file with the coordinate system.
capabilities.inputs: OBJ, PLY, XYZ, ABC, GLB, STL, 3MF, USD, USDZ, PTX, LAS, FBX, DXF, DAE; Export an info file; Save mesh by parts; vertex normals and colors

capabilities.does: Texture export can embed textures, export alpha, stitch to one image using u1_v1, (u,v) or UDIM tiles, force power-of-two sizes and pick pixel format.
capabilities.inputs: Texture maximal side 512 to 65536, Use pow2 texture size, Texture pixel format (24-bit BGR, 32-bit BGRA, 64-bit RGBA), Export texture alpha

capabilities.does: Models can be moved, rotated and scaled on export, with normals in world, object or tangent (Mikktspace) space and per-axis flipping for other renderers.
capabilities.inputs: Coordinate system, Move X/Y/Z, Rotate X/Y/Z, Scale X/Y/Z, Normal transformation Space, Flip X/Y/Z
capabilities.outputs: model in target axes and units

capabilities.does: Exports camera poses and focal lengths with FBX or Alembic, optionally with undistorted images and registered source images.
capabilities.inputs: Export cameras, Undistort images (Fit, Resolution), Export images
capabilities.outputs: cameras and images for other tools

capabilities.does: Reduces triangles by merging near-flat areas, to an absolute count, a percentage, or the larger or smaller of the two; can merge parts, keep or decimate borders, equalise density, and reproject colour and normals.
capabilities.inputs: Type Absolute | Relative | Maximum | Minimum, Target triangle count, Minimal edge length, Part merging, Border Decimation, Density Equalization, Color reprojection, Normal reprojection
capabilities.outputs: new reduced model (keeps colour, loses texture)

capabilities.does: Renders orthophotos and digital surface models from the model in arbitrary, top, side or map projection, sets resolution by size or pixel size, and can generate a DTM; jobs can be queued as a batch.
capabilities.inputs: Type Arbitrary | Top | Side | Map, Width, Height, Ortho pixel size, Rendering method, Generate DTM, Add to batch

capabilities.does: Splits vertices into classes by an AI tool (Ground, Artificial Object, None, Ignored), by labels transferred from images (up to 250 custom classes) or by ASPRS LiDAR classes; used to make a DTM and exported with LAS codes.
capabilities.inputs: Classificator type, Postprocessor type, sensitivity 0 to 1, Override classification, Export class LAS

capabilities.does: Masks exclude background or noise. AI Masking isolates the object before alignment, Masking from Mesh derives masks from a model, and masks can be imported, exported as PNG with EXR depth maps, or applied to alignment, meshing or texturing.
capabilities.inputs: Mask Images dropdown, Maps and Masks export, Input Layer = Mask

capabilities.does: RealityScan.exe runs commands in sequence from a prompt or .bat file, including a headless mode, instance naming and delegation, pause or abort, and .rscmd scripts with up to nine arguments.
A local service (RSNode.exe) offers a REST-like interface with bearer-token authentication to manage sessions, move session files and run CLI commands for custom applications.

Release 2.0 combines aerial imagery, aerial LiDAR and terrestrial data into orthographic projections, maps and 3D models, adds an AI segmentation model that removes backgrounds without manual masking, and changes alignment defaults for low-feature surfaces.
Release 2.0 shows heatmaps of incomplete areas before meshing and lets mesh quality be checked before texture and PBR work.

The help index lists further tools: alignment-quality assessment, matches display, ray-of-sight, video as input, marker detection, Map Wizard, scaling, georeferencing, hole closing, topology check, mesh smoothing, colour normalisation, texture reprojection, image layers, LOD export, Cesium ion upload, flythrough video, reports and a real-time scene renderer.
capabilities.inputs: Video as an Input, Detect Markers, LOD Export, Cesium ion, Flythrough Video, Reports

rea.restrictions: The licence page opened does not answer its EULA question and states nothing about reverse engineering; the EULA text itself was not read.
rea.notes: Renamed from RealityCapture to RealityScan with release 2.0 (17 June 2025); capturingreality.com now redirects to realityscan.com and the help site redirects to rshelp.capturingreality.com. Pricing is from the licence page on the day of reading and may change. Help-page defaults are mostly not stated.

entries.verified: 2026-11-02, how: help-site pages (alignment, reconstruction, export, CLI, texturing, control points, ortho, masks, simplify, classification, node API), release news and licence pages read via WebFetch; entry url not opened in this sweep (official domain, unchecked)

entries.name: Agisoft Metashape

licence.name: Commercial licence that is not time-limited: node-locked (Standard or Professional) or floating (Professional only); educational licence for accredited institutions; 12 months of support and free updates within 2.x.x per the licensing page

engines.name: Photo and scan alignment
engines.does: Finds key points, matches them into tie points, and solves camera positions and calibration by bundle adjustment, also aligning laser scans.

engines.name: Depth-map dense matching
engines.does: Computes depth maps for overlapping image pairs, merges them per camera, and turns them into a filtered point cloud with colours, normals and confidence.

engines.name: Surface builders
engines.does: Mesh, tiled model, DEM and orthomosaic generators that read depth maps, point cloud, tie points or laser scans.

engines.name: Distributed processing
engines.does: A server with worker nodes and clients splits chunks and sub-tasks over a network, or sends projects to Agisoft Cloud.

engines.name: Python and Java API
engines.does: Python 3.12 scripting inside the app or as a stand-alone module, and a Java library.

capabilities.does: Aerotriangulation with bundle adjustment. Accuracy sets image scale (Highest upsamples 4x, High full size, Medium 1/4 pixels, Low 1/16, Lowest 1/64); preselection by generic, reference (camera positions), estimated or sequential order limits pairs to match.
capabilities.inputs: Accuracy, Generic preselection, Reference preselection, Reset current alignment, Save project after each step

capabilities.does: Alignment limits and filters: key point and tie point limits (10 000 tie points advised), masks for key points or tie points, stationary tie point removal for turntables, guided image matching, adaptive camera model fitting.
capabilities.inputs: Key point limit, Tie point limit, Apply mask to, Exclude stationary tie points, Guided image matching, Adaptive camera model fitting

capabilities.does: Unaligned subsets form components that can be joined with at least three markers and merged; extra photos can be added to an aligned set if Keep key points was on.
capabilities.inputs: Components, Merge Components, Align Selected Cameras, Keep key points

capabilities.does: Frame, fisheye (equidistant and equisolid), equirectangular and cylindrical spherical cameras with distortion terms K1 to K4, P1, P2 and affinity B1, B2; separate calibration groups per physical camera, with manual input and fiducial marks for scanned analogue images.
capabilities.inputs: Camera Calibration dialog, calibration groups, Adaptive camera model fitting

capabilities.does: Handles structured terrestrial and unstructured aerial laser scans, aligns them with imagery, and uses them for models, DEMs and orthomosaics.
capabilities.inputs: Laser scan import, markers on scans, Point cloud + Laser scans source

capabilities.does: Dense point cloud from depth maps. Quality sets image downscale per step, depth filtering is Mild, Moderate, Aggressive or Disabled, and each point can store colour and a confidence count of contributing depth maps.
capabilities.inputs: Source data (Depth Maps | Model | Tiled model), Quality, Reuse depth maps, Depth filtering, Calculate point colors, Calculate point confidence

capabilities.does: Polygon mesh from tie points, point cloud, depth maps, laser scans or combinations. Arbitrary surfaces suit closed objects, height field suits terrain; face count, interpolation (disabled, enabled, extrapolated) and an option to split into blocks with block size and grid origin.
capabilities.inputs: Source data, Surface type, Quality, Face count, Interpolation, Split in blocks, Block size (m)

capabilities.does: Texture atlas as diffuse, normal, occlusion or displacement map from images, an orthomosaic or a more detailed model, with Generic, Orthophoto, Adaptive orthophoto, Single camera or Keep UV mapping and Mosaic, Natural, Average, Max, Min or Disabled blending.
capabilities.inputs: Texture type, Mapping mode, Blending mode, Texture size, Image downscale (x1 to x8), Pixel size (m), Page count

capabilities.does: Hole filling, ghosting filter, out-of-focus filter (Natural mode), texture transfer between models, anti-aliased baking with several rays per pixel, sharpening strength, and colour calibration before texturing.
capabilities.inputs: Enable hole filling, Enable ghosting filter, Enable out-of-focus filter, Transfer texture, Anti-aliasing, Sharpening strength, Calibrate Colors

capabilities.does: Hierarchical tiled model for city-scale scenes from tie points, depth maps, point cloud or mesh; opens in Metashape, the bundled Agisoft Viewer or other viewers, and needs a .psx project.
capabilities.inputs: Source data, Quality, Depth filtering, Transfer model texture, Enable ghosting filter

capabilities.does: Digital elevation model (DSM or DTM) in geographic, planar or cylindrical projection from point cloud, depth maps, tie points, model, tiled model or laser scans, optionally from selected point classes only.
capabilities.inputs: Projection type, Source data, Quality, Interpolation, Point classes

capabilities.does: Projects photos onto a DEM or mesh in geographic, planar (facades) or cylindrical projection, with Mosaic, Average or Disabled blending, a colour source, seamline refinement, hole filling and a ghosting filter for moving objects.
capabilities.inputs: Projection type, Surface, Blending mode, Color source, Refine seamlines, Enable hole filling, Enable ghosting filter

capabilities.does: Markers from coded targets (circular and AprilTag families, printable PDF) and non-coded targets, plus scale bars with known lengths, support georeferencing and scale.
capabilities.inputs: Create Markers, Detect Markers, Scale Bars, Coded targets

capabilities.does: Optimize Cameras runs a full bundle adjustment using GCPs, camera GPS, scale bars and a chosen coordinate system, with accuracy set per camera, marker or scale bar.
capabilities.inputs: Optimize Cameras, Reference pane, per-item accuracy

capabilities.does: Automatic ground point detection in two steps (lowest point per cell, then points within a distance and angle limit), manual assignment to standard LiDAR classes, and confidence filtering.
capabilities.inputs: Classify Ground Points: Max angle (default 15 deg), Max distance (m), Max terrain slope; Filter by Confidence

capabilities.does: Masks keep chosen photo areas out of alignment, depth maps, texturing, tiled models, orthomosaics and panoramas, and can be loaded from external sources.
Processes RGB, thermal and multispectral images, calibrates reflectance from panels or sun sensor data, and calculates vegetation indices such as NDVI.
Dynamic scenes from statically mounted synchronised cameras are held in multiframe chunks with a timeline, joint alignment and automatic marker tracking.
Several chunks can be processed one after another with Batch Processing, aligned to each other and merged when a scene is too large for one run.
capabilities.inputs: Add Chunk, Batch Process, Align Chunks, Merge Chunks

capabilities.does: Python 3.12 API in the console, by metashape.exe -r script.py, from an autorun folder, or as a stand-alone Python module; a Java library is available separately.
A server queues tasks for worker nodes over TCP with shared storage, splitting by chunk, frame or sub-task; projects can alternatively run on Agisoft Cloud.

Exports meshes (OBJ, 3DS, DAE, PLY, ABC, STL, WRL, U3D, FBX, DXF, GLB, OSGB), point clouds (LAS, LAZ, E57, PCD, COPC, potree, 3D Tiles, SLPK), orthomosaic and DEM (GeoTIFF, GeoPackage, MBTiles) and tiled models (TLS, 3D Tiles, 3MX).
capabilities.outputs: files for DCC, GIS and web viewers

capabilities.does: Imports camera orientation and tie points from other tools including COLMAP text, Bundler, BINGO, ORIMA, PATB and Blocks Exchange, and accepts images in formats such as JPEG, TIFF, PNG, EXR, DNG and thermal sequences.
capabilities.inputs: File > Import Cameras, Import tie points

capabilities.does: The manual covers lens calibration, automated mission planning, and a Reduce Overlap tool that finds excess images.
Distances, areas and volumes on models, point clouds and DEMs, stereoscopic measurement and vectorisation, automatic powerline detection; the features page also lists panorama stitching.

rea.restrictions: The licensing page says the licence does not allow giving third parties access to the software, including over the Internet or hosted. The EULA text and any reverse-engineering clause were not read.
rea.notes: Manual cited is the Professional Edition user manual, version 2.3 (2026). The page for the Python API PDF was listed but its contents were not opened. Prices are not on the licensing page opened.

entries.name: Luma AI

licence.name: Hosted commercial service with a free trial at app.lumalabs.ai; pricing tiers not captured

engines.name: Ray3.2 video model
engines.does: Generates and edits video from text, images or source clips, with keyframes, HDR colour and EXR output.

engines.name: Luma agent
engines.does: Assistant that researches, generates and refines video, image, audio and text assets for a brand.

capabilities.does: Ray3.2 makes native 5 or 10 second clips from text or an image at 360p draft, 540p, 720p (default) or 1080p.
capabilities.inputs: prompt, start image, resolution, duration (5 s | 10 s)

capabilities.does: Up to 16 keyframes can be set inside one clip for image-to-video and for modifying video; earlier Ray models controlled only the first and last frame.
Edits an existing clip: motion transfer, character transformation, visual effects, environment change, relighting and product swap; output runs to 20 s at 24 fps, 15 s at 30 fps or 7 s at 60 fps.
HDR generation produces native 16-bit colour, and EXR export writes 16-bit EXR frames in ACES2065-1 (AP0); HDR costs twice and HDR with EXR three times the SDR credits.
Applies cinematic camera moves across scenes, worlds and styles.
Reframes a video to other aspect ratios: 9:16, 3:4, 1:1, 4:3, 16:9 and 21:9.
Performance tracking and expressive facial performance (up to 8 faces) are listed among Ray3.2 capabilities.
Ray3.2 is offered through an API that exposes multi-keyframe control, performance tracking and EXR output.
Uni-1 carries style, character and visual references into generated assets; the homepage links an API post for Uni-1.1.

rea.notes: The 3D capture app (NeRF and splat capture) the brief asked for is not shown on the homepage; lumalabs.ai/capture returned 404 and docs.lumalabs.ai returned 403, so no capture capability is claimed here. A Wikipedia page on Luma Labs says nothing about capture either.

entries.verified: 2026-11-02, how: homepage and Ray3.2 page read via WebFetch; capture pages not found; docs gated (403)

entries.name: Polycam

licence.name: Free plan plus Basic (US$150 per year), Business (US$400 per user per year) and Enterprise (US$1,200 per user per year, 3-user minimum) per the pricing page

engines.name: Cloud photogrammetry pipeline
engines.does: Builds textured 3D models from phone photos or video in the cloud, in minutes.

engines.name: Space capture
engines.does: One walk-through yields a 3D model, a 3D room plan and a 2D floor plan, aligned to each other.

engines.name: Reconstruction API
engines.does: Cloud service that turns uploaded photo sets into photogrammetry models or Gaussian splats and notifies a webhook when done.

capabilities.does: Phone capture by walking around a subject; photos go to a cloud photogrammetry pipeline. Photo-count limits per capture are 150 (free), 300 (Basic) and 2,000 (Business, Enterprise).
capabilities.inputs: photos or video: image limit per capture, video 5 min (Basic) or 30 min (Business)

capabilities.does: Space mode records a room like a video and gives a photoreal 3D model, a 3D room plan and a 2D floor plan aligned together, with embedded dimensions within 0.5 inch on standard interior captures.
Gaussian splats are offered as a capture type; every paid plan lists unlimited splats.

On-device AI makes labelled 2D and 3D plans from one pass through the rooms, including walls, doors, windows and fixtures, over several floors; plans can be edited and exported as PDF, PNG, SVG or DXF.
capabilities.inputs: LiDAR iPhone Pro or iPad Pro (2021 or later) for capture

capabilities.does: Distances, areas and object dimensions can be measured on captures, with measurement overlays and a downloadable spatial report; Business adds advanced measure tools and AI reports.
Mesh formats named on the pricing page: GLTF, OBJ, FBX, DAE, STL, USDZ and ESX; Business adds geo-referenced LAS. Available formats depend on the capture mode.
Point clouds export as PLY, LAS, PTS, XYZ or DXF; documents as PDF, PNG, SVG or CSV; video is also listed.

Drone photos or video (PNG, JPG, MP4, MOV, AVI, M4V) are uploaded on the web and processed into large 3D models that can be measured for heights and distances; export targets named are SketchUp, Unity and AutoCAD.

Uploads photo sets from any camera and returns a photogrammetry model or a Gaussian splat with expiring download links and a webhook; estimates are 10 to 45 minutes for photogrammetry and 30 to 55 for splats; limited availability on Enterprise with prepaid credits.
capabilities.outputs: mesh, point cloud or splat download links

capabilities.does: Apps for iOS and Android, Apple Vision Pro support, a SketchUp extension, a Content API and a Transform Engine named on the homepage and pricing page.

Captures sync to a library, can carry comments and annotations, and are shared by link; Business adds shared libraries and virtual walkthroughs, Enterprise adds role-based folders and custom branding.

rea.notes: The help centre (learn.poly.cam) returned 403, so no help-centre page was read. Capture-mode details beyond Space mode come from the homepage and pricing page only. Terms of service were not read.

entries.verified: 2026-11-02, how: homepage, pricing and four feature pages read via WebFetch; help centre gated (403)

entries.name: SuperSplat

licence.name: MIT

engines.name: Browser editor
engines.does: Web app for inspecting, editing, optimising and publishing 3D Gaussian splats; a hosted copy runs at superspl.at/editor and a local build runs on port 3000.

engines.name: WebMCP tool layer
engines.does: A set of 29 browser-side tools covering scene inspection, selection, editing, camera control, timeline and keyframe authoring, and import or export, described in docs/webmcp.md.

capabilities.does: Imports splat files from an HTTP(S) URL without embedded credentials, optionally naming the file and a level of detail.
capabilities.inputs: import_url: filename, lod; formats PLY, SPLAT, SOG, SPZ, KSPLAT

capabilities.does: Downloads the selection, a layer or all visible layers as PLY, compressed PLY, SPLAT, SOG, SPZ or a standalone HTML or ZIP viewer; source spherical harmonic bands are kept by default and viewer exports use the current camera and background.
capabilities.inputs: export_scene: filename, format, scope (selection | layer | visible_layers)

capabilities.does: Selects or previews splats inside a world-space box, sphere or ellipsoid, inside or outside, testing either centres or full footprints.
capabilities.inputs: select_region: layer, shape, center, size, outside, preview, footprint (0 or 1)

capabilities.does: Selects visible splats or splats at all depths inside a viewport rectangle.
Selects or previews splats whose numeric property lies in a range; camera-dependent properties (camera depth, RGB, HSV) need a view token.
Select all, clear or invert on a named layer.
Deletes, hides or restores the selected splats on a layer.
Duplicates or separates a selection into a new layer; layers can be renamed, shown, hidden or made active.
Moves, rotates (Euler degrees) or uniformly scales a selection or a whole layer in world space around an optional centre.
Applies a colour adjustment to a scope and can reset it.
Undo and redo step through one shared editor history.
Sets the camera position, frames the content, and returns world positions under viewport points; display preferences change without altering splat data.
Reads the document, layers, counts, bounds, camera, viewport token, timeline summary and history; layer details include SH coefficients, and a GPU histogram gives a property distribution.
A timeline of frames at 1, 6, 12, 24, 30 or 60 fps with smoothness, loop and play state, and camera keyframes holding position, target and field of view that can be set, moved, copied or deleted.
capabilities.inputs: set_timeline: frames, frameRate, smoothness, loop, frame, playing; set_keyframes: frame, position, target, fov; move_keyframe; delete_keyframes

capabilities.does: The editor exposes its functions as browser tools so an agent can drive it; the repository also ships localisation files for the interface.

rea.notes: MIT licence per the repository page. The PlayCanvas user guide page for SuperSplat returned no readable text, so editor panels and selection tools beyond the WebMCP list are not described here.

entries.verified: 2026-11-02, how: repository README and WebMCP tool contract read via WebFetch

entries.name: Postshot

licence.name: Free tier (non-commercial), Indie (commercial, watermark-free, PLY and SPZ export) and Studio (CLI, HDR, above 4K, AprilTag alignment); prices on the pricing page showed EUR 0.00 and were not reliable

engines.name: Camera tracker
engines.does: Computes camera poses from images or video, or imports poses from other tools, before training.

engines.name: Radiance field trainer
engines.does: Trains Gaussian splat models locally on an NVIDIA GPU with profiles Splat3, Splat MCMC and legacy Splat ADC.

engines.name: Viewport and timeline
engines.does: Shows the trained scene, offers selection and transform tools, and animates virtual cameras for rendering.

engines.name: postshot-cli
engines.does: Headless executable that runs training jobs from the command line.

capabilities.does: Three radiance field profiles: Splat3 (recommended; fine foreground and background detail), Splat MCMC (more tolerant of input artefacts, fewer fine details) and Splat ADC (legacy, controlled by splat density).
capabilities.inputs: Radiance Field Profile: Splat3 | Splat MCMC | Splat ADC

capabilities.does: Caps model and image size: a maximum splat count (Splat3 and MCMC), a splat density factor (ADC; above 1.0 gives more splats), a limit on the larger image dimension, and a stop-after step count estimated from image count.
capabilities.inputs: Max Splat Count, Splat Density, Limit Image Size, Stop Training After

capabilities.does: Black and white masks matching colour image names and size: Remove Occluders ignores white regions in that image only; Remove Background trains black regions as empty and transparent.
capabilities.inputs: Image Masks, Mask Mode: Remove Occluders | Remove Background

capabilities.does: Use Best Images picks sharp, well-distributed frames (100 to 300 typical); Use All Images takes every one, for example for pre-selected sequences.
Corrects lens vignetting and exposure or white-balance changes between images.
Poses come from built-in tracking at a chosen quality, or from imported poses; options recentre the scene toward the origin (offset stored in the PLY) and assume a single lens and focal length.
capabilities.inputs: Camera Poses, Pose Quality, Recenter Poses & Points, Single Lens & Focal Length

capabilities.does: Takes JPEG, MP4, camera RAW, lossless and HDR video, and poses and points from COLMAP (bin or txt), Bundler (.out plus PLY), RealityScan (CSV plus PLY), BlocksExchange XML and Pix4D OPF.

Anti-aliasing reduces artefacts when zooming away from the training cameras (some viewers lack support); a maximum SH degree sets view-dependent colour data size; a sky model reduces floaters in outdoor shots.
capabilities.inputs: Anti-Aliasing, Max Sph. Hrm. Degree 0 to 3, Create Sky Model

capabilities.does: The homepage lists region-of-interest training to focus compute; the viewport tools treat regions of interest and crop boxes as scene objects that can be moved and scaled.

Orbit and ego navigation, translate, rotate and scale for fields, crop boxes, regions of interest and cameras, brush, rectangle and lasso selection of splats, and display toggles for ground plane, camera poses, points and radiance fields.
capabilities.inputs: Orbit Mode, Ego Mode (WASDQC), Translate, Rotate, Scale, Brush Select, Rect Select, Lasso Select

capabilities.does: Virtual cameras are animated with keys on position, orientation and focal length; Rove keys smooths sudden speed changes; playback and loop controls are provided.
capabilities.inputs: Add keys, Remove keys, Rove keys, Create Camera

capabilities.does: Render writes a movie from the selected camera, and an OpenXR toggle shows the scene on a headset or stereo display with head tracking.

Exports lossless PLY (non-standard header metadata for colour space, anti-aliasing and world origin), lossy SPZ with version 3 or 4 and quality 1 to 6, or an HTML web viewer, with a maximum SH degree option.
capabilities.inputs: Max. Sph. Hrm. Degree, Format Version, Quality, File Structure, Scene File Format

capabilities.does: postshot-cli.exe train computes poses and trains from image folders and saves a .psht project; the Studio tier lists the CLI.
A plugin for Unreal Engine 5.4 to 5.7 imports .psht projects as PostshotProjectAsset and places them as RdncFieldActor; packaged builds need the Postshot app installed.

Homepage lists no limit on image count or model size, 4K and 8K images, EXR, TIF, DNG, RAW, MOV, MP4 and MKV input, ACES colour handling, scene merging, and integration with Unreal Engine and After Effects.
Studio tier aligns scenes automatically from AprilTag detection; the homepage also mentions integration with geo-referenced data.

rea.notes: User guide pages for training, import, export, CLI, viewport, timeline and Unreal read. The release-notes index lists versions through v1.1.69 (2026-08-18) but its version pages were not opened. Needs a Windows 10 or later PC with an NVIDIA GPU of compute capability 7.5 or higher. EULA not read.

entries.name: KIRI Engine

licence.name: Free to download; the pages read mention a Pro version and a subscription but show no prices

engines.name: Cloud scan processing
engines.does: Uploaded photos, video or LiDAR data are processed on the vendor side into meshes or splats; 3DGS results are typically ready in about 7 to 20 minutes.

capabilities.does: Photogrammetry from photos for detailed, textured, non-reflective objects.
Scan mode for LiDAR-equipped iOS devices, covering 3D scans, floor plans and scene visualisation.
Mode for shiny, transparent or plain-coloured objects; the page says it is now part of 3DGS Scan.
3DGS Scan gives real-time renderable splats, previewed in app or browser before export; 3DGS Masking removes the background automatically and a sphere and plane brush edits shape and size.

Native splat format is PLY; with the mesh step enabled it also exports OBJ, FBX, STL, GLB, GLTF, USDZ, PLY and XYZ (up to eight formats).
A free, open-source Blender add-on opens and renders 3DGS files to match the online preview.

API with an API key, one credit per call for Photo Scan, Featureless Object Scan or 3DGS Scan (with mesh); a credit costs US$1 with a 500-credit minimum recharge, and ten credits are free at sign-up; the API is in testing.
In-app camera settings such as shutter speed and exposure value, quad mesh with PBR materials, high-poly output and built-in decimation.
