entries.name: Bullet Physics SDK (Bullet3, PyBullet)

licence.name: zlib licence (repository README)

engines.name: Collision module
engines.does: Shapes, broadphase, narrowphase and ray or convex sweep queries; the base layer that the dynamics sit on.

engines.name: Rigid body dynamics
engines.does: Single-body rigid dynamics with typed constraints, plus a reduced-coordinate multibody class for articulated trees.

engines.name: Soft body dynamics
engines.does: Rope, cloth and volumetric soft bodies with two-way coupling to rigid bodies.

engines.name: PyBullet
engines.does: Python bindings with a URDF loader, shape and body builders, robot control, rendering and VR events, built for robotics and reinforcement learning.

engines.name: OpenCL rigid body pipeline
engines.does: Experimental collision and rigid body pipeline written entirely as OpenCL kernels for discrete desktop GPUs.

capabilities.does: Closest-point queries returning distance and penetration, plus ray tests and convex sweep tests, run against a collision world that stores objects and exposes the query interface.
capabilities.inputs: btCollisionObject with transform and shape; query rays or swept convex shapes
capabilities.outputs: contact manifolds, ray hits, sweep hits

capabilities.does: Rejects object pairs by bounding-box overlap. Three structures are offered: a dynamic AABB tree, incremental 3D sweep and prune (16 and 32 bit), and a brute-force reference. Overlapping pairs persist so contact data can warm-start the solver.

Primitive convex shapes centred on the local origin: box (half extents), sphere (radius), capsule, cylinder and cone (each with Y, X and Z axis variants), and a multi-sphere hull that can build capsules.
capabilities.inputs: btBoxShape, btSphereShape, btCapsuleShape, btCylinderShape, btConeShape, btMultiSphereShape
capabilities.outputs: collision shape shared by many bodies

capabilities.does: Combines several convex child shapes, each with its own local offset, into one concave shape. Used to approximate concave meshes by convex parts; a helper recomputes principal axes to move the centre of mass.

Concave static meshes through a BVH triangle mesh shape that can serialize its tree, a scaled instance wrapper for reusing one mesh at several scales, a GImpact shape for moving concave meshes, and a heightfield terrain shape for 2D terrain.

Each shape carries a small safety margin, 0.04 by default (4 cm in metres), that speeds up and stabilises detection. Boxes subtract it from their extents; hulls, cylinders and cones grow by it; spheres use the full radius as margin.

Convex pair distance comes from GJK, penetration depth from EPA, both implemented inside Bullet. A dispatch matrix picks an algorithm for each pair of shape types and can be overridden with custom algorithms.

Three levels of selective collision: group and mask bit fields tested in the broadphase, a broadphase overlap filter callback, and a narrowphase near callback; the dispatcher class can also be subclassed for needsCollision and needsResponse.
capabilities.inputs: collision group, collision mask, btOverlapFilterCallback, near callback

capabilities.does: Single-body dynamics with dynamic (positive mass), static and kinematic (zero mass, user driven) bodies. A fixed internal rate of 60 Hz is decoupled from the frame rate by interpolation inside stepSimulation, with a cap on substeps.
capabilities.inputs: btRigidBody, mass, local inertia, btMotionState, stepSimulation timestep and max substeps

capabilities.does: Typed constraints between two bodies: point-to-point, hinge with limits and motor, slider, cone-twist for ragdoll limbs, and a generic 6-DOF constraint with spring variant in which each axis is locked, free or limited by comparing lower and upper limits.
capabilities.inputs: btPoint2PointConstraint, btHingeConstraint, btSliderConstraint, btConeTwistConstraint, btGeneric6DofSpring2Constraint, frames or pivots, limits
capabilities.outputs: joint behaviour inside the dynamics world

capabilities.does: A reduced-coordinate rigid body tree solved with the articulated body algorithm: fixed or floating base with revolute and prismatic joints. The manual calls it a recent, unfinished addition and points to the examples for use.

Arcade vehicle model: one rigid chassis, wheels approximated by ray casts against the world, simple anisotropic tyre friction. It plugs in through an action interface that runs inside the physics step.

Characters are either a capsule rigid body with angular factor zero, or an experimental kinematic controller that uses a ghost object for queries so it can climb stairs and slide along walls; the manual lists open issues for the latter.

Rope, cloth and volumetric soft bodies with two-way interaction with rigid bodies. A soft body stores per-node world positions, can be built from a triangle mesh, anchored to rigid bodies, pinned by zero mass, and pushed by per-node forces.
capabilities.inputs: btSoftBody, btSoftRigidDynamicsWorld, CreateFromTriMesh, appendAnchor, setMass(node,0), addForce

capabilities.does: Instead of node-against-triangle tests, a soft body can be split into convex deformable clusters for collision, switched on separately for soft-versus-rigid and soft-versus-soft pairs. This avoids missed hits on coarse meshes.
capabilities.inputs: generateClusters(subdivisions), collision flags CL_RS and CL_SS

capabilities.does: A from-scratch collision and rigid body pipeline written as OpenCL kernels, aimed at high-end desktop GPUs. The README calls it experimental and says it does not work on OpenCL CPU devices.
capabilities.inputs: OpenCL device, --enable_experimental_opencl in the example browser

capabilities.does: Dynamics worlds, shapes and constraints are dumped to a binary .bullet file through a default serializer and read back by a world importer; tools such as Blender and a Maya plugin could export physics to it or to COLLADA Physics.

PyBullet attaches to a physics server in several ways: in-process DIRECT without a window, in-process GUI with OpenGL, or SHARED_MEMORY, UDP and TCP to another process or machine. Takes a shared-memory key, host name, port and GUI options.

loadURDF places a robot or object description in the world with base pose, fixed-base and maximal-coordinate options, global scaling and flags such as merging fixed links, inertia from file, self-collision (with parent modes), implicit cylinders and sleeping.
capabilities.inputs: basePosition, baseOrientation, useFixedBase, useMaximalCoordinates, globalScaling, flags (URDF_MERGE_FIXED_LINKS, URDF_USE_SELF_COLLISION, URDF_ENABLE_SLEEPING)

capabilities.does: createCollisionShape makes sphere, box, capsule, cylinder, plane, mesh and heightfield shapes; createMultiBody assembles a body with links from shape ids, masses, joint types and axes, without any file. Both return -1 on failure.
capabilities.inputs: GEOM_SPHERE, GEOM_BOX, GEOM_CAPSULE, GEOM_CYLINDER, GEOM_PLANE, GEOM_MESH, GEOM_HEIGHTFIELD, halfExtents, radius, meshScale, baseMass, linkMasses, linkJointTypes, linkJointAxis

capabilities.does: createConstraint links a parent link to a child link or to the world with prismatic, fixed, point-to-point or gear joints; changeConstraint later edits maximum force, gear ratio, relative position target and error reduction.
capabilities.inputs: parentBodyUniqueId, childBodyUniqueId, jointType, jointAxis, parentFramePosition, childFramePosition, maxForce, gearRatio, erp

capabilities.does: setJointMotorControl2 drives joints in position, velocity, torque, PD and experimental stable-PD modes. Velocity motors are on by default, so zero force is needed for pure torque control.
capabilities.inputs: controlMode (POSITION_CONTROL, VELOCITY_CONTROL, TORQUE_CONTROL, PD_CONTROL), targetPosition, targetVelocity, force, positionGain, velocityGain, maxVelocity

capabilities.does: changeDynamics edits per-body or per-link properties after creation: mass, lateral, spinning and rolling friction, restitution, damping, contact stiffness and damping, anisotropic friction, CCD swept-sphere radius, collision margin, activation state and joint limits.
capabilities.inputs: mass, lateralFriction, restitution, linearDamping, angularDamping, contactStiffness, contactDamping, ccdSweptSphereRadius, collisionMargin, jointLowerLimit, jointUpperLimit

capabilities.does: setPhysicsEngineParameter sets world-level solver behaviour: fixed time step, solver iterations, split impulse and its threshold, substeps, error-reduction terms, cone friction, deterministic pair ordering, allowed CCD penetration, solver type, warm-starting factor and minimum island size.
capabilities.inputs: fixedTimeStep, numSolverIterations, useSplitImpulse, numSubSteps, erp, contactERP, enableConeFriction, deterministicOverlappingPairs, allowedCcdPenetration, constraintSolverType, warmStartingFactor

capabilities.does: rayTest casts one ray; rayTestBatch casts many with optional multithreading (0 uses all threads, -1 single), a filter mask, and reporting of the n-th hit. Each result gives object id, link, hit fraction, position and normal; id -1 means a miss.
capabilities.inputs: rayFromPositions, rayToPositions, numThreads, collisionFilterMask, reportHitNumber, fractionEpsilon
capabilities.outputs: per-ray object id, link index, hit fraction, hit position, hit normal

capabilities.does: getContactPoints lists contacts from the last step or collision pass; getClosestPoints finds pairs within a distance; getOverlappingObjects and getAABB give bounding-box queries (conservative); filter group/mask or per-pair switches turn collisions on and off.
capabilities.inputs: bodyA, bodyB, linkIndexA, linkIndexB, distance, aabbMin, aabbMax, collisionFilterGroup, collisionFilterMask, enableCollision
capabilities.outputs: positions, contact normal, distance, normal force, friction forces

capabilities.does: calculateInverseKinematics returns joint positions for an end-effector target, with damped least squares or selectively damped least squares solvers, optional target orientation, limits and rest poses for null-space behaviour, and iteration and residual controls. Jacobian and mass matrix are also exposed.
capabilities.inputs: endEffectorLinkIndex, targetPosition, targetOrientation, lowerLimits, upperLimits, jointRanges, restPoses, solver, maxNumIterations, residualThreshold

capabilities.does: getCameraImage renders colour, depth and segmentation images from a virtual camera with the OpenGL or the software TinyRenderer, with light and shadow controls on the latter. The depth buffer is non-linear; the mask can encode body and link together.
capabilities.inputs: width, height, viewMatrix, projectionMatrix, lightDirection, shadow, renderer (ER_BULLET_HARDWARE_OPENGL, ER_TINY_RENDERER), flags

capabilities.does: loadSoftBody reads an OBJ or VTK mesh into a deformable using mass-spring or Neo-Hookean material, with bending springs, self-collision, face contact, friction and repulsion; several parameters apply only to the finite-element model.
capabilities.inputs: fileName, mass, collisionMargin, useMassSpring, useBendingSprings, useNeoHookean, NeoHookeanMu, NeoHookeanLambda, NeoHookeanDamping, frictionCoeff, useSelfCollision

capabilities.does: saveState keeps a world snapshot in memory and returns an id; saveBullet writes a .bullet file; restoreState takes the id or a file name and restores joint and pose state onto bodies that already exist; removeState frees memory.
capabilities.inputs: saveState, saveBullet, restoreState (stateId or fileName), removeState

outcomes: game and VFX rigid body motion

rea.restrictions: README says all source files are under the zlib licence unless a folder or file says otherwise; nothing about reverse engineering was read.
rea.notes: Browser: no official WASM build in the sources read; ammo.js and other ports exist but were not checked. Manual read is Bullet 2.83; PyBullet doc is the quickstart guide text. Issue tracker is closed per README.

entries.verified: 2026-11-02, how: README, Bullet User Manual PDF text (v2.83), PyBullet quickstart guide text read

entries.name: NVIDIA PhysX 5 SDK

licence.name: BSD-3-Clause (repository README)

engines.name: Rigid body solver
engines.does: CPU rigid body dynamics with a choice of PGS or TGS solvers, persistent contact manifolds and optional GPU execution.

engines.name: Articulations
engines.does: Reduced-coordinate articulated bodies with drives, tendons, mimic joints and a cache for reading and writing joint state.

engines.name: GPU pipeline
engines.does: CUDA broadphase, contact generation and constraint solving for rigid bodies, plus the CUDA-only soft body and particle features.

engines.name: FEM soft bodies
engines.does: Finite-element deformable volumes simulated on the GPU from tetrahedral meshes.

engines.name: PBD particle system
engines.does: Position-based fluids, granular matter and other particle phases on the GPU.

engines.name: Scene queries
engines.does: Raycast, sweep and overlap against the scene with filtering and pruning structures.

engines.name: Vehicle SDK
engines.does: Component-based vehicle model with suspension, tyre, drivetrain and road-geometry queries.

engines.name: Character controller
engines.does: Kinematic capsule or box controller with slope, step and platform handling.

capabilities.does: Primitive geometries: sphere (radius), capsule (radius and half-height, along X), box (half-extents) and plane (static only; the shape pose defines it). Converters turn segments and plane equations into poses.
capabilities.inputs: PxSphereGeometry, PxCapsuleGeometry, PxBoxGeometry, PxPlaneGeometry, PxTransformFromSegment, PxTransformFromPlaneEquation

capabilities.does: Convex meshes (up to 255 vertices and faces), triangle meshes with BVH midphase choices and optional signed distance fields, and height fields are cooked offline into runtime objects. Scaling uses a mesh scale with orientation; triangle meshes accept negative scale.
capabilities.inputs: PxConvexMeshDesc, PxCookConvexMesh, PxTriangleMeshDesc, PxBVH34MidphaseDesc, PxSDFDesc, PxHeightFieldDesc, PxMeshScale, heightScale, rowScale, columnScale
capabilities.outputs: cooked convex, triangle and height field objects

capabilities.does: Dynamic and static actors, kinematic targets, per-axis locking, mass and inertia setters or automatic computation from shapes, force and impulse modes, damping, sleep thresholds, gyroscopic forces, dominance groups and an active-actors list.
capabilities.inputs: PxRigidDynamic, setKinematicTarget, PxRigidDynamicLockFlag, PxForceMode (eFORCE, eIMPULSE, eVELOCITY_CHANGE), setSleepThreshold, setDominanceGroup

capabilities.does: A scene picks the projected Gauss-Seidel or the temporal Gauss-Seidel solver, sets iteration counts per body, and can enable friction in every iteration, external forces in every TGS iteration, solver residual reporting and enhanced determinism.

Two continuous collision modes: sweep-based (scene flag, body flag and a pair flag in the filter shader) and speculative (body flag only, best with PCM). The number of passes, advance coefficient and re-sweep can be tuned.
capabilities.inputs: eENABLE_CCD, eENABLE_SPECULATIVE_CCD, ccdMaxPasses, setMinCCDAdvanceCoefficient, eDISABLE_CCD_RESWEEP, eENABLE_CCD_FRICTION

capabilities.does: A callback can edit contacts after generation and before solving, for example to set target velocities, limit impulses or scale mass for a pair. Contact reports with touch and force-threshold events are enabled by pair flags.

Joint types on a constraint base: fixed, distance, spherical, revolute, prismatic, gear, rack-and-pinion, and a D6 joint with per-axis free, limited or locked motion. Limits are hard unless stiffness and damping are given.
capabilities.inputs: PxFixedJoint, PxDistanceJoint, PxSphericalJoint, PxRevoluteJoint, PxPrismaticJoint, PxGearJoint, PxRackAndPinionJoint, PxD6Joint, setMotion(PxD6Axis, PxD6Motion)

capabilities.does: Revolute and D6 joints take drives with stiffness, damping, force limit and an acceleration mode; joints can break above force and torque thresholds, firing a callback. A custom constraint shader lets code write its own solver rows.
capabilities.inputs: PxD6JointDrive(stiffness, damping, forceLimit, acceleration), setDriveVelocity, setBreakForce, PxConstraintShaderTable, Px1DConstraint

capabilities.does: Reduced-coordinate articulations with fixed or floating base, fix, prismatic, revolute, unwrapped revolute and spherical joints, per-axis motion and limits, friction, armature, and force or acceleration drives with stiffness, damping and max force.
capabilities.inputs: PxArticulationReducedCoordinate, PxArticulationJointType, PxArticulationDrive, PxArticulationLimit, setArmature, eFIX_BASE

capabilities.does: A cache object copies joint positions, velocities, forces and root state in and out; utilities return generalized gravity, Coriolis and external forces, joint-space mass matrix, dense Jacobian, and joint accelerations or forces. Fixed and spatial tendons and mimic joints are also supported.
capabilities.inputs: PxArticulationCache, computeGeneralizedMassMatrix, computeDenseJacobian, PxArticulationFixedTendon, PxArticulationSpatialTendon, createMimicJoint
capabilities.outputs: mass matrix, Jacobian, forces, tendon constraints

capabilities.does: Raycast, sweep and overlap on the scene, with query flags for static, dynamic, pre and post filtering, any-hit and no-block; a filter callback and filter data masks; hit buffers; a cache for repeat queries; a batch interface.
capabilities.inputs: PxScene::raycast, sweep, overlap, PxQueryFilterData, PxQueryFlag, PxHitFlags, PxQueryCache, PxBatchQueryExt
capabilities.outputs: hit position, normal, UV, shape, face index

capabilities.does: Scene-query acceleration is configurable: static or dynamic AABB-tree pruning structures built ahead of time, secondary pruners for the dynamic tree, a rebuild rate hint, build strategies (fast, default, SAH), and replaceable query systems.

Capsule (recommended) or box controllers moved by displacement per call, with slope limit, step offset, contact offset, up direction, non-walkable handling, obstacles, hit and behaviour callbacks, riding on platforms, overlap recovery and controller-to-controller filtering.
capabilities.inputs: PxCapsuleControllerDesc, slopeLimit, stepOffset, nonWalkableMode, move(disp, minDist, elapsedTime, filters), PxControllerBehaviorFlag

capabilities.does: Component-based vehicle model in 5.x: direct-drive or engine-drive trains, suspension, tyre, wheel, rigid body and PhysX actor components updated in a sequence, with parameter structs for engine, clutch, gearbox, steering, Ackermann, brake and anti-roll bar.
capabilities.inputs: PxVehicleComponentSequence, PxVehicleEngineParams, PxVehicleClutchParams, PxVehicleGearboxParams, PxVehicleWheelParams, PxVehicleBrakeCommandResponseParams

capabilities.does: Enabling a CUDA context, GPU dynamics and a GPU broadphase moves broadphase, contact generation, body management and the solver onto the GPU. Convex hulls over 64 vertices, contact modification and non-D6 joint shaders still run on the CPU.

GPU-only FEM deformable volumes: a render mesh, a conforming tetrahedral collision mesh and a coarser voxel simulation mesh are cooked. Stiffness comes from Young's modulus and Poisson ratio (fixed corotated model); kinematic targets can pin vertices.

GPU position-based particle system with phases for fluid and self-collision, particle buffers for plain, fluid-plus-diffuse (spray, foam, bubbles) and rigid-shape-matching particles, and rest and contact offset tuning for fluid spacing.
capabilities.inputs: createPBDParticleSystem, PxParticleBuffer, PxParticleAndDiffuseBuffer, PxParticleRigidBuffer, createPhase, PxParticlePhaseFlags, setFluidRestOffset

capabilities.does: Particle cloth with spring links, triangle lists for aerodynamic forces and spring partitioning for parallel solving is marked deprecated in 5.4 in favour of a FEM cloth type; inflatables need a closed mesh and a pressure value.

simulate and fetchResults advance a scene; a split mode runs collide and advance separately, substepping repeats the pair per frame, and a scratch memory block can be passed in. Callbacks report contact, trigger, constraint break, wake, sleep and advance events.
capabilities.inputs: PxScene::simulate, fetchResults, collide, fetchCollision, advance, setSimulationEventCallback

capabilities.does: The repository README lists an ovphysx package: a C API with Python bindings that simulates USD physics scenes and exchanges tensors through DLPack, installable with pip. The README also lists the Blast destruction and Flow fluid and fire SDKs.

outcomes: deformable and particle fluid scenes (CUDA only)

rea.restrictions: README says BSD-3-Clause; whether the GPU binaries are open was not stated on the pages read.
rea.notes: Docs read are PhysX 5.4.0; the README mentions SDK versions 5.9.0 and 5.12.0 as paired releases. Soft body and particle features need CUDA. No browser build seen in the pages read.

entries.verified: 2026-11-02, how: PhysX 5.4.0 user guide pages and repository README read

entries.name: Havok Physics

licence.name: Commercial SDK licence; Unity package is binary-only; Babylon.js docs call the browser WASM build free under MIT

engines.name: Havok Physics
engines.does: Rigid body engine with continuous collision detection by default, a PGS solver with Baumgarte stabilisation and a direct solver option.

engines.name: Physics Particles
engines.does: Light particles for effects, destruction debris, air-suspended particles and fluid-like motion that do not affect gameplay.

engines.name: Havok Cloth
engines.does: Separate multithreaded cloth product for garments, hair, banners and foliage.

engines.name: Havok Navigation
engines.does: Separate product for navigation mesh generation, pathfinding and steering.

engines.name: Visual Debugger
engines.does: Tool with viewers and a heat map viewer for finding performance problems in a running simulation.

capabilities.does: Dynamic rigid bodies with runtime changes to physics properties, graceful recovery from invalid states, large-world support and predictable performance. The product page lists these in prose without parameter names.
capabilities.inputs: not documented on the public page

capabilities.does: Continuous collision detection is on by default, with a collision pipeline, collision response modifiers, custom shape combinations, level-of-detail shapes, geometry processing utilities and shapes that can change at runtime.
capabilities.inputs: not documented on the public page

capabilities.does: The constraint solver is projected Gauss-Seidel with Baumgarte stabilisation; a direct solver can be chosen instead.
Fast ray casts and shape casts for gameplay logic are listed as a headline feature.
capabilities.inputs: not documented on the public page

capabilities.does: Character controllers that collide reliably against landscape geometry are listed; no parameters appear on the public page.
capabilities.inputs: not documented on the public page

capabilities.does: Ragdolls are named among the simulation types on the product page.
capabilities.inputs: not documented on the public page

capabilities.does: Physics Particles: lightweight simulated objects for non-gameplay elements, enhanced destruction effects, air-suspended particles and fluid simulation; the Unreal plugin connects them to Niagara.
capabilities.inputs: not documented on the public page

capabilities.does: Havok Cloth is sold separately and covers garments, hair, banners, foliage, pouches and layered items with multithreaded simulation.
capabilities.inputs: not documented on the public page

capabilities.does: The page states the SDK gives cross-platform deterministic output, as long as the host engine is itself deterministic.

A Visual Debugger with viewers and a heat map viewer shows performance problems; in Unity it is off by default and switched on from the Havok configuration component. The Unity manual says profiling is on Windows only.
capabilities.inputs: Enable Visual Debugger field of HavokConfiguration

capabilities.does: In the Unity package, contact point welding smooths contacts for fast bodies sliding over each other and cuts ghost collisions. It is off by default and needs a matching custom body tag on bodies and in the configuration.
capabilities.inputs: Custom Body Tag, Body Tags for Contact Welding

capabilities.does: Resting dynamic bodies sleep automatically and wake when disturbed; the Unity configuration allows switching this off for testing.

Babylon.js loads Havok as a WebAssembly module from the npm package @babylonjs/havok and connects it through a plugin object; the page shows spheres and boxes with mass and restitution via an aggregate helper. Needs WebAssembly SIMD.

Havok Physics for Unity replaces Unity Physics inside the ECS with the same input and output data, so a project can switch backends; it is a binary-only package of Havok Physics 2021.2 with community support.

scripting: Unreal Engine plugin with Blueprint support

rea.restrictions: Unity manual: binary-only package, no C++ source; source access needs a Havok Physics SDK licence.
rea.notes: The SDK manual is not public; capability depth here is thin by necessity. Browser: yes, as a WebAssembly build through Babylon.js (@babylonjs/havok). The Unity manual pages for components and joints were not available.

entries.verified: 2026-11-02, how: product page, Unity package manual (2 pages) and Babylon.js plugin page read

entries.name: Jolt Physics

licence.name: MIT (repository README)

engines.name: PhysicsSystem
engines.does: The world object: holds bodies and constraints, runs the step with a job system, and exposes body, query and listener interfaces.

engines.name: Sequential impulse solver
engines.does: Warm-started velocity and position constraint solving at a configurable number of steps per update; 60 Hz with one collision step is the suggested base.

engines.name: Soft body module
engines.does: Vertex-based deformables with edge, bend, rod, volume and tether constraints.

engines.name: Vehicle constraint
engines.does: Wheeled, tracked and motorcycle vehicles built on a step-listener constraint.

engines.name: JoltPhysics.js
engines.does: Separate project that compiles the library to WebAssembly and asm.js for browsers and Node.

capabilities.does: Bodies are static, dynamic or kinematic and are made from creation settings and a body interface. Settings cover mass properties and override mode, allowed degrees of freedom, friction, restitution and linear and angular damping.

Convex and primitive shapes: sphere, box, capsule, tapered capsule, cylinder, tapered cylinder, convex hull, triangle, plane and an empty shape. A convex radius rounds shape edges for the collision algorithm.
capabilities.inputs: SphereShape, BoxShape, CapsuleShape, TaperedCapsuleShape, CylinderShape, ConvexHullShape, PlaneShape

capabilities.does: Compound shapes come as a static version and a mutable one that can add or remove children at runtime. Decorator shapes scale, rotate and translate a child, or move its centre of mass. Mesh and height field shapes cover static concave geometry.
capabilities.inputs: StaticCompoundShape, MutableCompoundShape, MeshShape, HeightFieldShape, ScaledShape, RotatedTranslatedShape, OffsetCenterOfMassShape

capabilities.does: Broadphase layers and object layers decide which bodies are tested; filters exist per object-layer pair, per object versus broadphase layer, per group, per body and per shape. Table-based and bit-mask helper classes ship ready to use.
capabilities.inputs: BroadPhaseLayerInterface, ObjectLayerPairFilter, GroupFilter, BodyFilter, ShapeFilter, ObjectLayerPairFilterTable, ObjectLayerPairFilterMask

capabilities.does: Ray casts, shape-versus-shape tests, shape casts and broadphase-only queries through a broadphase and a narrowphase query interface. A collector removes internal edge hits on meshes; a transformed shape type represents a shape with its world transform.

Each body has a motion quality: Discrete tests only at step end, LinearCast sweeps the body along its path to stop fast objects tunnelling. A CCD job runs between the velocity and position solver phases.
Any body can be flagged as a sensor, which reports overlaps through the contact listener without producing a physical response.

Constraint types: fixed, distance, point, hinge, cone, slider, swing-twist, six-DOF, path (spline), gear, rack-and-pinion, pulley and vehicle. A motor settings type with spring modes drives constraints, and constraints can be made breakable.
capabilities.inputs: FixedConstraint, DistanceConstraint, HingeConstraint, SliderConstraint, SwingTwistConstraint, SixDOFConstraint, PathConstraint, GearConstraint, MotorSettings, ESpringMode

capabilities.does: Animated ragdolls built from a skeleton and constraint settings; they can be driven by hard keying (set poses) or soft keying (motors), with a skeleton mapper to move between animation and physics skeletons.

Two controllers: a rigid body character stepped by the system, and a virtual character that sweeps its own shape and has an extended update call. Contact listeners and character-versus-character collision hooks are provided; an inner body can follow the virtual one.
capabilities.inputs: Character, CharacterVirtual, CharacterContactListener, CharacterVsCharacterCollision, ExtendedUpdate, mInnerBodyShape

capabilities.does: Wheeled, tracked and motorcycle vehicles. A vehicle constraint needs registering as a step listener, tests wheel collisions with a collision tester, limits pitch and roll, offers anti-roll bars, gravity override, friction-combine hooks and pre-step, post-collide and post-step callbacks.
capabilities.inputs: VehicleConstraint, VehicleConstraintSettings, VehicleController, SetMaxPitchRollAngle, SetVehicleCollisionTester, GetAntiRollBars

capabilities.does: Soft bodies are vertex sets with edge, bend, rod, volume and tether constraints, pressure and collision against rigid bodies. Shared settings define topology; a contact listener and manifold type report contacts; a section covers skinning soft bodies.
Strand-based hair simulated on the GPU, with limited collision support restricted to convex hulls and compound shapes, listed as a feature in the README.
Water buoyancy for bodies sitting in a liquid is listed among the library features; no fluid grid or particle fluid is named in the pages read.

A simulation gives identical results for the same binary and the same sequence of API calls. A CMake option extends this across platforms for about an 8 percent cost. Some outputs (broadphase queries, listener order, active body list) are not deterministic.

The whole physics state can be saved and restored for rollback, with a filter that limits which bodies are written; bodies can be created with a chosen ID so both sides of a rollback keep matching IDs.

PhysicsSystem::Update runs broadphase update, collision finding, velocity solving, CCD, position solving and soft body jobs across a job system. Step counts are physics settings; sleeping bodies are tracked and wake events reported.

Body data is accessed under read or write locks, single or multi-body, with a mutex array; a step listener hooks into the step, and multiple independent physics systems may run in parallel when they share no bodies.

A compile option stores positions as doubles and takes a base offset in queries, costing roughly 5 to 10 percent speed. The docs list remaining float limits (broadphase, velocities, rotations) and suggest splitting a universe into several physics systems.
Shapes, with their children, are saved and restored through binary or text object streams and a factory, so shapes cooked once can be reloaded.

With a compile switch, a user-implemented renderer class draws lines, triangles, geometry batches and text; the system draws bodies and constraints through it, and a simple base class gives a quick start.

JoltPhysics.js compiles Jolt to WebAssembly or asm.js (npm package jolt-physics) with seven build flavours, including multithreaded and debug ones. It exposes nearly the full C++ interface and requires manual destroy calls for created objects.
The README lists ports to C, C#, Java and Kotlin, JavaScript, Rust, Python, Zig, Jai and Nim, and plugins for Godot, Source Engine and Unreal Engine.
capabilities.outputs: Jolt from other languages and engines

scripting: C, C#, Java/Kotlin, Rust, Python, Zig bindings (third-party, per README)

rea.restrictions: MIT licence named in the README; nothing about reverse engineering was read.
rea.notes: Browser: yes, through JoltPhysics.js (WebAssembly). The architecture page was read in part; vehicle controller internals and ragdoll pages were not opened.

entries.verified: 2026-11-02, how: architecture documentation, README, vehicle constraint class page and JoltPhysics.js README read

entries.name: Rapier

licence.name: Apache-2.0 (repository README)

engines.name: PhysicsPipeline
engines.does: Rust step function with SIMD-batched solving, optional rayon multithreading and a dedicated thread pool setting.

engines.name: Query pipeline
engines.does: Ray, shape and point queries that reuse the broadphase BVH.

engines.name: Character controller
engines.does: Kinematic controller with sliding, autostep, snapping and platform support.

engines.name: Bindings
engines.does: Official npm packages for 2D and 3D (WebAssembly), a Python package, C/C++ bindings and Bevy plugins.

capabilities.does: Four body types: dynamic, fixed, kinematic driven by position and kinematic driven by velocity. Builders set pose, velocities, gravity scale, damping, axis locks, extra mass, dominance group, sleep permission and per-body extra solver iterations.
capabilities.inputs: RigidBodyBuilder::dynamic, fixed, kinematic_position_based, kinematic_velocity_based; linvel, angvel, gravity_scale, lock_translations, lock_rotations, linear_damping, additional_solver_iterations

capabilities.does: Forces, torques and impulses can be added to a body, optionally at a point; each call has a wake-up flag. Forces and torques can also be reset. Mass comes from the attached colliders, and zero mass counts as infinite.
capabilities.inputs: add_force, add_torque, add_force_at_point, apply_impulse, apply_torque_impulse, apply_impulse_at_point, reset_forces

capabilities.does: Collider builders for ball, cuboid and capsule (X, Y and in 3D Z), convex hull (computed) or convex mesh (assumed convex), trimesh, 2D polyline, heightfield, voxels, compound, and VHACD-based convex decomposition. Round variants add a border radius.
capabilities.inputs: ColliderBuilder::ball, cuboid, capsule_y, convex_hull, trimesh, heightfield, compound, convex_decomposition, round_cuboid

capabilities.does: Each collider has density (default 1.0), friction (default 0.5), restitution and sensor flag. Two colliders merge friction or restitution by a combine rule: average, min, multiply, max, clamped sum or geometric mean, with a fixed priority order.
capabilities.inputs: density, mass, friction, friction_combine_rule, restitution, restitution_combine_rule, sensor, contact_skin

capabilities.does: Collision groups stop both contacts and events; solver groups stop only contact forces. Active collision types control which body type pairs collide, and hook flags let user code filter contact pairs or modify solver contacts.
capabilities.inputs: collision_groups, solver_groups, ActiveCollisionTypes, ActiveHooks (FILTER_INTERSECTION_PAIR, MODIFY_SOLVER_CONTACTS), ActiveEvents::COLLISION_EVENTS
capabilities.outputs: allowed pairs; collision and intersection events

capabilities.does: A trimesh flag fixes internal edges to reduce ghost collisions and another flag makes a mesh one-sided. Meshes and polylines are two-sided with no interior by default, so the docs advise against them for dynamic bodies.

Fixed, spherical (3D), revolute and prismatic joint builders, plus free, cartesian, planar, cylindrical, pin-slot, rectangular and universal types through a generic joint. Anchors and axes are set in each body's local frame; prismatic joints take min and max limits.
capabilities.inputs: FixedJointBuilder, SphericalJointBuilder, RevoluteJointBuilder::new(axis), PrismaticJointBuilder::new(axis), GenericJoint, local_anchor1, local_anchor2, limits

capabilities.does: Motors on spherical, revolute and prismatic joints use a PD controller: stiffness tracks position and damping tracks velocity. Position, velocity or combined targets can be configured, and a spring-like motor model can be selected.
capabilities.inputs: configure_motor_position(target_pos, stiffness, damping), configure_motor_velocity(target_vel, damping), configure_motor, configure_motor_model

capabilities.does: Joints can be inserted either as impulse joints or as multibody (reduced-coordinate) joints, held in separate sets of the physics world.

Ray casts return the first or every hit, optionally with the normal. Max length bounds the ray; a solid flag decides if an origin inside a shape hits at zero. Query filters exclude types, groups, one collider or body, or run a predicate.
capabilities.inputs: cast_ray, cast_ray_and_get_normal, intersect_ray, max_toi, solid, QueryFilter(flags, groups, exclude_collider, exclude_rigid_body, predicate)
capabilities.outputs: collider handle, time of impact, normal

capabilities.does: Shape casts sweep a shape along a velocity, with options for max time of impact, target distance and penetration handling; a non-linear cast sweeps constant linear and angular motion. Point projection, point and shape intersection and conservative AABB tests are also offered.
capabilities.inputs: cast_shape, ShapeCastOptions(max_time_of_impact, target_distance, stop_at_penetration), cast_shape_nonlinear, project_point, intersect_point, intersect_shape, intersect_aabb_conservative
capabilities.outputs: time of impact, witness points, normals

capabilities.does: Kinematic controller that slides along obstacles and gentle slopes, climbs stairs and small steps, snaps to ground and interacts with moving platforms. Settings: up vector, offset, max slope climb angle, min slope slide angle, autostep and snap-to-ground distances.
capabilities.inputs: up, offset, max_slope_climb_angle, min_slope_slide_angle, autostep(max_height, min_width, include_dynamic_bodies), snap_to_ground, solve_character_collision_impulses

capabilities.does: Bodies can enable continuous collision detection; the world limits the number of CCD substeps per step (zero turns CCD off) and the smallest substep length. Fast rotation and soft CCD prediction are further per-body switches.

Integration parameters set the time step (1/60 s default), solver iterations (4), internal PGS iterations (1), stabilisation iterations, warm-start coefficient, 3D friction model (Simplified or Coulomb), contact softness as frequency and damping ratio, prediction distance, allowed linear error and velocity caps.
capabilities.inputs: dt, num_solver_iterations, num_internal_pgs_iterations, warmstart_coefficient, friction_model, contact_softness, normalized_prediction_distance, normalized_max_corrective_velocity, contact_clustering

capabilities.does: Results repeat on one machine with one build and one insertion order. Cross-platform repeatability needs the enhanced-determinism feature (not with simd8), IEEE 754-2008 floats including on WebAssembly, and nalgebra math functions for setup values; the parallel feature may stay on.

Constraint solving and contact processing are SIMD-batched, four manifolds per instruction; an optional parallel feature threads broadphase, narrowphase and solver through rayon. The README lists 2D and 3D, f32 and f64 crates.
capabilities.inputs: parallel feature; rapier2d, rapier3d, rapier2d-f64, rapier3d-f64; PhysicsPipeline::set_dedicated_thread_pool

capabilities.does: The README states the C and C++ bindings include soft bodies, and the rigid body page mentions an internal soft-frame body type; the world has shared soft body settings. Soft body documentation itself was not opened.

Official npm packages @dimforge/rapier2d and rapier3d load WebAssembly asynchronously; compat variants embed the WASM in the JS file and need RAPIER.init(). Worlds are created with a gravity vector, bodies and colliders from descriptors, and world.step() advances.
capabilities.inputs: @dimforge/rapier3d, @dimforge/rapier3d-compat, RAPIER.init(), new RAPIER.World(gravity), createRigidBody, createCollider, step

capabilities.does: In JavaScript, world.debugRender() returns line vertices and RGBA colours for every body and collider; colours depend on type and kinematic state and cannot be configured.
Language bindings: Rust crates (user guide version 0.36), JavaScript packages (0.21), a Python package with 3D f32 only, C and C++ bindings, and Bevy plugins for 2D and 3D.

rea.restrictions: Apache-2.0 per README; nothing about reverse engineering read.
rea.notes: Browser: yes, official WebAssembly npm packages. Rust guide is 0.36, JavaScript guide 0.21 (versions differ). README labels the MJCF crates as AI-assisted.

entries.verified: 2026-11-02, how: Rust and JavaScript user guide pages and repository README read

entries.name: MuJoCo

licence.name: Apache-2.0 for source; documentation CC BY 4.0 (repository README)

engines.name: Core simulator (C)
engines.does: Articulated dynamics in joint coordinates with soft convex contacts, stepped through mj_step on mjModel and mjData.

engines.name: MJCF compiler
engines.does: Reads the native XML model format (and URDF) and fills in inertias and collision rules.

engines.name: Native viewer and renderer
engines.does: OpenGL visualiser with perturbation tools, plus off-screen colour and depth cameras.

engines.name: MJX
engines.does: JAX-based API that runs batched simulation on GPU or TPU, with a JAX backend and a Warp backend.

engines.name: Python bindings
engines.does: Full C API access from Python with rollout, viewer and model-editing helpers.

capabilities.does: Bodies form kinematic trees in generalized coordinates with free (7 position, 6 velocity numbers), ball, slide and hinge joints. Loops are not allowed in the tree and are closed with equality constraints. Defaults assume SI units.
capabilities.inputs: free, ball, slide, hinge joints; mjModel, mjData

capabilities.does: Geom types include sphere, capsule, ellipsoid, cylinder, box, mesh and plane; heightfields are non-convex and handled as triangular prisms; signed-distance geoms come from plugins. Mesh collision uses the convex hull from qhull.
capabilities.inputs: geom type, size, mesh asset, hfield

capabilities.does: Soft, convex contact dynamics with torsional and rolling friction, frictionless contacts and dry friction in joints and tendons. Per-geom softness and friction are set by reference and impedance values, dimension, margin, gap, mixing weight and priority.
capabilities.inputs: solref, solimp, condim, friction, margin, gap, solmix, priority, impratio

capabilities.does: Constraint solvers: Newton (default), conjugate gradient and projected Gauss-Seidel; a NoSlip pass can follow a primal solver. Friction cones are pyramidal or elliptic. Constraint islands allow per-island parallel work and sleeping of resting islands.
capabilities.inputs: solver choice (Newton, CG, PGS), cone type that follows the solver, noslip post-processing, constraint islands, sleep flag

capabilities.does: Integrator choices: semi-implicit Euler with implicit joint damping, implicit, implicitfast, a new discrete mode, and fourth-order Runge-Kutta. Implicit modes use analytic velocity derivatives; explicit Euler is not supported.
capabilities.inputs: mjOption integrator (Euler, implicit, implicitfast, RK4, discrete)

capabilities.does: Broadphase is a sweep-and-prune variant sorted on the main axis of geom spread; midphase prunes geom pairs with per-body AABB trees; narrowphase uses GJK and EPA (the native pipeline) or a legacy MPR pipeline, and a multiccd flag returns several contact points per pair.
capabilities.inputs: nativeccd flag, multiccd flag, mjCOLLISIONFUNC custom colliders

capabilities.does: A geom pair collides when contype of one overlaps conaffinity of the other (both default 1). Explicit contact pairs add or override pairs, contact excludes remove body pairs, and parent-child body pairs are skipped by default unless the parent is static.
capabilities.inputs: contype, conaffinity, contact pair, contact exclude

capabilities.does: Actuators combine a transmission (joint, tendon, site, slider-crank, body), activation dynamics (integrator, filter, exact filter, muscle) and force generation. Shortcut elements include motor, position, velocity, intvelocity, pid, damper, cylinder, muscle, adhesion and dcmotor.
capabilities.inputs: transmission (joint, tendon, site, slider-crank, body), activation type (integrator, filter, filterexact, muscle), shortcut elements motor, position, velocity, intvelocity, pid, damper, cylinder, muscle, adhesion, dcmotor

capabilities.does: Sensors write to a data array that does not feed the simulation: touch, IMU, force-torque, joint and tendon position and velocity, actuator force, body frame, rangefinder, inside-site and user sensors.

Fixed tendons are linear combinations of joint positions; spatial tendons run through sites and wrap over spheres and cylinders, with pulleys splitting them into branches. Tendons can have length limits and can be actuated.
capabilities.inputs: fixed tendon, spatial tendon, site, wrap, pulley, range, width

capabilities.does: Equality constraints close loops and couple bodies; the weld type ties a body to a mocap body, and a flex constraint keeps deformable edge lengths. Solver softness values below zero are read as stiffness and damping.
capabilities.inputs: equality weld, flex equality, solref, solimp

capabilities.does: Mocap bodies are static bodies whose pose is set each step through arrays in the data structure; welding a dynamic body to one gives steadier results than moving the dynamic body directly.

Flex objects are 1D (capsules), 2D (triangles) or 3D (tetrahedra) deformables built from bodies, with contact and elasticity. Composite macros expand to ropes, cloth and deformable solids; skins deform visual meshes; a cable plugin adds elastic cables.
capabilities.inputs: flex, flexcomp, composite, skin, mujoco.elasticity.cable plugin

capabilities.does: Engine plugins add sensors, actuators, passive forces and signed-distance geoms as dynamically loaded shared libraries instantiated per model element.
Inverse dynamics are computed analytically and a flag compares them against forward dynamics for checking. Soft-constraint formulation keeps the inverse problem uniquely defined.
Native MJCF XML with CSS-like default classes and include files, plus URDF loading. Other forms: zipped MJZ, version-specific binary MJB, and programmatic specs saved with mj_encode.

Native OpenGL visualiser shows meshes, textures, reflections, shadows, fog and skyboxes, with overlays for contact forces, inertia boxes and joint or actuator axes, mouse perturbation of bodies, and off-screen colour and depth cameras.

Python bindings expose the full C API: MjModel.from_xml_path or from_xml_string, MjData, mj_step with a step count, a threaded rollout module, blocking and passive viewers, an MjSpec model editor and a least-squares minimiser.
capabilities.inputs: mujoco.MjModel, mujoco.MjData, mujoco.rollout, viewer.launch_passive, MjSpec, minimize.least_squares

capabilities.does: MJX copies a model and data to the device and steps them under JAX jit and vmap, adding batch axes for domain randomisation and parallel rollouts. The JAX backend runs on NVIDIA and AMD GPUs, Apple Silicon and TPUs and has limited autodiff.
capabilities.inputs: mjx.put_model, mjx.put_data, mjx.make_data, mjx.step, jax.jit, jax.vmap

capabilities.does: The Warp backend for NVIDIA GPUs supports nearly all MuJoCo features (not PGS, noslip or SDF geoms), needs contact and constraint capacity arguments, has no autodiff, and offers graph modes and a batched renderer.

The README lists first-party Python, C# with a Unity plug-in, and JavaScript with WebAssembly; third-party bindings for MATLAB Simulink, Swift, Java, Julia and Rust. Prebuilt binaries cover Linux, Windows and macOS.

rea.restrictions: README: source under Apache-2.0, doc directory under CC BY 4.0; nothing about reverse engineering read.
rea.notes: Browser: the README lists a first-party JavaScript/WebAssembly binding; its docs page was not opened. Docs pages are very long; modeling and computation pages were read in two windows each, not whole. The README did not mention MuJoCo Playground or Warp, but the MJX page covers the Warp backend.

entries.verified: 2026-11-02, how: overview, modeling, computation, MJX, Python pages and repository README read (long pages partly); entry url not opened in this sweep (official domain, unchecked)

entries.name: Taichi Lang

licence.name: Apache-2.0 (repository README)

engines.name: JIT compiler
engines.does: Compiles decorated Python functions to CPU or GPU code through LLVM and SPIR-V based paths.

engines.name: SNode data containers
engines.does: Tree of dense and sparse nodes that holds multi-dimensional fields, with switchable memory layout.

engines.name: Autodiff
engines.does: Reverse and forward mode differentiation by source transformation on the compiler IR.

engines.name: AOT runtime (TiRT)
engines.does: Loads precompiled kernel archives from a C interface and a header-only C++ wrapper.

engines.name: GGUI
engines.does: Vulkan or CUDA based window, 3D scene and widget layer for showing results.

capabilities.does: A decorated kernel is the entry from Python: typed arguments (scalars, vectors, matrices, structs, ndarrays, templates), at most one typed return value, globals captured at first compile. Functions called from kernels are force-inlined, so recursion is not allowed.

ti.init selects the backend and options: default float and integer precision, random seed, debug mode, offline kernel cache (on by default), kernel profiler, CPU thread count, fast math, advanced optimisation, CUDA device memory and verbosity.
capabilities.inputs: arch, default_fp, default_ip, random_seed, debug, offline_cache, kernel_profiler, cpu_max_num_threads, fast_math, advanced_optimization, device_memory_GB

capabilities.does: The README lists x64 and ARM CPUs, CUDA, Vulkan, OpenGL 4.3 and later, Apple Metal and an experimental WebAssembly target. The overview page names Vulkan, OpenGL and DirectX as work in progress.
Fields hold scalars, vectors, matrices or structs over up to 8 dimensions, created with a dtype and shape; a 0D field is read as x[None]. Slicing is not supported and small matrices are advised.
capabilities.inputs: ti.field, ti.Vector.field, ti.Matrix.field, ti.Struct.field, fill, shape, dtype

capabilities.does: Dense, pointer, bitmasked and dynamic SNodes build spatially sparse grids. Cells can be activated, deactivated and queried; struct-for loops visit only active cells in parallel. Reading an inactive cell gives zero and writing activates it.
capabilities.inputs: ti.root.pointer, bitmasked, dynamic, ti.activate, ti.deactivate, ti.is_active, snode.deactivate_all

capabilities.does: Reverse mode wraps kernel calls in a tape that fills gradient fields from a zero-dimensional loss; forward mode computes Jacobian-vector products with dual fields. Custom gradients and checkpointing are supported. Parallel loops and other statements cannot share one kernel.
capabilities.inputs: ti.ad.Tape(loss), needs_grad, kernel.grad(), ti.ad.FwdMode(loss, param, seed), needs_dual, ti.ad.grad_replaced, ti.ad.grad_for

capabilities.does: Kernels are compiled on a development machine into an archive and run later through the Taichi runtime. Python side builds a module and archives it; the C++ side loads it, allocates ndarrays, launches and reads results. Targets named: Vulkan, OpenGL, x86 and CUDA.
capabilities.inputs: ti.aot.Module, add_kernel, archive, ti::Runtime, load_aot_module, allocate_ndarray

capabilities.does: GGUI opens a window with a 2D canvas, a 3D scene with camera, particles, meshes with optional wireframe and instancing, lines, ambient and point lights, image display, Dear ImGui style widgets, depth and image readback, and headless saving.
capabilities.inputs: ti.ui.Window, get_canvas, ti.ui.Scene, ti.ui.Camera, scene.particles, scene.mesh, scene.point_light, save_image, show_window=False

capabilities.does: GGUI can read back the colour image and the depth buffer as NumPy arrays, and a video manager writes GIF or MP4 files from frames.

The overview page presents Taichi for physical simulation and cites a material point method run with more than 400 million particles on one GPU. Simulation code is written by the user in kernels; no solver is built in.

Python-embedded language that exchanges data with NumPy and PyTorch, offers quantised types under 64 bits, and compiles with dead-code elimination and other optimisations. The docs sidebar lists matching tutorials for accelerating Python and PyTorch code.

outcomes: compiled kernels shipped to Vulkan or CUDA apps

rea.restrictions: README says Apache-2.0; nothing about reverse engineering read.
rea.notes: No physics solvers are built in; simulations are user programs. Docs home lists v1.6.0 as the stable doc set; maintenance state not stated in the pages read. Browser: README lists an experimental WebAssembly target; not confirmed in docs. Python version range in README is 3.6 to 3.10.

entries.verified: 2026-11-02, how: Taichi docs pages (overview, kernel, field, sparse, autodiff, AOT, settings, GGUI) and README read

entries.name: NVIDIA Warp

licence.name: Apache-2.0 (repository README); some third-party parts such as libmathdx have their own terms

engines.name: Kernel JIT
engines.does: Compiles Python functions to CPU or CUDA kernels and launches them over a thread grid.

engines.name: Autodiff tape
engines.does: Records launches and replays generated adjoint kernels in reverse.

engines.name: warp.fem
engines.does: Finite element toolkit for PDEs on grids, meshes and NanoVDB geometry.

engines.name: Geometry module
engines.does: Mesh, hash grid, BVH and volume queries inside kernels, plus isosurface and swept-volume tools.

engines.name: Tile programming
engines.does: Cooperative block-level primitives for matrix products, factorisations and reductions.

capabilities.does: Python functions decorated as kernels are JIT-compiled and launched over a dimension with inputs and a device; user functions callable from kernels; thread index from wp.tid(). Targets CPU and CUDA devices.

Typed device arrays in 1 to 4 dimensions, created empty, zeroed or from NumPy, converted back with numpy(); element types include vec2, vec3, vec4, mat22, mat33, mat44 and quat alongside scalar types. wp.map applies a function over arrays.
capabilities.inputs: wp.array, wp.empty, wp.zeros, wp.from_numpy, wp.array2d, wp.vec3, wp.mat33, wp.quat

capabilities.does: A tape records kernel launches and backward() propagates gradients from a loss into arrays created with requires_grad. Custom adjoints and replay functions, native adjoint snippets, retained gradients and a flag that skips backward code are supported.
capabilities.inputs: wp.Tape, tape.backward(loss), tape.zero(), requires_grad, @wp.func_grad, @wp.func_replay, retain_grad, enable_backward

capabilities.does: Tools compare autodiff against finite differences: Jacobian by autodiff, Jacobian by finite difference, gradient check for one kernel or for a whole tape, Jacobian plotting, and a GraphViz dump of the tape. Dynamic loops are not replayed in the backward pass.
capabilities.inputs: wp.autograd.jacobian, jacobian_fd, gradcheck, gradcheck_tape, jacobian_plot, Tape.visualize

capabilities.does: Kernel built-ins query meshes: closest point (unsigned, signed by normal, signed by winding number), closest ray hit with a max distance, box overlap, and interpolated position or velocity from barycentric coordinates. BVH queries take a box or a ray; hash grid queries take a point.
capabilities.inputs: mesh_query_point, mesh_query_point_sign_normal, mesh_query_point_sign_winding_number, mesh_query_ray, mesh_query_aabb, mesh_eval_position, bvh_query_aabb, bvh_query_ray, hash_grid_query
capabilities.outputs: closest points, ray hits, neighbour iterators

capabilities.does: Sparse volumes (NanoVDB) can be sampled in index space with interpolation, with gradient, or by integer voxel lookup without interpolation, and index points can be mapped to world space.

Extracts triangle or quad surfaces from scalar fields with marching cubes or surface nets, from implicit functions through a Lipschitz octree with sparse marching cubes, and builds swept-volume meshes, fields and bounds for animated rigid meshes.
capabilities.inputs: IsoSurfaceMarchingCubes, IsoSurfaceNets, sparse_marching_cubes, lipschitz_octree, swept_volume_mesh, swept_volume_field

capabilities.does: Geometry utilities include Delaunay edge flipping on triangle meshes and triangle adjacency construction for a mesh.

warp.fem builds finite element discretisations on regular 2D and 3D grids, 2D triangle meshes, tetrahedral and other explicit meshes, NanoVDB volumes and adaptive grids; curved high-order geometry is possible, and double precision is chosen on the geometry.
capabilities.inputs: Grid2D, Grid3D, Trimesh2D, Tetmesh, AdaptiveNanogrid, make_deformed_geometry

capabilities.does: Function spaces: continuous and discontinuous Lagrange (P and Q, degree up to 3 for most), serendipity, B-splines on grids, Nedelec and Raviart-Thomas vector shape functions. Trial and test functions can live on different spaces for mixed formulations.

Weak forms are written in integrand functions and integrated into vectors or sparse block matrices; fields can be interpolated; operators include grad, div, curl, jump and average for discontinuous Galerkin; quadrature is automatic or manual, with boundary sides and partitions.
capabilities.inputs: @integrand, integrate, interpolate, Quadrature, PicQuadrature, BoundarySides, GeometryPartition, BsrMatrix, bsr_cg

capabilities.does: Shipped examples include SPH and DEM particle simulations in the core group, plus Stokes, Navier-Stokes, Taylor-Green, Kelvin-Helmholtz, shallow water and APIC fluid examples in the FEM group.

Tiles are cooperative block-level values: load and store with zero padding, fill and view, matrix multiply with optional TF32, Cholesky and triangular solves, FFT, map, reductions, sort and scans. Shapes are compile-time constants and need CUDA 12.6.3 or later for linear algebra.
capabilities.inputs: wp.launch_tiled, block_dim, tile_load, tile_store, tile_matmul, tile_cholesky, tile_fft, tile_reduce, tile_sum

capabilities.does: Warp arrays are shared with PyTorch, JAX and Paddle, so differentiable kernels can sit inside machine-learning pipelines. The docs have dedicated PyTorch and JAX interoperability pages.

Installed with pip install warp-lang (Python 3.11 or later). Wheels exist for Windows x86-64, Linux x86-64 and AArch64, and macOS on Apple Silicon (CPU only); CUDA needs a Turing or newer GPU and a recent NVIDIA driver.

outcomes: GPU kernels for simulation and geometry processing

rea.restrictions: README says Apache-2.0 with third-party terms for some dependencies; nothing about reverse engineering read.
rea.notes: Docs stable page shows version 1.19.0. No browser build seen. The warp.sim claim comes from the Newton README (warp.sim not listed in current Warp docs navigation). Warp.render and interop pages were not opened.

entries.name: Genesis World (Genesis)

licence.name: Apache-2.0 for source code (repository README)

engines.name: Multi-physics engine
engines.does: Rigid body, FEM, MPM and particle (PBD, SPH) solvers sharing one scene and state, joined by couplers.

engines.name: Quadrants compiler
engines.does: Lowers Python kernels to CUDA, ROCm, Metal, Vulkan, x86 and ARM64 and carries the autodiff machinery.

engines.name: Camera renderers
engines.does: Three camera backends: Nyx (in-house), Luisa ray tracer and Pyrender rasteriser, behind one camera-sensor interface.

engines.name: Couplers
engines.does: Explicit, SAP and libuipc (IPC) couplers resolve contact where solvers meet.

capabilities.does: RigidSolver with a Newton or conjugate gradient constraint solver, pyramidal or elliptic friction cone, iteration, tolerance and line-search controls, no-slip iterations, SAP or all-versus-all broadphase, gravity from options, and state get and set.
capabilities.inputs: RigidOptions, constraint_solver, iterations, tolerance, ls_iterations, friction_cone, noslip_iterations, get_state, set_state

capabilities.does: Collision can be switched off, and MPR is the default narrowphase with GJK as a slower, more stable option that follows the gradient setting; a contact patch option recovers the full polygon but is discouraged.
Joint limits can be enabled and set per DOF; weld and screw (axis, pitch, limits, friction) equality constraints can be added, removed and queried.

DOFs are commanded by force, velocity, position or combined position and velocity, with proportional and derivative gains and force ranges settable per DOF; link wrenches and mass matrix are readable.
capabilities.inputs: control_dofs_force, control_dofs_velocity, control_dofs_position, set_dofs_kp, set_dofs_kv, set_dofs_force_range, apply_links_external_wrench, get_mass_mat

capabilities.does: Most getters and setters accept environment indices; per-environment link, joint and DOF info supports domain randomisation and heterogeneous simulation. The overview claims 10 to 80 times the throughput of Isaac and MJX without loss of accuracy.

FEM entities with elastic and muscle materials, and MPM entities with elastic, elastoplastic, liquid, sand, snow and muscle materials. The MPM elastic material takes Young's modulus (default 300000), Poisson ratio (0.2), density (1000) and a corotation or neo-Hookean model.
capabilities.inputs: FEMEntity, MPMEntity, MPM Elastic(E, nu, rho, model)

capabilities.does: PBD cloth material with density per area (default 4.0), static and kinetic friction (0.15), stretch and bending compliance, stretch and bending relaxation, and air resistance; PBD also has elastic, liquid and particle materials.
capabilities.inputs: rho, static_friction, kinetic_friction, stretch_compliance, bending_compliance, stretch_relaxation, bending_relaxation, air_resistance

capabilities.does: Particle fluids: SPH liquid, PBD liquid and MPM liquid materials; sand and snow in MPM; a stable-fluid solver for smoke; an emitter entity; entity types for 2D, 3D, tetrahedral and free particles.
capabilities.inputs: SPHSolver, SFSolver, MPM Liquid, PBD Liquid, Emitter

capabilities.does: Solver options exist for rigid, MPM, FEM, PBD, SPH, stable fluid, tool and kinematic solvers; couplers are legacy, SAP and IPC. The overview lists rigid, FEM, MPM, PBD and SPH solvers sharing one scene.
capabilities.inputs: gs.options.RigidOptions, MPMOptions, FEMOptions, PBDOptions, SPHOptions, SFOptions, ToolOptions, KinematicOptions, LegacyCouplerOptions, SAPCouplerOptions, IPCCouplerOptions

capabilities.does: Sensors: camera, contact, IMU, raycaster, tactile and others; the overview lists differentiable tactile, IMU, lidar, depth camera, contact force, surface distance and temperature grid.

Cameras can render with Nyx (in-house photoreal renderer for robotics), Luisa (a DSL ray tracer) or Pyrender (a rasteriser), selected behind a shared camera interface; surfaces and textures (colour, image, batch) are set on entities.

Autodiff and backpropagation run through the Quadrants compiler, with hand-derived gradients for the hardest kernels. The rigid solver exposes gradient reset and a pre-coupling gradient step; the friction cone option is not supported in differentiable mode.
Entities are created from morphs; the overview lists URDF, MJCF, OBJ, GLB and USD asset parsing (not exhaustive), and the engine index lists terrain and drone entities.
capabilities.inputs: gs.morphs, URDF, MJCF, OBJ, GLB, USD

capabilities.does: Quadrants compiles to CUDA, AMD ROCm, Apple Metal, Vulkan, x86 and ARM64, so runs span laptop CPUs to data-centre GPUs. Install PyTorch first, then pip install genesis-world (Python 3.12 to below 3.14); extras exist for the IPC solver and Nyx.
capabilities.inputs: pip install genesis-world; pyuipc, gs-nyx extras

capabilities.does: Python API with a built-in GUI viewer, recorders for saving data, and robotics examples such as manipulation, differential and batched IK, domain randomisation and drone hover training.

rea.restrictions: README says source code is Apache-2.0; nothing about reverse engineering read.
rea.notes: The platform was renamed from Genesis to Genesis World. Operating systems are not stated on the pages read (platforms left empty); backends are CUDA, ROCm, Metal, Vulkan, x86 and ARM64. The 10 to 80 times speed claim is the vendor's. The README did not describe an 'avatar' solver or generative modules; none are claimed here. No browser build seen.

entries.verified: 2026-11-02, how: documentation overview, API index pages, three API reference pages and repository README read

entries.name: Box2D (version 3)

licence.name: MIT (repository README)

engines.name: Soft Step solver
engines.does: The README lists a Soft Step solver, with island-based sleep, as the version 3 dynamics method; its internals were not read.

engines.name: Continuous collision
engines.does: Sweeps dynamic bodies against static ones during the transform update; bullet bodies are handled after hit events.

engines.name: Dynamic tree and queries
engines.does: AABB tree behind ray casts, shape casts and overlap queries.

engines.name: Character movers
engines.does: A geometric mover and a dynamic mover for character movement, per the README.

capabilities.does: Static, kinematic and dynamic bodies created from a body definition: type, position, rotation, damping, gravity scale, sleep switches, motion locks on X, Y and rotation, bullet flag, safety factor and user data. Force, impulse and torque calls act on bodies.
capabilities.inputs: b2BodyDef(type, linearDamping, angularDamping, gravityScale, enableSleep, motionLocks, isBullet), b2Body_ApplyForce, b2Body_ApplyLinearImpulse, b2Body_ApplyTorque

capabilities.does: A world is created from a definition with gravity, restitution threshold and iterations, a friction callback, sleep switch and worker thread count, and is advanced with a time step and a sub-step count. Contact recycling distance is tunable.
capabilities.inputs: b2WorldDef(gravity, enableSleep, workerCount, restitutionThreshold, restitutionIterations, frictionCallback), b2World_Step(worldId, timeStep, subStepCount), b2World_SetContactRecycleDistance

capabilities.does: Shapes: circle, capsule, two-sided segment, convex polygon (up to 8 vertices, with box, rounded box and offset box helpers, hull computation and a rounding radius), and one-sided chain segments with ghost vertices to prevent ghost collisions.
capabilities.inputs: b2Circle, b2Capsule, b2Segment, b2Polygon, b2MakeBox, b2MakeRoundedBox, b2ComputeHull, b2MakePolygon, b2ChainSegment, b2CreateChain

capabilities.does: A shape definition carries density, a surface material (friction, restitution, tangent speed, user material id), a collision filter (category bits, mask bits, group index), a sensor flag, sensor-event flag and an option to update body mass.
capabilities.inputs: b2ShapeDef(density, material.friction, material.restitution, tangentSpeed, filter.categoryBits, maskBits, groupIndex, isSensor, enableSensorEvents)

capabilities.does: Joint types: distance (with optional spring, hertz and damping ratio), revolute and prismatic (limits and motors), weld, wheel (suspension spring plus motor), motor (linear and angular spring) and filter (disables collision only). Joints report constraint force and torque and can break by thresholds.
capabilities.inputs: b2DistanceJointDef, b2RevoluteJointDef(lowerAngle, upperAngle, enableLimit, maxMotorTorque, motorSpeed), b2PrismaticJointDef, b2MotorJointDef, b2WheelJointDef, b2FilterJointDef

capabilities.does: World queries use a filter with category and mask bits: coarse AABB overlap, accurate shape overlap with a proxy, ray cast whose callback return value clips or ignores hits, and shape cast along a translation. Callback order is not guaranteed.
capabilities.inputs: b2QueryFilter, b2World_OverlapAABB, b2World_OverlapShape, b2World_CastRay, b2World_CastShape, b2MakeProxy

capabilities.does: Standalone geometry functions: point tests, ray casts and shape casts against single shapes, GJK-based shape distance, and time of impact with a sweep. A dynamic tree and AABB type support custom broadphase use.
capabilities.inputs: b2CastRayPolygon, b2CastShape, b2ComputeShapeDistance, b2ComputeTimeOfImpact, b2Sweep, b2DynamicTree, b2AABB
capabilities.outputs: distance, time of impact, cast output

capabilities.does: After each step the world lists body move events (including fell asleep), sensor begin and end touch events, contact begin and end touch events, hit events above a threshold, and joint events.

Continuous collision runs for dynamic bodies against static bodies during the transform update and produces events on the following step. Bullet bodies, flagged on the body, are processed after hit events.
Resting islands move to separate storage and are split only when a body is slow enough to sleep, one split per step. Sensors ignore sleeping.

Results follow creation order and events are deterministic. Cross-platform determinism on 64-bit targets relies on compiler flags (precise math on MSVC, no float contraction on clang and GCC) and custom atan2, sine and cosine; the docs say it cannot be turned off.
The README lists two movers for character movement, a geometric mover and a dynamic mover; their function-level documentation was not available in the pages read.

Portable C17 library with a C API that Swift can import directly; SIMD paths for SSE2, AVX2 and Neon with a disable switch; multithreading; a samples app that doubles as a viewer for .b2rec recordings. Unsupported ports listed: Beef, box2cpp and a WebAssembly one.
The length unit per metre can be changed globally; bodies, shapes and contacts are referenced by id handles with null checks and equality macros rather than pointers.

rea.restrictions: README says MIT; nothing about reverse engineering read.
rea.notes: Docs read are version 3.2.0 (overview page). Browser: the repository has an Emscripten build script; a WebAssembly port (box2d3-wasm) is listed as unsupported/community. The simulation page was read in two windows. Pages for hello, shapes, mover and sensors detail were not opened.
