entries.name: Matter.js

licence.name: MIT (repository README)

engines.name: Engine
engines.does: Steps the world with position, velocity and constraint iteration counts, uniform gravity and a time scale.

engines.name: Composite and Composites
engines.does: Containers of bodies and constraints plus factories that build stacks, pyramids, chains and meshes.

engines.name: Render and Runner
engines.does: Canvas renderer and a fixed-step loop runner that ship with the library.

engines.name: Collision modules
engines.does: Detector, Resolver and SAT modules for pair finding and separating-axis tests.

capabilities.does: Rigid and compound bodies with mass, density, inertia (settable to infinity to stop rotation), static flag, sleep threshold, per-body time scale, forces applied at a point, and setters for position, angle, velocity, speed, centre of mass and vertices.
capabilities.inputs: Body.create, applyForce, setMass, setDensity, setInertia, setStatic, setVelocity, setPosition, setParts, setVertices, scale, rotate, translate

capabilities.does: Friction (default 0.1, combined as the pair minimum), static friction multiplier (0.5), air friction (0.01), restitution (0, combined as the pair maximum), density (0.001) and slop (0.05) are set per body.
capabilities.inputs: friction, frictionStatic, frictionAir, restitution, density, slop

capabilities.does: Collision filter with category bit field (default 1), mask of categories to collide with (default -1) and an integer group where a positive shared group always collides and a negative one never does; helpers hand out unique categories and groups.
A body flagged as sensor fires collision events without a physical response; bodies also fire sleep start and sleep end events.

Factories for rectangle, trapezoid (slope as a fraction of width), circle, regular polygon and compound bodies from vertex sets, with options to flag internal edges, remove collinear or duplicate points and drop small parts. Concave decomposition needs the poly-decomp package.
capabilities.inputs: Bodies.rectangle, trapezoid, circle, polygon, fromVertices, Common.setDecomp

capabilities.does: A constraint keeps a distance between two bodies or a body and a world point; low stiffness makes a spring, length zero with high stiffness makes a pin, damping limits oscillation. Render types are line, pin or spring.
capabilities.inputs: Constraint.create, bodyA, bodyB, pointA, pointB, length, stiffness (default 1), damping (default 0)

capabilities.does: Composite factories link bodies with constraints: chain, mesh (grid with optional cross braces), stack and pyramid; the soft body, car and Newton's cradle builders are deprecated and moved to examples, where softBody and cloth demos live.
capabilities.inputs: Composites.chain, mesh, stack, pyramid, softBody, car, newtonsCradle

capabilities.does: Engine settings: position iterations 6, velocity iterations 4, constraint iterations 2, sleeping off by default, gravity as direction times scale (default y 1, scale 0.001), global time scale. update advances by a delta in milliseconds and fires before and after update events.
capabilities.inputs: positionIterations, velocityIterations, constraintIterations, enableSleeping, gravity.x, gravity.y, gravity.scale, timing.timeScale, Engine.update(engine, delta)

capabilities.does: Events module offers on, off and trigger with event names and callbacks that fire in subscription order; engines fire beforeUpdate, beforeSolve, afterUpdate and collision events.

The module list includes MouseConstraint for dragging bodies, Query for hit tests, a canvas Render with sprite support per body, and Runner; per-module pages beyond Body, Engine, Constraint, Bodies, Composites and Events were not read.
Bodies carry render settings: fill style, stroke style, line width, opacity, visibility and a sprite with texture path, offsets and scale; the built-in renderer draws to a canvas.
capabilities.inputs: body.render.fillStyle, strokeStyle, lineWidth, opacity, sprite.texture, xScale, yScale

capabilities.does: Plain JavaScript library installed with npm install matter-js or a script tag, working in browsers and Node.js; supports plugins and ships a demo collection. The README calls it an original implementation, not a port.

rea.restrictions: README says MIT; nothing about reverse engineering read.
rea.notes: Runs in the browser natively (pure JavaScript, no WebAssembly). Docs are for version 0.20.0 (Constraint page). Maintenance status is not stated on the README, so status is unknown.

entries.verified: 2026-11-02, how: Matter.js API class pages (Body, Engine, Constraint, Composites, Bodies, Events) and README read; entry url not opened in this sweep (official domain, unchecked)

entries.name: Newton Physics
entries.vendor: Linux Foundation project (initiated by Disney Research, Google DeepMind and NVIDIA)

licence.name: Apache-2.0 for code, CC-BY-4.0 for docs (repository README)

engines.name: ModelBuilder and Model
engines.does: Builder assembles bodies, joints, shapes and particles from primitives or imported assets into a finalised model.

engines.name: Solver family
engines.does: Nine interchangeable solver classes that advance State under Control and Contacts.

engines.name: CollisionPipeline
engines.does: Broadphase, convex and mesh narrowphase, contact reduction, optional hydroelastic contacts and particle soft contacts.

engines.name: Sensors and viewers
engines.does: Contact, camera and IMU observations plus real-time or offline visualisation.

capabilities.does: Simulation loop objects: ModelBuilder produces a Model (structure and parameters); State holds positions and velocities; Control holds targets and forces; Contacts holds the active contact set from CollisionPipeline.collide; optional solver observables hold diagnostics.
capabilities.inputs: ModelBuilder, Model, State, Control, Contacts, CollisionPipeline.collide

capabilities.does: Nine solver classes: Featherstone, ImplicitMPM, Kamino, MuJoCo, SemiImplicit, Steel, Style3D, VBD and XPBD. A feature table lists which handle rigid bodies, articulations, particles, cloth, soft bodies and differentiability.
capabilities.inputs: SolverFeatherstone, SolverImplicitMPM, SolverKamino, SolverMuJoCo, SolverSemiImplicit, SolverSteel, SolverStyle3D, SolverVBD, SolverXPBD

capabilities.does: SolverMuJoCo runs rigid bodies and generalised-coordinate articulations through MuJoCo Warp, using MuJoCo collision by default or Newton's pipeline when use_mujoco_contacts is false. It is the only solver with equality constraints (connect, weld, joint).

XPBD and SemiImplicit simulate rigid bodies with maximal-coordinate articulations; Featherstone uses generalised coordinates; Kamino handles kinematic loops with hard frictional contacts and Steel offers matrix-free or split solve modes with joint friction and limits (both marked experimental).
capabilities.inputs: SolverXPBD, SolverSemiImplicit, SolverFeatherstone, SolverKamino, SolverSteel(solve_mode, drive_mode, enable_joint_limits)

capabilities.does: Cloth runs in VBD and Style3D (particles and cloth only), and, without self-collision, in XPBD, SemiImplicit and Featherstone. Style3D has no joint support.

Soft bodies are supported by Featherstone, SemiImplicit, VBD and, experimentally, XPBD. VBD also supports particle-body attachments and a rod joint with stretch, shear, bend and twist response; spanning two solvers needs SolverCoupledADMM.
SolverImplicitMPM simulates particles with an implicit material point method; it has no joint support and uses a friction coefficient. The examples list MPM among the categories.

Joint types: prismatic, revolute, ball, fixed, free, distance, D6 (up to 3 translations and 3 rotations) and rod. Limits and per-DOF settings are stored by DOF; armature adds to the mass matrix diagonal; support for each type differs by solver.
capabilities.inputs: newton.JointType, add_joint_revolute, add_joint_fixed, add_joint_free, add_joint_rod, joint_limit_lower, joint_limit_upper, joint_armature

capabilities.does: Joints are grouped into an articulation; a joint left out of the list becomes a loop-closing joint. eval_fk computes body poses and velocities from joint coordinates and eval_ik recovers joint coordinates from body state, both with masks and index filters.
capabilities.inputs: add_articulation(joint_list), eval_fk(model, joint_q, joint_qd, state), eval_ik

capabilities.does: A follower joint is tied to a reference joint by q_follower = offset + multiplier * q_reference, for prismatic, revolute and D6 joints only; eval_mimic updates follower coordinates, and all solvers except Kamino support it.

Shape types: plane, heightfield, sphere, capsule, box, cylinder, cone, ellipsoid, non-convex mesh and convex mesh. Signed distance data can be attached to meshes or primitives to improve contact queries.

Broadphase options are all-pairs, sweep and prune, or explicit precomputed pairs (default); narrowphase uses MPR and GJK for convex pairs and BVH or SDF queries for meshes; contact reduction is on by default. Collide returns a Contacts buffer.
capabilities.inputs: CollisionPipeline(broad_phase, rigid_contact_max, reduce_contacts, shape_pairs_max, requires_grad), pipeline.collide(state, contacts)

capabilities.does: Opt-in pressure-based contacts for pairs where both shapes enable them and carry SDF data; stiffness is set by kh and custom pressure laws by function and data. Planes, heightfields and non-watertight meshes are excluded.

Collision groups (0 off, positive collide within group and with negatives, negative collide with all but their own), world indices for parallel worlds, explicit filter pairs from parents, disabled self-collision and USD filtered pairs, plus per-shape switches for shape and particle collision.
capabilities.inputs: collision group, world index, shape_collision_filter_pairs, has_shape_collision, has_particle_collision

capabilities.does: Margin sets where contacts are placed and gap sets when they are generated; both add across a pair (builder default rigid_gap is 0.1). Speculative contacts widen the gap with velocity up to a cap.

When particles exist, soft contacts against shapes are found automatically with a slack distance and exposed as counts, indices and normals; full-surface deformable-versus-rigid mesh contact is available.
ModelBuilder reads URDF, MJCF and USD assets through add_urdf, add_mjcf and add_usd; the concepts index lists a USD parsing page and custom attributes.

The README lists example categories for contact, camera and IMU sensors. The overview says sensors compute observations from state, contacts, sites and shapes and may declare the solver observables they need.

Differentiable simulation for optimisation and learning is a stated goal; only the Featherstone and SemiImplicit solvers are marked with basic support, backed by diffsim examples. CollisionPipeline takes a requires_grad option.

Installed with pip install newton[examples] and run with python -m newton.examples; options include list, viewer, device and frame count. CUDA acceleration needs a Turing or newer NVIDIA GPU; macOS runs on CPU only.

rea.restrictions: README: code Apache-2.0, docs CC-BY-4.0; nothing about reverse engineering read.
rea.notes: Newton exists and is documented; it builds on NVIDIA Warp and extends the deprecated warp.sim module (README). Docs 'latest'; no browser build seen. Several solvers are marked experimental in the docs. Collisions page was read in part.

entries.name: glTF 2.0

licence.name: Described as a royalty-free specification; the repository licence files (LICENSE.adoc, COPYING.adoc, LICENSES folder) were not read

rea.notes: Specification and extension READMEs are public; this entry lists capabilities only from extension READMEs that were opened.

entries.verified: 2026-11-02, how: extension READMEs and schema files read via WebFetch

engines.name: Core JSON asset model
engines.does: Scene graph, meshes, accessors, materials, cameras, animations and skins described as indexed arrays in one JSON document.

engines.name: GLB binary container
engines.does: Packs the JSON and one binary buffer into a single file so a model loads as one request.

engines.name: Extension mechanism
engines.does: Optional features are named extensions listed in extensionsUsed and extensionsRequired, which lets a loader skip or reject what it cannot read.

capabilities.does: Every file carries an asset block with a version string and an optional minVersion, so a loader can refuse files newer than it understands. Entities refer to each other by array index.
Fixes a right-handed space with +Y up and +Z forward, so exporters from other axis conventions must convert before writing.
Nodes form a tree. Each node can hold a local matrix or translation, rotation, scale, plus a mesh, camera or skin. A scene lists its root nodes and the asset names a default scene.
capabilities.inputs: node.children, matrix, translation, rotation, scale, mesh, camera, skin, scene.nodes

capabilities.does: A mesh is a list of primitives. Each primitive maps vertex attribute semantics to accessors, may add an index accessor, a material and morph targets, and picks a topology from seven modes (points to triangle fan).
capabilities.inputs: attributes, indices, material, mode (0 to 6, default 4), targets

capabilities.does: Standard attribute names carry positions, normals, tangents, texture coordinates, vertex colours, joint indices and weights. Names starting with an underscore are free for application data.
capabilities.inputs: POSITION, NORMAL, TANGENT, TEXCOORD_n, COLOR_n, JOINTS_n, WEIGHTS_n

capabilities.does: Accessors describe how to read a buffer view as typed data: component type, optional normalisation, element count, min and max, and shape from scalar to 4 by 4 matrix.
capabilities.inputs: componentType (5120 byte, 5121 ubyte, 5122 short, 5123 ushort, 5125 uint, 5126 float), normalized, count, type SCALAR to MAT4, min, max

capabilities.does: A sparse accessor stores only the elements that differ from a base accessor, as strictly increasing indices plus values. Without a base view the base is all zeros. Used for morph targets.
Buffer views slice a buffer and may set a byte stride for interleaved vertex data. The stride is required when several attribute accessors share a view, and vertex elements must be 4-byte aligned.
Binary buffers come from external files, base64 data URIs (octet-stream or gltf-buffer media types) or the GLB chunk. Floats must be IEEE-754 single precision with no NaN or infinity.
The GLB file holds a header, a JSON chunk and an optional binary chunk. The buffer stored in the file must be the first buffer and have no uri; the chunk may be up to 3 bytes longer for padding.
capabilities.inputs: GLB header, JSON chunk, BIN chunk

capabilities.does: Core material model with base colour, metalness and roughness. Factors multiply texture values. In the combined texture, roughness is read from green and metalness from blue, both linear.
A tangent-space normal texture perturbs shading normals; one scale value multiplies the decoded X and Y components.
An occlusion texture, read from its red channel, darkens indirect light. A strength value from 0 to 1 blends between no occlusion and the full sampled value.
Core emission: a colour factor in 0 to 1 multiplies an emissive texture. Values above 1 need the emissive strength extension.
With alphaMode BLEND the base colour alpha blends the surface with what is behind it.
With alphaMode MASK each pixel is fully opaque or fully removed depending on alpha against a cutoff; OPAQUE ignores alpha.
doubleSided turns off back-face culling. Back faces are lit with reversed normals.
Samplers set magnification and minification filters (nearest, linear and four mip modes) and wrap mode per axis (repeat, clamp to edge, mirrored repeat). Default wrap is repeat.
capabilities.inputs: magFilter 9728/9729, minFilter 9728 to 9987, wrapS and wrapT 10497/33071/33648

capabilities.does: Textures pair an image with a sampler. Images are PNG or JPEG, loaded from a uri or a buffer view, and must match the declared mimeType.
Perspective camera with a vertical field of view in radians. If far plane is missing the client uses an infinite projection; if aspect ratio is missing the viewport ratio is used.
Orthographic camera defined by horizontal and vertical magnification and near and far planes.
An animation links samplers to node targets. A sampler pairs a time accessor with a value accessor and an interpolation mode; the target path is translation, rotation, scale or weights.
capabilities.inputs: channel.sampler, channel.target.node, target.path, sampler.input, sampler.output, sampler.interpolation LINEAR (default) / STEP / CUBICSPLINE

capabilities.does: A channel target names which node property to drive: rotation, scale, translation or weights. With no node set, an extension may define the animated object.
A skin lists joint nodes and an accessor of inverse bind matrices (identity when omitted). Vertices blend joint matrices using JOINTS_n and WEIGHTS_n attributes.

Morph targets store displacement deltas for position, normal, tangent, texture coordinates and colour. Default weights live on the mesh and can be overridden per node. All primitives need the same target count.
COLOR_n accessors hold per-vertex RGB or RGBA that multiplies the base colour term.
Optional features are named in extensionsUsed. Those a loader must understand are also in extensionsRequired, otherwise a loader may ignore them and use fallback data.
KHR_materials_clearcoat adds a glossy top layer, like lacquer, with its own intensity, roughness and optional normal map. The layer uses a Fresnel term for index 1.5 and darkens emission under it.
KHR_materials_sheen adds a soft grazing-angle highlight for cloth. Colour and roughness are set separately from the base material. Clearcoat, if present, sits over the sheen.

KHR_materials_transmission lets a share of light pass through a thin surface instead of being diffusely re-emitted. Base colour tints it and roughness blurs it. Refraction and absorption are not modelled here.
KHR_materials_volume turns a surface into the boundary of a homogeneous medium of given thickness, with light absorbed by distance. Needs a closed mesh and a transmission extension.

KHR_materials_ior replaces the fixed index of 1.5 with a chosen value of 1 or more, which changes dielectric reflectance at normal incidence. A value of 0 selects a specular-glossiness compatibility mode.
KHR_materials_iridescence models a thin film whose colour shifts with angle. Film index and a thickness range in nanometres are set; a texture picks the thickness inside the range.
capabilities.inputs: iridescenceFactor 0, iridescenceTexture (R), iridescenceIor 1.3, iridescenceThicknessMinimum 100, iridescenceThicknessMaximum 400, iridescenceThicknessTexture (G)

capabilities.does: KHR_materials_anisotropy stretches the specular lobe along a direction, as on brushed metal. Strength scales it; rotation turns the direction counter-clockwise from the tangent.
capabilities.inputs: anisotropyStrength 0, anisotropyRotation 0 (radians), anisotropyTexture (RG direction, B strength)

capabilities.does: KHR_materials_dispersion splits transmitted light into colour bands. The value is 20 divided by the Abbe number, so 1.0 equals Abbe 20. It builds on the volume extension.
KHR_materials_emissive_strength multiplies the emissive colour past the core limit of 1, for HDR glow. It cannot be mixed with the unlit extension.
KHR_materials_specular scales the strength and the normal-incidence colour of dielectric specular reflection. Metals are unaffected.
KHR_materials_unlit outputs the base colour term (factor, texture and vertex colour) with no lighting. The object has no properties; alpha and doubleSided still apply.

KHR_materials_variants lists named variants at the root, and each primitive maps a material to the variant indices it applies to. The viewer picks one variant at a time. Each variant index may appear once across mappings.
KHR_materials_diffuse_transmission sends a fraction of diffuse light through the surface with a colour tint, for leaves, paper and thin shells. Release-candidate status on the page.

KHR_materials_retroreflection blends the normal specular lobe with one that reflects back toward the light, for safety clothing and road markings. Release-candidate status on the page; matches the OpenPBR parameter specular_retroreflectivity.
Archived KHR_materials_pbrSpecularGlossiness describes a material by diffuse colour, specular colour and glossiness instead of base colour, metal and roughness. Replaced by the specular extension.
KHR_texture_transform applies a 2D offset, rotation and scale to UVs of one texture slot, and may switch the UV set. The order is scale, then rotation, then offset.

KHR_lights_punctual defines directional, point and spot lights in a root list and attaches one to a node. Intensity is in lux for directional and candela for point and spot; range cuts off beyond a distance.
capabilities.inputs: type, name, color [1,1,1] linear, intensity 1, range

capabilities.does: A spot light carries inner and outer cone angles in radians. The inner angle must be smaller than the outer, which is at most half pi. Engines with one angle should use the outer.
EXT_lights_ies points a node light at a measured IES photometry file, either by uri or buffer view with media type application/x-ies-lm-63. A multiplier and a colour tint scale the result.
capabilities.inputs: lights[].uri, bufferView, mimeType, node light index, multiplier 1, color [1,1,1]

capabilities.does: EXT_lights_image_based gives a scene one environment light made of spherical-harmonic diffuse coefficients (to l=2) and a prefiltered specular cube mip chain. RGBD PNG carries HDR.

KHR_mesh_quantization lets positions, normals, tangents and UVs use smaller integer types (byte, short, normalised forms) and moves the dequantisation scale and offset into node transforms or KHR_texture_transform. Elements must be 4-byte aligned.
capabilities.inputs: POSITION byte/short, NORMAL normalised byte/short, TEXCOORD_n byte/short

capabilities.does: KHR_texture_basisu lets a texture point to a KTX 2 image with Basis Universal compression, with the standard PNG or JPEG source as optional fallback. Dimensions must be multiples of 4.
The basisu extension prescribes ETC1S with BasisLZ for colour maps and UASTC for data maps such as normals, with colour-space rules in the KTX 2 header and a full mip chain advised.
KHR_draco_mesh_compression replaces a triangle or strip primitive with a Draco bitstream in a buffer view, with a map from attribute semantics to Draco attribute ids. A raw fallback may be kept.

EXT_meshopt_compression compresses a buffer view in one of three modes (attributes, triangles, indices) with an optional decode filter (octahedral, quaternion, exponential), and can point to a placeholder fallback buffer.
capabilities.inputs: buffer, byteOffset, byteLength, byteStride, count, mode, filter NONE
capabilities.outputs: GPU-friendly compressed vertex, index and animation data

capabilities.does: KHR_meshopt_compression is a release-candidate successor with the same v0 stream, a better v1 stream, and an added COLOR filter for YCoCg data. It cannot share a buffer view with the EXT version.
capabilities.inputs: same properties as EXT, filter adds COLOR

capabilities.does: EXT_texture_webp lets a texture reference a WebP image, with a PNG or JPEG fallback source. Without a fallback it must be listed as required.

EXT_mesh_gpu_instancing makes many copies of a node mesh from per-instance attribute accessors of equal count. Instance transform is translation, rotation, scale; custom attributes start with an underscore.
capabilities.inputs: attributes.TRANSLATION VEC3, ROTATION VEC4, SCALE VEC3, _CUSTOM
capabilities.outputs: few draw calls for many objects

capabilities.does: KHR_gaussian_splatting stores 3D Gaussian splats as POINTS primitives with rotation, scale, opacity and spherical-harmonic colour attributes. Colour space and kernel are named in the extension. Ratified.
capabilities.inputs: kernel "ellipse", colorSpace, projection, sortingMethod; attributes KHR_gaussian_splatting:ROTATION, SCALE, OPACITY, SH_DEGREE_n_COEF_m

capabilities.does: EXT_mesh_manifold marks a mesh as an oriented 2-manifold and stores sparse merge indices that restore the watertight topology lost when vertices split along attribute seams.
KHR_animation_pointer lets an animation channel drive any mutable property named by a JSON pointer, such as a material base colour or a camera field, using path "pointer".
KHR_xmp_json_ld stores XMP metadata (author, licence, dates) as JSON-LD packets at the root and links objects to a packet by index. It does not affect rendering.
KHR_node_visibility adds a boolean that hides a node and all descendants, including meshes, lights and particles. Cameras and picking are not affected. Animatable by pointer.

KHR_node_hoverability sets whether a node and its subtree can be the target of a pointer hover. A false value above overrides true below. Adds hover-in and hover-out events to the interactivity extension.
KHR_node_selectability sets whether a node and its subtree can be picked by a selection ray. Adds an onSelect event to the interactivity extension.

KHR_interactivity stores a directed acyclic behaviour graph in the asset. Nodes have domain/operation names such as flow/sequence, flow/for, math/add, variable/set and pointer/get, plus typed variables and custom events. Single-user scope.
capabilities.inputs: graph nodes with declarations, configuration, value and flow sockets; variables; events

entries.name: OpenUSD (Universal Scene Description)
entries.vendor: Pixar Animation Studios; Alliance for OpenUSD

licence.name: Tomorrow Open Source Technology License 1.0 (identical to Apache 2.0 except the trademarks section 6, per its LICENSE.txt header)

outcomes: layered scene interchange between DCC tools

rea.restrictions: LICENSE.txt header: differs from Apache 2.0 only in section 6 (trademarks); the text does not mention reverse engineering.
rea.notes: Source and API docs are public.

entries.verified: 2026-11-02, how: documentation pages and LICENSE.txt read via WebFetch

engines.name: Sdf (scene description foundations)
engines.does: Layers, specs, paths and value types; the storage layer that file formats read and write.

engines.name: Pcp (prim cache population)
engines.does: Computes composition: layer stacks, prim indexes, dependencies, errors and namespace edits across all arcs.

engines.name: Ar (asset resolution)
engines.does: Turns asset paths into resolved locations and readable assets through pluggable resolvers and contexts.

engines.name: Usd (core scene API)
engines.does: The stage, prim, attribute and relationship objects that clients use to author and read composed scenes.

engines.name: Schema domains
engines.does: Typed schemas for geometry, shading, lighting, skeletons, physics, volumes, render settings and media.

engines.name: Hydra
engines.does: Imaging framework that connects scene data to renderers, with Storm as its rasteriser and HdPrman for RenderMan.

capabilities.does: Stacks several layer files so a stronger layer overrides a weaker one. Lets departments work in separate files over one shared scene.
Pulls the contents of a prim in another layer into a prim of this scene. The main way to assemble assets into larger scenes.
A reference that can be loaded or unloaded after the stage opens, so a client keeps only the needed parts in memory.
Bundles alternate versions of an asset under named choices. A user selects a variant without editing the original asset.
Links a derived prim to a base class prim, so edits to the class flow to every inheriting prim. Class prims are skipped by normal traversal.
Like inherits, but the derived prim stays a refinement of its base in every view of the scene, even after stronger upstream composition.
When composition arcs conflict, a strength ordering decides which opinion wins. The introduction links the ordering but does not spell it out.

Each prim has a specifier such as def or class; a class prim is an abstract template. IsDefined, HasDefiningSpecifier and HasClassSpecifier test the state, and the composed specifier decides traversal.
Pcp understands relocates, which move or rename prims introduced through a reference. The namespace editor adds them when the original cannot be edited.

UsdNamespaceEditor renames, reparents and deletes composed prims and properties across layers, queued then applied together, and fixes relationship targets and attribute connections that point at them.
capabilities.inputs: RenamePrim, ReparentPrim, DeletePrimAtPath, MovePrimAtPath, ApplyEdits, CanApplyEdits, EditOptions.allowRelocatesAuthoring

capabilities.does: Marks a prim instanceable so copies share one prototype scenegraph, which saves memory and speeds composition when the copies need no individual edits.
PointInstancer draws many instances of prototype prims from per-instance arrays: prototype index, position, orientation, scale, velocities, ids. Instances can be masked by id.
capabilities.inputs: prototypes, protoIndices, positions, orientations, orientationsf, scales, velocities, accelerations, angularVelocities, ids, invisibleIds, inactiveIds
capabilities.outputs: vectorised, animatable instances with motion blur

capabilities.does: Imageable prims carry a purpose token (default, render, proxy, guide) that renderers use to include or skip them. Unauthored purpose is inherited from the nearest ancestor.
capabilities.outputs: proxy and render split in one scene

capabilities.does: UsdGeom defines Mesh, NurbsPatch, BasisCurves, NurbsCurves, Points, Capsule, Cone, Cube, Cylinder and Sphere. Meshes may carry subdivision properties; orientation can be right- or left-handed.
Xformable splits a transform into an ordered list of ops, each its own attribute, so one op can be overridden in a stronger layer. UsdGeomXform is the plain transform prim.
capabilities.inputs: ordered xform ops, one attribute per op

capabilities.does: UsdGeomCamera is a transformable camera with shutter open and close times for motion blur. UsdGeom is right-handed with +Y up.

Primvars are attributes in the primvars: namespace that carry shader data across a surface, with interpolation constant, uniform, vertex, varying or faceVarying, optional index arrays and elementSize. Constant primvars inherit down the hierarchy.
capabilities.outputs: per-vertex colours, UVs and custom data

capabilities.does: Points and instances can carry velocities and accelerations. MotionAPI adds motion:blurScale, which scales blur without changing the recorded animation.
Kind metadata marks prims as component, group or assembly in a model hierarchy; UsdPrim exposes IsModel, IsGroup, IsComponent and SetKind. Assemblies aggregate other models.
API schemas add a set of related properties to a prim without changing its type, either single-apply or multiple-apply with an instance name.
capabilities.inputs: ApplyAPI, RemoveAPI, HasAPI, CanApplyAPI, apiSchemas metadata

capabilities.does: Attributes hold a default value and time samples. Get resolves a value at a time; GetTimeSamples, GetBracketingTimeSamples and ValueMightBeTimeVarying query the samples.
Between samples the stage interpolates either held (constant until next sample) or linear. Types that cannot interpolate, or arrays of differing size, fall back to held.
Value clips supply time samples from other files, so one attribute can draw its animation from several clip files. Querying samples may open the clips.
Block removes all samples and authors a block so weaker layers contribute nothing; BlockAnimation removes only animated values and lets weaker defaults show.
Attributes can connect to source paths, which is how shading networks link. Connections are authored on the consumer and can be added, removed, set or cleared.

Backtick expressions with ${NAME} and fallbacks build asset paths and variant selections from expressionVariables stored on the root or session layer. Functions include if, and, or, not, eq, contains, at, len, matches_regex.

UsdCollectionAPI lists prims by includes and excludes with an expansionRule (expandPrims, expandPrimsAndProperties, explicitOnly), or by a path-pattern expression with globs, predicates and set operators.
capabilities.inputs: includes, excludes, includeRoot, expansionRule, membershipExpression, mode
capabilities.outputs: prim sets for linking and binding

capabilities.does: Sdf stores a scene as layers of prim, attribute, relationship and variant specs addressed by SdfPath. Value types range from scalars to matrices, quaternions, arrays and dictionaries.
Plugins register new metadata fields in plugInfo.json with a type, default, and the object kinds it applies to (layers, prims, properties, attributes, relationships, variants).
capabilities.inputs: SdfMetadata dictionary: type, default, appliesTo, displayGroup

capabilities.does: PcpCache computes layer stacks and prim indexes, caches results with their dependencies and errors, and reports change impact and namespace edits.
Ar resolves asset paths through a replaceable ArResolver, with a default search-path resolver, URI-scheme resolvers declared in plugInfo.json, thread-bound resolver contexts and scoped caches.
capabilities.outputs: resolved asset locations and readable assets

capabilities.does: UsdStage is the root object over a composition. UsdEditTarget maps scene paths to layer paths so edits land in the chosen layer, and UsdNotice reports content changes.
capabilities.inputs: UsdStage, UsdPrim, UsdAttribute, UsdRelationship, UsdEditTarget, UsdNotice

capabilities.does: Prim queries return active, loaded, defined, non-abstract children by default, with variants for all children and filtered descendants.
UsdShade has Material (bindable container), NodeGraph (nestable container), Shader (node) and typed Input and Output attributes joined by connections. A valid connection beats an authored value.
capabilities.inputs: UsdShadeMaterial, NodeGraph, Shader, ConnectableAPI, inputs:, outputs:surface

capabilities.does: MaterialBindingAPI binds a material to a prim by relationship or through a collection, and bindings inherit down the namespace. Renderers ignore binding if the API is not applied.
capabilities.inputs: material:binding, collection-based binding, binding strength, purpose

capabilities.does: UsdPreviewSurface is one preview shader for exchange, with specular and metallic workflows. It has no subsurface, anisotropy or cloth.
capabilities.inputs: diffuseColor, emissiveColor, useSpecularWorkflow, specularColor, metallic, roughness, clearcoat, clearcoatRoughness, opacity, opacityMode, opacityThreshold, ior, normal, displacement, occlusion

capabilities.does: The preview spec also defines UsdUVTexture, UsdPrimvarReader types (float, float2, float3, float4, int, string, normal, point, vector, matrix) and UsdTransform2d.
capabilities.inputs: UsdUVTexture: file, st, wrapS, wrapT, fallback, scale, bias, sourceColorSpace; UsdTransform2d: in, rotation, scale, translation

capabilities.does: The usdMtlx plugin reads .mtlx files as USD: nodes become Shaders, nodegraphs become NodeGraphs, materials become Materials, looks become variants, and collections become UsdCollectionAPI.
UsdLux gives DistantLight, DomeLight, DiskLight, RectLight, SphereLight, CylinderLight and PortalLight. LightAPI makes any prim a light, with power and colour attributes.
ShapingAPI sets focus, cone falloff and IES profile; ShadowAPI sets non-physical shadow controls; LightListAPI lists lights; light linking uses collections.
UsdSkel interchanges skinned meshes and joint animation with Skeleton, SkelRoot, SkelAnimation, BlendShape and BindingAPI, plus linear blend skinning and a geomBindTransform.
capabilities.inputs: Skeleton, SkelRoot, SkelAnimation, BlendShape, BindingAPI, GeomBindTransform, UsdSkelCache

capabilities.does: UsdPhysics adds PhysicsScene, RigidBodyAPI, CollisionAPI, MeshCollisionAPI (approximation such as convexHull), MassAPI and physics materials with friction and restitution.
capabilities.inputs: physics:rigidBodyEnabled, kinematicEnabled, startsAsleep, collisionEnabled, physics:mass, centerOfMass, density 1000 default, dynamicFriction, staticFriction, restitution

capabilities.does: Joint prims connect two bodies: fixed, revolute, prismatic, spherical, distance and generic D6 with per-axis limit and drive APIs. Collision groups and filtered pairs switch collisions off.
capabilities.inputs: physics:body0, body1, localPos, localRot, breakForce, breakTorque, minDistance, maxDistance, filteredGroups, filteredPairs, ArticulationRootAPI

capabilities.does: A Volume prim links to field prims through named relationships. OpenVDBAsset and Field3DAsset point at grid files by filePath, fieldName and fieldIndex; animation uses per-frame files.
UsdRender describes a render job: RenderSettings (resolution, pixelAspectRatio, aspectRatioConformPolicy, camera), RenderProduct outputs, RenderVar channels (AOVs) and RenderPass for multipass jobs.
capabilities.inputs: resolution, pixelAspectRatio, productName, sourceName, dataType, sourceType, orderedVars, passType

capabilities.does: UsdMedia holds a SpatialAudio prim placed in the transform hierarchy, plus AssetPreviewsAPI for thumbnails and AuthorshipAPI for recording who authored a prim.
USDZ is an uncompressed, unencrypted zip with each file at a 64-byte boundary and a native USD file first. It holds usd layers, png, jpeg, exr, avif images and m4a, mp3, wav audio.
Native text (usda), binary (usdc) and packaged (usdz) formats, with file-format plugins for others such as Alembic and MaterialX.

ColorSpaceAPI sets colorSpace:name on a prim, and a colorSpace metadata on an attribute overrides it. Tokens follow transfer_primaries_state, such as lin_ap1_scene or srgb_rec709_scene. Default is linear Rec.709. RenderSettings sets renderingColorSpace.
Hydra is the imaging framework that connects scene data to renderers. Storm is its rasteriser and hdPrman is the RenderMan renderer.
The core is C++ with Python bindings in the pxr package. A script creates a stage, defines prims with schema Define calls and saves the root layer. Bindings can be skipped at build time.
The toolset includes usdcat, usdview, usdedit, usddiff, usdrecord, usdresolve, usdtree, usdzip, usdchecker, usdstitch and usdGenSchema for schema generation.
The Alliance for OpenUSD, founded by Pixar, Adobe, Apple, Autodesk and NVIDIA under the Joint Development Foundation, is a non-profit that works on standardising and evolving OpenUSD.
The documentation index lists three specifications: the USD Core Specification, the UsdPreviewSurface specification and the Usdz file format specification.
Built on Linux, macOS and Windows (x64, ARM64). Libraries can be built for iOS and visionOS embedding and as WebAssembly static libraries, without command-line tools.

entries.name: MaterialX
entries.vendor: Academy Software Foundation (originated at Industrial Light & Magic)

licence.name: Apache-2.0

rea.notes: Specification markdown and code are public. Current library version v1.39.5 (22 May 2026) per materialx.org.

entries.verified: 2026-11-02, how: specification markdown, project site and repository page read via WebFetch

engines.name: Core document model
engines.does: Reads, writes and validates .mtlx documents made of nodedefs, nodegraphs, materials and looks.

engines.name: Standard and PBR node libraries
engines.does: Definitions for texture, procedural, math, compositing and physically based nodes, with reference implementations.

engines.name: MaterialXGenShader
engines.does: Turns a node graph into source code for a shading language through per-language generator classes.

engines.name: Viewer and Graph Editor
engines.does: Project tools that render a material with generated GLSL and edit node graphs.

capabilities.does: An .mtlx file has a materialx root with a required version, optional working colorspace (default data) and namespace. Other files are pulled in with xi:include, and older versions are upgraded on load.

A nodedef declares a node interface and outputs; a nodegraph holds connected node instances and can implement a nodedef. Instances set values through input elements and expose results through output elements.
capabilities.inputs: nodedef name/node/namespace, nodegraph, input name/type/value, output name/type/nodename

capabilities.does: typedef with member fields defines custom types; unittypedef, unitdef and unit define physical units with a multiplicative scale; geompropdef declares custom geometric properties.
capabilities.inputs: typedef semantic/context/inherit, member, unit scale, geompropdef space/index/uniform

capabilities.does: surfacematerial wraps shaders into a material. A look gathers materialassign elements, each binding a material to geometry named by a collection.
A colorspace attribute can sit on the root, on scopes or on single inputs, nearest declaration wins, and the value data means no conversion. fileprefix prepends a path to filename inputs in scope.
Texture source nodes: image, tiledimage, latlongimage, hextiledimage and triplanarprojection.
Procedural nodes produce patterns without images: constant, ramplr, ramptb, ramp4, splitlr, splittb, randomfloat and randomcolor.
Noise family: noise2d, noise3d, fractal2d, fractal3d, cellnoise2d, cellnoise3d, worleynoise2d, worleynoise3d, unifiednoise2d, unifiednoise3d, flake2d and flake3d.
Shape pattern nodes: checkerboard, line, circle, cloverleaf, hexagon, grid, crosshatch, tiledcircles, tiledcloverleafs and tiledhexagons.
Geometry query nodes: position, normal, tangent, bitangent, bump, texcoord, geomcolor, geompropvalue and geompropvalueuniform.

Math nodes cover arithmetic, trigonometry, vectors and matrices: add, subtract, multiply, divide, power, safepower, sin, cos, atan2, clamp, normalize, dotproduct, crossproduct, transformpoint, rotate3d, reflect, refract, place2d, normalmap and more.
Colour and value adjustment: contrast, remap, range, smoothstep, luminance, rgbtohsv, hsvtorgb, hsvadjust, saturate, colorcorrect.
Compositing nodes: premult, unpremult, plus, minus, difference, burn, dodge, screen, overlay, disjointover, in, mask, matte, out, over and mix.

Logical (and, or, xor, not), conditional (ifgreater, ifgreatereq, ifequal, switch) and channel nodes (convert, combine2 to 4, separate2 to 4, extract), plus convolution blur and heighttonormal, and time nodes frame and time.
The standard library also has shader-typed nodes surface_unlit, displacement and a shader-level mix.

BSDF nodes: oren_nayar_diffuse_bsdf, burley_diffuse_bsdf, translucent_bsdf, dielectric_bsdf, conductor_bsdf, generalized_schlick_bsdf, subsurface_bsdf, sheen_bsdf and chiang_hair_bsdf. Thin film is an option on the dielectric, conductor and schlick nodes.
capabilities.inputs: dielectric: tint, ior 1.5, roughness, thinfilm_thickness, scatter_mode; conductor: ior, extinction; sheen: color, roughness, mode

capabilities.does: EDF nodes uniform_edf, conical_edf (inner and outer angle) and measured_edf (file); VDF nodes absorption_vdf and anisotropic_vdf (absorption, scattering, anisotropy).
capabilities.inputs: color, inner_angle, outer_angle, file, absorption, scattering, anisotropy

capabilities.does: Shader nodes combine closures: surface (bsdf, edf, opacity, thin_walled), volume (vdf, edf) and light (edf, intensity, exposure).
capabilities.inputs: bsdf, edf, vdf, opacity, thin_walled, intensity, exposure

capabilities.does: Utility nodes layer, mix, add and multiply combine closures; roughness_anisotropy, roughness_dual and glossiness_anisotropy convert roughness forms; artistic_ior and blackbody derive optics and colour.
capabilities.inputs: top, base, fg, bg, mix, reflectivity, edge_color, temperature

capabilities.does: Autodesk Standard Surface (version 1.0.1) built from ten components with inputs for base, metalness, specular, transmission, subsurface, sheen, coat, thin film, emission and opacity.
capabilities.inputs: base, base_color, metalness, specular_roughness, specular_IOR, transmission, subsurface, sheen, coat, thin_film_thickness, emission, opacity, thin_walled

capabilities.does: The PBR document also defines UsdPreviewSurface as a node-graph composition with a specular workflow and a metalness workflow chosen by useSpecularWorkflow.
capabilities.inputs: diffuseColor, metallic, roughness, clearcoat, opacity, ior, normal

capabilities.does: The Khronos glTF PBR shader as a MaterialX graph, with inputs for transmission, specular, iridescence, sheen, clearcoat, emissive strength and anisotropy. The graph leaves out occlusion, thickness, attenuation and dispersion.
capabilities.inputs: base_color, metallic, roughness, transmission, iridescence, sheen_color, clearcoat, emissive_strength, anisotropy_strength

capabilities.does: OpenPBR Surface (version 1.1.2 in this document), maintained as a MaterialX subproject, has the largest interface of the four models.
capabilities.inputs: base_weight, specular_roughness, transmission_weight, subsurface_weight, fuzz_weight, coat_weight, thin_film_weight, emission_luminance, geometry_opacity

capabilities.does: MaterialXGenShader produces source text, not binaries, for one element and its upstream nodes. A ShaderGenerator subclass per language and a Syntax class handle language differences; a pixel stage is always present and hardware targets add a vertex stage.

A node can be implemented as an inline expression with {{input}} placeholders, a shading-language function linked by an implementation element, a nodegraph, or a C++ ShaderNodeImpl registered with registerImplementation().
The project lists generators for GLSL (including Vulkan GLSL), OSL, MDL, MSL, Slang, WGSL and an initial ESSL generator.
Translation graphs convert between shading models: Standard Surface to OpenPBR Surface and back, and Standard Surface to UsdPreviewSurface.

Python bindings use PyBind11 (Python 3.9 or later) and a javascript folder builds web bindings. The Viewer (MATERIALX_BUILD_VIEWER) renders generated GLSL; the Graph Editor (MATERIALX_BUILD_GRAPH_EDITOR) edits graphs.
The project lists support in OpenUSD, Houdini, Maya, 3ds Max, VRED, Arnold, RenderMan, V-Ray, OctaneRender, Unreal Engine, NVIDIA Omniverse and Apple platforms.

licence.name: Apache-2.0 per repository metadata (a page badge says CC BY-SA 4.0; the two conflict)

outcomes: standard production surface shader parameters shared across renderers

rea.notes: Specification v1.1.1 (2026-04-17) per the spec page; the first 200000 characters were read.

engines.name: Layered slab model
engines.does: Describes a surface as stacked layers: ambient medium, fuzz, coat, then a base made of metal and dielectric parts.

engines.name: MaterialX reference implementation
engines.does: A node-graph implementation of the model kept in the repository as open_pbr_surface.mtlx.

capabilities.does: Glossy-diffuse base: weight, colour and diffuse roughness control the dielectric diffuse lobe.
base_metalness blends between the dielectric base and a metal base, with weight 1 minus M on the dielectric; metal uses base colour as reflectance.
Specular reflection layer with colour, roughness, anisotropy and index of refraction.
capabilities.inputs: specular_weight default 1, specular_color (1,1,1), specular_roughness [0,1] default 0.3, specular_roughness_anisotropy [0,1] default 0, specular_ior default 1.5

capabilities.does: Translucent base for glass-like materials, with tint, absorption depth, scattering and dispersion set by Abbe number.
capabilities.inputs: transmission_weight, transmission_color, transmission_depth, transmission_scatter, transmission_scatter_anisotropy [-1,1], transmission_dispersion_scale [0,1], transmission_dispersion_abbe_number default 20

capabilities.does: Opaque base mix of glossy-diffuse and subsurface, with colour, radius, a per-channel radius scale and scattering anisotropy.
A fibre or dust layer on top of the coated base; low roughness gives a fabric sheen, high a dusty look.
A clear or tinted varnish layer over the base. Colour is the squared normal-incidence transmittance; darkening scales the loss from internal reflections.
capabilities.inputs: coat_weight, coat_color, coat_roughness, coat_roughness_anisotropy, coat_ior default 1.6, coat_darkening default 1

capabilities.does: Thin-film interference folded into the Fresnel terms of the metal and dielectric lobes. Thickness in micrometres.
capabilities.inputs: thin_film_weight default 0, thin_film_thickness default 0.5, thin_film_ior default 1.4

capabilities.does: Light emitted from beneath the coat, set as luminance in cd/m2 times a colour that may exceed 1.
geometry_opacity is a linear presence weight of the surface; in thin-walled mode it weights the wall.
geometry_thin_walled treats the surface as a two-sided sheet with no interior.
Separate shading normals for base and coat, and tangents that set the anisotropy direction on each layer.
Layering from outside in: ambient medium blended by opacity, fuzz, coat, then the base substrate (metal mixed with dielectric, dielectric mixed from opaque and translucent bases).

BSDFs must keep directional albedo at or below 1 (reflection plus transmission for transmissive ones). Layering scales albedo, and the page suggests multiple-scattering compensation such as Kulla-Conty or Turquin.

The repository holds the white paper, a parameter reference, and the MaterialX reference graph; third-party implementations include a WebGL pathtracer and Adobe's open-source BSDF. Repository metadata lists Apache-2.0.

rea.notes: Only the technical introduction page and repository page were read.

engines.name: EXR file format
engines.does: Specification of the scene-linear HDR image file with multi-part, multi-channel storage and open metadata.

engines.name: Reference implementation
engines.does: Library that reads and writes EXR files; licensed BSD-3-Clause.

engines.name: Imath
engines.does: Companion C++ library for 2D and 3D vectors, matrices and the 16-bit half float type, with optional Python bindings.

capabilities.does: Three pixel types: HALF (16-bit float, matches fp16), FLOAT (32-bit IEEE-754, for depth and other wide data) and UINT (32-bit integers for IDs).
capabilities.inputs: channel pixel type HALF, FLOAT, UINT

capabilities.does: Named channels each with a type and x and y sampling rates; R, G, B, A are predefined and alpha is premultiplied. Layers use dot-separated names such as light1.specular.R.
capabilities.inputs: channel name, pixel type, x and y sampling rates

capabilities.does: Channels may be sampled at a lower rate than the image, as with chroma, so data exists at only some pixel positions.
The display window sets the frame; the data window sets where pixels exist and may exceed the frame for blur padding or be smaller for partial renders.
Scanline files store rows that can be read in any order, sequential being fastest. They cannot hold multiple resolutions.
Tiled files split the image into fixed-size tiles that can be fetched in any order, enabling partial reads.
Tiled files can hold ONE_LEVEL, MIPMAP (each level half size in both dimensions to 1 by 1) or RIPMAP (independent power-of-two reduction per axis).
One file holds several parts, each with its own header, offset table and pixel data and a unique name. Part types: scanline, tiled, deep scanline, deep tile.
capabilities.outputs: one file for many render outputs

capabilities.does: Deep pixels hold a variable number of samples with reserved channels Z, ZBack, A, RA/GA/BA and id; volumetric samples have Z less than ZBack. Stored as deep scanline or deep tile parts.
Lossless codecs: PIZ, ZIPS, ZIP, RLE, ZSTD, HTJ2K32 and HTJ2K256, plus uncompressed storage.
Lossy codecs: PXR24, B44, B44A, DWAA, DWAB and LJ2K. PXR24, B44 and B44A are not allowed in deep files.
capabilities.outputs: smaller files for previews and delivery

capabilities.does: Required headers: windows, pixelAspectRatio, channels, compression, lineOrder, screen window values and tiles. Optional standard ones: colorInteropID, chromaticities, whiteLuminance, framesPerSecond, multiView, worldToCamera, worldToNDC, wrapmodes. Custom attributes are allowed.
colorInteropID and chromaticities are optional header attributes for colour encoding; the page says chromaticities are largely superseded. R, G, B channel names should be avoided for non-colour data.
Imath supplies the 16-bit half type and 2D and 3D vector and matrix classes used by the EXR library, with optional Python bindings.

entries.name: OpenColorIO (OCIO)

licence.name: BSD-3-Clause

rea.notes: Docs version latest, newest release listed OCIO 2.6; release notes cited are 2.4.

entries.verified: 2026-11-02, how: API and guide pages read via WebFetch

engines.name: Config
engines.does: Loads, edits and validates the YAML colour configuration: colour spaces, roles, displays, views, looks, rules.

engines.name: Processor
engines.does: Compiles a colour conversion into an optimisable operation list that runs on CPU or GPU.

engines.name: GPU shader generator
engines.does: Emits shader text and LUT textures for a processor in several shading languages.

engines.name: Transform library
engines.does: Building blocks such as matrices, LUTs, CDL, grading, exposure-contrast and fixed functions.

capabilities.does: A config is a YAML file, usually config.ocio, with a required ocio_profile_version of 1 or 2. The page advises generating it through the API and checking hand edits with ociocheck.
Roles give task names to colour spaces, for example scene_linear, reference or data, so applications run transforms without the user picking a space.

Colour spaces are declared for scene-referred and display-referred encodings. inactive_colorspaces hides spaces from menus but keeps them usable; OCIO_INACTIVE_COLORSPACES overrides it. family_separator builds hierarchical menus.
Displays and their views define how colour spaces are viewed. A config can list defaults, and the API adds, removes and queries display-view pairs.
Looks are named transforms for creative adjustment, managed through the config.
Named transforms have no fixed relationship to a reference space, such as a utility curve.
An environment section declares context variables with defaults; search_path lists directories for LUT files and may use variables such as $SHOT.
File rules map file paths to colour spaces and viewing rules limit which views apply, to give sensible application defaults.
Views can be shared between displays, and a virtual display holds views that apply to any display.
Built-in CG and Studio configs based on ACES 1.3 ship with the library and load by URI, for example ocio://default, ocio://cg-config-latest and ocio://studio-config-latest.
Release 2.4 previews ACES 2.0 with new fixed functions for output transform, RGB to JMh, tonescale compression and gamut compression, and 31 ACES 2 output view transforms.
ColorSpaceTransform converts between two named colour spaces; DisplayViewTransform applies a display and view, with optional bypass of looks and data spaces.
capabilities.inputs: src, dst, direction, dataBypass; display, view, looksBypass

capabilities.does: CDLTransform applies ASC slope, offset, power and saturation (styles CDL_ASC, CDL_NO_CLAMP). ExponentTransform and ExponentWithLinearTransform apply power curves, the latter with a linear toe as in sRGB.
capabilities.inputs: slope, offset, power, saturation; gamma, offset, negativeStyle

capabilities.does: ExposureContrastTransform applies exposure, contrast and gamma around a pivot for linear, log or video encodings, with dynamic parameters.
capabilities.inputs: exposure, contrast, gamma, pivot, logExposureStep, logMidGray

capabilities.does: GradingPrimaryTransform offers linear, log and video styles with brightness, contrast, gamma, offset, exposure, lift, gain, saturation, pivots and clamps. Only one grading transform per config can be dynamic.
GradingRGBCurveTransform fits monotonic B-spline curves per red, green and blue channel followed by a master curve; linear style units are stops relative to 0.18.
capabilities.inputs: x and y control points, slopes, setBypassLinToLog

capabilities.does: FixedFunctionTransform styles include ACES red modifier, glow, dark-to-dim, gamut maps and compression, Rec.2100 surround, RGB to HSV, XYZ to xyY, uvY and LUV, linear to PQ, gamma-log and double-log.
GpuShaderDesc generates shader code plus 1D, 2D and 3D LUT textures and uniforms from a processor. Names and prefixes are configurable so several processors can coexist.
capabilities.inputs: setLanguage, setFunctionName, setPixelName, setResourcePrefix, add3DTexture, addUniform, getUniformBufferSize

capabilities.does: Supported shader targets: Cg, GLSL 1.2, 1.3, 4.0, Vulkan 4.6, ES 1.0 and ES 3.0, HLSL DX11, MSL 2.0 and OSL.
CPUProcessor applies a conversion to image buffers or lists of floats; bit depths must match for RGB and RGBA buffers. The Python API releases the GIL while processing.
getOptimizedProcessor with OptimizationFlags merges and cancels operations, from OPTIMIZATION_NONE up to OPTIMIZATION_ALL, with presets lossless, very good, good and draft.
Dynamic properties (exposure, contrast, grading values) can change after a processor or shader is built. CPU and GPU processors keep independent copies.
Interpolation modes: nearest, linear, tetrahedral, cubic, default and best. Bit depths: UINT8, 10, 12, 14, 16, 32 and F16, F32.
The Config API creates configs from file, environment, stream, built-in name or as a raw config, validates, upgrades and serialises them.
Katana, Mari, Nuke, Maya, Houdini and Silhouette FX use OCIO. The project aims at Linux, macOS and Windows, and the repository holds Python packaging files.

engines.name: Abc and AbcCoreAbstract
engines.does: Object, property and time-sampling model that all schemas build on.

engines.name: AbcCoreOgawa, AbcCoreHDF5, AbcCoreFactory, AbcCoreLayer
engines.does: Storage back ends for Ogawa and HDF5 archives, a factory that picks one, and a layering core.

engines.name: AbcGeom, AbcCollection, AbcMaterial
engines.does: Geometry schemas plus collection and material schemas.

capabilities.does: Alembic stores computed results such as animated vertex positions and transforms, application-independent, and not the procedural graph that made them. Typical uses are lighting handoff and simulation input.
The library tree has separate Ogawa and HDF5 storage cores, a factory core that opens either, and a layer core. HDF5 1.8.9 is an optional build dependency.
AbcGeom provides input and output classes for PolyMesh, SubD, Curves, Points, NuPatch, Xform, Camera, Light and FaceSet.
capabilities.inputs: OPolyMesh/IPolyMesh, OSubD/ISubD, OCurves/ICurves, OPoints/IPoints, ONuPatch/INuPatch, OXform/IXform, OCamera/ICamera, OLight/ILight, OFaceSet/IFaceSet

capabilities.does: Each geometry parameter has a scope: constant, uniform (per face or patch), varying, vertex or face-varying, the same idea as RenderMan primitive variable classes. Stored in metadata key geoScope.
TimeSampling records the times of written samples as uniform, cyclic or acyclic, and finds the floor, ceiling or nearest sample for a time.
capabilities.outputs: animated properties on their own clocks

capabilities.does: Transform samples are built from XformOp entries, and cameras add film-back transform ops alongside the camera sample.
Headers for per-object visibility and archive bounds let a reader skip hidden objects and size the scene.
Additional modules hold collection schemas and material schemas.
Optional Python bindings are built with Boost and PyImath when USE_PYALEMBIC is on. The documentation links an introduction to PyAlembic.

entries.name: OpenVDB
entries.vendor: Academy Software Foundation (originated at DreamWorks Animation)

licence.name: Apache-2.0 (relicensed from MPL-2.0 per the repository README)

rea.notes: Docs version 14.0.0. Several tool header pages only gave file-level summaries, so tool parameters are limited to what they showed.

entries.verified: 2026-11-02, how: Doxygen pages and repository README read via WebFetch; entry url not opened in this sweep (official domain, unchecked)

engines.name: OpenVDB core
engines.does: Tree, transform and grid classes plus the tools library for sparse volumes.

engines.name: OpenVDB Points
engines.does: Point data stored in VDB trees with attributes.

engines.name: OpenVDB AX
engines.does: Expression language for volume and point processing, built with OPENVDB_BUILD_AX.

engines.name: NanoVDB
engines.does: Static-topology, pointer-less VDB for GPU and CPU rendering.

capabilities.does: A tree of RootNode, InternalNode and LeafNode levels stores voxel values far more compactly than a dense array. The standard 5-4-3 layout gives 8 by 8 by 8 leaves, then 16 and 32 cubed internal levels.
Values are voxel, tile or background; each voxel or tile is active or inactive. prune merges uniform regions into tiles without changing the volume.
A Transform maps index space to world space and back, with a Map giving local derivatives. Grids can share trees and transforms.
setGridClass marks a grid as level set (signed distance in a narrow band), fog volume (values 0 to 1) or staggered velocity, which changes how tools such as divergence behave.
Vector grids carry a type (invariant, covariant, contravariant) and a world-space flag, so transformVectors can apply a transform to the values correctly.

ValueAccessor caches tree traversal for coherent reads and writes; ValueAccessorRW is thread-safe. Iterators are named by constness and on, off or all (for example Tree::ValueOnCIter) and end with test().
Multi-grid files select grids by name, with ordinal suffixes for duplicates. Float grids can be saved as half floats, and io::File reads bounding box, voxel count and memory statistics cheaply.
capabilities.inputs: save float as half, grid name

capabilities.does: Interpolators sample grids in index or world space: PointSampler, BoxSampler, QuadraticSampler, staggered variants, GridSampler and DualGridSampler for source-to-target lookup.
GridTransformer resamples a grid into another transform with a chosen sampler; foreach, transformValues and changeBackground rewrite values in place.
CSG on level sets: union, intersection and difference. createLevelSetSphere and signedFloodFill help build and repair level sets.
compMax, compMin, compSum and compMul combine grids voxel by voxel; Tree::combine, combineExtended and combine2 take custom functions.

meshToLevelSet, meshToSignedDistanceField and meshToUnsignedDistanceField convert triangle and quad meshes into distance fields with separate exterior and interior band widths. Closed surfaces are needed; self-intersections are tolerated.
capabilities.inputs: points, triangles, quads, exterior and interior band width, conversion flags

capabilities.does: volumeToMesh extracts an isosurface from a scalar grid, as quads only, or adaptively as triangles and quads.
LevelSetFilter applies smoothing such as Laplacian flow, mean-value filtering and morphological opening to narrow-band level sets, optionally masked by a scalar alpha grid.
LevelSetAdvection moves narrow-band level sets through an external velocity field by hyperbolic advection.
VDB points functions create point data grids, populate attributes, compute a voxel size, move points with a deformer and advect them through a velocity grid.
capabilities.inputs: points::createPointDataGrid, computeVoxelSize, populateAttribute, movePoints, advectPoints, tools::createPointIndexGrid

capabilities.does: NanoVDB is a standalone static-topology VDB in one contiguous, pointer-less block. Values can change but topology cannot. Tested with CUDA, OpenCL, OpenGL, DirectX 12, OptiX, Vulkan, HLSL and GLSL.
The repository holds OpenVDB AX, a Houdini plugin, a Maya plugin, command-line tools in openvdb_cmd and a Python module. It builds with CMake on Linux, macOS and Windows with TBB.

engines.name: FBX SDK (C++)
engines.does: Autodesk library for building plug-ins, converters and applications that translate and exchange 3D assets through FBX.

capabilities.does: A free C++ SDK for writing plug-ins, converters and applications that translate and exchange 3D assets with FBX technology. Version 2020.3.11 is listed on the page.
capabilities.outputs: FBX import and export in custom tools

capabilities.does: A Python FBX SDK and Python bindings are offered as separate downloads next to the C++ SDK.
The SDK is published for Windows, macOS, iOS and Linux.
FBX files exist in binary and ASCII forms, and the SDK reads and writes both. The ASCII form is a tree of named identifiers.
The original object-based model, from Kaydara in 1996, covers motion, 2D, 3D, audio and video data, and is owned by Autodesk since 2006.
The FBX Extensions SDK exposes a description of the format through header files, since neither FBX form has an official public specification.
Open readers exist without the SDK: a Blender Python script, Godot importers (Assimp, a rewritten importer, an FBX2glTF fork, ufbx from 4.3) and a Java library in Field.

entries.name: 3MF (3D Manufacturing Format)

licence.name: Specifications listed as royalty-free; no licence name on the page

rea.notes: Specification table on 3mf.io page was embedded as encoded markup; versions and dates there are from a fetch model decoding and should be rechecked. Core 1.4.0 is listed as ISO/IEC 25422:2025.

entries.verified: 2026-11-02, how: specification page and GitHub specification markdown read via WebFetch

engines.name: Core package
engines.does: ZIP package (Open Packaging Conventions) with a 3D model XML part, relationships and optional thumbnails.

engines.name: Extensions
engines.does: Namespaced XML extensions for materials, production, slices, beam lattices and others, declared as required or recommended on the model.

capabilities.does: A 3MF file is an OPC package stored as a ZIP. A StartPart relationship points to the 3D model part, and other parts hold print tickets, textures, thumbnails and signatures.

The model element holds metadata, resources and a build. Resources are objects with a mesh or components; build items name the objects to output, each with an optional transform. Unit default is millimeter.
capabilities.inputs: unit (micron, millimeter, centimeter, inch, foot, meter), object id/type/name/partnumber, item objectid/transform

capabilities.does: Meshes are vertex lists with x, y, z and triangle lists with v1, v2, v3 and optional property indices p1, p2, p3 and pid.
capabilities.inputs: vertex x y z, triangle v1 v2 v3 p1 p2 p3 pid

capabilities.does: Composite objects reference other objects through component elements with objectid and a transform written as 12 values of a row-major affine matrix.

Objects carry a type: model, solidsupport, support, surface or other. Metadata names include Title, Designer, Description, Copyright, LicenseTerms, Rating, CreationDate, ModificationDate and Application.
Extensions are XML namespaces on the model. requiredextensions must be supported or the file is not processed; recommendedextensions should trigger a warning; unknown elements are ignored.
basematerials give named colours; colorgroup lists per-vertex colours by index. Core and the Materials extension both use pid and pindex to point triangles at them.
texture2d references a JPEG or PNG with tile styles (wrap, mirror, clamp, none) and a filter (auto, linear, nearest). texture2dgroup lists u, v coordinates for triangles.
capabilities.inputs: texture2d path/contenttype/tilestyleu/tilestylev/filter, texture2dgroup texid, tex2coord u v

capabilities.does: compositematerials mix base materials by ratios that are normalised. multiproperties stack several property groups per triangle with mix or multiply blending in linear RGB.
The Production extension adds RFC 4122 UUIDs to build, items, objects and components so parts can be tracked across jobs and devices.
A path attribute on items and components lets the root model reference objects stored in other model files, to cut parsing cost in large builds.
pa:alternatives list substitute versions of an object in priority order: fullres for printing, lowres for visualisation, obfuscated to hide sensitive areas. A production printer rejects lowres only.

The Slice extension stores print-ready 2D layers. A slicestack holds slices with ztop heights, each made of vertices and polygons built from segments; meshresolution says whether the mesh could regenerate the slices.
capabilities.inputs: slicestackid, zbottom, ztop, startv, segment v2/p1/p2/pid, meshresolution

capabilities.does: The Beam Lattice extension describes lattices as beams between mesh vertices with radii, end caps (sphere, hemisphere, butt) and optional balls, clipped against a clipping mesh.
capabilities.inputs: beamlattice minlength/radius/ballmode/ballradius/clippingmode/clippingmesh/representationmesh, beam v1 v2 r1 r2 cap1 cap2

capabilities.does: Balls sit at beam ends with their own radius and properties; beamsets give names and identifiers to groups of beams and balls for organisation only.
capabilities.inputs: ball vindex/r/p/pid, beamset name/identifier, ref index

capabilities.does: The specification page also lists Boolean Operations (v1.1.1), Displacement (v1.0.0), Secure Content (encryption, v1.0.2), Toolpath (v1.0.0) and Volumetric (voxel and implicit data, v1.0.0) extensions, all royalty-free.

entries.name: VRM (avatar format on glTF)

licence.name: Repository licence not shown on the pages read; VRM 1.0 models carry the VRM Public License URL in meta.licenseUrl

outcomes: humanoid avatars for VR and streaming

rea.notes: VRMC_vrm_animation, VRMC_springBone_limit, VRMC_springBone_extended_collider and VRMC_materials_hdr_emissiveMultiplier folders exist but were not opened.
