engines.name: VRMC_vrm
engines.does: Core extension: model metadata, humanoid mapping, expressions, look-at and first-person settings.

engines.name: VRMC_springBone
engines.does: Secondary-motion definition for hair and cloth chains with colliders.

engines.name: VRMC_node_constraint
engines.does: Roll, aim and rotation constraints between glTF nodes.

engines.name: VRMC_materials_mtoon
engines.does: Toon shading material extension.

capabilities.does: Metadata records name, version, authors, copyright, references, thumbnail and a licence URL, plus usage rights: avatar permission, commercial use, violent, sexual, political and hate use, credit, redistribution and modification.
capabilities.inputs: name, authors, licenseUrl, avatarPermission (onlyAuthor default), commercialUsage (personalNonProfit default), creditNotation, allowRedistribution false, modification (prohibited default)

capabilities.does: Maps glTF nodes to named humanoid bones under humanoid.humanBones, each bone once. Required: hips, spine, head, upper and lower legs and feet, upper and lower arms and hands on both sides; fingers, eyes, jaw, toes and shoulders are optional.

Facial expressions are presets: happy, angry, sad, relaxed, surprised; lip shapes aa, ih, ou, ee, oh; blink, blinkLeft, blinkRight; lookUp, lookDown, lookLeft, lookRight; neutral. Custom ones live in expressions.custom.

An expression drives morph targets (node, index, weight), material colour changes (colour, emission, shade, matcap, rim, outline) and texture transforms (scale, offset). isBinary snaps values above 0.5 to 1.
capabilities.inputs: morphTargetBinds node/index/weight, materialColorBinds material/type/targetValue, textureTransformBinds material/scale/offset, isBinary

capabilities.does: overrideMouth, overrideBlink and overrideLookAt each take none, block or blend, so one expression can suppress or mix with lip sync, blinking or gaze.
Gaze drives either eye bones or lookUp, lookDown, lookLeft, lookRight expressions. Range maps clamp the angle at inputMaxValue degrees and scale output by outputScale.
capabilities.inputs: type bone/expression, offsetFromHeadBone, rangeMapHorizontalInner, rangeMapHorizontalOuter, rangeMapVerticalDown, rangeMapVerticalUp (inputMaxValue, outputScale)

capabilities.does: meshAnnotations tag meshes as auto, both, thirdPersonOnly or firstPersonOnly for the VR camera. auto splits a mesh by head-bone weights and hides the head part from the first-person view.

Spring chains simulate hair and cloth. Each head-tail joint pair uses verlet integration with inertia, stiffness and gravity, the tail kept to bone length. Joints set hitRadius, stiffness, gravityPower, gravityDir and dragForce.
Sphere and capsule colliders attach to nodes (offset, radius, tail) and are grouped into colliderGroups that a spring references. The tail is pushed out by collider radius plus hitRadius.

VRMC_node_constraint offers roll (twist about X, Y or Z), aim (point an axis at a source) and rotation (copy the source rotation), each with source and weight from 0 to 1. Circular dependencies are an error.
capabilities.inputs: roll source/rollAxis/weight, aim source/aimAxis/weight, rotation source/weight

capabilities.does: MToon shades with a lit colour and a shade colour blended across a boundary, set by a shift, a toony width and GI equalisation.
capabilities.inputs: shadeColorFactor [0,0,0], shadeMultiplyTexture, shadingShiftFactor 0, shadingShiftTexture, shadingToonyFactor 0.9, giEqualizationFactor 0.9

capabilities.does: Matcap texture is added to lighting, and a parametric rim light has colour, mask, lighting mix, Fresnel power and lift.
capabilities.inputs: matcapFactor, matcapTexture, parametricRimColorFactor, rimMultiplyTexture, rimLightingMixFactor 1, parametricRimFresnelPowerFactor 5, parametricRimLiftFactor 0

capabilities.does: Outlines are drawn in world units or as a ratio of screen height, with a mask texture on the G channel, colour and a lighting mix.
capabilities.inputs: outlineWidthMode none/worldCoordinates/screenCoordinates, outlineWidthFactor 0, outlineWidthMultiplyTexture, outlineColorFactor, outlineLightingMixFactor 1

capabilities.does: UV scroll and rotation animate with constant speeds, and transparent materials choose depth writes and a render-queue offset for draw order.
capabilities.inputs: uvAnimationScrollXSpeedFactor, uvAnimationScrollYSpeedFactor, uvAnimationRotationSpeedFactor, transparentWithZWrite false, renderQueueOffsetNumber 0

capabilities.does: Recommended runtime order is look-at, expressions, node constraints, then spring bones. The repository also has spec folders for HDR emissive multiplier, spring bone limits and extended colliders, and VRM animation.

entries.name: KTX 2.0 and Basis Universal

licence.name: Basis Universal: Apache-2.0 (repository page); KTX 2.0 specification: Khronos, licence not read

outcomes: one file transcoded to many GPU formats

rea.notes: KTX spec page read to its first 100000 of 291438 characters.

entries.verified: 2026-11-02, how: KTX specification (first part) and Basis Universal repository page read via WebFetch

engines.name: KTX 2.0 container
engines.does: Khronos file format for GPU textures with a data format descriptor, level index and optional supercompression.

engines.name: Basis Universal encoder
engines.does: Compresses images into ETC1S, UASTC, ASTC and related codecs, written to .KTX2 or .basis.

engines.name: Basis Universal transcoder
engines.does: Converts the stored codec data into the GPU format a device supports; also built for WebAssembly.

capabilities.does: The header holds vkFormat (0 for universal formats), typeSize, pixel width, height and depth, layer, face and level counts, and the supercompression scheme. A 12-byte identifier catches transfer damage.
capabilities.inputs: vkFormat, typeSize, pixelWidth/Height/Depth, layerCount, faceCount, levelCount, supercompressionScheme

capabilities.does: The Data Format Descriptor states texel block layout, colour model, primaries and transfer function, and must match vkFormat when that is defined.
Sorted key-value pairs add metadata; KTXorientation gives axis direction such as rd, KTXswizzle remaps channels with r, g, b, a, 0 and 1, and KTXwriter names the tool.
Per-level supercompression schemes: none, BasisLZ for ETC1S universal textures, Zstandard and ZLIB. Each level is compressed alone so streaming and random access work.
Dimensions and counts define 1D, 2D and 3D textures, cube maps, arrays of each and cube map arrays.
Mip levels are stored from smallest to largest so small levels can arrive first. levelCount 0 tells a loader to generate mips; partial chains are allowed.
ETC1S is the low-to-medium quality, high compression codec, based on a subset of ETC1, stored with BasisLZ in KTX 2.
UASTC LDR 4x4 is an 8 bits-per-pixel high-quality LDR format, with optional rate-distortion optimisation.
HDR codecs: UASTC HDR 4x4 (standard ASTC data, fast transcode to BC6H), ASTC HDR 6x6 at about 3.56 bpp, and UASTC HDR 6x6 Intermediate.

Standard ASTC LDR in all 14 block sizes from 4x4 to 12x12, a supercompressed XUASTC LDR using weight-grid DCT and adaptive deblocking, and XUBC7, a supercompressed BC7. XUASTC in KTX2 is still being standardised with Khronos.
LDR targets: ASTC, BC1 to BC7, ETC1, ETC2, PVRTC1, PVRTC2, ATC, FXT1 and uncompressed 8888, 565 and 4444. HDR targets: ASTC HDR, BC6H and RGB_16F, RGBA_16F, RGB_9E5.
basisu options: -quality 1 to 100, -effort 0 to 10 (default 3), -mipmap, -linear for normal maps and other non-sRGB data, -no_multithreading. Reads PNG, QOI, TGA, JPEG, DDS, EXR and HDR input.

Encoder and transcoder compile to WebAssembly via Emscripten, with a JavaScript wrapper for WASM threading and WASM64; the CLI also runs under WASI and unpacks .KTX2 and .basis files. Python bindings exist. Licence Apache 2.0.

entries.name: Draco

licence.name: Apache-2.0

rea.notes: Only compression_shared.h and encode.h were read from source; draft bitstream spec not opened.

entries.verified: 2026-11-02, how: repository page and two headers read via WebFetch

engines.name: Encoder
engines.does: Compresses a mesh or point cloud into a buffer using per-attribute-type settings; ExpertEncoder allows per-attribute settings.

engines.name: Decoder and JavaScript decoder
engines.does: Restores geometry from Draco data, with WASM and JavaScript builds hosted for web use.

engines.name: Transcoder
engines.does: Adds Draco compression to glTF assets; built only when DRACO_TRANSCODER_SUPPORTED is on.

capabilities.does: Open-source library that compresses and decompresses triangle meshes and point clouds to cut storage and transfer size. Geometry types are point cloud and triangular mesh.
Meshes encode either sequentially or with Edgebreaker; SetEncodingMethod forces a choice and the encode call fails if the method does not suit the input.
Edgebreaker connectivity can use the standard or the valence coder (predictive is deprecated).
Point clouds encode sequentially or with a KD-tree.
SetAttributeQuantization(type, bits) quantizes all attributes of one type inside a box sized to their maximum extent. SetAttributeExplicitQuantization uses a chosen origin and range instead.
capabilities.inputs: quantization_bits per attribute type, num_dims, origin, range

capabilities.does: draco_encoder reads OBJ, STL or PLY. -qp sets position quantization bits (default 11), -cl sets compression level 0 to 10 (default 7), -point_cloud ignores connectivity.
SetSpeedOptions(encoding_speed, decoding_speed) takes 0 (slowest, best compression) to 10 (fastest, worst); the faster of the two limits which features the encoder uses.

Attribute values are predicted from neighbours before coding. Schemes include difference, parallelogram, multi-parallelogram, constrained multi-parallelogram, portable texture-coordinate and geometric-normal prediction. The encoder picks by default.
Attributes use a generic, integer, quantization or normals sequential encoder, with delta, wrap or octahedron-based prediction transforms for normals.
The changelog gave older defaults: texture coordinates 10 bits, normals 8, colour 8, generic 8; the page warns they may have changed since.
Constants show mesh bitstream version 2.2 and point cloud bitstream version 2.3.
draco_decoder writes OBJ, STL or PLY; draco_transcoder compresses glTF assets; WASM and JavaScript decoders and Unity and Maya plugin builds are provided. Licence Apache-2.0, version 1.5.9 listed.

engines.does: Companion single-header library for clustered continuous level of detail.

capabilities.does: Builds an index buffer from duplicate vertices: meshopt_generateVertexRemap for binary-equal vertices, a custom variant with a comparison callback, and a multi-stream variant; remapIndexBuffer and remapVertexBuffer apply the table.
Reorders triangles for GPU vertex cache locality. A FIFO variant targets fixed caches (size 16 suggested) and runs about twice as fast; a strip variant trades vertex efficiency for smaller indices.
Reorders triangles to cut overdraw, allowing a bounded loss in cache hit ratio set by a threshold.
capabilities.inputs: meshopt_optimizeOverdraw threshold (1.05 allows 5% worse cache hits)

capabilities.does: Reorders vertex data for memory locality in the order triangles use it, with a remap variant for multiple streams.
Convert floats to compact forms: unorm, snorm and half-float, with half dequantisation, and quantizeFloat to zero low mantissa bits ahead of compression.
Builds a depth-only index buffer, and filters degenerate and duplicate triangles from an index buffer.
Lossless compression of triangle lists, with a sequence variant for strips and line lists and version pinning.
Lossless vertex buffer compression with a level control and a version setting, made for fast decoding.
Optional filters before the codec: octahedral for normals, quaternion for rotations, exponential for floats (four modes: separate, shared vector, shared component, clamped) and a colour filter.

meshopt_simplify reduces a triangle mesh to a target index count within a target error. Options lock borders, allow sparse subsets, use absolute error or prune small components; permissive, regularize and preserve-folds options also exist.
meshopt_simplifyWithAttributes weighs vertex attributes and honours a per-vertex lock; simplifyWithUpdate also updates positions and attributes; simplifyScale gives the error scale.

meshopt_simplifySloppy ignores topology and may merge nearby disjoint parts at lower quality; meshopt_simplifyPoints thins point clouds, with a colour weight; meshopt_simplifyPrune removes small disconnected parts.
Builds meshlets for mesh shading: buildMeshlets (max_vertices, max_triangles, cone_weight) plus scan, flex and spatial builders (the spatial one aimed at ray tracing), optimiser and culling bounds.
capabilities.inputs: meshopt_buildMeshlets, _Scan, _Flex min_triangles/split_factor, _Spatial fill_weight, meshopt_buildMeshletsBound, meshopt_optimizeMeshlet, meshopt_computeMeshletBounds

capabilities.does: Cluster tools: spatial clustering of point clouds, partitioning clusters into groups, cluster-relative position exponents, and a meshlet codec.
spatialSortRemap orders points along a spatial curve for better compression; an experimental remesh builds a new mesh at a chosen resolution from 4 to 256.
Analyzers report vertex cache ACMR and ATVR, vertex fetch overfetch, overdraw and coverage, to measure whether optimisation helped.
Converts triangle lists to strips with a restart index.

gltfpack -c writes EXT_meshopt_compression, -cc adds extra compression for gzip delivery, -cz or -ce khr uses KHR_meshopt_compression, -cf adds uncompressed fallback buffers for browsers without WebAssembly.
gltfpack -tc converts textures to KTX2 with Basis Universal (needs KHR_texture_basisu), -tp adds a WebGL 1 compatibility mode, -tw converts to WebP (EXT_texture_webp).

gltfpack -si R simplifies meshes to ratio R from 0 to 1 and prunes point clouds for even density. Quantisation uses KHR_mesh_quantization by default; -vpf keeps float positions, -noq disables quantisation, -vtf disables texture transform use.

gltfpack -kn keeps named nodes and meshes, -km keeps named materials, -ke keeps extras, and -mi creates instancing through EXT_mesh_gpu_instancing. Unknown vendor extensions and unknown vertex attributes are dropped, apart from a few kept names.

gltfpack reads ASCII or binary PLY Gaussian splat data and writes KHR_gaussian_splatting. Bit options -vp, -vt, -vn, -vc set position, scale, rotation and SH precision; -gsd N sets the spherical-harmonic degree kept (default drops degree 3).

entries.name: Wavefront OBJ and MTL

licence.name: Informal public format; no licence text read

rea.notes: Capabilities come from the Wikipedia article only; no vendor specification was opened.

entries.verified: 2026-11-02, how: Wikipedia article read via WebFetch (secondary source)

capabilities.does: Text format with # comments: v vertices (optional w, default 1.0), vt texture coordinates, vn normals, vp parameter-space points, f faces as v/vt/vn lists starting at 1 (negative indices count from the end), l polylines.
capabilities.inputs: v, vt, vn, vp, f, l

capabilities.does: o and g name objects and groups, s sets smoothing groups, mtllib links a material file and usemtl applies a named material to following faces.
The format can describe higher-order surfaces such as B-splines, though support in third-party tools varies.
MTL files start each material with newmtl and set ambient Ka, diffuse Kd, specular Ks, exponent Ns, transparency d or Tr, transmission colour Tf, optical density Ni and an illum model number 0 to 10.
capabilities.inputs: newmtl, Ka, Kd, Ks, Ns, d, Tr, Tf, Ni, illum

capabilities.does: Texture maps are map_Kd, map_Ka, map_Ks, map_Ns, map_d, map_bump or bump, disp and decal, with options such as -s, -o and -imfchan.

Informal PBR extensions adopted by Blender and TinyObjLoader add Pr and Pm for roughness and metallic, Ps sheen, Pc and Pcr clearcoat, Ke emissive, aniso, anisor and norm; DirectXMesh adds map_RMA and map_ORM.
capabilities.inputs: Pr, Pm, Ps, Pc, Pcr, Ke, aniso, anisor, norm, map_Pr, map_Pm, map_Ke

capabilities.does: No animation, deformation or mesh hierarchy, and no units; scale can only be noted in a comment.

entries.name: STL (stereolithography file format)

licence.name: Informal public format; no licence text read

rea.notes: Capabilities come from the Wikipedia article only.

entries.verified: 2026-11-02, how: Wikipedia article read via WebFetch (secondary source)

capabilities.does: Stores only surface geometry as triangles, each with a normal and three vertices in Cartesian coordinates. Developed in 1987 by 3D Systems for stereolithography; used for printing, prototyping and CAM.
ASCII files begin with solid and an optional name, then facet normal blocks with outer loop, three vertex lines, endloop and endfacet, ending with endsolid. Numbers use scientific notation.
capabilities.inputs: solid, facet normal, outer loop, vertex, endsolid

capabilities.does: Binary files have an 80-byte header, a 4-byte little-endian triangle count, then 50 bytes per triangle: twelve 32-bit floats and a 2-byte attribute count, usually zero. The header should not start with the word solid.
capabilities.inputs: 80-byte header, uint32 count, 50 bytes per triangle

capabilities.does: Normals should point outward and many readers accept zero and recompute them from vertex order (right-hand rule). No scale is stored, so the importer asks for units, usually millimetres or inches.

Non-standard colour: VisCAM and SolidView use the attribute field for 15-bit RGB; Materialise Magics stores overall RGBA in the header and per-facet colour in the attribute field. The two schemes clash.
Standard STL stores no colour, texture or CAD attributes, discards connectivity, only approximates curves and does not enforce a closed manifold surface.
capabilities.outputs: print-ready only if the mesh is closed

entries.name: PLY (Polygon File Format, Stanford Triangle Format)

licence.name: Informal public format; no licence text read

rea.notes: Capabilities come from the Wikipedia article only; Gaussian splat use is documented in the gltfpack README, not here.

entries.verified: 2026-11-02, how: Wikipedia article read via WebFetch (secondary source)

capabilities.does: Also called Stanford Triangle Format, made for 3D scanner output. Describes one object as mostly flat polygons with colour, transparency, normals, texture coordinates and confidence values, with separate front and back properties.
An ASCII header starts with ply, gives format ascii 1.0, binary_little_endian 1.0 or binary_big_endian 1.0, then comment, element and property lines, ending with end_header.
capabilities.inputs: ply, format, comment, element, property, end_header

capabilities.does: Property types are char, uchar, short, ushort, int, uint, float, double, or the sized names int8 to uint32, float32, float64. A list property stores a count followed by that many values.

Typical elements are vertex (position plus optional normals, colours, texture coordinates) and face (a list of vertex indices; vertex_indices is more common than vertex_index). Edges, range map samples and triangle strips are possible.

entries.name: WebGL 2.0

licence.name: Khronos open standard (API specification); the spec copyright text was not read

engines.name: WebGL2RenderingContext
engines.does: The JavaScript context object, created with getContext('webgl2'), that carries the whole GLSL ES 3.00 draw pipeline: buffers, textures, framebuffers, queries, sync and transform feedback.

engines.name: WebGL extension registry
engines.does: A numbered list of optional features grouped by status: ratified, community approved, draft, proposed and rejected. Pages are read through getExtension().

capabilities.does: Vertex and fragment shaders in GLSL ES 3.00. The context reports a WebGL GLSL ES 3.00 version string, adds unsigned-integer uniform setters, and getFragDataLocation returns the colour number bound to a fragment output.
capabilities.outputs: linked programs that can write several fragment outputs

capabilities.does: Sized internal formats may differ from the upload format. A table in the spec lists the allowed internalformat, format and type combinations, and source array types must match the type argument or the call raises INVALID_OPERATION.
capabilities.outputs: textures in 8-bit, half float or float layouts

capabilities.does: Adds 3D textures and 2D array textures with upload, sub-upload, copy and compressed upload entry points. Array layers can also be attached to a framebuffer one at a time.
capabilities.inputs: texImage3D, texSubImage3D, copyTexSubImage3D, compressedTexImage3D, compressedTexSubImage3D, framebufferTextureLayer

capabilities.does: Allocates every mip level of a texture in one call so the size and format cannot change afterwards. The spec calls texStorage2D a preferred alternative to texImage2D.
Records vertex shader outputs into buffers, which allows GPU-side particle updates or geometry passes. Recording can be paused and resumed, and varyings are named before linking.
capabilities.inputs: createTransformFeedback, bindTransformFeedback, transformFeedbackVaryings, beginTransformFeedback, endTransformFeedback, pauseTransformFeedback, resumeTransformFeedback

capabilities.does: Shares blocks of uniform data between programs through indexed binding points. A block is located by name, assigned a binding point, and fed from a whole buffer or a sub-range of one.
capabilities.inputs: bindBufferBase, bindBufferRange, getUniformBlockIndex, uniformBlockBinding, getActiveUniformBlockParameter, getUniformIndices, getActiveUniforms

capabilities.does: Draws many copies of one mesh in a single call, with a per-attribute divisor that sets how fast an attribute advances per instance. Indexed and non-indexed versions exist, plus a range-limited indexed draw.
A fragment shader writes to several colour attachments in one pass. drawBuffers selects the targets, and MAX_DRAW_BUFFERS and MAX_COLOR_ATTACHMENTS give the limits.
capabilities.outputs: several render targets from one draw

capabilities.does: Clears one chosen buffer of the bound framebuffer, with float, signed, unsigned or depth-stencil value types, rather than clearing all attachments at once.

Multisampled renderbuffers let a pass render with several samples per pixel. Supported sample counts are read through getInternalformatParameter. A multisampled DEPTH_STENCIL renderbuffer raises INVALID_OPERATION.
Copies a pixel block between the read and draw framebuffers. The spec defines which destination pixels stay untouched and what happens when an attachment is missing.
Tells the driver that the contents of some attachments need not be kept. The sub-rectangle form restricts this to part of the attachment.
Separates filtering and wrap state from the texture, so one texture can be read with different settings from different texture units.
Fences inserted in the command stream. The client can block on one with a timeout, or make the GPU wait on it without blocking the script.
Asynchronous queries that are begun, ended and read later. Results are fetched by parameter, so the script does not stall on the draw.
Bundles attribute and element-buffer bindings in one object, so a mesh is bound with a single call. This was a WebGL 1 extension and is core here.
Vertex attributes can carry integers that reach the shader without conversion to float, for ids, flags or bone indices.
capabilities.inputs: vertexAttribIPointer, vertexAttribI4i, vertexAttribI4ui and the v forms

capabilities.does: Buffer-to-buffer copy on the GPU, and a blocking read of buffer data into an ArrayBuffer. The read raises INVALID_OPERATION if a transform feedback object is active on that target or the range exceeds the buffer.
capabilities.inputs: copyBufferSubData, getBufferSubData, bufferData and bufferSubData with source offset and length

capabilities.does: Texture uploads can read from a buffer bound to PIXEL_UNPACK_BUFFER with a byte offset instead of from a typed array. Without a bound buffer or texture the call raises INVALID_OPERATION.
capabilities.inputs: texImage2D, texSubImage2D, texImage3D with offset and a bound PIXEL_UNPACK_BUFFER

capabilities.does: EXT_color_buffer_float makes R16F, RG16F, RGBA16F, R32F, RG32F, RGBA32F and R11F_G11F_B10F renderable as colour attachments. RGB16F is not included. Fragment output is not clamped.
Removes the error that blocked blending into a 32-bit float draw buffer. The buffer itself must come from EXT_color_buffer_float or WEBGL_color_buffer_float.
Allows linear magnification and the linear and mipmap minification filters on float textures. The extension adds no new functions and is written against WebGL 1.
Measures GPU time with TIME_ELAPSED_EXT around a block, or records TIMESTAMP_EXT points. Check GPU_DISJOINT_EXT and discard results when it is set. Poll QUERY_RESULT_AVAILABLE before reading.
capabilities.inputs: queryCounterEXT(query, target) with TIMESTAMP_EXT, beginQuery with TIME_ELAPSED_EXT, QUERY_COUNTER_BITS_EXT, GPU_DISJOINT_EXT
capabilities.outputs: elapsed GPU time in counter units

capabilities.does: A non-blocking completion query for shader compile and link. Poll COMPLETION_STATUS_KHR per program and read LINK_STATUS only once it is true. It does not speed linking; it only avoids stalls. Exposed in workers too.

One call issues a list of draws, with offset arguments into typed arrays. Instanced variants exist, and the shader reads the draw index as gl_DrawID. The shader directive uses the GL_ANGLE_multi_draw name.
Renders several views into layers of a 2D array texture in one pass, for stereo or VR. The shader declares num_views and reads gl_ViewID_OVR. At least two views are guaranteed.
capabilities.inputs: framebufferTextureMultiviewOVR(target, attachment, texture, level, baseViewIndex, numViews), MAX_VIEWS_OVR

capabilities.does: ASTC block-compressed textures in 14 block sizes from 4x4 to 12x12, linear and sRGB. getSupportedProfiles lists ldr and hdr. Each upload must have a byte length of 16 times the block count.
BC7 (RGBA, sRGB) and BC6H (signed and unsigned float RGB) formats. Top-level width and height must be multiples of four, and the data size follows ceil(w/4) times ceil(h/4) times 16.
Ten ETC2 and EAC formats (R11, RG11, RGB8, sRGB8, punch-through alpha, RGBA8). In WebGL 2 they also work with the compressed 3D entry points, only on TEXTURE_2D_ARRAY.

DXT1, DXT3 and DXT5 compressed textures. Level dimensions and sub-image offsets must be multiples of four. The RGB DXT1 format may be mapped to RGBA on some platforms, so alpha is not guaranteed opaque.
Sets the maximum anisotropy of a texture or sampler with TEXTURE_MAX_ANISOTROPY_EXT. The ceiling comes from getParameter(MAX_TEXTURE_MAX_ANISOTROPY_EXT). Sampler support applies to WebGL 2 only.
capabilities.inputs: texParameterf or texParameteri with TEXTURE_MAX_ANISOTROPY_EXT, samplerParameterf, MAX_TEXTURE_MAX_ANISOTROPY_EXT

capabilities.does: Blend factors that use a second fragment shader output (SRC1 colour and alpha, and their one-minus forms). The shader enables GL_EXT_blend_func_extended. A draw raises INVALID_OPERATION if the shader does not write the secondary output.
Sets blend enable, blend equation, blend functions and colour write mask separately for each draw buffer, so each render target can blend differently.
capabilities.inputs: enableiOES, disableiOES, blendEquationiOES, blendEquationSeparateiOES, blendFunciOES, blendFuncSeparateiOES, colorMaskiOES

capabilities.does: User clip planes via gl_ClipDistance and cull planes via gl_CullDistance in ESSL 3.00 shaders, eight clip distances through CLIP_DISTANCE0_WEBGL to CLIP_DISTANCE7_WEBGL. Cull support is optional and its limits read as zero when missing.
Chooses whether flat-shaded varyings take their value from the first or the last vertex of a primitive. The default is the last vertex convention.
A capability flag, DEPTH_CLAMP_EXT, toggled with enable and disable. The WebGL page defers the exact clipping behaviour to the underlying EXT_depth_clamp text.
Context properties choose the colour space of the drawing buffer and the colour space textures are converted into when imported from the DOM.

rea.notes: Spec and extension pages are public. Browser implementations are separate products. The spec page read was cut at about half; the NPOT, compressed-texture and copy-buffer chapters were not read.

entries.verified: 2026-11-02, how: spec first half, MDN context page and extension registry pages read

entries.name: WebGPU and WGSL
entries.vendor: W3C GPU for the Web Community Group

licence.name: W3C specification; the W3C document licence text was not read

engines.name: WebGPU API (GPU, GPUAdapter, GPUDevice, GPUQueue)
engines.does: Entry through navigator.gpu to a physical adapter, then a logical device that creates buffers, textures, pipelines and command encoders, and a queue that submits work.

engines.name: WGSL shading language
engines.does: The shader language for WebGPU, with vertex, fragment and compute entry points, address spaces, atomics, texture and subgroup built-in functions, and enable directives for optional features.

capabilities.does: The page asks for an adapter, then a device. A compatibility feature level can be requested through requestAdapter. Adapters and devices expose feature sets and limits, and the API needs a secure context.
Compute pipelines run a grid of workgroups, either from counts given in the call or read from a buffer. The WGSL entry point carries @compute and a @workgroup_size.
capabilities.outputs: compute work on storage buffers and textures

capabilities.does: A render pipeline fixes vertex layouts, fragment targets and primitive state. Topologies: point, line list and strip, triangle list and strip. Options: frontFace, cullMode, stripIndexFormat. Layout may be 'auto'.
capabilities.inputs: primitive.topology, frontFace (ccw, cw), cullMode (none, front, back), stripIndexFormat (uint16, uint32), layout

capabilities.does: Describes each vertex buffer with a stride, a step mode of per vertex or per instance, and attributes (format, byte offset, shader location). The instance step mode supplies per-instance data for instanced draws.
capabilities.inputs: buffers[].arrayStride, stepMode (vertex, instance), attributes[].format, offset, shaderLocation

capabilities.does: Per-target blending with separate colour and alpha parts. Operations: add, subtract, reverse-subtract, min, max. Factors include constant, dst, src, saturate and src1 forms. A write mask picks which channels are stored.
capabilities.inputs: targets[].blend.color and alpha: srcFactor, dstFactor, operation; writeMask; setBlendConstant

capabilities.does: Depth write and compare function, front and back stencil faces with compare and fail, depth-fail and pass operations, read and write masks, and depth bias with slope scale and clamp (zero for line and point topologies).
capabilities.inputs: depthStencil: format, depthWriteEnabled, depthCompare, stencilFront, stencilBack, depthBias, depthBiasSlopeScale, depthBiasClamp

capabilities.does: Multisample state sets the sample count, a sample mask and alpha-to-coverage.
A render pass sets pipeline, bind groups, vertex and index buffers, viewport, scissor, blend constant and stencil reference, then issues direct or indirect, indexed or plain draws.
capabilities.inputs: setViewport, setScissorRect, setBlendConstant, setStencilReference, draw, drawIndexed, drawIndirect, drawIndexedIndirect

capabilities.does: Pre-records a batch of draw commands to replay in many passes, such as for repeated views. A bundle cannot set viewport, scissor, blend constant, stencil reference or occlusion queries; the pass supplies them.
Draw and dispatch parameters can be read from a GPU buffer instead of passed by script, so one compute pass can decide how much work a later pass does.
Occlusion queries count whether any sample passes the per-fragment tests for a set of draws. A query set is given in the render pass descriptor, and each query begins and ends inside the pass.
capabilities.inputs: createQuerySet({ type: 'occlusion', count }), occlusionQuerySet, beginOcclusionQuery, endOcclusionQuery, resolveQuerySet

capabilities.does: With the timestamp-query feature, render and compute passes record timestamps into a query set through timestampWrites. Results are resolved into a buffer. The feature allows measuring pass durations.

Buffers get usage flags (map read, map write, copy source and destination, index, vertex, uniform, storage, indirect, query resolve). mapAsync maps a range for CPU access, getMappedRange gives a view, and unmap returns it.
capabilities.inputs: GPUBufferUsage.*, mapAsync(mode, offset, size), getMappedRange, unmap, GPUMapMode.READ and WRITE

capabilities.does: Textures are created with size, mip count, sample count, dimension, format, usage and view formats. Usages include storage binding, render attachment and a transient attachment hint. Views choose 1d, 2d, 2d-array, cube, cube-array or 3d and subranges.
capabilities.inputs: createTexture, createView: format, dimension, aspect, baseMipLevel, mipLevelCount, baseArrayLayer, arrayLayerCount

capabilities.does: Sampler descriptors set address modes per axis, mag, min and mipmap filters, LOD clamps, an optional compare function for depth sampling, and a maximum anisotropy. Defaults seen: clamp-to-edge, nearest, LOD range 0 to 32, anisotropy 1.
capabilities.inputs: addressModeU/V/W, magFilter, minFilter, mipmapFilter, lodMinClamp, lodMaxClamp, compare, maxAnisotropy

capabilities.does: Resources are grouped into layouts and bind groups. Buffer bindings can be uniform, storage or read-only storage, and dynamic offsets selected at set time must meet alignment limits. Texture sample types: float, unfilterable-float, depth, sint, uint.
capabilities.inputs: createBindGroupLayout, createBindGroup, setBindGroup (with dynamic offsets), createPipelineLayout

capabilities.does: A shader stage can take override values for constants declared in WGSL, converted to bool, i32, u32, f32 or f16. Pipelines can also be built asynchronously and returned as promises.
Command encoders record buffer-to-buffer, buffer-to-texture, texture-to-buffer and texture-to-texture copies, zero-fill a buffer region, and resolve a query set into a buffer.
capabilities.inputs: copyBufferToBuffer, copyBufferToTexture, copyTextureToBuffer, copyTextureToTexture, clearBuffer, resolveQuerySet

capabilities.does: The queue submits command buffers and writes data straight into buffers and textures. It can copy an image, video frame or canvas snapshot into a texture and signal when submitted work is done.
A canvas context is configured with a device, a format (the preferred format can be queried) and an alpha mode. getCurrentTexture returns the texture composited next, and unconfigure releases it.
capabilities.inputs: getContext('webgpu'), configure({ device, format, alphaMode }), getCurrentTexture, unconfigure

capabilities.does: importExternalTexture wraps a video element or VideoFrame as a sampleable texture with an optional colour space. Textures made from video elements expire automatically.
Error classes cover validation, out-of-memory and internal errors, pipeline errors and device loss. Shader compilation yields messages. Encoders accept labels, debug markers and debug groups.
capabilities.inputs: GPUError subclasses, GPUDeviceLostInfo, GPUCompilationInfo, pushDebugGroup, popDebugGroup, insertDebugMarker

capabilities.does: The shader-f16 feature allows the half-precision f16 type in WGSL, enabled in the shader by an enable directive.

The subgroups feature enables SIMD-level cross-invocation operations in WGSL. WGSL lists subgroup built-ins such as subgroupAdd, subgroupBallot, subgroupBroadcast, subgroupShuffle, subgroupElect and the quad operations.
float32-filterable permits filtering on r32float, rg32float and rgba32float textures. float32-blendable permits blending on the same formats.
Features allow 2D BC, ASTC and ETC2/EAC compressed textures. Separate sliced-3d features extend BC and ASTC to 3D and depend on the 2D feature.
The indirect-first-instance feature allows a non-zero firstInstance value inside indirect draw buffers.
capabilities.outputs: indirect draws that start at a chosen instance

capabilities.does: The depth-clip-control feature lets a pipeline turn off depth clipping through the unclippedDepth primitive option.
The dual-source-blending feature allows the dual_source_blending enable directive in WGSL, the @blend_src attribute, and the src1 blend factors in pipeline blend state.
The clip-distances feature allows the clip_distances built-in in WGSL, for user clip planes written by the vertex stage.

bgra8unorm-storage allows storage binding of bgra8unorm textures. rg11b10ufloat-renderable allows rendering, blending and multisampling of rg11b10ufloat. Format tier 1 and tier 2 features add more renderable and storage formats.
primitive-index allows the primitive_index built-in in WGSL. texture-component-swizzle allows a swizzle in createView. depth32float-stencil8 allows textures in that depth-stencil format.
capabilities.outputs: primitive ids, remapped channels, 32-bit depth with stencil

capabilities.does: WGSL has bool, i32, u32, f32, f16, vectors, matrices, arrays, structs, atomics and pointers, plus texture and sampler types. Entry points use @vertex, @fragment and @compute. Resources use @group and @binding, and IO uses @location and @builtin.

Atomic operations on integers (load, store, add, sub, min, max, and, or, xor, exchange, compare-exchange). Barriers sync a workgroup, storage memory or textures, and workgroupUniformLoad reads a uniform value.
capabilities.inputs: atomicAdd and the other atomic functions, workgroupBarrier, storageBarrier, textureBarrier, workgroupUniformLoad

capabilities.does: Texture functions: textureSample with bias, grad, level and compare variants, textureGather, textureLoad, textureStore, and dimension, layer, level and sample counts. Also derivatives (dpdx, dpdy, fwidth) and data pack and unpack functions.
capabilities.inputs: textureSample*, textureGather*, textureLoad, textureStore, dpdx, dpdy, fwidth, pack2x16float

capabilities.does: Interpolation of stage outputs is set with the @interpolate attribute. Types: perspective, linear, flat. Sampling modes: center, centroid, sample, first, either.

outcomes: GPU compute and rendering in the browser

rea.notes: MDN marks WebGPU as limited availability and not Baseline. The W3C pages were read only in part: the WebGPU page text cut off before render and compute pass sections, and the WGSL page was read to character 100000 of 464047. Feature names subgroup-size-control, texture-compression-unaligned and atomic-vec2u-min-max appear in the GPUFeatureName list but their meaning was not read.

entries.verified: 2026-11-02, how: MDN interface pages and W3C WebGPU and WGSL pages read in part

entries.name: Vulkan

licence.name: Khronos open standard; the registry page states no licence for the specification, and says use of the Vulkan trademark needs Khronos Adopter membership and a fee

engines.name: Vulkan core API and extensions
engines.does: One published specification covers the latest core version and all registered extensions. Extensions are grouped by vendor prefix on the documentation site.

engines.name: Ray tracing extensions
engines.does: VK_KHR_acceleration_structure builds the scene hierarchy, VK_KHR_ray_tracing_pipeline adds shader-based tracing, and VK_KHR_ray_query lets any shader stage trace inline.

capabilities.does: A pipeline type for ray tracing with ray generation, intersection, any-hit, closest-hit, miss and callable shader stages. Traversal is started by a trace command, and it needs the acceleration structure extension.

A table of shader group handles links shaders to acceleration structure items. Regions are passed as strided device address regions, and the buffer needs the shader binding table usage bit. Handles are fetched from the pipeline.

Trace dimensions can come from a GPU buffer. The pipeline stack size can be queried per shader group and set dynamically. Limits include maxRayRecursionDepth, shaderGroupHandleSize and maxRayHitAttributeSize.
Ray tracing pipelines can be built as libraries through VK_KHR_pipeline_library and linked later, using an interface create info that declares payload and attribute sizes.

Builds and updates acceleration structures on the device or host, queries build sizes first, and is controlled by a build mode enum. A geometry type for instances supports top-level structures that point to others.

Structures can be copied, serialised to memory and restored. A query type reports the compacted size. A compatibility check tells whether serialised data fits a device. Indirect device builds are available.

Ray queries run in any shader stage, including graphics and compute, and return the traversal result to the caller. They cannot launch other shaders. The page's example uses a ray query for a shadow test.
Any-hit, closest-hit and ray query shaders read the three object-space vertex positions of a hit triangle straight from the acceleration structure. The build needs an allow-data-access flag.

Per-subtriangle opacity data attached to triangle geometry lets the traversal treat parts of a triangle as opaque, transparent or unknown. Formats have two or four states. Instance flags can disable micromaps. Now promoted to a KHR extension.

A task and mesh stage replace the vertex input path for building primitives. Draw commands launch task groups, with indirect and indirect-count versions. A mesh shader can mark primitives culled and write point, line or triangle indices.
Begins a render pass instance directly from attachment infos, with no render pass or framebuffer objects. Flags allow suspending and resuming a pass across command buffers. In core since Vulkan 1.3.
capabilities.inputs: vkCmdBeginRendering, vkCmdEndRendering, VkRenderingInfo, VkRenderingAttachmentInfo, VK_RENDERING_SUSPENDING_BIT, VK_RENDERING_RESUMING_BIT

capabilities.does: Fragment shaders inside a dynamic render pass can read what earlier fragments wrote to attachments. Two commands remap attachment locations and input attachment indices. Core in Vulkan 1.4, with depth and multisample support gated by properties.

Reworked barriers and submission with 64-bit stage and access masks. One dependency info carries memory, buffer and image barriers, and a new submit call takes per-semaphore and per-command-buffer info. Core since Vulkan 1.3.
capabilities.inputs: vkCmdPipelineBarrier2, vkQueueSubmit2, vkCmdSetEvent2, vkCmdWaitEvents2, vkCmdWriteTimestamp2, VkDependencyInfo, VkImageMemoryBarrier2

capabilities.does: A semaphore with a 64-bit counter that marks a point on a timeline. Host and device can wait, signal and read the value. Values are given to submits through a chained struct. Core since Vulkan 1.2.
Descriptor arrays can be indexed non-uniformly, partially bound, updated after bind or sized at allocation. These binding flags enable bindless resource tables. Core since Vulkan 1.2.

Returns a 64-bit address for a buffer so shaders can read it through pointers. Needs the shader device address usage bit and an allocate flag. Capture and replay addresses are for tools. Core since Vulkan 1.2.
One fragment shader run can shade a group of pixels. The rate is set per pipeline, per primitive or from an attachment, and combiner operations merge them. The device reports its supported rates.
Matrix types spread across the invocations of a scope, usually a subgroup, so a matrix multiply runs cooperatively in compute shaders. The device lists supported sizes and component types.

A single compiled shader stage as an object, bound with one call, as an alternative to full pipeline objects. Stages can be linked or unlinked. It needs dynamic rendering and many dynamic state commands.

The GPU writes its own command streams of draws, dispatches or ray traces, with push constants, vertex and index buffer binds and shader updates. A layout describes the stream, and an execution set holds pipelines or shaders.

outcomes: low-level GPU rendering and compute on desktop and mobile

rea.notes: Specification, reference pages, headers and conformance tests are public. Drivers are vendor products. The platform list was not read, so platforms is left empty.

entries.verified: 2026-11-02, how: Vulkan reference pages on docs.vulkan.org and the Khronos registry page read

entries.name: Direct3D 12

licence.name: Microsoft Windows graphics API; specification pages are public on GitHub Pages, their licence text was not read

engines.name: DirectX Raytracing (DXR)
engines.does: Ray tracing with shader-table dispatch, acceleration structures and inline ray queries. Tiers 1.1 and 1.2 add inline tracing, indirect dispatch and opacity micromaps.

engines.name: Agility SDK
engines.does: A redistributable D3D12 runtime that an application ships in its own folder, so it can use new features without waiting for an OS update.

engines.name: DirectX specs catalogue
engines.does: A site of feature specs grouped as rendering pipeline, structure, performance, video, HLSL shader models, developer features, GPU debugging and tools.

capabilities.does: Ray generation, intersection, any-hit, closest-hit, miss and callable shaders. DispatchRays launches a grid of ray generation invocations and works from graphics, compute and bundle lists. Hit groups bundle intersection, any-hit and closest-hit shaders.
capabilities.inputs: DispatchRays, TraceRay, ReportHit, IgnoreHit, AcceptHitAndEndSearch, CallShader, ray flags such as RAY_FLAG_FORCE_OPAQUE

capabilities.does: Bottom-level structures hold triangle or procedural AABB geometry, one type per structure. Top-level structures hold instances with transform, InstanceID and an 8-bit mask. Updates to bottom-level triangle structures are limited to vertex position changes.

A state object collects shaders and subobjects (hit groups, root signatures, shader config, pipeline config) with default or explicit associations. Shader records hold a 32-byte identifier plus local root arguments, and tables start on 64-byte boundaries.
capabilities.inputs: CreateStateObject, AddToStateObject, shader record stride (multiple of 32 bytes, up to 4096)

capabilities.does: Inline ray tracing (Tier 1.1): a RayQuery object traces from any shader stage and the caller steps traversal, so no separate hit shaders are needed. GPU-initiated DispatchRays through ExecuteIndirect is also in Tier 1.1.
capabilities.inputs: RayQuery, TraceRayInline, Proceed, CommitNonOpaqueTriangleHit, CommitProceduralPrimitiveHit, Abort, CommittedStatus

capabilities.does: Tier 1.2 opacity micromap arrays link to triangles in a BLAS and mark micro-triangles as opaque, transparent or unknown with 1-bit or 2-bit encodings. A pipeline flag enables them and a ray flag forces two-state behaviour.

MaybeReorderThread lets a ray generation shader regroup threads for coherence. HitObject splits traversal from closest-hit and miss shading. A device option reports whether the hardware actually reorders.

An amplification shader launches mesh shader groups through DispatchMesh with a payload. A mesh shader writes up to 256 vertices and 256 primitives per group. Input assembler and stream output are off. SV_CullPrimitive culls per primitive.
capabilities.inputs: DispatchMesh, SetMeshOutputCounts, [numthreads], [outputtopology], out vertices, out indices, out primitives, SV_CullPrimitive

capabilities.does: GPU work creation as a graph of nodes. Node launch modes are broadcasting, coalescing and thread; a node can output to itself up to a depth of 32. The app supplies backing memory sized by a requirements query. DispatchGraph starts the graph.

Tier 1 sets a shading rate per draw. Tier 2 adds per-primitive rate via SV_ShadingRate and a screen-space R8_UINT rate image, with combiners (passthrough, override, min, max, sum). Rates 1x1 to 2x2 are guaranteed; 2x4, 4x2 and 4x4 need an extra cap.

Records which mip regions of a texture a shader sampled, into a MinMip or MipRegionUsed feedback map paired with a texture. Shaders write with WriteSamplerFeedback variants. It supports texture streaming and texture-space shading.

Barriers split into sync scope, access and texture layout, as global, buffer and texture barriers. They can replace legacy resource barriers, support split barriers, subresource ranges and a discard flag, and have queue-specific layouts.

Rasterizes every pixel a primitive touches. Tier 1 has a half-pixel uncertainty region, tier 2 narrows it to 1/256 pixel, and tier 3 adds SV_InnerCoverage. Used for voxelization, light maps and occlusion culling.

Declares render target and depth dependencies so tile-based GPUs cut memory traffic. Beginning access can discard, preserve, clear or skip; ending access can discard, preserve or resolve. Passes can suspend and resume across command lists.

Descriptors live in CBV/SRV/UAV and sampler heaps. Root signatures carry descriptor tables, root constants and root descriptors within a 64-DWORD budget, plus static samplers. Binding tiers 1 to 3 raise the table limits.
capabilities.inputs: SetDescriptorHeaps, root signature (descriptor tables, root constants, root CBV/SRV/UAV), static samplers, ResourceBindingTier

capabilities.does: ExecuteIndirect reads draws, indexed draws or dispatches from a buffer, along with state changes such as vertex and index buffer views and root constants. A count buffer can cap the executed commands below a maximum.
capabilities.inputs: CreateCommandSignature, D3D12_INDIRECT_ARGUMENT_TYPE_DRAW, DRAW_INDEXED, DISPATCH, VERTEX_BUFFER_VIEW, CONSTANT, MaxCommandCount, pCountBuffer

capabilities.does: View instancing renders the same geometry to several views in one draw. A pipeline declares a view count (maximum 4) and per-view render target and viewport indices, and shaders read SV_ViewID. Tiers 1 to 3 differ in where the instancing happens.
capabilities.outputs: stereo or multi-target output from one draw

capabilities.does: Shader Model 6.9 allows vectors of 5 to 1024 elements, native vector types in DXIL 1.9 and whole-vector buffer loads. It also makes native 16-bit ops, wave ops and 64-bit integer ops mandatory, and adds isnormal.

An application exports D3D12SDKVersion and D3D12SDKPath and ships D3D12Core.dll beside the exe. At device creation the runtime uses the newer of that and the OS copy. A tool interface can select a version, only in Windows Developer Mode.
capabilities.outputs: newer D3D12 features on older Windows

outcomes: real-time rendering and compute on Windows GPUs

rea.notes: Feature specs are public. The long specs (raytracing 621k characters, work graphs 530k) were read to character 100000 only. The Learn programming guide page returned only its header text. Cooperative vectors were not found on the SM 6.9 page that was read.

entries.verified: 2026-11-02, how: DirectX-Specs pages read in part

entries.name: Apple Metal

licence.name: Apple platform graphics framework; the developer licence text was not read

engines.name: Metal 4 core API
engines.does: A newer family of MTL4 types for queues, command buffers, allocators, encoders, argument tables and barriers, adoptable step by step next to the older MTL types.

engines.name: MetalFX
engines.does: Upscaling effects for render passes: spatial and temporal scalers, plus frame interpolator and temporal denoised scaler types.

engines.name: Metal developer tools
engines.does: Metal debugger, performance HUD, API and shader validation layers, Instruments system trace and the Game Porting Toolkit.

capabilities.does: Metal 4 queues commit command buffers as a group from any thread. Command buffers come from the device, are reused after commit, and draw memory from allocators reset per frame. One compute encoder covers blit, compute and acceleration structure work.

An argument table stores resource bindings (buffers, textures, samplers) and is bound to stages of one or more encoders. Counts per type are set in a descriptor, and one table can be shared across encoders.

In Metal 4 every resource is untracked, so passes that read what an earlier pass wrote need a barrier. A barrier delays a pipeline stage until a previous stage finishes. Events synchronise across queues.
A pool of lightweight texture views that reinterpret a texture's data in another pixel format, each with its own resource ID in a contiguous range that can be reassigned.
capabilities.outputs: format-cast views at low memory cost

capabilities.does: Build acceleration structures, then trace through an intersector with a table of intersection functions, or through intersection queries that return to the caller. Intersectors run in compute kernels on all GPUs and in render shaders on Apple silicon only.
capabilities.outputs: ray-traced results in compute or render shaders

capabilities.does: Primitive structures hold triangles, curves or bounding boxes, and instance structures reference them. Structures can be built and refitted. Per-primitive data can be stored inside the structure. Indirect instance structures let the GPU fill instance data.

Geometry descriptors cover triangle, curve and bounding-box geometry. Curves have a type, a basis and end caps. Motion variants of each take keyframe data for motion ray tracing, and motion instance descriptors carry a user ID and motion data.
A table of custom intersection functions that Metal calls during traversal, created from a descriptor and function signatures for the kind of custom test.

Render pipelines for mesh shading have their own descriptors in both Metal 4 and the earlier API. The Metal 4 render encoder text says mesh shader techniques replace tessellation there. Object and mesh function details were not on the pages read.
Tile render pipelines run shaders on the tile data of a render pass on Apple GPUs. Compute passes can reserve tile memory as threadgroup or imageblock memory that stays on the GPU.
A rasterization rate map sets different rasterization rates across a render target, so low-detail regions cost less. A step scales the result back to the destination texture.
Vertex amplification runs the same vertex data into several outputs, with a view mapping that offsets render target and viewport index. Shaders can also select a viewport or a texture slice per draw.
capabilities.inputs: MTLVertexAmplificationViewMapping, multiple viewports and texture slices in a draw

capabilities.does: Custom MSAA sample positions can be set, and the pass must record when depth was made with programmable positions. Depth and stencil resolve have filter options.

Render passes set colour, depth and stencil attachments with load and store actions and clear values. Parallel render encoders split one pass across threads, and visibility result modes support occlusion counting. Sample buffers store GPU counters at pass start and end.

Draw and compute commands stored in a buffer and replayed later, once or repeatedly, encoded on the CPU or on the GPU. A compute kernel can pick visible geometry and an indirect buffer then draws it. Indirect argument layouts exist for draws, patches and dispatch.

Metal 4 runs Core ML models inside a command buffer through a machine learning encoder, with tensors as inputs and outputs. A tool converts a model into a Metal package. Shaders get tensor types and cooperative tensors.
capabilities.inputs: MTL4MachineLearningCommandEncoder, MTL4MachineLearningPipelineState, MTLTensor, tensor_handle, tensor_inline, cooperative_tensor
capabilities.outputs: model outputs consumed by later passes

capabilities.does: Compute passes run kernels over a thread grid. Kernels take argument buffers, function tables for visible and intersection functions, and tile memory. Threadgroup and grid sizes are chosen by the app, and dispatch can use indirect arguments.

MetalFX spatial scaling upscales one input texture. Temporal scaling uses several inputs over time. Both are configured through descriptors that also create the effect. Frame interpolator and temporal denoised scaler types are also listed.
A Metal 4 compilation API exists, along with shader libraries and function specialisation for pipeline variants. Generic pointers allow reusable GPU functions.
capabilities.inputs: shader libraries, function specialisation, Metal 4 compilation API

capabilities.does: Metal debugger inspects the pipeline from mesh shading to ray tracing and ML. Also a performance HUD, API and shader validation layers, an Instruments trace, and the Game Porting Toolkit for evaluating and converting games.
capabilities.inputs: Xcode Metal debugger, Metal performance HUD, validation layers, Instruments Metal system trace

outcomes: GPU rendering and compute on Apple devices

rea.notes: The HTML pages under developer.apple.com/documentation are script-rendered and returned only a title, so the documentation JSON that backs them (developer.apple.com/tutorials/data/documentation/...) was read instead. The Metal Feature Set Tables PDF could not be read as text. Metal 4 hardware per the product page: A14 or later on iPhone, iPad and Apple TV, M1 or later on Mac, and Vision Pro. Apple's frame interpolation, denoiser inputs and mesh function details were not shown on pages read.

entries.verified: 2026-11-02, how: Apple documentation JSON and developer.apple.com/metal read

entries.name: OpenGL 4.x (registry extensions)

licence.name: Khronos open standard; the registry page shows only a Khronos copyright and trademark notice

engines.name: Combined OpenGL registry
engines.does: Index pages for OpenGL, OpenGL ES and OpenGL SC, with API specifications, extension specs, headers, and the XML API registry that the headers are generated from.

capabilities.does: Loads SPIR-V modules into shader objects with glShaderBinary, then fixes the entry point and specialization constants before linking. Source and SPIR-V shaders cannot be mixed in one program. The page is written against OpenGL 4.5 core.
capabilities.inputs: SHADER_BINARY_FORMAT_SPIR_V_ARB, SpecializeShaderARB(shader, pEntryPoint, numSpecializationConstants, pConstantIndex, pConstantValue)

capabilities.does: A compute shader type with direct and indirect dispatch. Minimum limits: 65535 groups per dimension, 1024 invocations per group, 32768 bytes of shared memory. Built-ins give work group and invocation ids.
capabilities.inputs: DispatchCompute, DispatchComputeIndirect, COMPUTE_SHADER, DISPATCH_INDIRECT_BUFFER, gl_GlobalInvocationID, gl_LocalInvocationIndex

capabilities.does: Optional tessellation control and evaluation stages work on PATCHES primitives. Outer and inner levels drive triangles, quads or isolines with equal, fractional-even or fractional-odd spacing. Levels are clamped to MAX_TESS_GEN_LEVEL.
capabilities.inputs: PatchParameteri(PATCH_VERTICES), PatchParameterfv, gl_TessLevelOuter, gl_TessLevelInner, TESS_CONTROL_SHADER, TESS_EVALUATION_SHADER

capabilities.does: Objects are created with Create functions in their final state and edited by name, not by binding. It covers buffers, textures, framebuffers, renderbuffers, vertex arrays, samplers, queries, transform feedback and program pipelines.
capabilities.inputs: CreateTextures, CreateBuffers, NamedBufferStorage, TextureParameteri, NamedFramebufferTexture, VertexArrayVertexBuffer, BindTextureUnit

capabilities.does: Issues many indirect draws with one call. The indirect parameter is an offset in the draw indirect buffer, primcount is the number of commands, and a stride of zero means tightly packed.
capabilities.inputs: MultiDrawArraysIndirect(mode, indirect, primcount, stride), MultiDrawElementsIndirect(mode, type, indirect, primcount, stride)

capabilities.does: BufferStorage makes immutable buffer storage with flags for read and write mapping, persistent and coherent mapping, dynamic sub-data updates and a client storage hint. A mapped pointer stays valid while the GPU draws.
capabilities.inputs: BufferStorage(target, size, data, flags), MAP_PERSISTENT_BIT, MAP_COHERENT_BIT, DYNAMIC_STORAGE_BIT, CLIENT_MAPPED_BUFFER_BARRIER_BIT

capabilities.does: Textures and images are referenced from shaders by 64-bit handles stored in uniforms or buffers. A handle must be made resident before use, and the texture and sampler state become immutable once a handle exists.
capabilities.inputs: GetTextureHandleARB, GetImageHandleARB, MakeTextureHandleResidentARB, UniformHandleui64ARB, bindless_sampler layout
capabilities.outputs: large texture sets without bind calls

capabilities.does: SHADER_STORAGE_BUFFER blocks that shaders can read and write, with std430 packing and an unsized last array member. Memory qualifiers such as coherent and restrict apply. Minimum block size is 2^24 bytes.
capabilities.inputs: SHADER_STORAGE_BUFFER, buffer block, std430, ShaderStorageBlockBinding, SHADER_STORAGE_BARRIER_BIT

capabilities.does: Atomic add, min, max, and, or, xor, exchange and compare-swap on int and uint buffer variables in shader storage blocks.
capabilities.inputs: atomicAdd, atomicMin, atomicMax, atomicAnd, atomicOr, atomicXor, atomicExchange, atomicCompSwap

rea.notes: Only extension pages were read; the OpenGL 4.6 core specification and OpenGL ES pages were not opened, so version-to-core promotion facts are not recorded. Extension pages ARB_gl_spirv, ARB_tessellation_shader, ARB_direct_state_access and ARB_shader_storage_buffer_object were read to character 100000.

entries.verified: 2026-11-02, how: Khronos registry and ARB extension text pages read

entries.name: Intel Embree

licence.name: Apache-2.0

engines.name: CPU ray tracing kernels
engines.does: Optimised traversal and intersection kernels for SSE2 through AVX-512 on x86 and for ARM, with TBB, PPL or built-in tasking.

engines.name: SYCL GPU path
engines.does: Hardware-accelerated tracing on Intel Xe HPG and Xe HPC GPUs through SYCL devices, with the same renderer code able to run on CPU or GPU.

engines.name: BVH builder API
engines.does: A callback-based builder that lets an application build its own BVH with Embree's parallel builder and its own node layout.

capabilities.does: Triangle, quad and grid geometry created with rtcNewGeometry. Vertex and index buffers are either allocated by Embree or shared from the application.
capabilities.inputs: RTC_GEOMETRY_TYPE_TRIANGLE, QUAD, GRID, RTC_BUFFER_TYPE_VERTEX, RTC_BUFFER_TYPE_INDEX, rtcSetNewGeometryBuffer, rtcSetSharedGeometryBuffer

capabilities.does: Catmull-Clark subdivision meshes with faces of 3 to 15 vertices, edge and vertex creases, holes, non-manifold input and face-varying attributes. Edge tessellation levels go up to 4096. Not supported on SYCL.
capabilities.inputs: RTC_GEOMETRY_TYPE_SUBDIVISION, RTC_BUFFER_TYPE_FACE, LEVEL, HOLE, EDGE_CREASE_INDEX, EDGE_CREASE_WEIGHT, VERTEX_CREASE_INDEX, rtcSetGeometrySubdivisionMode, rtcSetGeometryTessellationRate

capabilities.does: Flat ribbons for distant hair, normal-oriented bands for grass, and round or cone tubes for close views. Bases are linear, Bezier, B-spline, Hermite and Catmull-Rom. Vertices hold position and radius.
capabilities.inputs: RTC_GEOMETRY_TYPE_FLAT_*_CURVE, NORMAL_ORIENTED_*_CURVE, ROUND_*_CURVE, CONE_LINEAR_CURVE, RTC_BUFFER_TYPE_TANGENT, NORMAL, FLAGS, rtcSetGeometryTessellationRate

capabilities.does: Points as true spheres, ray-facing discs, or normal-oriented discs, each with a radius in the vertex buffer. A hit returns the distance and geometry normal; u and v are zero.
capabilities.inputs: RTC_GEOMETRY_TYPE_SPHERE_POINT, DISC_POINT, ORIENTED_DISC_POINT, RTC_BUFFER_TYPE_VERTEX (x, y, z, radius), RTC_BUFFER_TYPE_NORMAL

capabilities.does: Procedural geometry through application callbacks for bounds, intersection and occlusion. Primitives with empty bounds are ignored.
capabilities.outputs: procedural primitives in the same BVH

capabilities.does: Instances place a scene into another with a transform. Nesting is multi-level up to a compile-time limit. A hit reports an instance ID stack, and deeper levels are ignored in release builds.
Instance arrays hold a transform buffer in four matrix or quaternion formats and map instances to one or several scenes through an index buffer. Hits report instPrimID, the index of the hit instance.
capabilities.outputs: large instance counts with low memory

capabilities.does: rtcIntersect1 finds the closest hit of one ray. The caller sets origin, direction, tnear, tfar, mask, time and flags, and geomID must start at RTC_INVALID_GEOMETRY_ID. On a hit it returns tfar, Ng, u, v, instID, geomID and primID.
Occlusion queries and 4, 8 and 16 wide packet versions of the intersection and occlusion calls. Ray streams from Embree 3 were removed in Embree 4.
capabilities.outputs: hit or shadow results for ray groups

capabilities.does: Searches the BVH for primitives near a point within a radius and calls a callback for each candidate. The callback may shrink the radius to prune traversal. Works with instancing but not with points, curves or subdivision surfaces.
capabilities.inputs: rtcPointQuery, RTCPointQuery (x, y, z, radius, time), RTCPointQueryContext, rtcSetGeometryPointQueryFunction

capabilities.does: Intersects the BVHs of two scenes and calls a callback with batches of candidate primitive pairs (geomID0, primID0, geomID1, primID1). Only scenes made of user geometry are supported, and pairs can be false positives.
Callbacks that accept or reject candidate hits, set per geometry for intersection and occlusion, or passed in the traversal arguments. A filter rejects a hit by writing 0 to the valid mask.
Multi-segment, deformation and quaternion transform motion blur. Geometry takes 2 to 129 time steps, each with its own buffer slot, and rays carry a time in [0, 1].

Scene build quality trades build time against trace speed (low, medium, high). A geometry can also be marked refit when only vertices move. Scene flags (see inputs) change memory and precision trade-offs.
capabilities.inputs: rtcSetSceneBuildQuality, rtcSetGeometryBuildQuality, RTC_BUILD_QUALITY_LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH, REFIT, RTC_SCENE_FLAG_COMPACT, RTC_SCENE_FLAG_ROBUST

capabilities.does: An application passes primitives and callbacks to build its own BVH with Embree's builder. Settings: quality, dynamic flag, branching factor, depth, SAH block size, leaf sizes, traversal and intersection costs. A split callback enables spatial splits.
capabilities.inputs: rtcBuildBVH(RTCBuildArguments), rtcNewBVH, createNode, setNodeChildren, setNodeBounds, createLeaf, splitPrimitive, buildProgress

capabilities.does: A geometry mask is ANDed with the ray mask, and a hit needs a nonzero result. Backface culling options exist for triangles, curves and spheres. The default geometry mask became 0x1 in Embree 4.

SYCL devices run tracing on Intel Arc (Xe HPG) on Linux and Windows and Xe HPC on Linux. Builds use JIT or ahead-of-time compilation. Device-side traversal calls replace host calls, and host and device memory variants exist.

Kernels exist for SSE2, SSE4.2, AVX, AVX2 and AVX-512 plus ARM. Tasking systems are TBB (default), PPL on Windows or an internal one. An ISPC interface and per-geometry CMake toggles let a build drop unused features.
The C API follows a device, scene, geometry pattern with reference counting. A device reports its version, errors and last message. The repository ships about 100 man pages for the rtc functions.
capabilities.inputs: rtcNewDevice, rtcNewScene, rtcCommitScene, rtcGetDeviceProperty, rtcGetDeviceError, rtcReleaseDevice

outcomes: ray tracing kernels inside CPU and GPU renderers

rea.notes: Repository licence shown as Apache-2.0. README read to character 200000 of 382997; the version in the README text is 4.4.1. The man3 listing showed 100 files and said more may exist.

entries.verified: 2026-11-02, how: GitHub README (raw), man pages and project page read

entries.name: NVIDIA OptiX

licence.name: NVIDIA proprietary SDK. The developer page says it is free for commercial use. The public optix-dev headers carry a notice that use or distribution needs an NVIDIA licence agreement.

engines.name: OptiX ray tracing pipeline
engines.does: A single-ray programming model in C++ shaders on a GPU pipeline: ray generation, hit groups, miss, callables and exception programs, with RT Core acceleration.

engines.name: OptiX AI denoiser
engines.does: A host API that denoises rendered images, optionally with albedo and normal guide images, temporal input and 2x upscaling models.

capabilities.does: A programmable ray tracing pipeline accelerated by RT Cores. It scales over several GPUs and can pool GPU memory over NVLink for large scenes. Debugging and profiling work with Nsight tools.
Program groups are of kind raygen, miss, exception, hitgroup or callables. A shader binding table links them to scene items, and each record header is packed with a helper call.

Module options set register cap, optimisation and debug level, bound values and payload types. Pipeline options declare motion blur use, payload and attribute counts, exception flags, launch parameter name, primitive types in use and whether micromaps or clustered geometry are allowed.
capabilities.inputs: OptixModuleCompileOptions (maxRegisterCount, optLevel, debugLevel, boundValues), OptixPipelineCompileOptions (usesMotionBlur, numPayloadValues, numAttributeValues, exceptionFlags, allowOpacityMicromaps, allowClusteredGeometry)

capabilities.does: Modules can be created as a set of tasks that run on several threads, with serialised task output. A compile cache can be switched on and relocated, and sized in a database.

Rays are cast from device code with optixTrace. Payload values are read and set in numbered slots, 0 to 31, with payload types and semantics declared per module. The remaining trace depth can be queried.

Traversal can be split from shading with hit objects. optixTraverse produces a hit object, optixReorder regroups threads by hit data for coherence, and optixInvoke runs the shading. Hit objects can also be built by hand.

Build inputs are triangle, curve, sphere, custom primitive, instance and instance pointer arrays. Flags: allow update, allow compaction, prefer fast trace or build, and random vertex or instance access. Build and update are operations; structures can be compacted and relocated.
capabilities.inputs: OptixBuildInputType, OptixBuildFlags, OptixBuildOperation, optixAccelBuild, optixAccelCompact, optixAccelRelocate, optixAccelEmitProperty

capabilities.does: Motion options give key count, flags and a time range for a structure. Motion transforms come as matrix or scale-rotate-translate keys, and start or end vanish flags hide an object outside its time range.
capabilities.inputs: OptixMotionOptions (numKeys, flags, timeBegin, timeEnd), OptixMatrixMotionTransform, OptixSRTMotionTransform, OPTIX_MOTION_FLAG_START_VANISH

capabilities.does: Instances carry flags for face culling, flipped facing, any-hit control and micromap handling. Traversable types include static, matrix motion and SRT motion transforms, and device code can walk the transform list of a hit.

Round curve types cover linear, quadratic and cubic B-spline, Catmull-Rom and cubic Bezier bases, plus a flat quadratic B-spline, with optional end caps and rocaps variants. Device code reads the curve parameter and vertex data, and ribbon queries exist.
capabilities.inputs: OPTIX_PRIMITIVE_TYPE_ROUND_CUBIC_BSPLINE, ROUND_LINEAR, FLAT_QUADRATIC_BSPLINE, OptixCurveEndcapFlags, optixGetCurveParameter, optixGetRibbonParameters

capabilities.does: A built-in sphere primitive type and a sphere build input array. Device code can fetch the data of the hit sphere.

Custom primitive arrays take application intersection programs. Those report a hit with up to eight attributes, can ignore an intersection or terminate the ray, and read triangle barycentrics for built-in triangles.

Opacity micromap arrays with two-state or four-state formats are built on the device and attached to triangle inputs, in linear or indexed mode. Instances and builds can force two-state mode or disable micromaps.

Host functions compute memory use for and build cluster acceleration structures, and a pipeline option allows clustered geometry. Hit queries return a cluster id. Details of the cluster types were not in the parts read.

The denoiser is created, sized, set up and invoked from the host. Model kinds: AOV, temporal AOV, 2x upscale and temporal 2x upscale. Options enable albedo and normal guides and alpha denoising. Helpers compute intensity and average colour.
capabilities.inputs: optixDenoiserCreate, OptixDenoiserModelKind, OptixDenoiserOptions (guideAlbedo, guideNormal, denoiseAlpha), optixDenoiserInvoke, optixDenoiserComputeIntensity

capabilities.does: Cooperative vector support covers element types (float16, float32, int and uint 8 or 32, float8 E4M3 and E5M2) and matrix layouts (row, column, inferencing-optimal, training-optimal), with a matrix description type.
capabilities.outputs: types for small neural network layers in shaders

capabilities.does: Exception programs catch stack overflow, trace depth exceeded and user exceptions, enabled by flags. Device code can throw with up to eight details. Stack sizes are set from call depths or directly.
Host functions convert a matrix between layouts and compute the size of a converted matrix.

rea.restrictions: The header optix_types.h carries an NVIDIA proprietary notice: use, reproduction, disclosure or distribution requires an express licence agreement with NVIDIA or an affiliate.
rea.notes: The programming guide at raytracing-docs.nvidia.com failed with a certificate error for both optix8 and optix9 paths, so no capability cites it. Headers were read from the public optix-dev repository: optix_types.h and optix_host.h in full, and optix_device.h to character 100000 of 126095. Displacement micromaps were not found in the parts read. The SDK version is not stated on the pages read. The optix-dev repo page showed LICENSE.txt without its text.

entries.verified: 2026-11-02, how: OptiX developer page and public optix-dev header files read

entries.name: Intel Open Image Denoise

licence.name: Apache-2.0 (as stated in the GitHub README)

engines.name: RT filter
engines.does: A general neural denoising filter for Monte Carlo ray-traced images, taking a colour image and optional albedo and normal images.

engines.name: RTLightmap filter
engines.does: A filter variant for HDR lightmaps, with a mode for normalized directional lightmaps.

engines.name: Device backends
engines.does: CPU, SYCL, CUDA, HIP and Metal devices that run the network, chosen by type or by physical device id.

capabilities.does: The RT filter denoises path-traced images. Inputs are colour, albedo and normal, output is a denoised image. Flags: hdr, srgb, cleanAux. Optional inputScale, quality and weights parameters tune it.
capabilities.inputs: filter 'RT': color, albedo, normal, output; hdr, srgb, cleanAux, inputScale, quality, weights

capabilities.does: The RTLightmap filter takes colour and writes output, for HDR lightmaps only. Setting directional to true handles normalized directional coefficients in the range -1 to 1.
capabilities.inputs: filter 'RTLightmap': color, output, directional, inputScale, quality

capabilities.does: Albedo and normal images usually preserve detail. cleanAux tells the filter these are noise-free. If they are noisy, run separate RT filters in place on each first, then denoise the beauty image with cleanAux on.
Quality levels trade speed for result. High is the stated default and suits final frames, while balanced and fast suit interactive use.
Images can be HDR or LDR, set by the hdr flag, and sRGB-encoded when the srgb flag is set. An input scale parameter exists, and it must be set when HDR images are denoised in tiles.
capabilities.outputs: correct handling of encoding and exposure

capabilities.does: maxMemoryMB asks the filter to limit memory use (default -1). For manual tiling, tileAlignment and tileOverlap give the constants a tile layout must respect.
Device types: default, CPU, SYCL, CUDA, HIP and Metal, each with its own constructor. CPU devices take a thread count and an affinity setting.
capabilities.inputs: OIDN_DEVICE_TYPE_CPU, SYCL, CUDA, HIP, METAL, oidnNewSYCLDevice, oidnNewCUDADevice, oidnNewHIPDevice, oidnNewMetalDevice

capabilities.does: Physical devices can be counted and described, and a device created by index, UUID, LUID or PCI address. An environment variable sets the default device and others switch backends.
capabilities.inputs: oidnGetNumPhysicalDevices, oidnNewDeviceByID, oidnNewDeviceByUUID, oidnNewDeviceByLUID, oidnNewDeviceByPCIAddress, OIDN_DEFAULT_DEVICE

capabilities.does: Buffers can live in host, device or managed storage, or wrap shared memory. Data moves with sync or async read and write calls. Map and unmap calls were removed.
capabilities.inputs: oidnNewBuffer, oidnNewBufferWithStorage, oidnNewSharedBuffer, OIDN_STORAGE_HOST, OIDN_STORAGE_DEVICE, OIDN_STORAGE_MANAGED, oidnReadBuffer, oidnWriteBuffer

capabilities.does: Filters run synchronously or asynchronously, with a device sync call. A progress monitor callback reports progress and can cancel, which raises OIDN_ERROR_CANCELLED, though cancellation is not guaranteed.
Custom network weights pass through the weights parameter and attach as shared filter data. A training toolkit trains on a user dataset, and a script converts the result to a .tza weights file.
C99 and C++11 APIs. Devices report version numbers. The README lists v2.5.1 and says the network was trained for inputs from 1 sample per pixel up to nearly converged.

The README lists 64-bit CPUs (Intel with SSE4.1, ARM64), Intel Xe GPUs, NVIDIA Turing to Blackwell, AMD RDNA 2 to RDNA 4 and Apple M1 and newer, on Windows, Linux and macOS. The RT filter is not temporally stable.

rea.notes: The documentation page itself shows only a copyright line and does not state licence terms; Apache-2.0 is from the GitHub README. README read to character 100000 of 121973.
