entries.name: AMD FidelityFX SDK (FSR SDK)

licence.name: The README says the FSR samples are open source under MIT; it gives no licence for the SDK kits themselves

engines.name: DX12 and Vulkan backends
engines.does: Backend layers that run the effects on DirectX 12 or Vulkan. A GDK backend is also listed in the manual. Vulkan is not supported for ray regeneration and radiance caching.

engines.name: FSR ML effects
engines.does: Machine-learning upscaling, frame generation and ray regeneration listed in the GitHub README for SDK 2.4.0.

capabilities.does: FSR1 is spatial single-frame upscaling, FSR2 is temporal upscaling, and FSR3 has an upscaler and a combined upscaling and frame generation package.
capabilities.inputs: FidelityFX Super Resolution 1.2 (FSR1), 2.3.3 (FSR2), 3.1.4 (FSR3 upscaler and FSR3 upscaling plus frame generation)

capabilities.does: Frame interpolation creates extra frames from real frames and motion data. A DX12 swapchain replacement presents them with frame pacing. A separate optical flow effect does block-based motion estimation.
capabilities.inputs: FidelityFX Frame Interpolation 1.1.3, Frame Interpolation Swapchain 1.1.3, Optical Flow 1.1.2

capabilities.does: A denoiser that removes artifacts from reflection and shadow rendering.
Stochastic screen-space reflections for high-fidelity reflections from the depth buffer.
CACAO, a combined adaptive compute ambient occlusion technique that uses adaptive sampling.
Contrast adaptive sharpening restores high-frequency detail after upscaling or anti-aliasing.
Brixelizer builds a sparse distance field of the scene, and Brixelizer GI computes global illumination from it. A classifier effect sorts screen tiles to guide ray tracing work.
High-quality depth of field with bokeh.
Chromatic aberration, film grain and vignette in one effect. A separate blur effect offers Gaussian and radial blur.
The luminance preserving mapper does tone and gamut mapping for HDR content.
Variable rate shading driven by analysing the luminance of screen tiles.
Stable GPU parallel sort, a single-pass downsampler with optional mip generation, and a breadcrumbs tool that helps analyse GPU crashes after the fact.
capabilities.inputs: FidelityFX Parallel Sort 1.3, Single Pass Downsampler 2.2, Breadcrumbs 1.0.1
capabilities.outputs: sorted data, mip chains, crash traces

capabilities.does: The README for SDK 2.4.0 lists an ML upscaler (FSR Upscaling 4.1.2), a temporal Super Resolution (2.3.4), an FSR 3.1.6 upscaler, FSR frame generation 3.1.6, swapchain versions 3.1.7 and 4.0.0, and an ML frame generation 4.0.2.
capabilities.inputs: FSR Upscaling (ML-Upscaler) 4.1.2, Super Resolution (Temporal) 2.3.4, (Upscaler) 3.1.6, FSR Frame Generation 3.1.6, (Swapchain) 3.1.7 and 4.0.0, (ML) 4.0.2

capabilities.does: FSR Ray Regeneration 1.2.1 is an ML denoiser, and Radiance Caching is a preview effect. The README says Vulkan is not supported for these two.
capabilities.inputs: FSR Ray Regeneration (ML-Denoiser) 1.2.1, FSR Radiance Caching (Preview)

outcomes: upscaled and generated frames in games

rea.notes: Two documents disagree on versions: the manual page lists FidelityFX SDK 1.1.4 techniques, the GitHub README lists FSR SDK 2.4.0 (Redstone) effects. Both are cited by effect. gpuopen.com/fidelityfx-sdk returned 404. The source licence of the SDK kits was not stated on the pages read, so the readable-source label rests on the public GitHub repository only.

entries.name: Slang shading language
entries.vendor: shader-slang project (no vendor named on the pages read)

licence.name: Apache 2.0 with LLVM Exception (as stated in the GitHub README)

engines.name: slangc compiler
engines.does: The command-line compiler. A shared compiler library and the slang.h header ship in binary releases.

engines.name: Module system
engines.does: Separate compilation: modules can be compiled ahead of time to a custom intermediate form and linked at run time.

capabilities.does: A module system for separate compilation. Modules are precompiled to a custom IR, optionally obfuscated, and linked at run time into DXIL or SPIR-V.
Generics constrained by interfaces (also called type traits or protocols). They are checked before specialisation, which avoids the long error chains of C++ templates.
Generates forward and backward derivative code, including for functions with arbitrary control flow and dynamic dispatch. A Python integration, SlangPy, connects it to PyTorch training workflows.

A capability system checks at type-checking time whether a feature is available for the chosen target. Pointers are allowed when generating SPIR-V, and target code or SPIR-V can be embedded in a shader.
capabilities.inputs: capability annotations, pointers, inline target code

capabilities.does: The syntax is close to HLSL and accepts most existing HLSL code. A GLSL compatibility module eases moving GLSL shaders.

Direct3D 11 and 12 are supported through HLSL output. D3D12 code is DXIL with rasterization, compute and ray tracing stages (raygeneration, intersection, anyhit, closesthit, miss, callable). The target page says mesh shaders are not supported there.
capabilities.inputs: root signature mapping, register and space bindings

capabilities.does: Vulkan output is SPIR-V or GLSL. Parameters use set and binding pairs, root constants map to push constants, and ray tracing uses a shader table.

Metal output is Metal Shading Language and is marked experimental in the README. Stages include vertex, optional mesh and task, optional tessellation and fragment. Buffer arrays are not supported as of Metal 3.1.
WebGPU output is WGSL and is marked experimental. It covers vertex, fragment and compute. Bindings are grouped in bind groups, and ParameterBlock controls the grouping.
CUDA output is C++ for compute only. OptiX output is in progress. A CPU target emits C++ kernel and host code, a standalone executable or a dynamic library, and is marked experimental.
A language server gives IntelliSense in Visual Studio Code and Visual Studio over the Language Server Protocol. Shaders can be debugged with RenderDoc and SPIR-V tools.

rea.notes: The project page does not state a licence or version; the licence is from the GitHub README. The README and the target page disagree on a few points: the README does not name DXIL or PTX as outputs while the target page does, and the target page is inconsistent on mesh shader support.

entries.name: NVIDIA DLSS

licence.name: NVIDIA proprietary. The pages read do not state whether SDK access is gated or free. The public DLSS repo has a LICENSE.txt that was not read.

engines.name: DLSS plugins
engines.does: An official Unreal Engine plugin for UE 5.5 through 5.8 and Unity support for Super Resolution from Unity 2021.2 Beta.

engines.name: NVIDIA Image Scaling SDK
engines.does: A spatial scaling and sharpening algorithm shipped as compute shaders for DX11, DX12 and Vulkan, included in the DLSS repo.

capabilities.does: Super Resolution reconstructs a higher-resolution frame from a lower-resolution render, using an AI model, to raise frame rate.

Frame Generation adds AI-made frames between rendered ones and pairs with NVIDIA Reflex to keep input responsive. Multi Frame Generation makes up to five per rendered frame and needs GeForce RTX 50 Series or RTX PRO Blackwell GPUs.
Ray Reconstruction adds AI-generated pixels to heavily ray-traced scenes, which the page says raises image quality.
DLAA is an AI-driven anti-aliasing technique that the page says raises image quality.
NVIDIA Image Scaling provides one spatial scaling and sharpening algorithm as compute shaders that integrate with DX11, DX12 and Vulkan.

outcomes: higher frame rates and image quality in real-time rendering

rea.notes: Only the marketing page and a thin repo README were readable. The DLSS programming guide, API names and version were not found. The page calls Streamline an open-source cross-IHV solution, which was not opened. GPU requirements other than Multi Frame Generation are not stated.
